item.skycraft.relic.side_bm_hatchling_pa: Imperial labor contracts for nine 'orphaned hatchlings', countersigned with a Stormhold ledger-seal.
item.skycraft.relic.side_bm_leviathan_to: As long as a forearm and yellow as old sap. Many-Notches will want it for his tail.
A Legion standard-top, green with corrosion. The eagle has been bent, deliberately, until its wings touch.
item.skycraft.relic.side_bm_runner_ledge: Casks, dates and a buyer in Bravil. The supplier is written only as 'the one with the copper earring'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_bm_tap_spike.de: A copper spike for drawing sap, crusted amber. Someone filed a maker's mark off it in a hurry.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_blighted_ro: A grape root wrapped in pale threads, like hair. It smells of wet earth and something sweeter.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_dim_welkynd: A blue Ayleid stone, nearly dark. It warms slightly when held under the open sky at night.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_istirus_rol: The fort's last roll of the watch, in the prefect's own hand. One name is marked absent, and it is his.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_livia_feath: A long hagraven quill tied with a faded Vallarius ribbon in green and gold.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_ninth_turn_: Unsigned, sealed in grey wax. It speaks of 'the stranger who kills for us' as though it were a blessing.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_rimeoath.de: An old Nord sword rimed with frost that never melts. Runes along the fuller name a promise, not an owner.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_sadrathi_ur: A small urn of red Morrowind clay, sealed with wax. It is heavier than ash should be, and it occasionally sighs.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_salt_ledger: A smuggler's book of cargo: welkynd stones by the crate, paid for in Summerset gold. Some payments go to the Anvil customs house.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_turned_dagg: A plain iron dagger with a hilt wrapped in grey silk. The blade has been bent three times and straightened three times.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_undimmed_la: A welkynd lantern no bigger than a fist. The light inside it does not flicker, and it does not feel friendly.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_valcis_ledg: An undertaker's book of names and prices. Most entries end in 'buried'. Some end in 'sold'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_vallarius_l: Accounts, births and deaths of House Vallarius. A page near the back has been cut out with a very sharp knife.
item.skycraft.relic.side_cyr_vine_hearts: A seed the size of a plum, green and faintly warm, with a pulse you can feel if you hold still.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_ahzir_signe: A gold ring with a lion's head, worn smooth at the edges from sealing a great many documents it should not have.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_ancient_son: A clay tablet with the true burial song of the First Claw, scratched quickly by someone who knew it would be hidden.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_bride_locke: A silver locket holding two portraits. One face has been scratched out, carefully, with a claw.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_dark_lamp.d: A lamp of black glass that does not shine but swallows. Candles placed near it go out.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_dragon_bone: A splinter of dragon bone, still hot to the touch. The cult believed it was a bone of Alkosh. It was not.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_empty_manif: A caravan manifest listing forty crates of silk and spice. The crates were full of sand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_grey_powder: Fine grey dust that smells of iron and lamp-black. One pinch in an irrigation ditch could sour a field of moon sugar.
The last entry is in a shaking hand: 'A ship with serpent sails, lights burning green, and she asked for me by name.'
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_lattice_len: A lens ground from moonstone, designed to gather the light of Jone and Jode and bend it where it was never meant to go.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_luck_contra: A contract in red ink: twenty years of luck for the merchant Ma'jhad, payable in full at the end. The end is marked as last month.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_mortgage_bu: Loans on every cane-field in western Pellitine, all held by one Senchal lender who signs with a sugar-tooth.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_pelt_of_sca: A senche-tiger pelt as wide as a tent, striped with old scars. Three skooma-darts are still lodged in the shoulder.
item.skycraft.relic.side_els_sweet_ledge: A ship's ledger listing farmers, their debts and the cargo they now owe in moon sugar and skooma.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_double_purse: Two purses knotted together. One is stitched with the at-Senna crescent, the other with the Bel-Tavir scales.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_feed_tag.des: A tag from a crate of goat meat, stamped with the sign of a Skaven apothecary.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_gilt_forgery: A fine copy of an old Hew's Bane scimitar. Fine enough to fool anyone who has never held the real one.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_ledger_of_na: Page after page of names in a careful hand, each one dragged out of a dead mouth.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_star_shard.d: A splinter of black glass flecked with points of light that do not match any sky you know.
A black thorn as long as a hand, bound in red thread. It is warm in a way wood should not be.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_thornwatch_d: A request for relief, sealed in wax that never cracked. The ink has faded to the colour of rust.
Sailing dates of merchant ships, copied from a harbour register in a neat clerk's hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_tonal_cylind: A brass cylinder ringed with grooves. It hums a low note when held near Dwemer metal.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_venom_sac.de: Heavy, warm, and faintly sloshing. Bashir says not to squeeze it.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hf_wager_slip.d: A Sentinel bookmaker's receipt forty years old, naming a duel and the man paid to lose it.
Half-burnt pages of loans and foreclosures. The surviving names are all Stormhaven farmers.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_heron_seal.d: The silver seal of the Order of the Heron's grandmasters, tarnished black.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_hunters_writ: A list of names with a line through most of them. The newest is Isolde Thrale.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_ilsabet_bell: A small iron bell wound in red wool, the sign of the Daughters of Wroth. Its clapper is missing.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_lighthouse_k: An iron key on a ring of tarred rope, still wrapped in a dead man's fingers when you found it.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_morvayne_sig: A heavy silver ring with the Morvayne owl. It is cold to the touch and stays cold.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_pact_stone.d: A flat stone carved with an orc's hand and a giant's foot, pressed side by side.
Five thousand drakes, the north road, at moonrise. The handwriting is very good for a kidnapper.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_river_manife: Not crates. Names. Families, mostly, with a price beside each.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_saerendil_jo: Elven script in violet ink, the last pages written in a shaking, bony hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_vile_token.d: A wish written in a tidy hand and countersigned in something that is not ink: Never to die.
item.skycraft.relic.side_hr_ysmay_ring.d: A thin gold band, worn smooth on the inside. It was still on the ghost's finger when she gave it to you.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_cipher_order: A poisoner's instructions in a palace cipher, in a palace hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_day_book.des: Velsa Taren's notes: doses, dates, and 'the itching is better today'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_dream_journa: The handwriting starts small and careful. By the last page it fills the margins.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_egg_crate.de: Six leathery eggs packed in kelp, still warm, still moving.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_gall_sack.de: Bitter, sticky, and stamped with the Setus mine's tally mark.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_heartseed.de: A pale fungal seed the size of a fist. It is warm, like a held hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_oath_ring.de: A Nord arm-ring stamped with the three-headed Pact seal and a Dunmer captain's mark.
A sliver of black Daedric steel that is always slightly wet.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_strongbox.de: Dented, ash-caked and still locked, which says something for Hlervu locksmiths.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_sugar_ledger: Payments by the moon, and one name repeated each month: C. Ventrilla.
A Dwemer inventory plate; every entry is struck through but one, a regulator coil.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_varyn_seal.d: A brass coffin-seal of the Necrom embalmers, its wax still soft.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_widow_letter: Sealed in Ulvon's urn: a widow's account of who poured the poison, and for whom.
item.skycraft.relic.side_mw_wreck_ledger: Twenty years of ship names, cargoes and dates, in a neat fisherman's hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_pya_mist_lanter: A lantern of blue glass whose light seems to push fog aside.
item.skycraft.relic.side_pya_serpent_egg: A leathery egg the size of a man's head, warm, packed in Woodhearth sawdust.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_heart.desc: Still warm. Still, faintly, beating. It will not keep forever.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_heirloom.de: A family's keepsake, scratched where the thief pried out a stone and thought better of it.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_herbs.desc: A bundle of roots, caps and petals, wrapped in damp cloth so they keep.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_ledger.desc: Names, dates and debts in a cramped hand. Several of the names are important.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_relic.desc: Old, heavy and humming faintly. Whoever wanted it wanted it badly.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_salvage.des: A lockbox from a wreck, swollen with water and sealed with somebody's crest.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_token.desc: Something the captive pressed into your hand so their family would know you.
item.skycraft.relic.side_rad_tome.desc: Its clasp is shaped like a closed eye. The pages are warmer than they should be.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_bleakwind_t: Cut at the root with a woodsman's saw, still smelling of the giant's fire.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_coldvein_le: A guest book in a fine hand. Beside each name: a date, and the word 'rested'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_custodial_k: A small brass key stamped with a Dwemer glyph for 'return'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_dravyne_urn: A Dunmer ash-urn sealed with wax, salt-crusted but unbroken.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_false_lante: A ship's lantern with a shutter, the initial H scratched into the brass.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_fellhammer_: A Legion roll book, every name ticked present, night after night, in fresh ink.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_gerda_lette: Folded small and pinned under a crow's skull, addressed to Bjarni.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_mire_torc.d: A twisted band of black bronze, always cold, always faintly damp.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_orvald_tall: A notched stick with a buyer's name burned beside every notch.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_promise_log: A ship's log, swollen with seawater; the last pages are written in a hurried hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_ransom_tabl: A slate tablet listing warriors whose ransom was promised and never paid.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_resonance_r: A brass rod that hums when tapped, and keeps humming far longer than it should.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_sugar_ledge: Sums paid and received, in a neat Khajiiti hand, with one buyer marked only 'the widow'.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sky_wooden_hors: A child's toy horse, its tail tied with the grey thread of a priest's prayer cord.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_claim_lette: A stalhrim claim and a letter to Astrid, written in a hand that was getting cold.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_duty_roster: A Legion roster, last entry: 'Relief requested. Courier Brenn dispatched.'
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_resonance_p: A Dwemer prism of smoky crystal. It hums a single note when held to the ear.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_seal_ring.d: An iron ring stamped with a lock, worn smooth by a jailer's thumb.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_skaal_mitte: A Skaal mitten stitched with a snow-hare. Someone's mother made this.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_tally_board: Chalk marks past the Redoran safe-line, and a bonus figure circled twice.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sol_war_totem.d: A carved tusk bearing the old seal of Thirsk, and tally-marks of mead never paid.
A small silver bell crusted with coral. It has no clapper, and it rings anyway when the tide turns.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_circle_minu: Minutes of a radical society, mostly complaints about the Dominion, and one furious argument about who keeps painting herons on corpses.
A curved shard of coral grown, not cut, into a lens. It pulses faintly, like something breathing underwater.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_debt_ledger: A record of every coin collected from Neliril Sunhallow. Someone has added it up. Nobody has stopped collecting.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_grey_berrie: Berries the colour of old ash, with a faint taste of brimstone. Someone grafted the bush they grew on.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_grey_feathe: A feather that was a loaf of bread two hours ago. It points, gently but insistently, toward the west.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_gryphon_egg: A speckled egg the size of a helm, warm as a hearthstone. Something inside it taps back when you tap.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_heron_brush: A fine sable brush caked with white lime paint, stamped on the handle with the seal of the Firsthold Watch quartermaster.
A letter in Aldmeris, addressed to 'my wife in the southern isles'. The salutation is written in Pyandonean.
A blue-spiralled conch carved with Maormer tide-notes. Blown at night, it sings in a voice that is not quite yours.
item.skycraft.relic.side_sum_valtaryon_l: Nine centuries of entries, each ending in a payment marked only 'to the Patron'. The final entry, unpaid, reads: the Crystal Tower's wards.
Eleven years of tight Aldmeris script on how the Crystal Tower's wards breathe in and out. Read carefully, it is a burglar's manual.
item.skycraft.relic.side_thr_coral_ledge: Pages of pressed coral, each etched with names and the debts owed by their great-grandchildren.
item.skycraft.relic.side_thr_covenant.de: A contract written on dried kelp. The last signature belongs to a priest of Stendarr.
A face of shed antler and living vine. It is warm, and it breathes slightly when held near the mouth.
Dried strips of bark tied with a cord and tagged with an apothecary's mark. Some of the strips still twitch.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_blooded_horn: A horn of black antler with a name scratched along its bell. The name is Thrandir Quickstep, crossed out, and yours written under it.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_bottled_stor: A stoppered vial of ink that whispers in a Spinner's voice when shaken. It smells of old paper and low tide.
A bone chit promising four hundred drakes to Cassian Dorvel, signed in a flourishing hand: Gaenor Bitterleaf.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_guest_book.d: Names of guests at Elorin's open table. Beside one name each new moon, a different hand has drawn a small red cup.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_jaqspur_shav: A pale ribbon of living wood, still sticky with sap. Whoever cut it had a very sharp knife and a very sure hand.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_knot_cord.de: A Spinner's cord of nine knots. The ninth is tied tighter than the rest, as if by a hand in a hurry.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_legate_diary: A Legion diary swollen with damp. The last pages are written very neatly, by a man who believed every word was justified.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_party_toggle: A coat-toggle carved with the mark of an Elden Root hunting party. It was lying in the ashes of a cold fire.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_story_jars.d: Dozens of ink vials, each labelled with a name. One of the labels reads Ollanwe, in Ollanwe's own hand.
One row of notches counts bows sold. The second row only makes sense if you are counting trees.
item.skycraft.relic.side_vw_welkynd_hear: A blue Ayleid stone wrapped in fig roots that grew around it on purpose. It hums a tune you almost know.
item.skycraft.relic.side_yok_nhalar_diar: A field diary; the last pages list the diggers' names, each crossed out in order.
item.skycraft.relic.side_yok_unblooded_s: A Ra Gada blade of fine old steel without a single nick along its edge.
item.skycraft.relic.sigil_stone.desc: Torn from the top of an Oblivion gate's tower. It's warm, and it pulses like a heart.
item.skycraft.relic.silver_hand_orders.d: Orders to burn Jorrvaskr's hounds out of their den, signed by Krev the Skinner.
item.skycraft.relic.skeleton_key.desc: Nocturnal's own key. It opens anything: locks, doors, minds.
Vaermina's staff. It feeds on dreams.
item.skycraft.relic.smuggler_ledger_tong: A smuggler's accounts, with a column of payments to a Balmora fence named Corvo.
item.skycraft.relic.smuggler_manifest.de: Cargoes ferried across Lake Rumare by night, and the Waterfront warehouse each was bound for.
item.skycraft.relic.ss_magistrate_seal.d: An Imperial seal from a province that no longer belongs to the Empire. Its owner pretended otherwise.
item.skycraft.relic.ss_morag_tong_writ.d: A sealed writ naming every Shadowscale in the Stormhold enclave. Signed by Weighs-the-Coin, in a careful, greedy hand.
item.skycraft.relic.ss_slaver_brand.desc: A Dunmer house-mark on an iron rod. It has been used recently.
item.skycraft.relic.ss_stolen_clutch.des: Six warm, leathery eggs wrapped in moss, packed for a long journey to a collector in Cyrodiil.
item.skycraft.relic.staff_relic_magnus.d: Old Morokei's prize. It drinks magicka from whatever it is pointed at.
item.skycraft.relic.stamped_ebony.desc: Ebony bearing the East Empire Company's stamp, found in a smugglers' cave. It should never have left the warehouse.
item.skycraft.relic.stormcloak_axe.desc: A war axe, sent as a message: choose a side.
item.skycraft.relic.substructure_map.des: A crumbling chart of the Ayleid passages under the Imperial City, older than the Empire above them.
item.skycraft.relic.teekeeus_concordance: A fat, much-annotated index of the Chorrol library. Faintly singed, and missing a corner the scamp chewed off.
item.skycraft.relic.th_blade_insignia.de: A dragon on a dulled steel badge. Its owner kept it hidden for thirty years and polished it every night.
Found under a loose cobble on the Alinor quay. The cipher is clumsy; the treason is not.
item.skycraft.relic.th_orvanwe_letters.d: Letters in a careful hand, sold to a Windhelm buyer: patrol routes, prisoner lists, and the Emissary's own notes.
item.skycraft.relic.th_talos_amulet.desc: Taken from a hidden shrine near Rorikstead. Its worshippers would call it faith. The Thalmor call it evidence.
item.skycraft.relic.thalmor_dossier.desc: Thalmor notes on an old Blades archivist believed to hide beneath Riften.
item.skycraft.relic.thread_renegade.desc: A black thread carried by a renegade who thought it would protect him. It did not.
item.skycraft.relic.thread_ruin.desc: A black thread from the Daedric ruin of Yansirramus, warm as skin.
item.skycraft.relic.thread_shrine.desc: A black thread that never tangles, taken from Mephala's shrine.
item.skycraft.relic.tong_death_list.desc: Names of Hlaalu loyalists in Balmora, several crossed out. The last name is Nileno Dorvayn's.
item.skycraft.relic.troll_fat_offering.d: A slab of fat cut from a living troll, for Malacath's shrine.
item.skycraft.relic.umbranox_signet.desc: The ring of the Counts of Anvil, missing for decades. The Gray Fox gave it to me to return.
item.skycraft.relic.und_barrow_torc.desc: A twisted band of black iron, cold enough to sting the fingers. The dead king wore it for a few thousand years.
item.skycraft.relic.und_broodmother_fang: A hooked fang as long as a dagger, still beaded with venom. Glirion wants it for the trophy wall.
item.skycraft.relic.und_dreloth_mask.des: A carved bonemold mask from the Dreloth family niche. The grave-robber had already scraped the name off half of it.
item.skycraft.relic.und_malatar_varla.de: An Ayleid star-stone humming with stored light. It pulses brighter whenever it is carried away from the ruin.
item.skycraft.relic.und_mazzatun_idol.de: A squat stone figure with jade eyes, worn smooth by the hands of a people who no longer come to pray.
item.skycraft.relic.und_volenfell_core.d: A Dwemer heart of brass and spinning rings. It is still turning, and it is still warm.
item.skycraft.relic.und_warden_horn.desc: A war-horn of yellowed bone bound in bronze, taken from the deepest hall of Labyrinthian.
item.skycraft.relic.uvirith_spores.desc: A sealed pouch of Telvanni tower spores, ready to be coaxed into a mushroom tower.
item.skycraft.relic.vg_collectors_casket: A lacquered box of Daedric curios. Something inside scratches, very faintly, when no one is looking at it.
item.skycraft.relic.vg_dagon_sigil.desc: A shard of black stone that glows like a coal and never cools. Dug out of the ground beneath Mehrunes Dagon's shrine.
Orders sealed in dark red wax: watch the Hall of the Vigilant, count its keepers, and report when the Keeper travels.
item.skycraft.relic.vilkas_blade.desc: Notched from the training yard. Eorlund will know what to do with it.
item.skycraft.relic.welkynd_stone.desc: A blue crystal cut by Ayleid hands. It hums against the palm with stored light.
item.skycraft.relic.wuuthrad_fragment.de: A shard of Ysgramor's legendary axe, carried home across the sea.
story.skycraft.boss.lw_bm_2_boss: The Lord of the Long Supper
story.skycraft.boss.lw_bm_4_boss: Lord Heel of the Dry Fields
story.skycraft.boss.mq_bm_hs_warden: The Warden of the Ninth Gate
story.skycraft.boss.mq_bm_lm_gulper: Old Gulper of the Fourth Canal
story.skycraft.boss.mq_els_tomb_tenant: The Tenant Beneath the Third Stone
story.skycraft.boss.mq_els_weaver_shade: The Weaver Who Would Not Stop
story.skycraft.boss.mq_for_tiger_guardia: The Guardian of the Third Trial
story.skycraft.boss.mq_for_winter_wight: The Wight of the Ninth Winter
story.skycraft.boss.mq_hf_ab_pier_master: Captain Zubair of the Moving Pier
story.skycraft.boss.mq_sum_false_door_ke: The Door That Wore a Face
story.skycraft.boss.mq_sum_gate_warden: The Warden of the Sixteenth Gate
story.skycraft.boss.side_els_mother_nhir: Mother Nhirra, Voice of the Great Dark
story.skycraft.boss.side_hr_aubert: Aubert Morvayne, Eldest of the Vraseth
story.skycraft.boss.side_hr_saerendil: Saerendil Direnni, Warden of the Spire
story.skycraft.boss.side_sum_calanwe: Lady Calanwe of the Drowned Choir
story.skycraft.npc.adamus_phillida.greet: Commander of the Legion in the Heartland, and I have more roads than soldiers. If you can hold a sword and follow an order, we can talk.
story.skycraft.npc.aela.greet: If you've come to stare, the training yard is around back. If you've come to hunt, talk to me.
story.skycraft.npc.agronak_gro_malog.gre: They call me the Gray Prince. The crowd loves the name. I've never been sure what it means, and nobody has ever told me.
story.skycraft.npc.ahzid_at_hel_ra.greet: Cousin Hamaad thinks the past is a fortress. I think it is a tomb. Lovely weather, isn't it?
story.skycraft.npc.alvor.greet: Iron, steel, a bit of leather. If you need it mended, my forge is warm.
story.skycraft.npc.amaund.greet: You are late. Never mind. What I am about to ask has not been asked in four hundred years.
story.skycraft.npc.amiel_lannus.greet: The Priory has been empty for a long time. I kept the lamps lit anyway. Someone had to believe the order would come back.
story.skycraft.npc.ancano.greet: The Thalmor take an interest in the College's work. Purely as advisors, of course.
story.skycraft.npc.ansei_zahreh.greet: The Shehai is not a blade you carry. It is a blade you become. Most who ask me about it are disappointed by that answer.
story.skycraft.npc.aranea.greet: The Lady of Twilight told me you would come. She tells me many things, at dusk and at dawn.
story.skycraft.npc.arelle_vantis.greet: Welcome to the Leyawiin hall. Don't mind the empty benches. The Blackwood Company took the contracts, and the members followed the coin.
story.skycraft.npc.armand_christophe.gre: Easy, friend. On the Waterfront, a man who asks too many questions gets answers from the lake. Ask me the right one.
story.skycraft.npc.arngeir.greet: The Voice is a gift of the gods. We spend our lives learning to use it rightly. Few have the patience.
story.skycraft.npc.astrid.greet: Every family has its rules. Ours are simple: obey, don't betray, and never kill a Brother or Sister.
story.skycraft.npc.athyn_sarethi.greet: Councilor Sarethi. Forgive the bare walls; Redoran spends its coin on swords and grain, not tapestries.
story.skycraft.npc.atub.greet: Largashbur is cursed. Our chief is too proud to ask the Furious One why. I am not.
story.skycraft.npc.aubrec_valmont.greet: A knight of the Rose is courteous to the poor, honest with the powerful and terrible to the wicked. Most days I manage two of the three.
story.skycraft.npc.aventus.greet: Go away. Unless... unless you're the one. Are you the one the Night Mother sent?
story.skycraft.npc.azadhi.greet: Jone and Jode are the two moons, walker. Masser and Secunda, you call them. Their dance tells Khajiit who we are.
story.skycraft.npc.balgruuf.greet: Whiterun stands at the heart of Skyrim, and I intend to keep it standing. What brings you before me?
story.skycraft.npc.bersi.greet: Pottery, fine pottery. And if you break it, you've bought it.
story.skycraft.npc.boethiah_cultist.gree: Boethiah respects only strength, and betrayal is a kind of strength. Have you come to prove yours?
story.skycraft.npc.bolvyn_venim.greet: I am Archmaster of this House. Whatever you want, say it plainly, and do not waste the Archmaster's time.
story.skycraft.npc.borri.greet: (Master Borri says nothing. His eyes go to the courtyard gate, and back to you.)
story.skycraft.npc.brenna_ashfall.greet: Stendarr bids us hunt monsters. He never said they'd all have fangs. Some carry silver and call themselves heroes.
story.skycraft.npc.brother_dranos.greet: I tend the sick, and I read old books, and I ask old questions. Some in the Temple think the last of these is the most dangerous.
story.skycraft.npc.brynjolf.greet: Never done an honest day's work in your life for all that coin you're carrying, eh lass? Or lad. The light's poor.
story.skycraft.npc.burguk_gro_dushnikh.g: Dushnikh Yal does not feed strangers. Strangers feed Dushnikh Yal, or they leave. Which are you?
story.skycraft.npc.burz_gro_khash.greet: Edge on that blade's gone soft. Leave it on the bench, I'll fix it, and you'll listen to me complain while I do.
story.skycraft.npc.canctunian_ponius.gre: The East Empire Company moves the wealth of an Empire, and I move the Company. Keep your hands clean and your ledgers cleaner.
story.skycraft.npc.captain_noraya.greet: I've run cargo past pirates, storms and Imperial tax-men. The tax-men were the worst.
story.skycraft.npc.carcette.greet: Stendarr's mercy is for the lost. His hammer is for the things that lose them. Which have you come about?
story.skycraft.npc.carnius_magius.greet: Factor of Raven Rock. This colony runs on ebony, and the ebony runs through me. Remember that, and we'll get along famously.
story.skycraft.npc.celarus.greet: Every question you ask me has been asked before, usually by someone more patient. Ask anyway. The asking is the lesson.
story.skycraft.npc.celinar.greet: You found Artaeum. Or Artaeum let itself be found by you. That distinction will matter, later.
story.skycraft.npc.cicero.greet: Hello, hello! Cicero tends the Mother. Cicero does not like to be interrupted. Unless it's for a joke!
story.skycraft.npc.corvinus_aelius.greet: Fine silks from the Market District, priced for people who never ask the price. Are you that kind of person?
story.skycraft.npc.corvo_malaxius.greet: Looking to sell something? I'm looking to buy. No questions, no names, and especially no Tong.
story.skycraft.npc.crassius_curio.greet: Oh, a new face! Do come in. I am Councilor Crassius Curio, patron of the arts, friend of the House, and an enthusiastic judge of character. Mostly of the character's calves.
story.skycraft.npc.dalvilu_arethan.greet: Balmora's temple keeps its doors open and its lamps lit. If you are troubled, sit. If you are here to help, there is always more to do.
story.skycraft.npc.dame_maelis_corbel.gr: I train the squires. If you've come to be one, roll up your sleeves. If you've come to watch, there's a bench by the wall.
story.skycraft.npc.dame_orielle_fontaine: Manners first, then the sword. You'd be amazed how many fights end at the manners.
story.skycraft.npc.dar_jazad.greet: Senchal has a hundred smugglers and only one Dar'jazad. The others will cheat you. This one will cheat you honestly.
story.skycraft.npc.deeja.greet: The Hist speaks in sap and dreams. This one listens. Lately, the Hist sounds afraid.
story.skycraft.npc.delphine.greet: Rooms are ten septims. Mead is cheaper. Questions cost more.
story.skycraft.npc.delvin.greet: Business has been terrible since the curse. Not that I believe in curses. Mostly.
story.skycraft.npc.dervenin.greet: My master is on vacation! He's in the head of a dead king, and he won't come out! Help a poor madman?
story.skycraft.npc.dexion.greet: A Moth Priest reads the Elder Scrolls, and pays for it with his eyes. I will pay, if the cause is worth it.
story.skycraft.npc.divayth_fyr.greet: Four thousand years, and visitors still knock as though I might be asleep. I am never asleep. Come in, and touch nothing.
story.skycraft.npc.dulcia_marcanus.greet: Three goats gone this month and a cart burned. If the Guild doesn't help, I'll have nothing left to pay it with.
story.skycraft.npc.dulnea_ralaal.greet: The kwama are restless and something bigger is down there with them. I've been hiding in this side tunnel for a day.
story.skycraft.npc.einarth.greet: (Master Einarth inclines his head, slowly, as if even a nod were a word he must not waste.)
story.skycraft.npc.elenwen.greet: Skyrim is cold, its people are loud, and its gods are wrong. Otherwise it is a perfectly pleasant posting. What do you need?
story.skycraft.npc.elsabet_mornay.greet: Father sits on the King's council. Everyone is very polite to me, and nobody tells me anything.
story.skycraft.npc.eltrys.greet: Not here. Not in the open. Markarth has ears in the stones, and most of them are paid for.
story.skycraft.npc.eno_hlaalu.greet: The Morag Tong is the oldest guild in Morrowind, and the only one the law permits to kill. We do it by writ, in daylight, and we sign our work.
story.skycraft.npc.eola.greet: You look hungry. Not for bread, I think. For something rarer.
story.skycraft.npc.eorlund.greet: The Skyforge was old when the first Companions came. I only keep it fed.
story.skycraft.npc.erandur.greet: Dawnstar dreams badly, and every dream has the same mother. I know her name. I served her once.
story.skycraft.npc.erunor_vaelanwe.greet: You stand straighter than most recruits. Good. The Thalmor notice posture. We notice everything, eventually.
story.skycraft.npc.esbern.greet: Forty years I've been waiting for the world to end. You'll forgive me if I'm not good company.
story.skycraft.npc.ethasi_rilvayn.greet: This hall keeps the writs for the West Gash. If you're here to hire us, state the name. If you're here to join, state your reasons.
story.skycraft.npc.ezhar_at_taneth.greet: Yokuda is under the sea, friend, and the sea is where the money is. Sit down. Have you ever read a bill of lading?
story.skycraft.npc.faendir.greet: Mind your feet. That moss was here before your grandmother's grandmother, and it will be here after you, if you mind your feet.
story.skycraft.npc.falco_galenus.greet: Somebody has to keep the colony's books honest. Apparently that somebody is me, whether I like it or not.
story.skycraft.npc.faleen.greet: The Jarl has no time for you. I'll decide whether he makes some.
story.skycraft.npc.falion.greet: Morthal has little use for a conjurer, and less for questions. Still, you have the look of someone who needs one.
story.skycraft.npc.faralda.greet: The bridge is narrow and the drop is long. State your business with the College.
story.skycraft.npc.farengar.greet: Unless you've brought me a dragon, or something about dragons, I'm rather busy.
story.skycraft.npc.farkas.greet: Vilkas says I talk too much. I don't think so. Do you think so?
story.skycraft.npc.farouz_the_drover.gre: Salt, dyes and Yokudan steel. Everything in these crates is older than the Empire's roads and worth more than its coin.
story.skycraft.npc.feldras_morvayn.greet: A tower is not built, it is persuaded to grow. Bring me patience and spores, and I'll give you a home.
story.skycraft.npc.frea.greet: The All-Maker's stones are sick, and my people walk in their sleep. If you can help, help. If not, stand aside.
story.skycraft.npc.gaius_eruvan.greet: Officially, the Blades were disbanded and there's nobody up here but an old man and some goats. Unofficially, mind your step on the ice.
story.skycraft.npc.galmar.greet: You want to fight for Skyrim? Good. Let's see if you can.
story.skycraft.npc.garrick_vane.greet: I serve the Chancellor. That is all you need to know about me, and more than most people learn.
story.skycraft.npc.geldis.greet: The Retching Netch serves the best sujamma on Solstheim. It's also the only sujamma on Solstheim.
story.skycraft.npc.gerdur.greet: The mill doesn't run itself. But for a friend of my brother's, I can spare a minute.
story.skycraft.npc.ghamrash_gra_shura.gr: Every wall in Orsinium starts as ore in somebody's hands. Usually mine. What have you brought me?
Sit, sit. Nobody joins the Undaunted sober, and nobody leaves this table until the cask is dry or the floor is comfortable.
story.skycraft.npc.gray_fox.greet: You'll forget my face the moment you look away. Don't take it personally. It's an old trick, and not one I chose.
story.skycraft.npc.green_lady.greet: The Silvenar speaks for the people. I hunt for them. If you are here to waste his time, you will find I am quicker than he is.
story.skycraft.npc.gurak.greet: Orsinium has been burned down more times than any city in Tamriel. It is still here. So am I.
story.skycraft.npc.hadoba.greet: The moons are dancing well tonight, walker. This one can always tell. Sit, and let Hadoba see what kind of shadow you cast.
story.skycraft.npc.hadvar.greet: Mind the keep, the walls are still coming down. Whatever that thing was, the Legion will need every sword.
story.skycraft.npc.haelga.greet: Dibella blesses all who come to her with an open heart. Or an open purse.
story.skycraft.npc.hamaad_at_hel_ra.gree: My grandfather's grandfather crossed the sea with a sword and the songs of Yokuda. I still have the songs. Have you come to learn them, or to sell me something?
story.skycraft.npc.hannibal_traven.greet: The University is open to anyone with patience and a mind. The first is rarer than you would think.
story.skycraft.npc.harkon.greet: You stand in Castle Volkihar, mortal, and you still have your blood. Consider that a courtesy.
story.skycraft.npc.hestor_aldrinus.greet: Antiquities, curiosities, rarities from every corner of Tamriel. Nothing dangerous, of course. Almost nothing.
story.skycraft.npc.hieronymus_lex.greet: Captain Lex, Imperial Watch. Every theft in this city is a crime against the Emperor, and every unsolved one is a crime against me.
story.skycraft.npc.hlaalu_factor.greet: House Hlaalu deals in everything. Even information. Especially information.
story.skycraft.npc.iachesis.greet: Hm. You arrived exactly when I expected you, which is to say three days late. Sit. Time is a river, and we are about to go fishing.
story.skycraft.npc.ilmaril_senwe.greet: The Crystal Tower has kept the memory of the Aldmer since before the first Bosmer sang the first tree into shape. Do not touch the shelves.
story.skycraft.npc.ilvia_tarn.greet: The Akaviri left us their swords, their walls and their oaths. I keep all three dusted. Mostly the oaths.
story.skycraft.npc.irileth.greet: Keep your hands where I can see them. The Jarl has had enough surprises this year.
story.skycraft.npc.isran.greet: The Vigil of Stendarr failed. The Dawnguard won't. Vampires are getting bolder, and somebody has to be bolder still.
story.skycraft.npc.ivo_brennault.greet: The King is very busy. I am very busy on his behalf. Speak quickly, and beautifully if you can manage it.
story.skycraft.npc.jo_vassa.greet: This one has walked from Rimmen with bad knees and a good heart. Only a little further now. Only a little.
story.skycraft.npc.kaie_briar_mother.gre: The Reach remembers who it belongs to. The stone remembers. The roots remember. Do you?
story.skycraft.npc.karliah.greet: Twenty-five years I've waited for someone to hear the truth. Sit, and listen.
story.skycraft.npc.keerava.greet: The Bee and Barb serves drink and food. Trouble, it does not serve.
story.skycraft.npc.kesh.greet: Kesh tends the Taskmaster's shrine. Kesh is clean. The others? Not so clean.
story.skycraft.npc.klimmek.greet: My knees used to climb that mountain. These days they mostly complain about it.
story.skycraft.npc.kodlak.greet: Jorrvaskr has stood longer than Whiterun's walls. We take work for coin and honor both, and we don't ask which a job pays in.
story.skycraft.npc.lady_yasreen.greet: My father believes the old ways will keep us. I believe they will, if someone is willing to bleed for them.
My family has held Aldcroft for six generations. I mean to hold it for a seventh, if I can get there alive.
story.skycraft.npc.larak_gro_khazgur.gre: Burguk sends a messenger instead of coming himself. That tells me most of what I need to know.
story.skycraft.npc.lucien_lachance.greet: Don't be alarmed. I've been watching you for some time, and I like what I've seen. The Family has an offer for you.
story.skycraft.npc.lucretia_valga.greet: Imperial Commissioner of Charters. Every company in the Empire trades by the Emperor's leave, and I decide how long that leave lasts.
story.skycraft.npc.madanach.greet: So the Silver-Bloods have sent me another one. Sit. The mine has nothing but time, and I have spent a great deal of it waiting for someone useful.
story.skycraft.npc.magister.greet: Alinor welcomes scholars. Barbarians, it merely tolerates. Which are you?
story.skycraft.npc.maj_al_ragath.greet: Glirion sends me his drunks and calls them recruits. Prove me wrong about you, and do it before I finish this cup.
story.skycraft.npc.malborn.greet: I don't know you. Unless Delphine sent you, in which case, keep your voice down.
story.skycraft.npc.mallam_ryon.greet: I speak for the masters of this House, who cannot be bothered to speak for themselves. You may consider that an honour. They would.
story.skycraft.npc.mane.greet: The Mane speaks for the moons and for every Khajiit under them. Speak plainly, and the Mane will listen.
story.skycraft.npc.marcella_tullus.greet: I build walls. Good ones. The trouble is that people keep wanting to knock them down.
story.skycraft.npc.marius_faelian.greet: Imperial goods, Imperial prices, Imperial receipts. I don't deal in anything that isn't on the books.
story.skycraft.npc.master_aryon.greet: Most of my colleagues think the world ends at the edge of their towers. I am trying to persuade them otherwise. It is slow work.
story.skycraft.npc.master_gothren.greet: The Council needs no new voices. The Council needs fewer. Leave my tower while you still have legs.
story.skycraft.npc.maven.greet: If you're here to beg, the Temple of Mara is down the street. If you're here to work, sit down and close your mouth.
story.skycraft.npc.mercer.greet: Brynjolf vouches for you. That buys you a seat at the table. Keeping it is up to you.
story.skycraft.npc.meril_vandas.greet: Give me stone, coin and a season without raiders, and I'll give you a manor the whole West Gash will envy.
story.skycraft.npc.millona_umbranox.gree: Anvil has had a countess and no count for a very long time. I have grown used to answering for both.
story.skycraft.npc.mirabelle.greet: If you've lost your way, I can point you. If you've broken something, I'd rather know now.
story.skycraft.npc.mistress_dratha.greet: Stand further back. Further. There. Men are tolerable at a distance, and you are not yet tolerable.
story.skycraft.npc.modryn_oreyn.greet: I've buried more contracts than most men have signed. Ask your question and I'll tell you whether it'll get you killed.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_dusk.greet: Eighty fathoms to the water, and not a drop to spare. Do not pour out what you cannot return. Drink slowly. Count each swallow.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_eeka.greet: The Hist does not speak. It hums, and the humming means something different to everyone who lies down beneath it. Do not ask what it said to me.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_eesh.greet: We do not pray for the dead. We tell them where they are. It is amazing how few of them know.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_fasteyes.greet: I see a lot. I say about a tenth of it. Ask nicely and I might tell you the tenth that is useful.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_gaar.greet: Funeral lamps. Waterproof. Windproof. Argument-proof. Take one; light it on the barge. The dead like to see the way.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_horu.greet: A cut is a conversation. You ask the tree. The tree decides. If it bleeds gold, you have been polite.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_hushmoss.greet: The Root Cellar. Dry rooms between wet roots. We do not have a menu; we have what the tree gives that day. It gave soup.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_kessa.greet: Rope, pitch, peg and plumb. If it is tied, I tied it. If it fell, you did not follow my instructions. Do not ask me about the bridge.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_kessta.greet: I have come to see my brother. The barge-mother says the living do not cross. I have been sitting here three days. I will sit three more.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_kulasha.greet: The Stable Steed. A bed for a guar, a bed for a rider, and the guar eats first. It is not discrimination. It is economics.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_moons.greet: The Hist remembers every hatchling's first breath, and every ship's last. Sit. It will not mind. It has been listening since before the boats.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_mortar.greet: The Broken Ring. The roof is new, the walls are old, and the beds are somewhere in between. Rooms by the night. Rubble by arrangement.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_mudtoe.greet: Every canal in this city has a name and a mood. Learn the mood, and the boat goes where you will. Learn the name, and the boat goes where it likes.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_mussa.greet: Rice. Three seasons a year. It tastes of mud and sun. Sit. You are too thin. Eat. We shall not mention it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_nesa.greet: Pots, jars, tiles and one very ugly, very beloved idol. If it breaks, I make another. If it breaks twice, I take it personally.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_noo.greet: A mason measures twice and still apologises to the stone. Mind the plumb. Mind the mortar. Mind your elbow; the chisel is behind it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_nook.greet: Every stone has a face under its face. I only take away what is not it. Do not touch the idol. It has not forgiven the last person.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_nulaa.greet: At the centre of the spiral is a fire. At the edge of the spiral is a door. In between is a very long walk. Do not hurry. Do not speak. That is the whole of it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_ocheeva.greet: Cloth from Cyrodiil, wine from Cyrodiil, regrets from Cyrodiil. I import it all and sell it dear. Do not haggle. I like it, which is the problem.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_padar.greet: Every stone I lift was somebody's wall. Every wall I raise will be somebody's ruin. It is called building. You may call it stubbornness; I will not argue.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_pebble.greet: Gorge goods: rope, hook, climbing-oil, a very good line in sensible boots. What do I have that is not for sale? The gorge.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_pi.greet: Each bed is for one family's dead. White lilies for the quiet. Red for the angry. If it blooms black, I stop. That is the whole rule.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_pip.greet: Why do you talk so much? Elder says you should not talk at the fire. Are you going to walk the spiral? I walked it. It is very long.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_ruu.greet: Hist-sap by the thimble. Not the sacred kind. The kind that the sacred kind rubs off on. Do not ask me for a receipt. Do not ask me for anything.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_scales.greet: A bridge is a promise: that both ends will still be there tomorrow. I am the keeper of that promise. State your business and keep to the stones.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_seeth.greet: I carry the dead. Not the whole way; only to the isle. They go the rest on their own. It is a kind of ferry. I am paid in lilies.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_seshi.greet: Grain by the measure, bread by the loaf, and I know who has cheated me by the weight of their pockets. Do not stand there. You are in the shade.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_softstep.greet: The Two Hills Rest. One door for each ziggurat; the beds are on both hills and the soup is on the bridge. Do not drop the bowl.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_tamtam.greet: From the watchtower I see three days of road. I see dust. I do not see rain. I have been watching for rain for eleven years.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_teeba.greet: Before the ring broke, the stairs went somewhere. Now they stand on their own and are polite about it. I remember where they led. I have not told anyone.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_teek.greet: I hunt in silence. It is not that I have nothing to say. I have found that most of it can wait. Eat. Sit. We shall not talk about it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_varro.greet: Legion customs, sera. I count what comes in and what goes out. Neither seems to match, and I am told that is the marsh's way. I do not accept it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_verrus.greet: Court is in session. Do not interrupt, do not editorialise, do not bring a goat. The goat is a long story and I am still annoyed.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_wetwhisk.greet: The Dripping Reed. Rooms on stilts, soup in the shell, and a rule: no one leaves without telling someone where they are going. The canals are patient. They are not forgiving.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_bm_yill.greet: I know every root-walk in Thorn. I have fallen off most of them. The ones I have not fallen off, I do not recommend.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_dufrane.gre: Retired. Entirely. A man who has spent thirty years smuggling cheese has earned the right to sell maps to anyone fool enough to buy one. Sit, sit, and pretend you did not hear that.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_eudora.gree: The Drowned Compass: ale, hammocks, and the only inn in Anvil that has never lost a guest to the sea. We lost two to the cellar, but the cellar is a different matter. Say hello to Gull. Gull does not like you.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_hob.greet: Chandler to the harbour, rope to the nation. Buy a coil, take a coil. If you leave without a coil the harbour gets nervous, and a nervous harbour is a leaky harbour.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_marga.greet: Needle, twine, and a very good memory. I mend what the sea breaks. I also remember which boats it breaks twice, and which it stops breaking altogether, if you follow me.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_olwen.greet: The lamp is mine. The lens is mine. The oil is the Harbourmaster's, and the dark is, I am told, nobody's fault. Do you often climb stairs for no reason?
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_an_teodor.gree: Manifests are in order, duties are paid, and the tide table is accurate to the quarter-hour. If you came to ask about a particular name, I regret that I have mislaid it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_brandt.gree: Bellows run on the creek, hammers run on my arm, and the iron runs when I tell it. If you want it by Morning Star, tell me now. If you want it pretty, tell me after.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_hrodgar.gre: Candles by the stone, by the pound, by the hour. Beeswax for the temple, tallow for the poor, a black one for the nights you do not want to be seen. And if you ask nicely, a rumour.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_ilsa.greet: Pass is open, but only just. Snow slides every second dawn and the courier road is a coin toss. If you can ride, I could use a rider. If you cannot, mind the ice.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_matina.gree: The Chapel is open to all who come in peace, and to a few who do not, provided they wipe their boots. I am copying the Dragon-Blood prayers. It is slow. The ink freezes.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_wulf.greet: Three sleds I have lost to that pass, and I have named the last one Patience. If the road is closed, I am your man. If it is open, I am drunk.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_br_ysolde.gree: Welcome to the Jerall View. Thirty-one steps up, and every one of them worth it. The stew is hot, the beds are warm, and the window faces north, so you can watch it snow on someone else.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_nettle.gree: Eels for coin, secrets for eels, and a free word for anyone who can lift a basket. I have fed this hill for sixty winters, child, and I know what every stair has eaten.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_ottilie.gre: Welcome to the Lonely Suitor Lodge, ten storeys of balcony and one of dignity. We number the rooms to ninety-nine. Do not ask about forty to fifty-nine. Everyone asks. It is tiresome.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_pellia.gree: If you are here to tell me the Count's clerk has done something, get in the queue. I have been writing the queue down. It is nine pages long and I have no one to give it to.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_tomas.greet: Lucky knots, three for a copper! The Lady blesses every fisherman who ties one. If it fails, it was tied wrong. If it works, it was tied right. Either way, I did my part.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_ulrich.gree: The man gestures at his throat, then at the slate hanging from his belt. It reads, in careful, rounded letters: I am sorry. I do not speak. Please do not be unkind.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_bv_vedius.gree: The Count's counting-house is closed to the public on Sundas. And Tirdas. And, as it happens, today. What business could possibly require my attention?
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ch_arden.greet: I tend the Oak. Not the town, not the guild, not the Count, the Oak. It is two thousand years old and has never once asked me for anything. I am beginning to suspect it is too polite.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ch_hesk.greet: Scribe of Weynon Priory, here on business that is not business. If a man leaves you a letter and says, burn it, do not burn it. Read it first, then burn it. That is the proper order.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ch_mabyn.greet: Welcome to the Hungry Heron. That is Heron on the wall. Do not ask him to move. He has been there since my husband died, and he does not like to be bothered. He is, as you can see, a very good listener.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ch_tarn.greet: Wells, cisterns, drains and the occasional grave. A good well is a good argument, I say. You dig down until the earth stops disagreeing. I have never dug a wet one that I could not talk my way out of.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ch_thorne.gree: Tinctures, poultices and one very effective cough syrup that is mostly honey. If you are ill, I can help. If you are dying, I can tell you the date. Either way, no credit.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_cy_brenius.gre: Cheydinhal has been my town for sixty years, and it will be my town for twenty more. The market is mine by long custom. The newcomers may sell at the edges, and be grateful.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_cy_ilvesa.gree: The Refugee Hall is not a charity and not a prison. It is a roof, a pot and a roll of names. If you have a complaint, tell it to the roll. If you have a coin, tell it to me.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_cy_nelas.greet: He keeps his hood up and his voice low. If asked, he says he is a cooper from Ald'ruhn. His hands, when he thinks no one is looking, still fold into the Ordinator's salute.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_cy_odell.greet: The bridge is open, the toll is one riddle or one copper, and I will not hear arguments about the ratio. Last month a scholar paid in the answer to the riddle I had not yet asked. I let him through.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_cy_sarel.greet: I keep the peace, and I keep it fairly. That means everyone is a little angry with me all the time. It is the only sign I am doing it right.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_aurex.greet: Elven Gardens night watch. I count lamps, locks and people, in that order, and tonight one of those sums is wrong. State your business or walk on.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_calvus.gree: Every sin in the Imperial City is whispered to me at least once. Do not worry. I have the memory of a sieve. Only the heavy things stay behind.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_cato.greet: Merrit & Son, wax, seals and stationery. Your signet, your sealing ring, your good name: all of them cost less than you think and exactly what they are worth.
Bargeman, not boatman. Boats are for people with somewhere to be. I carry whatever the river hands me, and I do not read what is written on it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_junius.gree: Pell, Drainmaster of the Waterfront, forty-one years in the dark with a lantern and a ledger. If it flows, I know where. If it should not flow, I know where too.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_odalis.gree: Welcome to the Third Ledger. Every cup comes with a receipt, stamped in triplicate, and no, I will not take it off the bill if you lose it. Rules are rules. Sit.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_pomponia.gr: Careful of the glasshouse door, it sticks. The Arboretum keeps three thousand living species and four hundred years of botanical grudges. I water both.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_ic_verus.greet: The Palace is aware of your presence, citizen. It is also aware of a number of things you would prefer it were not. Be brief.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_kv_dorrik.gree: Stone by stone, lad. The Count said rebuild and I said how, and he said stone by stone. So that is what I do. If you find a cellar the city forgot, you tell me first. Before the priests.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_kv_hetta.greet: The Canvas Cup, under the arena stands, which is why the mugs are dented Legion helmets and the soup is a bit gritty. Do not ask whose helmets. Sit down and have some. It is all paid for.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_kv_ilvara.gree: Water is boiled, bandages are boiled, bread is cut. If you are hurt, sit. If you are not, lift. The roll of the lost is on the wall. Please do not touch it with dirty hands.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_kv_pell.greet: Quartermaster to the rebuilding. Pay, pitch, plaster and pins. If you are doing anything with a hammer, I want a receipt. If it is the wrong hammer, I want a different receipt.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_kv_tilly.greet: I have a kite. It is my da's kite. He said I could keep it if I did not fly it near the big hole. I am not near the hole. I am going to be at the hole in about a minute.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_sk_brother_gal: The Count's Garden Chapel has no walls, only columns. People say the Nine do not need roofs. I say the Nine do not pay for roofs. Mind the bees; they are tenants.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_sk_ferro.greet: Cask-sticks and spigots, the finest corks this side of Chorrol, and cheap rope in case a customer wishes to hang themselves from disappointment. My own wine, however, is excellent.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_sk_gaspara.gre: The Two Sisters Lodge! No sisters, mind. I am the daughter and the Lodge is the other half. The arbour is open until the grapes are crushed. Then it is open until the wine is drunk.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_sk_lucan.greet: The Count's ledger is the only honest document in Skingrad, and it is missing a page. If that is a joke, I am too tired to laugh. If it is not, I would like very much to meet the one who stole it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_cyr_sk_orla.greet: Barrel hoops, press screws, pruning shears, and a very fine spoon if you know where to look. I do not make swords. A sword never fed anyone. Sit. Tell me about your hoop.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_ajh.greet: Ajh poles a long canal-boat between the arching bridges and hums off-key. He knows every sluice, every bridge-ghost and which canal-side window to avoid after midnight.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_breezy.greet: The Sweet Breezes is a three-storey inn where every room faces the sea and every window has been broken at least once by a wind that insists on coming in. Zhaleh swears the wind pays for its own glass.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_cane_widow.gre: Tathara grew sugar for thirty years. This season her fields burned in a night. She stands where the cane was and says nothing, and the neighbours know better than to ask.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_claw_inn.greet: The Claw-and-Cistern keeps a rain barrel in the middle of the taproom that is always full, even in drought. Ruzhi will not say why. She pours the best cold water in Anequina and charges for it like wine.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_dar.greet: Dar keeps the ring of moonstones in the centre of Hakoshae and sweeps it every dawn. He says the stones have never once been dirty, and he sweeps them anyway, because it is a courtesy.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_eighth_spoke.g: The Eighth Spoke stands on the eighth lane of the Wheel, which most visitors will tell you does not exist. It does. It is just always hidden behind the seventh. Shakhra pours from a skin on a hook and never repeats a drink twice the same way.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_green_barge: Skipper Rha'ni of the Green Barge
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_green_barge.gr: The Green Barge is a moored river-barge that has been a tavern for eleven years and has not left its moorings in nine. Rha'ni swears it is still ready to sail. The barge, privately, is not so sure.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_hajir.greet: Hajir sells cups of water from a rolling barrel and a very small bell. He sells the same cup four times a day. He swears the water is fresher each time. It probably is.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_hive_cub.greet: Ji'sha has been stung more than anyone in Corinthe and counts it as a rank. She will tell you how many stings she has, which hive, and what the bee was thinking.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_jakhar.greet: Ja'khar inspects every crate, barrel and bucket that crosses the Senchal quay. He once confiscated a sack of flour because it smelled "ambitious".
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_jaro.greet: Jaro keeps the lunar ledger and has ink to the elbow. He rises at moonset, eats at moonrise, and has not seen a noon since the harvest tax of three years ago.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_kahlil.greet: Kahlil has made rings for three Princes and a spoon for a cat who outlived all of them. He is the finest hand in Rimmen and he will tell you so while you are in the middle of a sentence.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_ke.greet: Ke has walked to every moon-temple of Elsweyr and is on his second lap. He has no goal. He says that is the pilgrimage.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_khir.greet: Khir collects the toll at the hub of the Great Market Wheel. Every lane pays him a copper a cart, and every cart tries to look as if it has paid already. He has never once been fooled, and he is still annoyed about it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_lek.greet: Lek advises the Prince on matters of trade, war and marriage. He advises on the weather, too, but only as a courtesy to the weather.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_mala.greet: Mala keeps the rooftop cisterns and has counted every drop that has fallen on Orcrest since she was a cub. She keeps the number in her head and tells it to no one.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_matisha.greet: Welcome to the Purring Ledger. Ma'tisha keeps every tab in pawprints, not numbers, so no one can say she cheated them. She only has to remember whose paw is whose. She is very good at paws.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_mizra.greet: Mizra knows the roads of Anequina by the smell of their dust. She can tell you which oasis has gone bad by the way the camels refuse to look at it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_mura.greet: Mura tends the Garden Cathedral and its three hundred hives. She wears a veil of fine mesh and answers to the hum of her bees before she answers to her name.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_netch_ballooni: Q'ri pilots a balloon made from a grown netch and always has one story too many. She trades rides for tales. She trades tales for rides. She is rumoured to have no home on the ground at all.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_nuri.greet: Nuri tells fortunes in a striped tent and has never been wrong, which is exactly why she is not very popular. She always tells you more than you paid for. She says it is a flaw in her scales.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_raz.greet: Raz commands the Claw Gate and is not a cat who smiles. He has a scar from ear to jaw and will explain it, in detail, if you ask nicely. No one has asked nicely.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_rest_house.gre: Hamza runs the Pilgrim's Rest, a long low house with seventeen beds and no locks. He says the moonstones watch the door. Nobody has stolen anything from there in living memory, which is a long time among cats.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_rhal.greet: Rhal is the Prince's cousin, which he mentions in the first sentence, the second, and the invoice. He is generous, never on time, and always about to do you a favour that costs you money.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_ridar.greet: Ri'dar weighs every sack that enters the Exchange. He can tell a short measure by the sound it makes in the scale pan, and he is not shy about letting the seller hear it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_route_trader.g: Ha'bir carries the Baandari route book and counts sorry the day it was taken from his wagon. He is polite to everyone, and he counts their fingers.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_shahra.greet: Shahra sings the hours of the Mane's Court: Masser's hour, Secunda's hour, and the held-breath hour when neither moon is up. People forget a singer is in the room. Shahra remembers everything they said.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_sihe.greet: Sihe watches the plateau from the highest watchtower and says she can tell a bandit from a trader at four miles by how the dust sits. She is right more than seems fair.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_sira.greet: Sira holds the key to the necropolis door and has never once lent it. The dead of Rimmen are her family. She is very particular about visitors, and she does not care how they are dressed.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_star_tutor.gre: Zhazir tutors three cubs in the stars beneath the adeptorium dome. A chart has gone missing, and he has been counting ceiling-tiles ever since to avoid saying so.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_suri.greet: Su'ri is the tomb-guardian of the east side and carries a spear that has not once been used in anger. She says that is the whole point of a good spear.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_tamhir.greet: The Sugar Bowl is a bowl-shaped courtyard tavern and Tamhir is its famous single employee. He pours, cooks, sweeps and sings. Ask for the house wine only if you are prepared to ask what is in it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_tazhi.greet: Tazhi runs notes between the Exchange, the Court and the Observatory for a copper each. Tazhi has read none of them. Tazhi has read all of them.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_tema.greet: Tema runs the third boiling-floor of the Sugar Boil House. Her forearms are burn-scarred to the elbow and she calls each vat by a name. They are all named after exes.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_twin_keeper: Keeper Ma'tir of the Twin Moons
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_twin_keeper.gr: Ma'tir runs the Twin Moons roadhouse where travellers wager on the moon-phase. She has lost every wager she ever made against the sky, and says it keeps the house honest.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_zhel: Matron Zhel of the Orchard Hall
story.skycraft.npc.mq_els_zhel.greet: Zhel is matron of the orchard guild and keeps the grafting-book that no one else is allowed to read. She is courteous, firm, and in thirty years has never once been caught telling the truth about a pear.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_anwar.greet: Anwar has spent forty years in Sentinel's archives chasing a single rumour: that the Yokudan Way of the Sword is still taught, on an island no one has charted. He is eighty. He is very impatient.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_caelir.greet: Caelir has watched the Maormer fleet from a rock in the strait for twelve years, and has learned their lamps. She says she knows each ship by its smell. She does not say which smells she prefers.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_captive: The Captive of the Brine Tank
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_captive.greet: A thin man in a ragged Altmer cloak is held in a tank of brine, up to his chin. He says he is a scholar. He says it quickly, and often, and with great sincerity.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_ghost_monk.gre: The tiger-monk stands at the shrine gate and does not move, and does not breathe, and does not speak. Villagers say he has been there for four hundred years. They greet him anyway. It is only polite.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_grim.greet: Grim hunts on the shelf where the ice cracks. He has seen a dragon there, once, asleep under a skin of ice with its eye open. He says it winked. Nobody else believes him, and he does not mind.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_hiro: Master Hiro of the Tiger Shrine
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_hiro.greet: Hiro teaches blades by never touching one. He says a sword is a letter, and a swordsman is a person who has learned to read. His students are very quiet, and extremely well-read.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_hjoldis.greet: Hjoldis buys, sells and sponsors anything that has ever been rumoured to come from Atmora. She keeps a map with a very big blank in the north, and a very small ship in her ledger that has not yet returned.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_hrafn.greet: Hrafn rules the last longhall on the ice. He has no steward, no housecarl and no heir. He has a very large axe and ten dozen stories, and he gives all of them away to strangers, for stories are lighter to carry than sorrow.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_ilu.greet: Ilu grinds shells into armour and ships' fittings in a workshop that smells of rain and old teeth. She is the only artisan the Admiral has never once overruled, and she is very careful to keep it that way.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_jai.greet: Jai is the finest of Sahar's students and the angriest. He has not won a bout against his master in nine years. He does not intend to lose the tenth.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_jin.greet: Jin was a pirate once, and now keeps a stall of knotted cords. He says each cord is a good memory he has bottled, and sells them at a fair price. He does not say what he does with the bad ones.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_li.greet: Li serves tea to sailors and says what each one needs to hear. Most of it is tea. Some of it is not. She has a very good memory and a very short temper for lies.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_mei.greet: Mei weaves cloth in white and vermillion that is sold as far as Tamriel, and no one there has ever worn it correctly. She has a pleasant, patient way of correcting strangers by smiling at them.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_nehra: Admiral Nehra of the Coral Flagship
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_nehra.greet: Nehra commands the fleet from a throne of fused coral and says nothing that has not already been decided. Her officers are terrified of her. Her cabin-boy is not, and has been told never to say so.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_nine_kettles: Host Aoi of the Nine Kettles
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_nine_kettles.g: The Teahouse of the Nine Kettles has, as promised, nine kettles. Each one boils a different tea, each one has a different name and each one, Aoi says, has a mood. She does not take sides in their disputes.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_ooma.greet: Ooma dives the Sload pools for a living, and is the only person in Thras who will tell you it is a living. She wears a mask of waxed leather and a very large amount of gold. The gold, she says, is not for decoration. It is for the debt she owes the pools.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_rolla.greet: Rolla sings the Migration Song, which is four hundred verses long and has been sung without pause, in shifts, since the first Nords sailed. She is on verse three hundred and sixty, and her voice has begun to sound like the sea itself.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_sahar: Master Sahar of the Sword Courtyard
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_sahar.greet: Sahar teaches the Way of the Sword in a sunken courtyard of sand, with no walls, no weapons rack and no rules. He says the first rule is that you may walk away. The second is that you never will.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_wen: Captain Wen of the Silent Junk
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_wen.greet: Wen sails a dragon-prowed junk and a very small grudge. The grudge is against a ship. The ship has not been seen in nine years. He thinks about it every morning, and says this is the secret of his good health.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_witness.greet: A pale figure sits on the highest bench and has never been seen to leave it. Students say the ghost keeps the score. The ghost says nothing at all. Nobody has ever won an argument with a ghost who is simply watching.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_ysa: Mead-Wife Ysa of the Last Hearth
story.skycraft.npc.mq_for_ysa.greet: The Last Hearth is a half-buried longhall where the fire has not been out in nine hundred years. Ysa keeps it fed with driftwood and whale-oil and a quiet, stubborn refusal to be the one who lets it die.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ab_hadiya.greet: Pirates? No such thing. There are merchants with different manifests, and customs men with different prices. If you ask me who has been taking ships, I will tell you the sea has. It is the oldest answer, and it has never once been wrong.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ab_karim.greet: Nets are knots, and knots are promises, and a promise is only worth what it costs to keep. I have kept mine for sixty years. I know every mooring in this bay by its sound. A rope that has been moved sings differently.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ab_salwa.greet: The Barnacle Bride! Fish, beer, and the finest view of the Landing Light for forty miles. Do not mind the barnacles on the stools. The stools were there first. We merely sit on them.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ab_tarek.greet: Things come and things go. I deal in neither, strictly. I deal in the space between them, which is where most of the profit is. If you have something you wish to be rid of, I am the man to be rid of it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ds_dahab.greet: Seven fights. Three tiers. One ranking. I have run this arena for twenty-two years and every dead fighter has been recorded, every winner paid, and every bet honoured. If you wish to enter, sign. If you wish to bet, see Rim.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ds_grisha.greet: I mend what the arena breaks. Helm dents, shield rims, a collar-bone if the client insists. I do not take sides. Sides are for bookmakers. I take payment, and I take it in advance.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ds_hanif.greet: The Wounded Odds! A drink is priced by the record of the fighter whose seat you are in. Sit in a champion's chair and it is a copper. Sit in a loser's and it is free. The loser's chairs are very comfortable.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ds_rim.greet: Odds on all seven. The favourite is always the one who has never lost. The upset is always the one who has never won. Put your money where your faith is. If your faith is in me, put it in the other pocket.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_ds_safiya.greet: I have won thirty-one bouts and I have never once been the better fighter. I am the better liar. Do not tell the bookmaker. He pays the same either way.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_el_amir.greet: I copy the Spire's star-tables by lamplight, in ink that does not run in the wind. It is a very windy city. The ink has taken some persuading. The scribe, it must be said, has taken more.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_el_jul.greet: One hundred and one steps. Nobody believes me. The tourists say one hundred. The priests say one hundred. I say one hundred and one, and the extra one is under the third landing, and I will not show you.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_el_kaia.greet: The Spire stands. The wind-wall stands. The granary stands. These are the only three things in Elinhir that I have to worry about, and I worry about them very hard. Speak.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_el_mira.greet: Every drop the Spire drinks has to be carried up. All hundred and one steps. I have carried water for twenty years, and my legs are the only part of me that has opinions. They are very strong ones.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_el_qadir.greet: The Hundredth Step. Rooms by the stair, priced by the landing. First landing a copper, second a silver, third a gold. Top landing is not for sale. It is my own, and I sleep in it, and I have not had a good night since I moved.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_rh_dhalia.greet: The Seventh Courtyard. There are six. Do not ask where the seventh is. A guest asked once and was not seen again until he was found in the lemon tree. He was fine. The lemon tree is not.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_rh_farid.greet: Camels, water, news, and a very small amount of luck. I have taken caravans to Sentinel and Elinhir and back, and I have never once lost a camel. A friend, yes. A few. But never a camel.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_rh_lila.greet: I can take you anywhere in Rihad in the time it takes you to say your name wrong. The maze moves, you know. It moves with the shadow of the minaret. I have been counting it since I was five.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_rh_rasul.greet: Cinnamon, cumin, cardamom, and a certain red pepper that I am not permitted to describe. I sell flavour and I sell silence. The silence is the dearer of the two.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_rh_tahir.greet: I keep the hours of the Minaret. Each is named, and each has a verse, and I know all but one. It was lost in my grandfather's time. I am looking for it. If you hear it in a market, or a lullaby, tell me.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sm_brulla.greet: The Draggin' Tale. Every drink is named after a tall story: the Kraken's Lunch, the Cursed Mudcrab, the Admiral's Wife. Tell a better story than the one on the menu and the drink is free. Nobody has ever won. I have been waiting for a very long time.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sm_makki.greet: The harbour is mine. The toll is mine. The island, depending on the day and the tide and the temper of the Governor, is mine too. If you can count, you will know that is three things, and if you can multiply, you will know I own a great deal.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sm_salim.greet: Maps! Honest ones, honest-ish ones, and ones that are only a story about a place that was never there. You may choose. I will not tell you which is which. A map is a promise, and a promise is only as good as the man who keeps it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sm_zahra.greet: Toll for ships, toll for cargo, toll for crews, and a small fee for being annoyed at the toll. I do not set the rates. I record them, and they are, as a rule, recorded in my favour.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sn_dalia.greet: Welcome to the Cobalt Peacock. My parrot, Vizier, announces the day's debts aloud each evening. It is a house tradition and a nuisance. Please pay promptly and do not speak to him.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sn_ink.greet: Ink for the Vizier, ink for the scribe, ink for the lover who writes at midnight and regrets it by dawn. I make three shades of black, and each tells the age of the page. Show me your page, and I will tell you its sin.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sn_layla.greet: Docks are closed to idlers. If you are not here to carry, sail, sell or be arrested, say so now and I will point you to a very nice tavern. If you are, show me your papers.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sn_samir.greet: You may speak. I will decide afterward whether it was worth my time. Keep it concise. The Dome Palace has eleven hundred petitioners a day and one Vizier.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_sn_zareen.greet: Indigo from Tamriel, saffron from Rihad, cobalt from a place I am not permitted to name. Every colour on this stall has a story, and most of them are lies. Ask me which. I will tell you, for a coin.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_tn_benyam.greet: Ship-book, tide-book, debt-book. Every vessel that has ever tied up at Taneth is written here, with her master, her cargo and her fate. Fates are the interesting column. Would you like to see a few?
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_tn_dina.greet: The Pool of Lanterns. A drink here is paid for in verse, not coin. Four lines, scanning, about the sea or about a person you regret. If your verse is good, you drink free. If it is bad, you drink free, but I will tell you.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_tn_jalil.greet: Welcome to the Turquoise Palace, traveller. The sea is very loud this evening, and I find I have no one to answer it. Tell me, do you know any verses? No? Then you will be useful in other ways.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_tn_najwa.greet: Mind the water-lilies; they bite. Not literally, but the pool-keeper who ignored them never lived it down. I know the verse of the gardens. It is one line long, and nobody has ever managed to say it right.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hf_tn_pearl.greet: Down there it is quiet. Quieter than a tomb, quieter than a temple. If you have never been under, you do not know what the word means. I am the only man in Taneth who has heard the sea say something back.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_cm_elric.greet: Penance is a bell, child. A bell with a very low voice and a very long memory. Say what you have to say. Afterward, I will tell you what it weighs.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_cm_hvarine.gree: Darling, you must be new. Sit. I will tell you who is sleeping with whom in the black slate spires, and, for a very small fee, who is not and wishes they were.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_cm_osric.greet: Hush. Keep your voice down. The bell hears everything. I mean that quite literally. It has a very good memory. I should not have said that. Forget I said that.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_cm_tam.greet: I cast bells. Small, large, cracked, mute. A bell that does not ring is just a very heavy cup. If you want a story, I sell those too. The price is whatever you think a story is worth to a man in your boots.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_cm_wynn.greet: Welcome to the Quiet Peal. We are soundproofed. No singing, no shouting, no bells. Whispers only, and I fine for laughter. If you want to be loud, there is a cellar. If you want to be very loud, there is a different cellar.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_alaric.greet: I bear a letter that must reach its lady without a seal on it. No, I cannot say why. No, I cannot say who. Yes, I am aware that sounds like a crime. It is a very small one.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_clemence.gre: I run the castle's correspondence, and I am the only person in Daggerfall who has never once been surprised by a letter. Please do not try.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_hobb.greet: Three Bridges Inn! Rooms on all three. The bridge you sleep on is your choice, and the toll to reach it is on your bill, itemised. Keep your receipts. The Madam audits every guest.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_ines.greet: Weights, measures, counterweights and, if you ask quietly, one very old pair of brass scales that are never wrong. They have never been used, because they frighten people. Would you like to see them?
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_pelline.gree: The Bridge Toll, per person, per crossing, per animal, per wagon. I do not set the toll. I collect it, and I collect it correctly, and I will thank you not to look at my scale in that tone.
