story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_dg_perrin.greet: Don't stand downwind. Don't stand upwind either. Stand where I tell you and breathe through your mouth. I know smells and secrets, and I know which of them is which by the third lungful.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_ev_ansel.greet: The cathedral records go back nine centuries and the cathedral cellar goes back eleven. I am the archivist. I am also, as of this winter, the only person who will go down there.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_ev_iselle.greet: Four coppers across, six back, ten if you are carrying a corpse and do not want to discuss it. I hear everything on the water, and I say nothing on the land. That is my one rule.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_ev_mallory.gree: The cathedral stands on its island because the lake would not have it anywhere else. If you have come to pray, the nave is open. If you have come to ask questions, the bishop is, as ever, reluctantly available.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_ev_pernel.greet: The Wet Candle. Yes, the candles burn upside down. Yes, it is a miracle. No, I do not know why. If you can prove it is a trick, I will give you a month of free ale. Many have tried. The ale is still mine.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_ev_vey.greet: Seven hundred lamps and a long pole, and a lake that tries to put them out. I do not mind the lake. It is only doing what a lake does. It is the people who live beside it I do not trust.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_gp_corwin.greet: There was a wreck, you know. The Lonely Tortoise. A fine ship, a poor captain, a lovely wind. Went down in a night. They say her bell still rings at low tide. I say it is only the sea being clever.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_gp_dunstan.gree: Glenpoint is small and honest, and I would like it to stay both. If you have come to smuggle, do it somewhere else. If you have come to buy salt, the pans are on the left, and the price is posted. It is the same price for everyone, and it is fair.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_gp_edda.greet: I read the water the way you read a face. The tide says someone is lying, and the moon says it is not the tide. If you need a boat taken through the Spiral, I am your woman. If you need a lie told convincingly, ask someone else.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_gp_sorrel.greet: The Brine Pan. Everything here is salted: bread, butter, stew, ale, and my husband's jokes. Don't ask for water. The well is salted. We are all salted. It keeps us.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_np_gill.greet: The moor moves. I know what you will say. Moors do not move. This one does. I have cut the same bank for forty years, and each spring it is nearer the lighthouse by a stride.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_np_hester.greet: The Fog Horn Arms. When someone buys a round, I sound the horn, so every sailor in the bay knows there is a free drink going. It has not once been mistaken for a fog. It has been mistaken for a very large cow.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_np_maude.greet: Northpoint is a town of seven hundred souls, one lighthouse, and one very large moor. It runs on salt, peat and common sense. If you came for any of the first two, you are welcome. If you came for the third, you are in the wrong town.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_np_sorley.greet: There is one lamp in the tower and one lamp on the moor. If you have been told otherwise, you have been told wrong by someone who has never kept either.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_np_tolliver.gre: Smoked herring, smoked eel, smoked mutton, and a very good smoked cheese that is entirely a rumour. Taste a sliver. Everything is smoked here. We find it keeps the sea from getting in.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_or_bolgrat.gree: Trophies, trinkets, tusks. Every orc has one thing he is ashamed of selling and one he cannot get rid of fast enough. I stock both. I can tell which is which by the way you sniff.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_or_gulmak.greet: You are in Orsinium. It was built stone by stone. We do not say please. We say, show me. Show me you can lift. Show me you can last. Then, perhaps, we will say please.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_or_mazgul.greet: The Iron Throat. One drink, house brew, awful. If you complain I give you a second one for free. If you praise it I know you are lying, and I charge double. There is a rule; there is no logic to it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_or_torog.greet: Sit. Not there; that is the Chieftain's. There. I sing of old victories. I sing them loud, and a little long, and I add a few more orcs to each one. A song with more orcs in it is a better song.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_or_ushra.greet: The forge burns because I tell it to. The iron bends because I allow it. If you came to ask for a blade, bring ore. If you came to ask for advice, bring ale. If you came for neither, stand somewhere else.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_sh_alder.greet: Goose-feather, grey-goose, and the odd crow for the fussy. Arrows are honest things. They go where you point them. The people who buy arrows are the ones I trade secrets with. No, I do not give them away.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_sh_brom.greet: I am drunk, and I am correct. Both are true. Neither is a problem. The sergeant's art is knowing the first without ever losing the second. Now, if you are not here to sign the book, buy me one.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_sh_hale.greet: Don't. Don't call the Marshal. We are not deserters, we are... on extended leave. A very long leave. Three of us. We saw something in the wall. We will tell you, but you must not tell her yet.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_sh_hazel.greet: The Red Muster Tap. We sort drinks by banner. Blue for Daggerfall, green for Wayrest, red for the house. If you ask for the wrong colour I will serve you, but I will give you a look.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_sh_ysolde.greet: You are standing in the muster-ground of Shornhelm. Every banner here has a number, every number has a man, and every man has a bunk. If you are carrying a sword for hire, sign the book. If not, stand to the side.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_aumaric.gree: You have the look of a person with a delicate matter. Good. The duchess has a great many indelicate ones, and a chamberlain deserves variety.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_corisande.gr: Gloves. Fans. A very few small knives, under the fans. I sell to ladies and to the ladies who wish to be seen as ladies, and I know which is which by their gloves. Do come in.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_ferrand.gree: Welcome to the Courteous Cormorant. A complaint, if you must make one, is to be submitted in rhyming couplets. Prose complaints are filed under weather and ignored. Yes, it is a house rule. Yes, it is law.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_jules.greet: I count crates. Crates have no opinions, no politics and no hands. I like crates. If you are carrying a crate of unusual weight, you may stop now and show it to me.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_odelle.greet: The harbour shrine of Mara is small. It is meant to be. The sea is large, and a small thing standing in front of a large thing is, I find, a very good arrangement.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_hr_wy_pike.greet: Down here, you can tell a Wayrest nobleman from a Wayrest thief by how loudly he complains about the smell. The thief is quieter. He also knows the way out.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_aldrin.greet: I have dug four hundred graves in this town. I will not dig the fifth one they asked for. Do not ask which. Do not ask why.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_aryn.greet: Information is a river, sera: it flows downhill, to whoever stands lowest. I stand very low indeed. Coin, please.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_bethal.greet: Bethal's Dry Goods and Wet Alibis. Umbrellas, oilskins, and a good word for a bad evening. Yes, it never rains. That is why they are cheap.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_brara.greet: Honour is a debt that compounds, sera. I intend to be rich in it, and I would like a witness to the count.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_brarmin.greet: The tunnels under this town run deeper than the town does. Mind your head, mind the eggs, and never whistle.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_corvus.greet: Order is a habit, not a gift. I intend to keep the habit. A name will be handed to me by evening, and I will arrest the man it belongs to.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_dalyne.greet: The Gateway Inn, sera. Every room has a window. Not every window has a view of the same place twice. Do not ask; the Magisters like it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_dathan.greet: Cornerclub rules: no singing before sundown, no cheating after. Everything between is a negotiation.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_dren.greet: Twenty years I have cut glass out of the lava channels. Never once have I looked at it straight. A man who does gets a certain look.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_dron.greet: A good merchant owns the river, not the boat. A better one owns the man who owns the boat.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_durgul.greet: I am a duellist for hire. Not an assassin. The difference is a witness and a very small piece of paper.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_felmin.greet: The Company buys, ships and sells. Dunmer silk, Imperial steel, anything with a margin. Do ask about the margin. It is the one thing we do not hide.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_fendil.greet: A pilgrim! Wonderful. The Last Stair is the best stair. It costs a little extra, for the view.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_fennik.greet: Spore & Sundry. Dried caps, glass jars, fumigation salts. If a jar glows when you open it, please close it again and say nothing.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_gaela.greet: The Silver Samovar, sera: tea, honey-cake, and a back table where deals take place. Do not ask which deals. I serve the tea cold when I'm listening.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_gaenor.greet: Do not curtsey. I am levitating, you see, and the angle is unflattering for both of us. Something to wager? I am so very bored.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_hesta.greet: I make poultices and, on quieter days, apologies. Last week a customer paid me in both.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_hlaren.greet: Forty stalls, one rule: nothing sold here is stolen. Everything sold here was stolen *once*. It is the first sale that matters.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_hlenil.greet: Ferry to any canton, any hour, and I'll only tell you the shortcuts if you stop asking what's underneath.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ilnoth.greet: Ladies, gentlemen, and those who prefer not to say! Tonight's fight is real. The odds are not. Come, place a coin.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ilu.greet: I keep the canton lift. Three bells down, three bells up, no exceptions for weather, kings or prayer.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_kesha.greet: Glass, obsidian, ash-salts, a small selection of lava-polished jewellery that is, I promise, not cursed. Not recently.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_lisara.greet: A palace archivist. Do not stack the maps and do not mention the second basement. We have all agreed that there is no second basement.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_loris.greet: The garrison's confessions are the shortest in the Empire. Nobody does anything wrong. Nobody does anything at all. It is a very quiet war.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_marga.greet: The Bastion's Heel. Two kinds of beer: the one the garrison drinks and the one it pretends it doesn't. I'll serve you the second.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_maro.greet: Wolverine Hall. Imperial garrison. We keep the peace, we keep the books and we keep very, very far from the Telvanni towers.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_mavia.greet: I collect ashes, sera. Not the dead's. The living's. Everyone leaves a little behind. I am only the one who sweeps it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_mirele.greet: The Pilgrims' Rest. Candlelit alcoves, quiet suppers, and no sermons after dark. We count the candles. Do not be offended; the dead count them too.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_nerevi.greet: Outlanders do not walk the Row. Not out of cruelty, sera. Out of arithmetic: the Row has twelve houses and each house has a guest list.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_nerva.greet: The Rat in the Pot, sera, and no, there is no rat. There was a rat. There is a pot. You will find the connection is purely nominal.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_nilena.greet: Fence? Never. I am a freight consultant. If something was stolen before it reached me, that is a matter between it and its conscience.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_orlen.greet: Hlaalu bronze, Redoran steel, and the odd piece of Dwemer scrap that hums at night. The smithy opens when I stop shouting at the anvil.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_orrel.greet: Silt striders do not like flat ground, loud noises, or being thanked. Be none of those, and we are friends.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_orvyn.greet: The Cinder Cup. Warm rooms, warm soup, warmer company. It is also the only inn in Morrowind where you pay for the cooling.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ravos.greet: A walk through the plaza, a lost glove found, a purse that was never there. Quite innocent. I am a student of public architecture.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_rilvo.greet: Bridge duty. Keep to the left, keep moving, and do not stop to peer at the water. People have fallen off the right side, in my shift, for their trouble.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_rolfa.greet: Captain. I do not bend rules, I explain them slowly. Do not make me explain them slowly.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ruvene.greet: The Sunken Lantern. Rooms by the night, soup by the bowl, and the stairs to your room by the flight. Don't look at me like that; I counted them.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_salvu.greet: The dead are not quiet. They are polite. There is a difference, and it is the difference between a household and a haunting.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_sedyn.greet: Down there, the same streets, and the same lamps. Only the ghosts pay rent. I take a lantern and a bad knee and I go down every Sundas.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_sirela.greet: Eight Plates. Eight plates of stew a night, no more, no fewer, and the ninth person goes hungry. It is a policy, not a shortage.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_skeema.greet: Careful. The blue ones sing. The green ones listen. I have not decided what the grey ones do, and I would like not to find out in company.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_tadrik.greet: Funerary wares: shrouds, ash-urns, memorial lanterns and an excellent line in sympathy cards. We do not do refunds. The dead never complain.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_telyne.greet: Warden of the Hlaalu canton's stairs, sera. Four hundred and twelve of them, and I know which ones are loose.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_tevra.greet: Marshmerrow, hackle-lo, trama root and a very patient face. Poisons? Not here, no. Never here. Ask Rilu behind the shell.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_tolan.greet: South gate, third bell. Quiet shift. Always a quiet shift. Do not ask about the purse; it is for my mother.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_tosa.greet: Water goes where water wants. My work is to disagree with it politely, with gates.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ulvani.greet: The Temple is patient. It has had to be. Do sit. Nobody is listening, which is rare in Mournhold, so let us use it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_ulveni.greet: My tower has fourteen floors, eleven guardians and one very short temper. Which of the three were you hoping to meet?
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_velan.greet: Chitin armour, bonemold, and a good word for your elbows. If it breaks, you may bring it back. If you broke it, you may not.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_mw_veya.greet: Seven years I have carried my master's slippers up and down fourteen floors. I want to learn something that is not a cobweb.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_am_miller.gree: Gudrun runs Anga's Mill with a firm hand and a firmer opinion of the river, which she believes is working against her. She has been proved right three times, which she counts as an average.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_bb_farmer.gree: Erlend tends the Battle-Born farm and has a great many opinions about his neighbours, the Whiterun Guard and the proper depth of a turnip furrow. He is rarely asked for any of them.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_bb_lodge_stewa: Ravenna keeps the Black-Briar Lodge, which is not a lodge so much as a family with a mead-hall attached. She says every lodge has a secret. This one has three, and she is only willing to say two.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_bm_brewer.gree: Hjorth brews a very fine brandy in the cellar and a very poor apology in the kitchen. He is a gifted distiller and an ungifted husband, and everyone, including the husband, knows it.
Bjarnhild ferries travellers across the Darkwater on a flat boat pulled by a rope and her own stubborn will. She says the river is only as deep as you believe it is.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_db_lamp.greet: Hilde runs the Lamp-Wife's, a tiny tavern just off the bridge, and keeps a lantern hung out all night so no one drowns in the dark. She has never lost a guest. She says that is the secret of good business.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_db_toll.greet: Aldis takes the toll at the bridge and has opinions on everyone who passes. He says a bridge sees more of a person than their mother ever will, and about as much as their banker.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_heartwood_fore: Hrolf runs the Heartwood Mill and says a sawmill is the only honest industry in Skyrim, because the saw does not lie about what it has done.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_helgen_mason.g: Orvar is rebuilding the Helgen road-gate one block at a time, mostly alone. He says a gate is a promise, and that Helgen has made several it could not keep.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_helgen_widow.g: Sigrun lost a husband and a house on the same bad morning. She now keeps a candle in the window of the second, and will tell you, kindly, which of the neighbours were not at home when it happened.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_hj_farmer.gree: Ketil keeps the Heljarchen farm in the shadow of a ruined tower and refuses, on principle, to be impressed by it. He says a ruin is only a very old farm that has stopped trying.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_hl_farmer.gree: Ysolda married into the Hlaalu farm from Windhelm's Gray Quarter and has never let anyone forget how much better the soup was there. She makes a surprisingly good ash-yam stew nonetheless.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_iva_lodge.gree: Wulfgar keeps the Vilemyr and says he has been told, very often, that he runs the quietest tavern in Skyrim. He considers this high praise. The other regulars consider it a warning.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_iva_stair: Pilgrim Dagny of the Seven Thousand
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_iva_stair.gree: Dagny has climbed the Seven Thousand Steps eleven times. She never reaches the top. She says that is not the point. It would be a very long walk to prove it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_karth_mine.gre: Ulfhild oversees the Sanuarach mine under a pressing sense that the Forsworn are watching, and the other mine-owners are watching the Forsworn, and the Forsworn are watching her, a little more kindly than the rest.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_kyn_miner.gree: Dorlag runs the Kynesgrove steel-mine and says he has never lost a miner to anything but old age. This is technically true, as he has chosen not to count the ones who died in their thirties.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_nz_orc.greet: Grazbar keeps the forge at Narzulbur and says an Orc stronghold needs two things: a good axe, and a better argument. She supplies both, for a small fee.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_oh_shepherd.gr: Guthlaf has watched Old Hroldan fall into ruin for sixty years, and has begun to suspect that he is the last thing holding it up. He may be right.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_rs_stable.gree: Gunnar keeps the Riften stables with an air of lingering disappointment, as if the horses were a pale reflection of horses he once knew. He has never named which.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_sa_farmer.gree: Rannveig runs the Sarethi farm and its famous nirnroot-and-snowberry salve. She speaks to her herbs, her salve and the bees, in that order, and lets her customers wait.
Dagmar runs the Solitude Sawmill since her husband was lost to a falling oak, and curses the forest roundly every morning, and then asks it, politely, for a little more timber.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_sh_goatherd.gr: Brunwulf herds goats over the Stonehills crags and says a goat is the only creature in Skyrim with the sense to be suspicious of everything, including you.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_shors_prospect: Hakon lost a finger to the Northwind mine and says it was a fair trade for what he found. He has not yet told anyone what he found. He is a little drunk, and very close to telling.
Ragna keeps the old watch-tower above Shor's Stone and has seen three armies pass and a fourth start. She considers herself a person of settled opinions.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_sj_digger.gree: Orm delves the sinkhole for the Sanuarach and says the hole has been getting deeper by a hand-span a month. He uses it as a calendar, and a worry, and an excuse to have an opinion.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_ss_farmer.gree: Aldis keeps the Snow-Shod farm and swears the name is a joke by an ancestor. The horses are shod in snow, he says, in winter. In summer they do not need shoes. Visitors have not been able to find the joke.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_wh_stable.gree: Brenuin tends the Windhelm stables and has never been known to say a harsh word to a horse. He saves them all for the riders, in a low voice, very precisely, when they are not listening.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sky_wi_farmer.gree: Torvald runs the Windstad Manor farm with a fisherman's patience and an invalid's opinions of the weather. He lost his taste for the sea after a wreck, and has never lost his taste for complaint.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_aslfur.greet: I brought a horn from the north shore. It is a good horn. Do not ask what animal. The animal has asked me not to say.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_bodil.greet: Pelts, bone needles, drying racks, boat-oil. We trade at the south gate, in the Skaal way: no haggling, but a great deal of silence.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_brynja.greet: Tracks in the snow are letters, sera, written in a language older than speech. Most people read them and see only mud.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_decimus.greet: Imperial steel, Imperial rivets, Imperial cold. Nothing I make ever feels like a luxury. It feels like a promise.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_duvren.greet: Fetch this, carry that, do not touch the mushroom with the ribbon on it. I have been here two years. I have touched the mushroom with the ribbon on it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_gorm.greet: The ebony does not care who digs it. The foreman does. Mind the ledger; mind your feet. Both are slippery.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_hale.greet: The wall holds. The wall always holds. It is the only thing in Frostmoth that behaves. State your purpose and wipe your boots.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_hjalm.greet: The fire has burned since before my grandmother's grandmother. It does not need me. I need it. Sit, if you will. The wind is going to take a while.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_hrolf.greet: A hall is only as good as its last hunt. Mine was a boar. A boar! Sit. There is mead, and there is still a beast out there with my name on it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_ildar.greet: My uncle is brilliant and insufferable. I am brilliant and merely petulant. Do not confuse the two; he does not like it, and neither do I.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_ilvani.greet: A chapel of one hall. A congregation of forty, on a good Sundas. The ash makes them pious, and the cold makes them punctual.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_ingrid.greet: Sit. I am about to sing the death of a bear who never existed, in a fight that did not happen, to a crowd who will weep. It is called the craft.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_ketil.greet: Wren says the wind has a name. I think it is Frodi. I told Wren. Wren did not say no.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_odd.greet: My mead is honest. My dice are not. Come, a game: a drake a throw. Do not look at my left hand. It has been the same hand for sixty years.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_orsk.greet: Boiled barley, boiled mutton, boiled something I will not name. It is the garrison's idea of variety. Sit. You look underfed.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_pelli.greet: Mind your step. The gills are moist and the moss has teeth. Did you wipe your boots? You did not wipe your boots.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_rolan.greet: The wharf is rough planks and rougher manners. If you fall in, shout. If you shout, it is already too late. Mind the bollards.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_sigrun.greet: I hang the ribs, I mend the beams, I sharpen the spears that did not kill the beast the first time. Mind the whalebone. It has opinions.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_tindra.greet: Tindra's Salvage and Salt. Whatever the mine spits out, I price. Whatever the sea spits out, I price twice. Ask nothing; owe nothing.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_tisa.greet: Blue lantern, two flashes, wait; three flashes, run. If you see five, the gate is open and I have not opened it. Mark the time.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_torvald.greet: I patch the hulls the sea has opinions about. It has a great many opinions. I am the only one who answers it politely.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_tuvi.greet: I trade at the gate and sleep outside it. The walls are not built for me. They are built for what I carry in my tongue: news.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_veleth.greet: Rations are counted by the bowl, sera. The count is not for sale, and neither am I. State your business and keep to the left.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_wren.greet: The wind has been quiet since Sundas. A quiet wind is an animal holding its breath. I should like to know what it is waiting for.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sol_yarda.greet: I fish. I listen. I sell what I hear to whoever pays in coin or in cake. The Magister pays in neither; he pays in being surprised.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_aelwen.greet: Aelwen guards the Ledger of Precedent, in which is written every ruling the Royal Court has made since the Dawn. She has never once been seen to consult it. She simply knows. That, she says, is the whole point of a ledger.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_apple_claimant: Syllaen swears the great apple tree at King's Haven is hers by right of her grandmother's grandmother. Her neighbour swears otherwise. Both of them harvest the same branches on alternate days and leave a polite apple at the other's door, which neither will eat.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_aviel.greet: Aviel keeps the palace running and the lord from noticing. She has been loyal for twenty years and mildly insane for fifteen. She counts the glass panes of the Balcony Walk every morning, and has not yet arrived at the same number twice.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_bell_sexton.gr: Aldaer rings the dawn bell every morning. For two weeks it has been ringing at midnight, and he has not touched the rope. He sleeps in the belfry now, with a lantern, to catch it in the act.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_cael_priest: Priest Cael of the Rock Chapel
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_cael_priest.gr: Cael rings the Rock Chapel's bell at every tide and prays a different prayer for each one. He says the sea is a congregation and he is its very patient clerk.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_calantir.greet: Lord Calantir has inherited a palace with no walls and a title with no duties. He is bored in a very expensive way. He will pay almost anything to be entertained, and almost nothing to be amused.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_dog_ear.greet: The Dog-Eared Page is a quiet tavern where conversation is held at a whisper and every drink comes with a small slip of paper bearing a line from a poem. Ellanwe selects the poem. She says it is a diagnosis.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_eilen.greet: Eilen keeps the quay of Dusk with a voice like a closing door. She speaks seldom and never repeats herself. When she does speak, ships turn.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_ewen.greet: Ewen pilots the sea-lift, a counterweighted cage that carries visitors from the palace balconies to the water. He is afraid of heights, which he considers a professional qualification.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_fen.greet: Fen runs the Lantern Docks like a clock. He keeps a rota for every ship, every crane and every seagull he has personally named. He does not have friends. He has a very large number of acquaintances.
Ilmen watches a single tree at Shattered Grove that has grown eleven feet in a week. He has measured it with a gold ribbon, twice a day, and the ribbon is no longer long enough.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_ildren.greet: Ildren cuts light for a living. He keeps a rack of quartz wedges by the window and says he can make a ray bend, a beam split or a sunrise last four minutes longer. He says no one has ever asked for the fourth.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_lantern_pole.g: The Lantern Pole is a dockside tavern with a single enormous lamp-pole in the middle of the common room, hung with eleven lanterns for every ship that has docked here. Miravel lights them in order. She has never once been wrong about the order.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_lilac_quill.gr: The Lilac Quill is a harbour tavern with lilac-paned windows through which the whole town looks bruised at dusk. Wenlin keeps a book of every ship that failed to return. He writes a new page each night, in lilac ink.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_lyn.greet: Lyn fishes from the platforms at low tide and is never in a hurry. She says the fish are not afraid of nets, they are afraid of people who are in a rush.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_maelia.greet: Maelia keeps the Great Library's catalogue and has not misplaced a book in forty years. She has misplaced one this week. She is holding herself together very precisely.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_maril.greet: Maril is the brightest student at Skywatch and the quickest to say so. She has found a planet that is not on the charts. She has not yet decided whether to tell the Astronomer.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_matchmaker.gre: Belenwe has made four hundred matches at Mara's Kiss, of which three hundred and ninety-nine have held. She talks about the one that did not as though it were an old friend.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_netch_pilot: Racer Quil of the Golden Netch
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_netch_pilot.gr: Quil has entered the Golden Netch race eleven times and come second in every one. The winner never returns. Quil is of two minds about it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_novice_mute.gr: Tevildo has broken a vow of silence, and will say why only to a stranger. He writes his name in the dust and rubs it out, again and again, as if testing whether it will stay.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_olo.greet: Olo rows the narrow strait to Artaeum and says she has done so for eleven years, though every year she has made exactly the same number of crossings. She is not sure how. She has stopped asking.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_ond.greet: Ond has swept the outer ring of the Great Orrery for sixty years. He has not looked up in all that time, because "it is not my department."
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_orla.greet: Orla sells bone-white lace, lilac wax and candles that burn the colour of twilight. She only opens her stall after sunset, and no one has ever seen her eat. Customers describe her as "restful".
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_prism_plover: Ondolemar of the Prism and Plover
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_prism_plover.g: The Prism and Plover is a glass-walled tavern whose roof is a ceiling of faceted quartz that splits the noon sun into forty separate rainbows. Ondolemar charges extra for the rainbows. He has never explained why they are optional.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_quenel: Adept Quenel of the Psijic Order
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_quenel.greet: Quenel is polite, patient and not entirely sure what hour it is. He tends the ruins of the old college with a small silver broom and says the stones prefer to be swept in the order they fell.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_rilen.greet: Rilen is nineteen, brilliant and very sure of it. He is hoping for a particular forbidden volume. He will tell you that it is "for research." He has been saying that for a month.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_ro.greet: Ro keeps the Tide Gate and knows the water's moods the way a baker knows dough. He says the sea has three tempers: sulking, working and showing off. It is always one of the three.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_sen.greet: Sen lights the lamps of Dusk at the first purple hour and puts them out at the first grey one. He knows every lamp by name and calls the dim ones "the sleepy". He has not been seen in daylight since the winter of his wedding.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_seventh_ring.g: The Seventh Ring is a round tavern at the top of the Orrery, where the tables turn very slowly on a hidden gear. Eilis says it makes one full turn per night, so everyone sees every view. She has never explained who winds the gear.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_taleth.greet: Taleth measures the heavens to the fourth decimal and has never once been caught guessing. She wears three pairs of spectacles at once, each ground for a different star.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_thalor.greet: Thalor tends the bronze rings of the Orrery Court. He winds them every dawn with a golden key and a brief apology to each. The planets, he says, have feelings, and the feelings are mostly regret.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_thel.greet: Thel is an initiate of the Order and has not yet learned to forget what he is not allowed to say. He says half of every sentence aloud and the other half, he insists, is understood.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_tide_inn.greet: The Tide-Turn Inn sits on the causeway itself, so that at high tide its front steps are underwater and at low tide its back steps are dry. Naereth keeps two doors and charges accordingly.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_tor.greet: Tor steers by a knot of coloured string that he refuses to explain. He is gruff, patient and has never been lost. This, he says, is because he has never admitted to it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_valia.greet: Valia tests the loyalty of Alinor's lesser officials by leaving gold in unlocked rooms and noting who takes what. She considers it a courtesy. They do not.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_wall_less.gree: The Wall-Less Inn has a roof and a floor and no walls whatever. It is therefore always in a draught. Ariadwe serves hot drinks in cups with lids, and warns every patron, kindly, not to lean back.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_sum_yeli.greet: Yeli stitches teal sails in the sail-loft and says a sail is a wish with a seam. She will sew your name into the hem of your sail for free, so the wind knows whom to blow.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_acorn.greet: The Hollow Acorn is a tavern built inside a knot of the great tree itself, with tables on three tiers and no two of them level. Fenwe serves meat only, as the Pact demands, and apologises for it to the tree each night.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_aeth.greet: Aeth speaks for a king who rarely speaks for himself. Every sentence is a courtesy and every courtesy is a measure of how much you are worth to the Court.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_beron.greet: Beron taps the lower roots for the sap that lights every lantern in the city. He talks to the tree while he works, and the tree, he swears, has begun to talk back, mostly about the weather.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_bough_host: Host Tamlin of the Green Bough
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_bough_host.gre: Tamlin runs the Green Bough, an inn in a tree whose bough grows another floor every year. He has stopped adding rooms and started adding apologies. Nobody knows why the tree does it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_bough_inn: Ilwen of the Four Seasons' Bough
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_bough_inn.gree: The Four Seasons' Bough is a tavern in the city's first limb. It has been moved eleven times and never once re-hung its sign. Ilwen says that is because the city would only move it again.
Maral says the shared bridge-plank is hers. Her neighbour says it is his. They have each been sweeping the plank every dawn for six years, in opposite directions.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_cael.greet: Cael walks the Thorn Wall at dusk and again at dawn and, once, in the middle of the night, because he felt a draught. The wall is very proud of him. He is not sure the wall understands.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_drabul_chief.g: Borgakh holds the Orc outpost in the forest, in an uneasy truce with the Bosmer neighbours. He has never once raised his voice. He has never once needed to.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_eld.greet: Eld tends the hanging terraces in Arenthia and has never been seen to stand on level ground. She talks to the roses in the third person and listens to their replies.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_eri.greet: Eri carries the memory of every site the city has stood on. She can tell you which spring flood took a ford and which autumn fire took a copse. She never forgets, and neither, she says, does the tree.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_firefly_lanter: The Firefly Lantern is the only tavern in Silvenar, and it is lit entirely by jars of captive fireflies that are released on the stroke of midnight, in a ceremony that irritates the fireflies enormously. Pip is sorry. Pip does it anyway.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_gatewarden.gre: Wren keeps the Firefly Gate and is in a permanent mood about it. She says the gate is too wide, the flies too bright and the visitors too numerous. She would prefer the city were found by no one.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_hael.greet: Hael has been following the walking city for eleven years. He has never once arrived at the same time as it. He is very patient and very, very tired.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_huln.greet: Huln shoes horses, forges spearheads and mends pots. He says seven words a day, and spends all of them on the pot.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_hush.greet: Hush speaks for the families who live beneath the bridges and have never been invited above them. She is the quietest woman in Woodhearth, and the only one nobody has ever interrupted.
Mauhulakh leads Jathsogur's stronghold and wants a trial of strength witnessed by someone who owes the clan nothing. He is fair. He is also very, very large.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_lirael.greet: Lirael holds the Root Gate and has counted every foot that has crossed it for nineteen years. She will not tell you the total. She says it would only embarrass you.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_loru.greet: Loru keeps the Root Archive, where scrolls hang from rafters in net-bags like fruit. He can find anything in it, so long as he is not asked to find it quickly.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_maelin.greet: Maelin tends the great roots that carry Falinesti across the forest, one slow step each season. He knows when it will turn, and he is never wrong, and he is never glad to say.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_mohr.greet: Mohr stands at the Caravan Gate and has not been relieved since the autumn. He is not complaining. He is simply sitting, with great dignity, on his shield.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_monk_singer.gr: Brother Hael has sung the same hymn for three days and nights and cannot stop. His voice has gone to a croak. His brothers sing in shifts. All of them look horrified.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_orwen.greet: Orwen sells nets, ropes and woven baskets in Fisher's Hang. He is generous with prices, stingy with news, and has the fastest knots in Greenshade. He says a net is only a promise that something will not get away.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_prophecy_hermi: Orlen carves one line of a prophecy per year on his doorframe and has done so for forty years. He says he has not decided what it will say. The line is not up to him.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_pura.greet: Pura weaves your fortune into a bracelet while you wait and then, very gently, ties it onto your wrist. She says a fortune you can see is a fortune you can argue with. Most people argue.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_rope_den: Zhan'ra of the Rope Market Den
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_rope_den.greet: The Rope Market Den is an upstairs room with cushions and a hookah and a very long waiting list. Zhan'ra serves moon-sugar tea and gossip in equal measure and will tell you which one is stronger.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_scribe.greet: Ethelwe writes every word the Silvenar has said in public, and a few he has not. She wears a ring of ink-stains on her left index finger, and says it is the only ring a scribe should ever wear.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_sel.greet: Sel keeps the waterfall shrine and prays from behind the curtain of water, so the faithful have never seen her face. She says the water prays better when she is not in the way.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_shaka.greet: Sha'ka sells silk, spice and moon-sugar from a bamboo stall strung above the street and will not take a coin that does not ring. She knows every caravan road in Reaper's March and every Pact patrol that watches it.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_slack_rope.gre: The Slack Rope hangs from three trees and sways on windy nights. Brenna serves the soup in lidded bowls and the ale in mugs bolted to the table. She says the regulars are very steady drinkers. She says the visitors are very quick learners.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_teva.greet: Teva cooks for the Watch Hall and listens to everyone. She never repeats a thing, except at the next table, in a different order. She calls it "tasting".
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_thorn_inn.gree: The Thorn-and-Thistle is a squat inn set into the Thorn Wall itself, its back room a hollow in the living hedge. Aldis says it is the safest tavern in Valenwood, because the wall itself will bite a brawler, and has.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_tilu.greet: Tilu walks the Great Weave every dawn with a mallet and a coil of rope, checking each plank by ear. She says a sound bridge sings a high note, and a tired one sings low. She has never once been wrong about a bridge.
story.skycraft.npc.mq_val_wynn.greet: Wynn weaves moss into cloth and cloth into banners. Her work smells of rain and wears like leather. She sells to Bosmer, to Orcs and, on one occasion, to a very polite wraith.
story.skycraft.npc.murbul.greet: Malacath watches the stronghold through my eyes. Today they are tired eyes, so speak plainly.
story.skycraft.npc.nazir.greet: Contracts, coin and corpses. In that order, if we're lucky.
story.skycraft.npc.nelkir.greet: There's a door in the cellar that whispers. It tells me things about my father. Want to know what it says?
story.skycraft.npc.neloth.greet: If you're here to waste my time, do it efficiently. If not, you may be useful.
story.skycraft.npc.neminda.greet: House Redoran asks three things of its people: duty, honor and endurance. The ash will test the third. I will test the other two.
story.skycraft.npc.nibani_maesa.greet: The ancestors whisper about strangers before they arrive. They were whispering about you this morning. Sit by the fire.
story.skycraft.npc.nileno_dorvayn.greet: House Hlaalu does not ask where you were born, only what you can do and what it costs. Sit. Let us discuss the second part first.
story.skycraft.npc.njada_stonearm.greet: The whelps in Jorrvaskr fight with their mouths. I fight with a shield. Guess which of us gets more work.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_ans: A necromancer in Ansilvund has been forcing hired diggers to unearth an ancient burial vault.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_cra: Outlaws in Cragslane Cavern are running illegal wolf-pits on the southern ridge.
Conjurers in Cragwallow Slope stole our copper stills from the malachite mine.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_cro: Giant spiders in Cronvangr Cave dragged off our salt-caravan mules.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_for: Warlocks in Fort Amol ambushed the pitch-wagon bound for Windhelm's docks.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_gal: Witch-hunters in Gallows Rock have been seizing our timber sledges for barricades.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_los: Bandits in Lost Knife Hideout raided our winter fur storehouse.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_mor: Warlocks in Morvunskar have been firing the pine-breaks above Kynesgrove.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_tra: Highwaymen at Traitor's Post have been robbing Dunmer peddlers on the northern road.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_east_yng: Strange blue motes drift out of Yngol Barrow whenever the sea-ice cracks.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_anc: Poachers broke into Ancestor Glade to strip the canticle trees.
Wind-carved tablets atop Ancient's Ascent have been defaced by grave-robbers.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_ang: Outlaws have been prowling the high ridge near Angi's Camp.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_ani: Strange smoke rises from the cellar trapdoor at Anise's Cabin.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_ban: Outlaws in Bannermist Tower drop felled pines across the western coaching road.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_bil: Someone altered the tally-weights at Bilegulch Mine.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_blo: Blood-red blossoms grow inside Bloated Man's Grotto even under deep snow.
Hunters heading toward the southern peaks never return from Bloodlet Throne.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_bon: No pack-mule crosses Bonechill Passage while frost trolls hold the ice-bridge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_bri: Necromancers in Brittleshin Pass have blocked the shortcut between the plains and the lake.
Undead spilling from South Brittleshin Pass have been overturning our drying racks.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_cra: Mercenaries locked themselves inside the vaulted cellar of Cracked Tusk Keep.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_emb: Bandits in Embershard Mine sawed through the main gallery props.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_eve: Lumberjacks won't cut near Evergreen Grove while the pond-guardians are riled.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_for: Deserters in Fort Neugrad seized the border pay-chest when Helgen fell.
Mercenaries on Fort Sungard's towers tax every shepherd crossing the western ridge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_gle: Feather-totems on the game trails mean the covens in Glenmoril are cursing the deer runs.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_gre: Pack-horses bolted at the scent coming from Greywater Grotto.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_hae: Vampire thralls in Haemar's Shame have poisoned the mountain pass cistern.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_hal: A pale pillar of light burns inside Halldir's Cairn, drawing restless dead from the woods.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_ili: When the lake freezes thin, you can hear the drowned tower's bell ringing under the eels.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_kni: Our corundum carts vanish within sight of Knifepoint Ridge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_orp: Hagravens on Orphan Rock have hung hex-cages over the eastern pine trail.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_pea: Herb-gatherers below Peak's Shade Tower were driven back by spriggans.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_pin: A homestead with ten pairs of muddy boots on the porch and no livestock in the pen is no farm.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_roa: Someone pried the bronze offering-bowl from the Roadside Ruins.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_shr: Cold laughter echoes down from North Shriekwind Bastion on moonless nights.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_sky: The watch-fire at North Skybound Watch has gone dark.
Smugglers use South Skybound Watch to bypass the border customs.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_sou: Spiders and renegade conjurers have nested in Southfringe Sanctum.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_sun: Fire-cultists in Sunderstone Gorge have been burning funerary cedars.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_twi: Grave-robbers have been prying at the outer vestibule of the Twilight Sepulcher.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_falk_wat: Necromancers seized the signal bell atop Falkreath Watchtower.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_haaf_ste: Frost-Matron Krevna and her poachers in Steepfall Burrow have been raiding our coastal traps.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_hjaal_de: Grave-robbers locked the outer grate of Dead Men's Respite with an old bardic seal.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_hjaal_hi: Vokun's Gate-Warden has risen in High Gate Ruins and threatens the coastal fishery.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_hjaal_ro: Bandits in Robber's Gorge have stretched a toll-chain across the western road.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_hjaal_sn: Necromancers in Fort Snowhawk seized our curing-salt wagons.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_hjaal_va: Draugr in Lost Valkygg have been marching out onto the southern pass road.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_pale_dus: Falmer in Duskglow Crevice have been stealing iron tires and tools from the farm smithy.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_pale_iro: An adventurer couple opened the hearth-crypt at Ironbind Barrow and unleashed its warlord.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_pale_sil: Grave-robbers broke the ice-seal on Silverdrift Lair and woke the barrow-king.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_ar: Tremors from Arkngthamz have been cracking the stronghold's forge-flues.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_ba: Forsworn on Bard's Leap Summit have barred pilgrims from the waterfall ledge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_bl: A hagraven coven in Blind Cliff Cave has been taxing travelers along the Karth gorge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_br: Forsworn in Broken Tower Redoubt captured a shipment of temple incense.
Raiders at Bruca's Leap Redoubt have been firing arrows at river barges.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_cl: Poachers at Cliffside Retreat stole a silver-mounted hunting horn.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_cr: A hagraven seized Cradle Stone Tower and drives travelers off the ridge.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_de: A hagraven on Dead Crone Rock has been lighting blood-braziers above the city.
Outlaws camped at Deep Folk Crossing are stripping bronze plates from the Dwemer bridge.
Forsworn in Deepwood Redoubt have barred the stone gate to the hidden vale.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_gl: Falmer in Gloomreach have been collapsing the lower timber props.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_ha: A rogue enchanter in Harmugstahl has been breeding venomous spiders in the old keep.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_ko: Forsworn raiders took Kolskeggr Mine and extinguished the gold-smelting furnaces.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_li: Falmer Tunneled up into the bandit taproom at Liar's Retreat.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_lo: Forsworn chanters in Lost Valley Redoubt are tolling the cliff-bells day and night.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_pu: Slaughterfish and looters in Purewater Run have fouled the stables' water trough.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_ra: Two skull-keys in Ragnvald keep the ancient Canal-Warden sealed, and grave-robbers just turned the first lock.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_re: Draugr in Reachcliff Cave have been rattled awake by grave-robbers.
Tomb-raiders entered the waterfall cave at Reachwater Rock.
Outlaws have been stripping brass pipes from the Dwemer tower at Reachwind Eyrie.
Grave-robbers have been prying at the sword-slot inside Rebel's Cairn.
Chieftains at Red Eagle Redoubt are gathering war-bands above the valley.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_so: Miners in Soljund's Sinkhole broke through into a draugr tomb at the bottom of the moonstone shaft.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_va: Dark vapors leaking from Valthume's vestibule are blighting the southern scrub.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_reach_vo: Bandits in Volskygge broke the outer totem-doors and woke the temple dead.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_ang: Draugr in Angarvunde broke through the side-gallery barricades.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_arc: Wind-bells on Arcwind Point have been ringing backwards since the barrow-lords woke.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_aut: Cultists lit a black-smoke brazier atop Autumnwatch Tower.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_bou: A rogue conjurer in Boulderfall Cave has been trapping miners with frost runes.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_bro: Cutthroats in Broken Helm Hollow ambushed our eastern tax-rider.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_bth: Looters have been prying brass gearing from the Ruins of Bthalft.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_cry: Goblins and wild beasts in Crystaldrift Cave scattered a pack-train of luminescent geodes.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_dar: Hagravens in Darklight Tower have been casting blight-spores toward our hunting grounds.
Chaurus from Darkwater Pass have been creeping up the river trail at night.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_fal: Poachers in Faldar's Tooth have been baiting pit-wolves with stolen farm sheep.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_for: Cultist relics inside Forelhost's outer refectory are being looted by mercenaries.
Highwaymen in Fort Greenwall stole a crate of steel crossbows.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_gei: Scholars pay good coin for a charcoal rubbing from Geirmund's Hall on the island.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_gol: Mercenaries on Goldenglow Island have been smoke-burning the rival hives.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_hon: Bears in Honeystrand Cave have been spooking the stable colts.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_nil: Bandits at Nilheim pose as wounded travelers to rob the Ivarstead wagons.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_nor: Skeletons woke in Northwind Mine when the upper drift broke into a tomb.
Offerings left on Northwind Summit were scattered by grave-robbers.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_pin: Bears in Pinepeak Cavern smashed our resin-taps along the river.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_red: Miners who drink from the peddler's red-water casks come back pale and hollow-eyed.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_rku: Scavengers at the Ruins of Rkund have been prying bronze plaques from the cliff terrace.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_ruu: Miners sent to Ruunvald Excavation stopped sending word a fortnight ago.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_sho: Raiders took Shor's Watchtower during the fog.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_shr: Treasure-seekers broke the outer seal of Shroud Hearth Barrow and woke the gate-guard.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_ste: Vampire scouts have been testing the perimeter around Stendarr's Beacon.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_rift_tre: Mercenaries seized Treva's Watch and barred the river-road portcullis.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_whiterun: Vampires don't care whose sheep they scatter on the moor.
Trolls in Darkshade have driven our wood-crews away from the waterfall pines.
Trolls under the ridge chewed through three stave-wagons last week.
Game runs scarce when poachers bait the hollow with salted meat.
Smoke on Guldun Rock means the giants and outlaws are trading stolen cattle again.
Even the quiet dead of Hamvir's Rest rattle their chains when grave-robbers pry the lintels.
Travelers taking the northern cut toward Morthal vanish near the open ruin.
My uncle traded ash-salts across these plains forty winters ago.
The spring ditch ran bone-dry after the frost set in.
Lunar iron rings different on the anvil when it's forged under a clear sky.
Never sign a promissory note by lantern-light.
Logs jam the bend whenever those cave-raiders hang a chain.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_ble: Frost trolls in Bleakcoast Cave have trapped a salvage crew's crates on the beach.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_dri: Mercenaries in Driftshade Refuge hijacked a shipment of silver bars.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_for: Necromancers in Fort Kastav have locked travelers in the courtyard cells.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_fro: The beacon atop Frostflow Lighthouse went dark after chaurus breached the cellar.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_jou: Bandits in Journeyman's Nook stole an apprentice's lockbox of ward-scrolls.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_mou: Frost-cultists below Mount Anthor have defiled the pilgrim cairns.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_sig: Steam-vents in the Sightless Pit have been scalding travelers on the shrine path.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_sky: Draugr in Skytemple Ruins guard an unrecorded island inscription.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_sno: Grave-robbers pried the outer lintel at Snow Veil Sanctum.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_sti: Falmer in Stillborn Cave have been raiding the coastal trap-lines.
story.skycraft.npc.npc_side_sky_wint_yng: A necromancer on the ice-island of Yngvild has been robbing coastal graves.
story.skycraft.npc.ocheeva.greet: The Sanctuary is your home now. Eat, sleep, train. When there is work, Vicente will tell you. When there is trouble, I will.
story.skycraft.npc.odric_hollenmoor.gree: Daggerfall has been burned, besieged and betrayed, and the Dragon has stood at its gate through all of it. Kneel or stand as you like. Just don't waste my time.
story.skycraft.npc.old_huzail.greet: The harbour talks, if you know how to listen. It talks louder for a coin or two.
story.skycraft.npc.old_tamsin.greet: A septim for an old woman? Or a crust. Or a kind word. I'm not choosy, dear, I'm only hungry.
story.skycraft.npc.orvas_dren.greet: My brother sits in the Duke's chair in Ebonheart and smiles at Imperials. I grow saltrice and keep the Tong fed. One of us is honest about what Morrowind needs.
story.skycraft.npc.owyn.greet: Blademaster of the Arena. I don't care where you're from or what you did before. On the sand, all I care about is whether you're still standing.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_eastmarch_: Bertrand Vanne, Imperial Geographical Society. Forgive the boots. They are borrowed. So, at present, is my dignity.
You look like someone who doesn't spit when they pass the Grey Quarter. That already makes you rare.
Looking for work? I've got a giant that wants killing and two hundred septims that want spending.
Goldenrock ore, best in the hold. If you're buying, good. If you're asking about Mistwatch, better.
Have you come from Windhelm? Have you seen a tall lad in blue, with his father's crooked nose?
You're a long way into Orc country, outsider. Either you're lost or you're useful. Which?
Kyne's breath on you, traveller. Mind the graves as you pass. Some of them are emptier than they should be.
Mind the saw. And if you're headed west, past Gallows Rock... no. Never mind. Mind the saw.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_falkreath_: Coffins, cradles, doors. Mostly coffins, this being Falkreath.
Mind the saw. It doesn't care who you are.
Ah, a traveller. Tell me, have you seen any large holes in the ground lately? Holes of a draconic character?
If it's about bandits, the Jarl knows. If it's about the graveyard, the Jarl knows. The Jarl knows everything and does nothing.
Arkay keep you. Have you come to light a candle, or to ask why so many are already lit?
Mind the fresh earth. Some of it's fresher than it ought to be.
You came up the Helgen road? Is there... is there anything left?
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_drav: Another Nord who wants to tell me to go home? Ask Red Mountain where home is.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_hall: Twenty planks every Loredas, and not one of them for my own roof.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_ragn: Mind the shavings. A keel's no good with a stranger's boot-print in it.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_thor: Lucky. Ha. They still call me that. Buy me a drink and I'll tell you how lucky.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_thyr: If you've come to sell me a charm against bad dreams, keep walking. I've bought enough.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_vesk: Mind the papers. No, not those. Those are filed. By a system. Mine.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_north_ysol: Listen. Do you hear it? No. Of course not. The tide's too high.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_reach_: If you've come about the Dwemer, you'll have to wait. If you've come about my assistant, you may sit down.
Bread's two septims, cheese is three. News of my brother is free, if you have any.
You smell of the road. Good. The road is better than the cave.
Silver's the only thing in Karthwasten that stays where you put it. People don't.
Need your horse watered? Fine. Need directions to Ragnvald? Don't.
Mine clerk, at your service. If you're buying moonstone, I'm afraid we're a little short this month.
Outsider. You have the look of someone who goes into tombs. Do you?
Mind the stairs, traveller. And if you hear footsteps upstairs tonight, mind your own business.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_b: Grandfather's asking about his pick again. Every night, the same question.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_e: The lake's quiet today. It's always quiet after it takes something.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_g: Stranger. You have the look of someone who walks into barrows. Good. Sit.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_h: Have you been up north of the lake? Have you seen a tall lad with a copper bracelet?
Mara's peace on you. Mind the candles, they're all I've got to keep the dark off.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_i: Clerk to the Jarl's steward. Which means I count what the Black-Briars let me count.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_o: Eighty-one years and seven thousand steps still to climb. And no bell to ring at the top.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_the_rift_t: If you're from Ruunvald, keep walking. If you're going there, stop and listen.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_west_coast: East Empire Company, Solitude office. If you've come about the lighthouse, sit down. If you've come about a job, sit down faster.
Don't tell me to stop hoping. Everyone in this town has told me to stop hoping.
You came up the south road? Did you pass anyone on it? A young man with an axe too big for him?
Salves, tinctures, cures for marsh-cough. Nothing with spider in it, not this month. Don't ask.
Need a horse brushed? A carriage? Or... you haven't seen a girl with red braids, have you? On the north road?
Rockwallow's closed to strangers. Unless you're the sort of stranger who goes down holes for a living.
Highmoon Hall's business is the Jarl's business. Unless you've news of my patrol. Then it's mine.
Mind the papers. No, not those. Or those. Just stand very still and tell me what you want.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_a: Potions, salves, tinctures. And if you happen to be going west, I have a favour or two to ask.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_e: If you've come to buy mead, buy it quick. Whatever I don't sell, the bandits will drink.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_g: You haven't seen a brown cow with a white face, have you? Answers to Brindle. Probably answers to giants too, now.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_h: Kynareth keep you, traveller. Forgive me if I seem distracted. The Temple has lost one of its own.
Have you come down from the north-west hills? Did you pass a hut? A tall man with a grey beard?
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_k: Twenty years carrying letters and the first time I lose a satchel it's the one with the Steward's seal on it.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_s: Sorry, I can't stop. The field won't plough itself, and my brother can't help any more.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_skyrim_whiterun_t: Mind the pool below the bridge. Something in there has teeth and no manners.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_solstheim_aevar.g: I work stalhrim. No, I will not sell you any. No, I will not tell you how. Yes, you may watch, if you are quiet.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_solstheim_aulus.g: My family has buried its dead on this island for two hundred years. Some of them never got the burying.
Welcome to Thirsk. The mead's ours again. The spear isn't. Sit down, drink, and tell me whether you can fight.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_solstheim_helga.g: If you've come down from the hills, did you pass the old lodge below Hvitkald? Was there smoke in the chimney?
Redoran Guard. If you're here to make trouble, the Bulwark has seen worse. If you're here to help, it's seen less of that.
Ash-yams, fresh dug. Or as fresh as anything is under all this grey.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_solstheim_ulvo.gr: Are you sturdy? You look sturdy. I have a great deal of scholarship that needs a sturdy person.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_solstheim_yrsa.gr: You walk loudly, outlander. The seals will hear you coming from Horker Island.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_ahzi: You stand like someone who has been in a fight and won it by luck. Sit. This one will teach you to need less luck.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_fevy: You're not from the Council Club, are you? No. Good. They laughed at me. Will you listen, at least?
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_gale: Weald Shiraz, the finest vintage in Colovia. Buy a bottle. Or... have you been west, into the hills? Did you hear music?
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_ilva: Twilight keep you, outlander. Forgive me if I look past you. I am always looking south at this hour.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_joru: Bread's on the counter, stew's on the fire. If you're going north, you're going past the stones. Are you going north?
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_mirv: Walk softly in Necrom, traveller. The dead are listening, and some of them are very cross with us this month.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_osto: Don't lend me anything. Please. Not a copper, not a kind word. You don't know what happens to people I owe.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_east_rija: This one has nothing to sell. This one had twelve wagons once. Now this one has a story, and the story is not a happy one.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_aldo: Mind the jars. The blue ones cure. The green ones... also cure, eventually. Of everything.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_gasp: Huntmaster Lorne. If you've come about the autumn hunt, it's off. If you've come about the bear, it isn't a bear.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_ilth: Greenshade Watch. Speak plainly and keep your fire in its pit, and we'll get along.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_nere: Ashtown welcomes you, stranger. We have little, but the Lady taught us to share the dusk with anyone who walks in it.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_qama: Sweet water, a copper a cup. The sweetest in Skaven. Don't ask why. Everybody asks why.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_shaz: Welcome to the Two Moons. Shazah has beds. Shazah does not promise you will stay in them.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_tire: Ah. A visitor who is not a Justiciar. Sit, please, before one arrives and spoils it.
story.skycraft.npc.pln_tamriel_west_ysme: You have an honest face. How refreshing. At court we would have it painted over by now.
story.skycraft.npc.primate_artorius.gree: The Temple of the One welcomes every soul, the faithful and the merely tired alike. Sit, if you need to. The Nine are patient.
story.skycraft.npc.prophet_of_anvil.gree: They laugh at me in the street. Let them. Something old is waking under the Heartland, and the Nine have no knights left to meet it.
story.skycraft.npc.quaranir.greet: You've noticed me. Good. The Psijic Order watches; it seldom speaks. Today it speaks to you.
story.skycraft.npc.ra_khaj.greet: If you are here to question this one again, he still knows nothing. If you are here for something else, please be quick.
story.skycraft.npc.ralof.greet: Gerdur's cooking, a roof, and a dragon somewhere to the north. Talos keep us, what a day.
story.skycraft.npc.raminus_polus.greet: Master of Initiates. Which means I read your recommendation letters, and I find out which of them were exaggerated.
story.skycraft.npc.ranabi_erabenimsun.gr: Gulakhan of the Erabenimsun. Urshilaku friend, are you? Then you're a long way from friends.
story.skycraft.npc.rawan_dar.greet: Rawan-dar sells spice, silk, and absolutely no opinions about politics. None. Would you like some silk?
story.skycraft.npc.razum_dar.greet: Raz is only a humble envoy of the Queen. Humble, handsome, and listening to everything you say. Sit, sit.
story.skycraft.npc.redoran_warden.greet: House Redoran keeps the ash at bay. Duty first. Speak quickly.
story.skycraft.npc.rikke.greet: Skyrim is my home too, whatever Ulfric says. The Legion is how we keep it whole.
story.skycraft.npc.rolan_dufresne.greet: Camlorn sends its best to the lists every year, and every year Daggerfall pretends to be surprised when we win.
story.skycraft.npc.sabine_larrenne.greet: I study the Dwarves. Mostly that means I study the inside of locked crates and the outside of my purse.
story.skycraft.npc.sabjorn.greet: Honningbrew mead, best in the hold. Or it will be, once I get rid of these skeevers.
story.skycraft.npc.sam.greet: A drinking contest! Win, and I'll give you a staff that'll make you famous. Lose, and you buy.
story.skycraft.npc.savlian.greet: Kvatch was burned once, in the Oblivion Crisis. We rebuilt it. Now there's a gate in the hills again, and nobody wants to say it out loud.
story.skycraft.npc.savos_aren.greet: The College is a place of learning. I'd like it to remain one, whatever the Jarl and the townsfolk think of us.
story.skycraft.npc.sedrisa_vandu.greet: Half the village is coughing ash and the other half is too frightened to come near them. I'm running out of everything.
story.skycraft.npc.sees_behind_eyes.gree: You hatched under the Shadow, little one. I smelled it on you before you reached the door. Come in out of the light.
story.skycraft.npc.septimus.greet: The box, the lock, the heart within... Hm? A visitor. How dreadfully interruptive.
story.skycraft.npc.serana.greet: I've been asleep a long time. Tell me the world hasn't changed too much. Actually, don't.
story.skycraft.npc.shazrah.greet: Welcome to the camp of the Laughing Blades, walker. We laugh because the nobles have taken everything else. Why are you here?
story.skycraft.npc.shishara_assemanu.gre: Guar hides, kwama eggs, trama root. Honest goods, honest prices. Don't haggle like a Hlaalu and we'll get along.
story.skycraft.npc.side_aka_maveri.greet: You have the look of someone who goes places. Unwise places. Excellent.
story.skycraft.npc.side_aka_ulrika.greet: If you've come about the overdue library books, I returned them. Mostly.
story.skycraft.npc.side_atm_brunhild.gre: I rivet hulls for the Stormcloak fleet. My great-grandfather built ships that sailed the other way.
story.skycraft.npc.side_atm_skjold.greet: Forty years on the Sea of Ghosts. I've seen things on the ice I don't tell my wife about.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_asheel.greet: The city coughs and the Lukiul hand out boiled water. The Hist has better medicine, if anyone would ask it.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_decimus_tslee: Decimus, yes. My egg-name is longer and harder to fit on a ledger. Are you buying, or are you staring?
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_esh_teeka.gre: Mind your boots near the warm-mud. Every pool you see has someone in it who has not been named yet.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_flavia_fennic: My family has kept a candle for the Ninth since before I was born. You are not here to sell me another, I hope.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_heem_ra.greet: Boil your water. Wash your hands. I will say it to the King himself if he comes in coughing.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_hixil.greet: The Tsleeksh lay their eggs in this sand every spring. Every spring, some are gone by morning. Walk carefully.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_hulum_ei.gree: Warm-blood. You smell of roads. Sit downwind of me and we will both be happier.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_jee_tazei.gre: Every hull that ties up in Lilmoth pays a little, and every hull is a little heavier for it. That is my gift to the city.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_junal_lei.gre: Tariffs, tithes and births. If it happens in Stormhold, I have a column for it.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_livia_corvane: The Legion left Stormhold. I did not. Someone has to write down the glyphs before the moss eats them.
Count them if you like. One notch for every beast that tried to swallow me. The tail has run out of room.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_okan_zeeus.gr: The Hist of Okeeh drinks slowly this season, and so do I. Forgive an old tender. My roots are in two places today.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_reezal_jul.gr: Murkmire is small, and the roots here are old. They notice when a stranger walks on them.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_seeks_tomorro: Cloth, rope, Cyrodilic nails. I sell what the marsh cannot grow. Tomorrow I will sell more of it.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_wanes_in_shal: The fish are where they always were. It is the fishers who are missing.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_wiz_tul.greet: Hatch-Mother says I talk too much for someone with no name-scales yet. I say she listens too little.
story.skycraft.npc.side_bm_xil_mareeh.gr: My nephew wears trousers and an Imperial name. I still love him. It takes effort.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_aldo_castell: Castellus red. Forty years in the cask, and the best thing you will ever taste. Assuming the Merovanes leave me a single vine to make it with.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_cassia_valla: You may bow, or not. My grandfather would have had you whipped for the omission. I am trying very hard not to be my grandfather.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_drevis_hlare: Captain of the Cheydinhal watch. Speak plainly, outlander. Three merchants are dead and I am out of patience for riddles.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_ervyn_sadrat: Did my mother send you? Whatever she said, I was nowhere near the shrine. I was at the tavern. Ask anyone. Ask the tavern.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_feldsa_sadra: Forgive the mess, sera. Our family shrine was robbed, and a house without its ancestors is only a pile of furniture.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_hrefna.greet: Every song in Bruma is about snow. I mean to write one about something that bites back.
The singing stopped. Is it safe to stop holding my breath now?
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_marcellin_he: Harbor customs. Everything that comes into Anvil passes my desk, and everything that leaves it without passing my desk is my problem.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_pellio_brash: Put the sword down. I'm not who you think I am. Well. I am, but not the way you've been told.
If you've come for a burial, the shop is shut. Master Valcis has not come home in nine days, and I cannot lift the coffins alone.
Keep your hands where the lantern can see them. Nobody comes to Hrota Cave for the view.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_seeks_the_sh: My boat goes where the water goes. If you want somewhere the water does not go, find a horse.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_septima_meru: I keep the graves of men who have no graves. It is quieter work than it sounds, until someone asks me why.
Mind the ink, it is still wet. I have been copying Ayleid lamp-glyphs since dawn and my hand has forgotten how to stop.
Lend a coin, borrow a coin, it's all the same to Tullo. Unless you're late paying it back.
story.skycraft.npc.side_cyr_ysmene_merov: Merovane tawny, my friend. Sweeter than Castellus and twice as honest. If old Aldo sent you, you may leave the way you came.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_ahnissi.gree: Every ship that ties up in Senchal smells of sugar. Ahnissi's job is to learn which kind.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_ahzir.greet: Lord Ahzir does not usually speak to people with road dust on them. Today he will make an exception. Briefly.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_azirr.greet: Azirr counts stars, moons and the steps between them. Tonight the count is wrong, and Azirr does not like wrong.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_hanzira.gree: Hanzira hunts what the Mane's riders will not. Usually this means things with very large teeth.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_inzirr.greet: Inzirr keeps the sand-graves of Torval tidy. The dead do not complain, which is restful.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_ja_neema.gre: Ja'neema sells her father's luck-charms. She would sell his luck too, if she could find where he put it.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_jo_zhirr.gre: Jo'zhirr has fought Thalmor, bandits and one very angry mother senche. He has scars from all of them. The senche left the best ones.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_khali.greet: Khali counts what leaves Rimmen and what arrives elsewhere. The numbers should match. Khali is paid to worry when they do not.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_ma_dara.gree: Sit, sit. Ma'dara knows three hundred songs of Anequina, and every one of them is mostly true.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_ri_zhassa.gr: Ri'zhassa grows the sweetest cane in Pellitine. Grew. This season she is not sure what she grows.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_shavi_ra.gre: Shavi-ra judges disputes over sugar, land and sometimes cats. The cats are the most honest of the three.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_shirra.greet: Shirra's father kept the old light on the south rocks. He stopped writing in his log one night. Shirra has not stopped waiting.
story.skycraft.npc.side_els_zaba_jo.gree: Zaba-jo lights the lamps of the low streets every dusk. Lately, every dusk, he lights them twice.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_bahrun.greet: My grandmother's grandmother read the sky over Craglorn before Elinhir had walls. Lately the sky has been writing back.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_bashir.greet: I can see a scorpion's tail over a dune at half a league. Close up I need spectacles, but don't tell anyone.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_eriq.greet: Water. Then light. Then you can tell me how long I've been in here.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_fahim.greet: The sun is too loud today. Do you ever feel that? As if it were shouting at you.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_ghesh.greet: Few climb this high without a reason or a knife. Let me guess which one you brought.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_hamid.greet: Every hull that enters this harbour passes through my ledger. Every hull. I am very proud of my ledger.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_huzayra.greet: Lovely boots. Very quiet. I always notice boots.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_ilvane.greet: Dwemer tonal architecture, if you must know. No, it doesn't sing. Not unless you ask it in exactly the right key.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_imran.greet: Dates, figs, and a grudge older than either. Only the first two are for sale.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_jafar.greet: You're not one of them. Gods, you're not one of them. Is Neyra all right?
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_jazira.greet: The at-Kherun had a ship once, and a hall, and a sword-singer at every wedding. Now we have a name and a roof that leaks.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_maradh.greet: The at-Senna kept the old songs when the Bel-Tavir were still learning to count Imperial coin. Remember that, whatever they tell you.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_nahrin.greet: Forgive me if I seem distracted. A mother counts the hours her son is away, and lately there are a great many.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_neyra.greet: Mind the nets. And if you're headed out past the point, mind the boats with no colours on them.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_nisha.greet: Salves for burns, teas for the cough, and something for whatever else ails you. Ask nicely about the something.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_nisha|side_hf: You return with word from the road?
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_qadira: Qadira, Keeper of the Last Rites
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_qadira.greet: Tu'whacca guides the dead to the Far Shores. My work is only to make sure they are buried facing the right way.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_salima.greet: Have you seen a boy, nine years old, missing a front tooth? No. No, of course you haven't.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_tariq.greet: I didn't cry. The little ones cried. I told them stories so they'd stop.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_turaz.greet: My hands shake when I lift a cup. They never shake when I lift a sword. Forty years of practice buys you that much.
story.skycraft.npc.side_hf_veshra.greet: The Bangkorai passes are my charge. If you've come about a post, I need sentries who can stay awake.
