story.skycraft.q.ic_stendarrs_hammer.des: Worshippers of Mehrunes Dagon, the remnants of the old Mythic Dawn, have gathered at the Prince's shrine south of the Heartland. Primate Artorius has asked me to carry Stendarr's justice to them.
Travel to the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon
Drive out the cultists and their summoned servants
Kill the cult's leader, Ruinous Cassia
Stendarr's mercy is for the repentant. His hammer is for those who would burn the world twice. You knew the difference. I will see this idol ground to dust.
Bring the idol to Primate Artorius
The cult is broken. Their idol, for the Temple to destroy.
story.skycraft.q.ic_stendarrs_hammer.out: I broke a Mythic Dawn remnant at the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon and brought their idol to the Temple to be destroyed.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_covenant_lists.d: Knights from every corner of the Daggerfall Covenant have come to the autumn lists outside Daggerfall. Dame Maelis has entered my name, and the favourite is Sir Rolan Dufresne of Camlorn.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_covenant_lists.o: Someone had to. Half the Covenant heard about Baelborne Rock and wants to know if it's true. The other half wants to knock you down to prove it isn't. Sir Rolan of Camlorn is in the final. Go and introduce yourself.
Speak with Dame Maelis about the tournament
You entered my name in the lists?
The dragon-slayer. I'll try not to embarrass you too badly; Daggerfall needs its heroes. Blunted steel, first to yield. Unless you'd rather make it interesting.
I hear we're to meet in the final.
Rolan was quicker than I expected and prouder than he should have been. When his shield arm finally dropped, he raised his visor and called the yield himself.
Defeat Sir Rolan in the final bout

A humbling one. Here, a winner's purse, and something worth more. My grandfather swore the Banner of the Red Wyrm lies in Cath Bedraud, with the knight who carried it. Daggerfall never went to look. Maybe its dragon-slayer should.
Speak with Sir Rolan after the bout
I won the Covenant lists against Sir Rolan Dufresne of Camlorn. In defeat he told me where the order's lost founding banner may lie: the old crypts of Cath Bedraud.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.desc: Lord Commander Odric Hollenmoor of the Knights of the Dragon agreed to consider me as an aspirant. I must keep the vigil at the dragon-stone and then pass Dame Maelis Corbel's trial.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o0.jo: The stone is carved with a coiled dragon worn nearly smooth by centuries of hands. Around midnight the cold came up out of the ground, and I stayed where I was.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o0.te: Keep vigil at the dragon-stone in the courtyard
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o1.re: Your eyes are red and your hands are steady. Good. Now the useful part. Wolves have been taking lambs from the farms outside the east gate. A knight serves the people before the crown. Go and serve them.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o2.te: Kill the wolves raiding the farms outside Daggerfall
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o3.re: And the farmers? Did you speak to them, or just leave carcasses in their fields? Never mind. One last thing before the Lord Commander. Every aspirant answers this.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o4.c0: To guard those who can't guard themselves.
The oldest answer, and still the right one. Hold on to it when the lords start giving you orders.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o4.c1: For glory, and a name the bards remember.
Honest, at least. Glory comes to knights who are too busy to look for it. You'll learn.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o4.c2: For Daggerfall, and for the Covenant.
Spoken like a native. The Lord Commander will like that.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.o4.te: Tell Dame Maelis why you would be a knight
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.offer: I'd like to serve the Knights of the Dragon.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.outro: I kept the vigil at the dragon-stone and passed Dame Maelis Corbel's trial. Lord Commander Hollenmoor accepted me as an aspirant of the Knights of the Dragon.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.pitch: Everyone would like to. Few last the night. Every aspirant keeps vigil at the old dragon-stone in the courtyard until dawn, alone, without sleep. Then Dame Maelis will see whether you can do more than stand still.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_long_vigil.title: The Long Vigil
The Banner of the Red Wyrm, the founding standard of the Knights of the Dragon, may lie in the crypts of Cath Bedraud. Dame Maelis will ride with me to bring it home.
Fight through the restless dead of Cath Bedraud
A Bloodthorn necromancer had made the crypt her workshop and was singing the knights out of their graves to guard it. Her song ended in the middle of a verse.
Take down the Banner of the Red Wyrm
Two hundred years. Maelis, call the whole order into the hall. Every knight, every squire, every stable-hand who can stand. This one is going to be done properly.
Carry the banner home to Daggerfall
The Banner of the Red Wyrm, Lord Commander.
I recovered the Banner of the Red Wyrm from Cath Bedraud and carried it home. Lord Commander Hollenmoor knighted me before the whole order and gave me a captain's command.
The Banner of the Red Wyrm
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_road_to_aldcroft: Lord Commander Hollenmoor ordered me to escort Lady Ysolde Merrival from Daggerfall to her estate at Aldcroft. Bloodthorn cultists have been active along the road.
One knight. Not even a knight, I'm told. Well, Hollenmoor has never yet wasted my time. Keep close, and if anything with thorns in its hair comes out of the woods, kill it before it reaches me.
The Lord Commander sent me to see you to Aldcroft.
The cultists had grown a hedge of black thorns across the lane overnight. When we cut through it, they were waiting on the other side.
Fight off the Bloodthorn ambush at the village edge
So I am, and with my skin intact. I shall write to Hollenmoor that his aspirant fights like a knight and talks like a farmhand. He will understand both are compliments.
Do you have work for an aspirant?
I brought Lady Ysolde Merrival safely to Aldcroft through a Bloodthorn ambush. She has written to the Lord Commander on my behalf.

Lady Ysolde Merrival must reach her estate at Aldcroft before the harvest court, and the road runs through country the Bloodthorn cult has been stirring up. She wants a whole company. She gets you. See that it's enough.
story.skycraft.q.kd_the_wyrm_of_baelborn: A dragon has made its lair on Baelborne Rock, west of Daggerfall, and has been burning farmsteads across Glenumbra. The Knights of the Dragon took their name from such a beast, and the Lord Commander wants it dead.

Glenumbra has a dragon problem. This order has a dragon on every shield and banner, and I'll not have it said we hid behind the walls while a real one burned the countryside. It nests on Baelborne Rock. Bring me proof it's dead.
Lady Ysolde says you have a dragon problem.
It came down out of the cloud with a sound like a forge bellows the size of a church. When it fell, the rock shook under me for a long time.
Slay the dragon of Baelborne Rock
Take a tooth from the wyrm's jaw

By the Eight. The first dragon this order has killed in a hundred years, and an aspirant did it. Squire, then, from today. And I'll have this tooth mounted over the hall door so the lords can admire it on their way in.
Bring the tooth to Lord Commander Hollenmoor
The dragon of Baelborne Rock is dead.
I killed the dragon of Baelborne Rock. Lord Commander Hollenmoor raised me to squire and hung its tooth above the hall door.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_divine_crusader.des: The Prophet told me that Umaril's spirit will come down to face me in Garlas Malatar under the night sky. If I destroy his avatar there, he will never return.
I heard the bells, even from here. The order is yours to lead, Divine Crusader. I'll be proud to serve under you.
Return to Sir Amiel at the Priory
Umaril is gone. All of him.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_divine_crusader.off: Umaril's spirit escaped. How do I follow it?
story.skycraft.q.kn9_divine_crusader.out: I destroyed Umaril's avatar and ended him for good. Sir Amiel named me Divine Crusader, head of the Knights of the Nine.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_divine_crusader.pit: You don't follow it. You call it. Go back to Garlas Malatar under the night sky, wearing Pelinal's blessing, and Umaril's pride will bring his avatar down to meet you. When it falls, nothing of him will return.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_mace_of_the_crusade: The Ayleids hid Pelinal's Stendarr-blessed mace in Garlas Agea, a ruin near Lake Rumare. Umaril's Aurorans are already inside.
Travel to the Ayleid ruin of Garlas Agea
Destroy the Aurorans searching the ruin
Take the Mace of the Crusader
Only a step. They will not get closer. The relics are whole, and so is the order. Now we find Umaril.
Bring the mace to Sir Amiel
The Mace of the Crusader. The Aurorans were a step behind me.
I took the Mace of the Crusader from Garlas Agea ahead of Umaril's Aurorans. The relics of Pelinal Whitestrake are gathered at the Priory.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.desc: A street preacher in Anvil who calls himself the Prophet asked me to walk a pilgrimage to the chapels of the Nine, and then present myself at the Priory of the Nine near Kvatch.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o0.journ: Kvatch's chapel is still half scaffolding. A mason stopped work to let me pray, and did not ask why.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o0.text: Pray at the rebuilt Chapel of Akatosh in Kvatch
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o1.text: Pray at the Chapel of Julianos in Skingrad
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o2.text: Pray at the Great Chapel of Stendarr in Chorrol
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o3.reply: Then the Prophet was right, and I was right to wait. Kneel. In the name of the Nine, I accept you as a knight of this order. There are few of us. There will be more.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o3.text: Present yourself to Sir Amiel Lannus at the Priory of the Nine
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.o3.topic: The Prophet sent me. I've walked the pilgrimage.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.outro: I walked the pilgrimage of the Nine and was received into the Knights of the Nine by Sir Amiel Lannus at the Priory near Kvatch.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.pitch: That the Nine need knights again. Not soldiers. Knights. If you would be one, walk the pilgrimage: pray at the chapels of Kvatch, Skingrad and Chorrol, and come to the Priory of the Nine outside Kvatch. Sir Amiel waits there.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_pilgrimage.title: Pilgrimage of the Nine
story.skycraft.q.kn9_relics_of_the_white: Pelinal's helm and gauntlets were laid with the first knights of his order in an ossuary near Anvil. The dead there do not welcome visitors.
Travel to the Ossuary of the Knights
Lay the restless dead of the ossuary to rest
Take the Helm of the Crusader
Something had disturbed the knights' rest before me. Gold scratches on the stone, like the marks of a gauntleted hand. Umaril's servants are hunting the relics too.
Take the Gauntlets of the Crusader
Pelinal's own. I never thought I'd see it. Set it on the altar, beside his cuirass that the Priory has kept all these years. Do you have the gauntlets?
Bring the helm to Sir Amiel
Aurorans. Meridia's fallen warriors, Umaril's servants. Then he is truly stirring. One relic remains: the mace.
Bring the gauntlets to Sir Amiel
And the gauntlets. Something else was looking for them.
I recovered Pelinal's helm and gauntlets from the Ossuary of the Knights. Umaril's Auroran servants are already searching for the rest.
story.skycraft.q.kn9_shrine_of_the_crusa: Sir Amiel believes the spirit of Pelinal Whitestrake, the Divine Crusader, can still be reached at a forgotten shrine in the hills near Kvatch, and that it will tell us where his relics lie.
Find the Shrine of the Crusader
Umaril. The Ayleid sorcerer Pelinal fought to the last. If he's returning, we will need every relic the Crusader left. Follow the ember.
Tell Sir Amiel what you saw
Pelinal spoke to me. Umaril the Unfeathered is returning.
At the Shrine of the Crusader I saw Pelinal Whitestrake, who warned that Umaril the Unfeathered is returning, and told me where his relics lie.
Umaril the Unfeathered has taken flesh again in Garlas Malatar, the ruin where his last followers waited. Sir Amiel has blessed the relics. It is time to fight him.
I struck down Umaril's body in Garlas Malatar, but his spirit escaped to Meridia's realm. He is not finished.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.de: Lord Aubrec Valmont of the Knights of the Rose set me a first task: end the extortion of the fishwives on the Wayrest docks.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.o0: The Gullhook boys. They sell 'protection' to women who gut fish for a living, and break their tables when they can't pay. Give them the chance to leave. If they refuse it, don't give them a second.
Lord Valmont sent me about the docks.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.o1: I told them to leave the docks. Their leader laughed and drew a gutting knife. The fishwives cheered at the end, which I did not expect.
Break the Gullhook gang on the docks
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.o2: I watched from the harbour wall. You offered them the door first. Good. That's what separates us from the men we fight. Go and tell Lord Valmont.
The Gullhook gang won't trouble anyone again.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.o3: Dame Orielle has already sung your praises, which she does about once a decade. Take the Rose, Aspirant. Wear it where people can see it, and behave accordingly.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.of: I'd like to earn a place among the Knights of the Rose.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.ou: I broke the Gullhook gang that preyed on the fishwives of the Wayrest docks. Lord Aubrec Valmont accepted me as an aspirant of the Knights of the Rose.
story.skycraft.q.kr_a_courteous_blade.pi: Then begin where we all begin, with the people nobody else bothers about. A gang has been squeezing coin out of the fishwives on the Wayrest docks. Dame Orielle will tell you more. Settle it, and settle it like a knight, not a brawler.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.desc: Chancellor Ivo Brennault has fled to Saltreef Hold to sail out of the King's reach. Lord Valmont has given me the honour of bringing him to justice.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o1.te: Cut down the Chancellor's hired swords on the shore
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o2.jo: The Chancellor was a battlemage in his youth, it turns out, and had kept his hand in. It did not save him. The pirate ship sailed without him.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o2.te: Stop Ivo Brennault before he reaches the ship
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o3.re: Then Wayrest owes you its honour twice over. Come to the chapel tonight. The order has a question to ask you, and an oath to hear.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o3.te: Return to Lord Valmont in Wayrest
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.o3.to: The Chancellor won't trouble the court again.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.outro: I stopped Chancellor Brennault at Saltreef before he could escape across the bay. In the chapel of the Rose I swore the order's oath, and Lord Valmont named me Lord of the Rose.
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_roses_oath.title: The Rose's Oath
story.skycraft.q.kr_the_saltreef_hostage: Elsabet Mornay is held by pirates at Saltreef Hold on the coast west of Wayrest. Lord Valmont wants her brought home alive before the Chancellor's allies decide she knows too much.
Fight through the pirates of Saltreef Hold
Red Brannoc told me, with his last breath, that he had been paid to take the girl and paid again to keep her. He didn't say by whom. He didn't need to.
Kill the pirate captain, Red Brannoc
I heard them talking about the Chancellor. My father was going to vote against his new tariff. They were going to hold me until the council met. Please, take me home.
Lord Valmont sent me. You're safe now.
A councillor's daughter stolen to buy a vote. The King must hear it, from her own mouth, before the whole court.
Elsabet is home. She heard the pirates name the Chancellor.
I rescued Elsabet Mornay from the pirates of Saltreef Hold. She heard them name Chancellor Brennault, who had her taken to force her father's vote on the King's council.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.desc: Accused before the court, Chancellor Brennault claimed the old Breton right of trial by combat, and named Sir Garrick Vane his champion. Lord Valmont has named me champion of the Rose.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o0.r: An old law, and he knows Garrick Vane has never lost a duel. If his champion wins, Stendarr has judged him innocent, and nobody may speak of it again. I am too old to be sure of beating Vane. You are not.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o0.t: The Chancellor wants a trial by combat?
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o1.c: I'll fight to make him yield. The truth needs a winner, not a corpse.
That is the Rose's way, and the harder one. Vane will not offer you the same courtesy.
Whatever it takes. Vane chose his master.
Then go with Stendarr, and don't let anger make you careless.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o1.t: Tell Lord Valmont how you will fight
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o2.j: Garrick Vane was the best swordsman I have ever faced. When he went down he did not ask for mercy. He simply looked up at the gallery, and saw his master's chair empty.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o2.t: Defeat Sir Garrick Vane on the duelling ground
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o3.r: Through a servants' door with half the treasury's seals in his pockets, and a pirate ship waiting at Saltreef, no doubt. He has run to the only friends he has left.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.o3.t: The Chancellor fled before the duel ended.
story.skycraft.q.kr_trial_by_combat.outr: I defeated Sir Garrick Vane in a trial by combat, and the court of Wayrest judged the Chancellor guilty. Brennault fled before the verdict, toward his pirate allies at Saltreef.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.desc: Pirates have kidnapped Elsabet Mornay, daughter of a royal councillor. Chancellor Ivo Brennault wants the ransom paid at once, and Lord Valmont suspects something is wrong.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o0.r: Valmont asked, did he? Very well. Read it, by all means. The girl's life is on a clock, and the Rose should be helping me pay, not reading over my shoulder. The money goes to the docks tonight.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o0.t: Lord Valmont asked me to look at the ransom letter.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o2.j: The go-between was no pirate. He wore a clerk's ink stains under his sailor's coat, and he fought like a man who had never expected to.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o2.t: Catch the go-between collecting the ransom on the docks
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o3.t: Take the purse the go-between carried
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o4.r: Paid to the pirates by the Chancellor's banker, before the ransom was ever announced. Brennault arranged this himself. The question is why. We need the girl back before anyone thinks to silence her.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.o4.t: Bring the purse and the letter to Lord Valmont
The go-between was carrying this. It's the Chancellor's own coin.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.outr: The ransom for Elsabet Mornay was being paid out of Chancellor Brennault's own purse before the kidnapping was announced. The Chancellor arranged it. Lord Valmont wants her rescued before she can be silenced.
story.skycraft.q.kr_very_good_paper.pitc: I am. Iliac Bay pirates have taken Elsabet Mornay, whose father sits on the King's council. Chancellor Brennault wants the ransom paid quietly and quickly. Something about it smells wrong. Go and see the Chancellor, and look at that letter with a knight's eyes.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_ashes_of_fort_sutch: Daedra have been seen around Fort Sutch, where an Oblivion gate once burned near Anvil. Commander Phillida has called up the Legion to hold the fort, and I am to lead the defence.
Hold the walls against the first wave of Daedra
Valkynaz Ruuth laughed when he fell, and promised to come back. Perhaps he will. The fort is still ours.
Kill the dremora warlord Valkynaz Ruuth
Then the Gold Coast sleeps tonight because of you. The Legion needs officers who stand when the sky turns red. Consider yourself promoted.
Report to Adamus Phillida in the Imperial City
Fort Sutch held. Their warlord carried this.
I held Fort Sutch against the Daedra and killed their warlord. Commander Phillida raised me to Tribune.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_blood_on_the_gold_r: A bandit warlord named Varn Ironjaw holds Fort Urasek on the Gold Road and has been robbing every caravan bound for Skingrad. Commander Phillida ordered me to retake the fort.
Travel to Fort Urasek on the Gold Road
Retake Fort Urasek from the bandits
Varn Ironjaw had a strongbox full of caravan seals and a Legion helmet he'd taken off a dead patrol. He fought like a man who thought nobody would ever come for him.
Then the Gold Road is open. Skingrad's merchants will remember the Legion kindly, for a month or two. Well done, soldier.
Fort Urasek is ours again. Ironjaw is dead.
I retook Fort Urasek and killed the warlord Varn Ironjaw. The caravans run again between the Imperial City and Skingrad.
A warlord calling himself Varn Ironjaw has taken Fort Urasek on the Gold Road and is taxing every caravan between here and Skingrad. Take the fort back. Bring me his head, or at least his surrender.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_hunting_the_fox.des: Captain Lex wants the Gray Fox, master of the Thieves Guild, in a cell. He has sent me into the Waterfront to find where the smugglers' cargo ends up. Anyone in the Guild will see this as a betrayal.
Behind a false wall in a Waterfront warehouse I found a grey hood hung on a peg, a lamp still warm, and a man whose face I could not keep in my mind. He did not run. He asked me what I was going to tell Lex.
Then tell me where, soldier. Tell me exactly where.
I found the Gray Fox's hideout.
It was empty. He was gone before I got there.
Gone. Always gone. Very well. I'll get him another day, and you'll be there when I do.
The Waterfront, behind the warehouse wall. I'll take you there.
At last. We'll raid it tonight. If he slips the cells again, it won't be for lack of trying on your part.
Decide whether to give the Gray Fox up to Captain Lex
story.skycraft.q.lgc_hunting_the_fox.out: I tracked the Gray Fox to the Waterfront and made my choice about what Captain Lex would hear.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.desc: Captain Lex believes smugglers cross Lake Rumare by night to supply the Waterfront. He sent me to their cove on the north shore to find out who they work for.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.o0.t: Find the smugglers' cove on Lake Rumare
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.o1.t: Wait for the smugglers' boats after dark
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.o3.t: Search the smugglers' boat for papers
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.o4.r: Of course it does. The Waterfront means one thing to me: the Gray Fox. This is the closest I've been in years.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.o4.t: Bring the manifest to Captain Lex
The smugglers kept a manifest. Every cargo goes to a Waterfront warehouse.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.offe: Captain, you look like a man with a grudge.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.outr: The smugglers on Lake Rumare were supplying the Waterfront. Captain Lex is convinced the trail leads to the Gray Fox himself.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_mist_on_rumare.pitc: Smugglers are running boats across Lake Rumare at night, straight into the Waterfront. I want to know what they're carrying and who they're carrying it for. There's a cove on the north shore. Go after dark.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_stones_for_kvatch.d: Commander Phillida assigned me to escort the master mason Marcella Tullus to Kvatch, where Savlian Matius is rebuilding the city's walls.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_stones_for_kvatch.o: Just you? Well, I've seen the Legion send fewer. My tools are on the cart. Try to keep the bandits off them; they're worth more than I am.
Meet Marcella Tullus in the Imperial City
Drive off the scavengers picking over the convoy road
Whole! I'd nearly forgotten that was possible. Stay a moment. I want you to see this.
I brought Marcella Tullus safely to Kvatch. The first stones of the new walls went up while I watched.
story.skycraft.q.lgc_stones_for_kvatch.p: Kvatch is still rebuilding, and every mason we send gets robbed on the road. Marcella Tullus is the best builder in the Heartland. Take her to Savlian Matius in Kvatch, alive and with her tools, and see the first walls go up.
Commander Adamus Phillida will take me into the Imperial Legion if I serve a first duty with the Imperial Watch: clearing the thugs who rob travellers on the Red Ring Road.
A recruit. Wonderful. The Red Ring Road, south shore. Four of them, maybe five, and they're bold because nobody stops them. Stop them.
Commander Phillida sent me to you.
Clear the thugs off the Red Ring Road
Captain Lex says you did it cleanly. Raise your right hand. You serve the Empire, its laws and its people, for as long as it needs you. Welcome to the Legion, Auxiliary.
Return to Adamus Phillida and take the oath
The Red Ring Road is clear.
I want to serve the Legion.
I cleared the Red Ring Road and swore the oath of the Imperial Legion before Commander Adamus Phillida.

Good. The Watch is short of hands, so you'll start there. Thugs have been robbing travellers on the Red Ring Road in sight of the city walls. Clear them off and report to Captain Lex. If you're still standing, you'll take the oath.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.desc: A barrel stamped with a sun and a tally of casks sold abroad, and a scratched warning that the Root is not for sale.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.find: A sap-barrel behind the mansion's boat-shed is stamped with a golden sun and a tally of casks sold abroad. Beneath, in an Argonian hand: 'The Root is not ours to sell.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.o0.text: Take the keeper's tear-vial from the shrine to the weeping falls.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.o1.text: Carry the wamasu-tear to the river-fortress of Stormhold.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.o2.text: Copy the pharmacists' sap manifest at Stormhold's river gate.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The tapped root's cries lead from a hollow shrine and a weeping falls through a river fortress to a hag-lair and the black pool.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.pitch: A boatman says the merchant's mansion has more sap than anyone should.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_a.title: The Tapped Root
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.desc: The tapped root's cries lead from a hollow shrine and a weeping falls through a river fortress to a hag-lair and the black pool.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.o0.text: Take the corrupt priest's licence to the hag-lair in the swamp.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.o1.text: Cut the tap-pipe in the hag-lair and quiet the bogmother.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.o2.text: Pull the brass tap-fitting from the Black Maw's pool.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.outro: At the black pool I stopped the tap and the sap ran clear into the pool again. The merchant's coffers will be lighter. The marsh is quieter. The Root remembers who listened.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.pitch: A boatman says the merchant's mansion has more sap than anyone should.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_1_b.title: The Tapped Root (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.desc: A warm-count carved on an egg-shaped stone shows each season's heat a notch lower than the last.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.find: An egg-shaped stone on the hill has a warm-count carved in it, each season's temperature a notch lower than the last. A fresh notch is chiselled this week, deeper than any.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.o0.text: Follow the steam-thread from the pools into Lilmoth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The cooling pools, the capital's ziggurat and a rotting pavilion are all part of the same missing warmth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.pitch: The hatchery keepers say the pools are a degree colder each season.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_a.title: The Warm Count
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.desc: The cooling pools, the capital's ziggurat and a rotting pavilion are all part of the same missing warmth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.o0.text: Follow the cold's direction from Lilmoth's ziggurat into the mire.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.o1.text: Take a seat at the pavilion's table and end the supper.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.outro: The pavilion's guests rose from their chairs and drifted out into the mire, and the plates cooled. In the warm pools, a week later, the eggs began to hatch with ordinary colour.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.pitch: The hatchery keepers say the pools are a degree colder each season.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_2_b.title: The Warm Count (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.desc: A rice-counter's tally has forty-one workers at sunrise and forty-two at dusk.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.find: A rice-counter's tally: forty-one workers at sunrise, forty-two at dusk. Below, in a careful hand: 'Did I miscount? I never miscount.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.o0.text: Record the Hist's whisper at Root Whisper and bring it to Thorn.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.o1.text: Look into the Hist-pool at Thorn and follow the figure to the border.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The extra one's seat has been kept at a village table, a Hist pool and a border-post, and its owner waits in the xanmeer.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.pitch: The rice-counter says there is always one more to feed at the evening bowl.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_a.title: The Extra One
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.desc: The extra one's seat has been kept at a village table, a Hist pool and a border-post, and its owner waits in the xanmeer.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.o0.text: Copy the monolith's unreadable name and carry it into the xanmeer.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.o1.text: Descend the shaft and speak the founder's name.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.outro: I named him, at last, in the flooded hall: not a name of any tribe but a name of the marsh. The last chair at every table was, for the first time in a thousand years, empty. The Hist hummed a note I had not heard.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.pitch: The rice-counter says there is always one more to feed at the evening bowl.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_3_b.title: The Extra One (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.desc: A fishing hamlet's grave, its marker moved inland from the shore, with a note that the dirge no longer goes to the water.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.find: A fishing-hamlet grave is empty, its marker moved a hundred paces inland from the shore. Scratched on the stone: 'The dirge doesn't go to the water any more.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.o0.text: Take the singers' map to the lone plateau to see the dirge's new road.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.o1.text: Sight the dirge's two routes from the plateau and take the survey to Gideon.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.o2.text: Take the lord's contract from the plantation courtyard at Gideon.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The dirge's new path crosses a plateau and a plantation city and ends in a mire ringed by black teeth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.pitch: A fisher says the grave-singers no longer sing the dead to the sea, and nobody will tell why.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_a.title: The Rerouted Dirge
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.desc: The dirge's new path crosses a plateau and a plantation city and ends in a mire ringed by black teeth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.o0.text: Take the island keepers' chart to the deep mire.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.o1.text: Learn the last verse from the Murkmire singer and take it to the ring of teeth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.o2.text: Sing the old verse in the centre of the teeth and restore the dirge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.outro: At the ring of teeth I sang the old verse and the dirge came back to its water. The plantation lord's fields went dry. The marsh knows the debt it owes and the debt it must still collect.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.pitch: A fisher says the grave-singers no longer sing the dead to the sea, and nobody will tell why.
story.skycraft.q.lw_bm_4_b.title: The Rerouted Dirge (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.desc: A tally of a thousand names at an abandoned Ayleid dig led me toward an Alessian gate and a family of winemakers.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.find: A scaffold post has been chalked with a tally of a thousand strokes, and beneath it, scratched deep: 'Do not say them aloud. Take the rubbing to the Alessian gate.' A grape leaf is pinned through the tally.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.o0.text: At the Gate of Alma Ruma, match the rubbing to the cut-out page and follow it to a winery.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.o1.text: Drink the Remembrance vintage at Thalaras Winery and follow what it shows.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The wine, the pool and the Count's silent castle all point at the vault of names under Miscarcand.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.pitch: Diggers at the cut-away stopped work when someone read a name aloud. They were paid in wine, not coin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_a.title: The Debt of Names
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.desc: The wine, the pool and the Count's silent castle all point at the vault of names under Miscarcand.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.o0.text: Read the names in the mirror pool at night, then carry them to Skingrad.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.o1.text: Slip into the Count's cellar at Skingrad and take the steward's key.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.o2.text: Reach the vault under Miscarcand and settle the Warden's debt.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.outro: The last warden fell silent and the plate of names lay in my hands. I could carry it to a priest, a vintner or a flame. What is owed to the dead is a hard thing to settle.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.pitch: Diggers at the cut-away stopped work when someone read a name aloud. They were paid in wine, not coin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_1_b.title: The Debt of Names (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.desc: A drowned-men's prayer at the Lunar Fang Docks speaks of a door that was only latched. It led me to a hidden sanctuary and a ruined city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.find: A dock lectern holds a salt-stained prayer-sheet to 'the ones the water kept', every line struck through but the last: 'Light the Candle when the tide is out. The door is only latched, not locked.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.o0.text: Break the inner coffin-room at the Cyrodiil Sanctuary and read the dead priest's letter.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.o1.text: Climb the Anvil lighthouse and ask who has been lighting it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The trail of the Ashen Candle ends at the crater edge where the Gate first opened.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.pitch: Fishermen at the Lunar Fang Docks light a single candle each low tide and will not say for whom.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_a.title: The Gate That Was Opened
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.desc: The trail of the Ashen Candle ends at the crater edge where the Gate first opened.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.o0.text: Wade the Hollow at low tide and carry its bone candle to Kvatch.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.o1.text: Dig through the north ward of Kvatch for the register of the night the Gate opened.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.o2.text: At the crater lip of Kvatch Gate, face the last keeper of the door.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.outro: At the crater lip I found the last candle still burning in a ring of lava glass. Whoever latched the door is long dead, but the debt they left is the city's to settle, not theirs.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.pitch: Fishermen at the Lunar Fang Docks light a single candle each low tide and will not say for whom.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_2_b.title: The Gate That Was Opened (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.desc: A clapperless bell in a priory orchard says seven bells keep a door shut and four are gone. It points to a statue on the Valus road.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.find: A bell without a clapper hangs from the priory orchard wall. Scratched on its rim: 'Seven bells keep the door shut. Four are missing. Ask the statue what it watches.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.o0.text: Read the line of the Sentinel's hand and follow it to Bruma.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.o1.text: Find the old Bruma chapel bell and carry its clapper up to the Cloud Ruler.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The missing bells led from Bruma to a cliff-top keep and a wizard's rock, and on to the old Akaviri fortress.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.pitch: A priory brother says the bell in the orchard rings once a night with no hand on it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_a.title: The Dragon-Hunters' Vigil
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.desc: The missing bells led from Bruma to a cliff-top keep and a wizard's rock, and on to the old Akaviri fortress.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.o0.text: Ask the Cloud Ruler archivist for the lowest ledger and follow it to the wizard's rock.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.o1.text: Take the Frostcrag bell from the storm-room, or persuade its keeper to part with it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.o2.text: Hang the seven bells in the deepest nave of Sancre Tor and face what answers.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.outro: I set the last bell in its cradle at Sancre Tor and the air, which had been humming for days, went still. Whatever sleeps beneath the barrow, it sleeps for now.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.pitch: A priory brother says the bell in the orchard rings once a night with no hand on it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_3_b.title: The Dragon-Hunters' Vigil (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.desc: An inn on a bridge pays a water-tax to something called the Ring. The same signature shows up in three cities.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.find: The innkeeper's accounts hang on a hook: a column headed 'water' where the bridge-inn pays more every season, in a hand that signs only 'by order of the Ring'.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.o0.text: Find the clerk's cipher in Chorrol's oak and read the sluice-list.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.o1.text: Lower a bucket in Cheydinhal's refugee well and read the gate-list on the stone.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The Ring's water runs under every great city and ends beneath the Imperial City itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.pitch: The innkeeper at the Imperial Bridge Inn says the river is falling, though it rained all week.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_a.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.desc: The Ring's water runs under every great city and ends beneath the Imperial City itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.o0.text: Cut the welded hatch under the Lucky Old Lady and follow the water upriver.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.o1.text: Open the sealed grate under the Waterfront and close the Ring.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.outro: Below the Waterfront the old reservoir lay black and still, ringed by sluice-gates stamped with a clerk's seal. I closed one. It was a start, and I left proof for the Palace.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.pitch: The innkeeper at the Imperial Bridge Inn says the river is falling, though it rained all week.
story.skycraft.q.lw_cyr_4_b.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.desc: A star-watcher's log insists that the second moon is rising late, and that the priests' almanac is a lie.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.find: A little academy's observation log, kept by a mage who has never been believed: 'Secunda late again, seven minutes. The priests' almanac says on time. One of us is lying to the moon.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.o0.text: Compare the new and old moon-marks and take the rubbing to Torval's priests.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.o1.text: Slip into the palace dome and copy the true almanac.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The drift of the moon leads through a capital, a ridge-top temple and a choir-tomb to a vault of blades that wake at moonrise.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.pitch: A mage at the Star Haven Adeptorium says the priests' almanac is wrong, and gets laughed at.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_a.title: The Late Moon
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.desc: The drift of the moon leads through a capital, a ridge-top temple and a choir-tomb to a vault of blades that wake at moonrise.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.o0.text: Take the key-wheel from Agamanus to the tuned rooms of the choir-tomb.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.o1.text: Fetch the tuning-fork from the lowest chamber of the Moon Singers' tomb.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.o2.text: Set the three keys at moonrise and quiet the waking blades.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.outro: I stood in the vault as Secunda rose seven minutes late and, one by one, the lunar blades woke. I set the three keys and slowed the waking. The Moon-Priests will have to admit the almanac is a story.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.pitch: A mage at the Star Haven Adeptorium says the priests' almanac is wrong, and gets laughed at.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_1_b.title: The Late Moon (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.desc: A burial mask in a roadhouse urn, with a receipt from the Baandari caravan stop.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.find: A funerary mask lies in an urn behind the roadhouse's second lantern, the mask's mouth stuffed with a receipt: 'Delivered, Baandari stop, one of nine. The priests ask no questions.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.o0.text: Take the mask-account to the moonstone-ring village at Hakoshae.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.o1.text: Take the circle-stone key from Hakoshae to Rimmen's cliff gate.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The masks' trail runs through the moonstone ring, the cliff city and its aqueduct to the lunar clock under the dead.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.pitch: A traveller at the Twin Moons says a faceless Khajiit walked past the lanterns last night and bowed.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_a.title: The Faceless of Rimmen
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.desc: The masks' trail runs through the moonstone ring, the cliff city and its aqueduct to the lunar clock under the dead.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.o0.text: Find the mask-carvers' ledger and the buyers' names.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.o1.text: Follow the smugglers' lead boxes through the aqueduct to the necropolis undergate.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.o2.text: Fill the niches of the lunar clock chamber with the masks you have gathered.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.outro: In the clock chamber I set the masks back, one by one, until the last faceless stopped. They did not thank me. They knelt, and their masks, for a moment, almost smiled.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.pitch: A traveller at the Twin Moons says a faceless Khajiit walked past the lanterns last night and bowed.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_2_b.title: The Faceless of Rimmen (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.desc: A sugar-jar that hums and tastes of iron, and a farmer's wife who slept three days.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.find: A sugar-jar at the boil-house is warm and humming. A farmer has written on its lid: 'Does not taste like the meadow. Tastes of iron. Asked my wife. She slept three days.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.o0.text: Follow the glowing ditch from the meadow to the hanging inn.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.o1.text: Take the sample vial from the Netch's cellar to the garden city of Corinthe.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The glow's source runs through a meadow, an inn and a garden city to a hall of colossal machines.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.pitch: The farmer at Tathara says this year's sugar glows too bright and tastes wrong.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_a.title: The Glow Beneath the Sugar
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.desc: The glow's source runs through a meadow, an inn and a garden city to a hall of colossal machines.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.o0.text: Take the herbalists' findings from Corinthe to the sugar port at Senchal.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.o1.text: Take the boil-house's colossus dust from Senchal back to its source.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.o2.text: Seal the colossus's chest and end the leak.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.outro: The colossus's chest was cracked and weeping a luminous oil. I sealed it and the glow in the meadow dimmed to a gentler moon-colour. The sugar will be less sweet. It will be safe.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.pitch: The farmer at Tathara says this year's sugar glows too bright and tastes wrong.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_3_b.title: The Glow Beneath the Sugar (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.desc: A blade-shard tied with a ribbon at the claw-gate fort, with orders to carry it to the hill.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.find: A fort gate-post is scored with a hundred small crosses, one for each oath. A blade-shard is jammed in the crack and tied with a ribbon: 'Carry to the hill. Don't ask whose.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.o0.text: Take the shard-wagon's ledger from Dune to the ruined plateau city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.o1.text: Gather the oath-hall's first shard and climb the hill of swords.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The shards lead from a caravan crossroads and a plateau city to a hill of blades and a bone-trough.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.pitch: A guard at the claw-gate says every caravan out of Orcrest carries one blade-shard, and no one asks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_a.title: The Oath-Forge
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.desc: The shards lead from a caravan crossroads and a plateau city to a hill of blades and a bone-trough.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.o0.text: Gather the hundred-oath shard from the hill and carry it to the dragon-scour.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.o1.text: Quench the hundred-oath blade in the dragon's ribs and decide who carries it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.outro: The blade quenched in the dragon's ribs and I held it for a breath before laying it back. A hundred oaths is too heavy for one hand. Someone had to carry the weight; I put it down in the bone.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.pitch: A guard at the claw-gate says every caravan out of Orcrest carries one blade-shard, and no one asks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_els_4_b.title: The Oath-Forge (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.desc: A sailor's skeleton at a landing of broken ships holds a rune-tablet: the ice will crack and a ship sleeps in a howe.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.find: A broken ship's ribs, and in the sand a dead sailor with a rune-tablet clutched in both hands: 'Ice cracks under the long halls. The captain's ship sleeps in the howe. Wake her before the thaw.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.o0.text: Take the captain's last page to the hold at Kjolvik.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.o1.text: Persuade the elders of Kjolvik and take the hold-token to the dragon mound.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The tablet's trail passes a shield-fort and the last long halls to a frozen dragon and a buried ship.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.pitch: The old hold at Kjolvik keeps hearing the ice speak at night.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_a.title: The Last Voyage Home
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.desc: The tablet's trail passes a shield-fort and the last long halls to a frozen dragon and a buried ship.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.o0.text: Bind the dragon's thaw with the cold shard and go on to the howe.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.o1.text: Speak the forgotten word before the wolf-jarl's ship and set her free.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.outro: The great ship shook the barrow's snow from her ribs and rose. Her ropes were rotten, her mast a frozen pole, but the hold's people climbed aboard, one by one, with their ancestors' shields.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.pitch: The old hold at Kjolvik keeps hearing the ice speak at night.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_1_b.title: The Last Voyage Home (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.desc: A watch-tower's border stone carries a fourfold seal, three quarters worn smooth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.find: A watch-tower's border stone carries a fourfold seal, three quarters worn smooth. On the fourth, a handful of Akaviri characters: 'Three bow. One waits in the ice.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.o0.text: Take the harbour's quarter from the dragon-prow and cross to the mountain village.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.o1.text: Take the lantern's quarter and climb to the serpent temple.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The seal's quarters are held across a harbour village, a mountain village and a serpent temple, ending at a valley of ribs and an ice throne.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.pitch: The watchmen at Tang Mo say the border stone has been rubbed away by pilgrims who pay no coin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_a.title: The Four-Court Seal
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.desc: The seal's quarters are held across a harbour village, a mountain village and a serpent temple, ending at a valley of ribs and an ice throne.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.o0.text: Barter or take the third quarter from the serpent temple.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.o1.text: Cross the valley of ribs with the three quarters and find the ice throne.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.o2.text: Join the four quarters on the throne and decide whether the valley stays shut.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.outro: I laid the fourth quarter against the other three and the valley of ribs, which had been groaning for a thousand years, fell quiet. The serpent-court will come, but not through that door.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.pitch: The watchmen at Tang Mo say the border stone has been rubbed away by pilgrims who pay no coin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_2_b.title: The Four-Court Seal (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.desc: A pen-keeper's totem sprouting pink coral, with a note that the pens are growing strangely.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.find: A pen-keeper's totem is hung with pink coral-shards that have started to take root in the wood. A scratch on its post: 'The pens are eating it. The pens are growing. Who feeds the pens?'
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.o0.text: Take the admiral's chart from the flagship and sail for the plague-coral sea.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The reef's walk leads past the shell-raft fleet and the coral tower of Thras to the sea-serpent citadel's window on the deep.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.pitch: The pen-keepers say the serpents have been eating something pink, and it has not agreed with them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_a.title: The Walking Reef
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.desc: The reef's walk leads past the shell-raft fleet and the coral tower of Thras to the sea-serpent citadel's window on the deep.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.o0.text: Reach the heart-chamber of the coral tower and take the seed.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.o1.text: Close the sea-gate against the reef and counsel the sleepless king.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.outro: At the citadel's window, the reef's great pink head lay pressed to the glass. I closed the sea-gate against it. For a week the fleet slept. Then, far below, the head turned, patient, to wait for the next tide.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.pitch: The pen-keepers say the serpents have been eating something pink, and it has not agreed with them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_3_b.title: The Walking Reef (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.desc: A training-post carved with four forms, the fourth to be taught on the water.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.find: A training-post is carved with four forms. Three have a student's name. The fourth reads only: 'The Last Lesson, taught on the water.' A master's sandal sits on the step.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.o0.text: Earn the second form's stone at the sunken dojo and go on to the serpent temple.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The lesson's next forms are in a sunken dojo and a serpent temple, and the last in a sunken temple of kings.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.pitch: A veteran at the Ra Gada camp says the fourth form has not been taught in living memory.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_a.title: The Last Lesson
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.desc: The lesson's next forms are in a sunken dojo and a serpent temple, and the last in a sunken temple of kings.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.o0.text: Dance the third form on the scales and bring the token to the sunken temple.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.o1.text: Row the funeral barge out through the sea-gate and finish the Last Lesson.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.outro: I rowed the funeral barge out of the sunken temple's flooded hall and through a gate of light. The kings did not speak. I think they were satisfied that someone, finally, had finished the lesson.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.pitch: A veteran at the Ra Gada camp says the fourth form has not been taught in living memory.
story.skycraft.q.lw_for_4_b.title: The Last Lesson (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.desc: A roadhouse tally-board lists wells owed and wells paid to someone called 'the Herald', and tells me to ask the goat.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.find: A roadhouse tally-board: caravans listed with a tithe column. At the bottom, in a dead man's hand: 'Water owed: thirty-one wells. Paid: nine. Ask the goat.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.o0.text: Open the older well under the goat statue and take the shaft-map to Sentinel.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.o1.text: Take the water-merchant's debt-roll from Sentinel's harbour warehouse.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.o2.text: Find the pump under Volenfell's sand and recover its stop-key.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The water-tithe trail crosses Sentinel's harbour and three desert tombs to the glass-roofed shaft of a lost city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.pitch: The Silver Pilgrim's keeper says the caravan masters all pay a tithe in water to a man nobody has met.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_a.title: The Thirst of the Buried City
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.desc: The water-tithe trail crosses Sentinel's harbour and three desert tombs to the glass-roofed shaft of a lost city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.o0.text: Take the herald's seal from the Motalion niche and carry it to the throne-hall.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.o1.text: Press the herald's seal to the decree and open the sand door.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.o2.text: Reach the great cistern of the lost city and settle the water-tithe.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.outro: The lost city's great cistern drank deep for a moment and then, slowly, began to give. In the far oases the wells rose a hand's breadth. The dune-king's herald is a shadow now, and the account is closed.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.pitch: The Silver Pilgrim's keeper says the caravan masters all pay a tithe in water to a man nobody has met.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_1_b.title: The Thirst of the Buried City (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.desc: A relief at the Valley of Scars shows a dozen travellers on a staircase, one of whom looks like me.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.find: A relief panel at the canyon mouth shows a scene half-carved: a dozen travellers on a staircase. The carving is fresh, and one of the faces looks very like yours.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.o0.text: Compare the Valley of Scars rubbing with Elinhir's blank constellation.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.o1.text: Steal the arena-master's schedule from Dragonstar and see which panels remain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The panel leads through a star-watchers' city, an arena and a sealed sphere to the stair of the spire.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.pitch: A guide says the wall at the canyon mouth is being carved by nobody.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_a.title: Reliefs That Remember Forward
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.desc: The panel leads through a star-watchers' city, an arena and a sealed sphere to the stair of the spire.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.o0.text: Open the archive's dusk seam and read the complete panel-roll.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.o1.text: Take the cult's key from the mirror-pool and climb the pinnacle.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.o2.text: Stand on the platform at dusk and decide what the last panel means.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.outro: At the top of the spire I stood on the last panel and understood it. It was not an ending but a stairway. I did not carve my own face; I stepped off it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.pitch: A guide says the wall at the canyon mouth is being carved by nobody.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_2_b.title: Reliefs That Remember Forward (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.desc: A shackle on a grave at Thrall Cove, with a note that a freedman's debts were bought rather than cancelled.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.find: A rusted shackle lies on a sand-grave at the old slaver's cove. Scratched on the stone: 'Paid for, not freed. Ask who buys the debts.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.o0.text: Trace the seed-jar manifest from Abah's Landing to Taneth.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.o1.text: Take the physician's unsigned certificates from Taneth to the lord's palace.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The debt-buyer's trail passes a palace and a walled bazaar and ends beneath a necropolis.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.pitch: A freedman at Thrall Cove says someone paid his debt and then asked him to plant a palm.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_a.title: The Gardener of Ahaleb
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.desc: The debt-buyer's trail passes a palace and a walled bazaar and ends beneath a necropolis.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.o0.text: Take the steward's ledger from the Hubalajad conservatory to the walled bazaar-city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.o1.text: Trace the palm-bloom tincture from Rihad's spice gate to its source.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.o2.text: Enter the hidden oasis chamber and wake the gardeners.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.outro: In the garden under the skylights the palms bent towards me. I carried out one seed and left the gardener's ledger where his heirs could find it. The dead have waited long enough.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.pitch: A freedman at Thrall Cove says someone paid his debt and then asked him to plant a palm.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_3_b.title: The Gardener of Ahaleb (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.desc: A hidden cabinet at the harbour gate holds a manifest for a ship that was never expected to return.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.find: A lever behind a harbour crate opens a small cabinet. Inside, a ship's manifest for a sailing in the fifth year: 'Cargo: sealed. Destination: not recorded. Return: not expected.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.o0.text: Take the shrine-token from Saintsport to the inn with the dragon's tail.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.o1.text: Win the lot at the Draggin Tale and take passage to the old harbour.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The ship's descendants gather at an inn with a dragon's tail over the door, and the cargo's trail ends at a ring of wind-carved arches.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.pitch: The port clerk says every fifth year a ship leaves with a sealed cargo and nobody asks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_a.title: The Sunken Clause
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.desc: The ship's descendants gather at an inn with a dragon's tail over the door, and the cargo's trail ends at a ring of wind-carved arches.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.o0.text: Read the sealed clause in the Stros M'Kai lighthouse and follow the fifth-year ship.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.o1.text: Open the niche in the great arch and take the torn page of the ledger.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.outro: The wind sang through the arches and the torn page lay in my hands, a map of tides with a missing corner. The fifth-year ship is no longer owed. Someone, somewhere, will have to fill the corner.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.pitch: The port clerk says every fifth year a ship leaves with a sealed cargo and nobody asks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_ham_4_b.title: The Sunken Clause (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.desc: A barge with only stone dust, chisels and a priest on its manifest sails from Aldhaven by night.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.find: The harbour-master's chain-log has a line where the same barge sails at night, three times a month, with a manifest that reads only 'stone dust, chisels, one priest'.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.o0.text: Take the mason's apron from the Glenpoint boat-shed to Wayrest.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.o1.text: Take the Quiet Chisel's payment list from Wayrest's archives.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.o2.text: Convince the Daggerfall scribe to part with his marginal genealogy.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The masons' trail crosses three crowns and a cursed crypt, and ends in the tomb of the lost kings.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.pitch: The chain-keeper at Aldhaven Harbor says the same barge leaves every ninth night, riding low and quiet.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_a.title: The Uncounted King
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.desc: The masons' trail crosses three crowns and a cursed crypt, and ends in the tomb of the lost kings.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.o0.text: Copy the half-erased inscription in the lower chapel of Camlorn's cathedral.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.o1.text: Break the plaster in the Cath Bedraud niche and read the buried name.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.o2.text: Reach the sealed eighth king-room before the master-mason finishes the wall.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.outro: The eighth king's name was almost gone, scraped to a ghost in the stone. I traced it in charcoal before the masons returned. What three crowns do with it is theirs to decide.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.pitch: The chain-keeper at Aldhaven Harbor says the same barge leaves every ninth night, riding low and quiet.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_1_b.title: The Uncounted King (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.desc: A perfumed invitation on the table of a one-lamp inn says to leave your lantern behind.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.find: A cream-coloured card lies on the inn's single table, perfumed with plum. 'You are cordially invited. Dress as you were when you were happiest. Do not bring your lantern.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.o0.text: Take the shrine's candle-end ward to the fog-bound port of Northpoint.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.o1.text: Take the silver bell from the Northpoint harbour-master toward Shornhelm.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The guest-list led from a hamlet shrine and a fog-bound port to a black spire and on to the party itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.pitch: The innkeeper says every guest who stayed the night is gone, and leaves a card on the table.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_a.title: Cream-Coloured Invitations
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.desc: The guest-list led from a hamlet shrine and a fog-bound port to a black spire and on to the party itself.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.o0.text: Take the plum-ink guest-book from the Shornhelm keep's cellars.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.o1.text: Take the necromancer's second ledger and find the Host's door.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.o2.text: Enter the demesne and decline the Host's final invitation.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.outro: The hall was warm, music still playing, the table laid. No one asked me to leave. It was the hardest door I have ever closed behind me.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.pitch: The innkeeper says every guest who stayed the night is gone, and leaves a card on the table.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_2_b.title: Cream-Coloured Invitations (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.desc: A name has been carved at the stronghold gate with a date nine days ahead.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.find: A freshly chiselled name stands at the foot of the palisade, with a date nine days ahead. Below, in Orcish letters: 'Carved by no hand.' The stronghold's smith has covered it with a hide.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.o0.text: Take the rubbing of the newest names to the broken ridge of the Wrothgarian peaks.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.o1.text: Follow the wrong-way shadow down to the rebuilt city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The column's unseen carver leads through the broken ridge and the rebuilt city to the first city's cold forge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.pitch: The smith at the Morkul stronghold keeps a hide over a stone that gets a new name each dusk.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_a.title: Names Before Death
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.desc: The column's unseen carver leads through the broken ridge and the rebuilt city to the first city's cold forge.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.o0.text: Find the sealed door below Orsinium's forge-pits and descend.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.o1.text: Stand at the anvil in Old Orsinium and take the hammer from the smith-spirit.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.outro: The forge-spirit stilled its hammer as I broke the last unlit name on the anvil. I do not know whether it will begin again, but the names on the column are, for now, only names.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.pitch: The smith at the Morkul stronghold keeps a hide over a stone that gets a new name each dusk.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_3_b.title: Names Before Death (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.desc: A fisherman's totem says the tide is wrong because a giant has begun to drink again.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.find: A fisherman's totem at the lighthouse base has been wired with a small brass drip-cup. Scratched on it: 'The tide is wrong. The giant is drinking again. Ask Evermor.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.o0.text: Taste the giant's tears and follow the water toward the lake city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.o1.text: Take the engineer's flooding survey from Evermor to the ring of towers on Balfiera.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The giant's thirst runs from a lake city and a ring of towers to a Dwemer pump and the old Direnni seat.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.pitch: Koeglin fishermen say their nets come up full of salt water where there is no sea.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_a.title: The Giant That Drinks
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.desc: The giant's thirst runs from a lake city and a ring of towers to a Dwemer pump and the old Direnni seat.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.o0.text: Take the key-bar from the lock tower on Balfiera to the Dwemer bastion at Mthartzel.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.o1.text: Reach the pump hall at Mthartzel and silence the Keeper.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.o2.text: Climb to the lens room and meet the last Direnni heir.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.outro: The pump fell silent and the great stone chest of the giant sighed one last time. In the bay, the ring of towers on Balfiera slowly lifted toward the sun.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.pitch: Koeglin fishermen say their nets come up full of salt water where there is no sea.
story.skycraft.q.lw_hr_4_b.title: The Giant That Drinks (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.desc: An empty grave and a pair of slippers in Khuul. The ash around them has pressed a path uphill.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.find: A fresh grave on the cliff stair is empty. Slippers lie beside it, ash on their soles, and a child's chalk map pins down a route up the mountain with one word: 'Sleeping'.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.o0.text: Take the Ald Velothi night-watch roster to the Urshilaku wise woman.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.o1.text: Take the wise woman's dream-lantern to the thinning in the ghostfence.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.o2.text: Pass through the person-shaped gap in the ghostfence and find the sanctum behind it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The path of the sleepers crosses the ghostfence and ends in a ruined fortress at the foot of the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.pitch: In Khuul they say someone walks up the cliff stairs every night, asleep, and no one will wake them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_a.title: The Sleepers of the Ashlands
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.desc: The path of the sleepers crosses the ghostfence and ends in a ruined fortress at the foot of the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.o0.text: Descend Missamsi and take the dream-crystal from the cultists' sleeping hall.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.o1.text: Take the performer's mask from the Kogoruhn stage and climb the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.o2.text: Sit in the dreamer's seat and face the ash's audience.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.outro: At the crater lip the ash lay in rows like beds. I lit the dream-lantern and the sleepers on the slope turned, one by one, and began to walk down.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.pitch: In Khuul they say someone walks up the cliff stairs every night, asleep, and no one will wake them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_1_b.title: The Sleepers of the Ashlands (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.desc: A pier ledger at Seyda Neen counts pilgrims landed against pilgrims left. The gap grows each month.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.find: A customs ledger on the pier has one column crossed out: 'Pilgrims Landed' and 'Pilgrims Left'. The difference is circled in red every month, and written beneath: 'Where do they sleep?'
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.o0.text: Follow the chalk crescents out of Pelagiad to the old shrine fields.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.o1.text: Take a pilgrim's token from the Kummu shrines to Ald Sotha's sunken door.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.o2.text: Use the Kummu token at Ald Sotha and follow the underwater stair toward Vivec.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The missing pilgrims trail through shrines and an Imperial fortress to the six cantons of Vivec, and the seventh below them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.pitch: The customs clerk at Seyda Neen says more pilgrims land than ever sail home.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_a.title: The Seventh Canton
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.desc: The missing pilgrims trail through shrines and an Imperial fortress to the six cantons of Vivec, and the seventh below them.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.o0.text: Climb the pilgrims' ladder to the sealed door and read its wax seal.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.o1.text: Take the 'seventh quiet' stipend ledger from the Ebonheart factor's cellar.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.o2.text: Enter the quiet canton under Vivec and face its keepers.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.outro: I walked out of the quiet canton at dawn with a roll of names the Temple had filed and forgotten. The Archcanon's clerks asked me politely to hand it back. I have not decided.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.pitch: The customs clerk at Seyda Neen says more pilgrims land than ever sail home.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_2_b.title: The Seventh Canton (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.desc: Fishermen at Hla Oad are hauling up brass cogs stamped with a thumb, and selling them all to one buyer.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.find: A fishing urn at the smoke-racks is full of tiny brass cogs, each stamped with the same little hand. A note says: 'Same buyer. Pays double for the ones with the thumb-print.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.o0.text: Carry the courier's token from Gnaar Mok to the collector's cellar in Balmora.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.o1.text: Break into the Balmora cellar and take the Attendant's missing spring.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The buyer, the spire and the old fabrication floor are all building the same machine.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.pitch: Smoke-rack fishers at Hla Oad say a trader pays triple for brass cogs, as long as they carry a thumb-print.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_a.title: The Guest of Brass
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.desc: The buyer, the spire and the old fabrication floor are all building the same machine.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.o0.text: Reach the vent-chamber of Rkuldumz Spire and take the tuning rod.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.o1.text: Cross the Halls of Fabrication to the forge-pit and recover the thumb-mould.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.o2.text: Reach the centrifuge chamber and answer the Attendant's question.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.outro: The brass guest knelt in the centrifuge hall and asked me, in a voice like struck copper, whether its makers had been seen. I told it the truth. It asked me to stay a while.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.pitch: Smoke-rack fishers at Hla Oad say a trader pays triple for brass cogs, as long as they carry a thumb-print.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_3_b.title: The Guest of Brass (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.desc: A Telvanni tower's servants keep bequests dated after the heirs died, signed by ancestors.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.find: A servant's lectern in the tower hall has a stack of bequests, all dated after the heirs' deaths, all signed by ancestors. Beneath: 'To the quiet vote, with respect. Seat unfilled.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.o0.text: Recover a seat-plaque from the Molag Mar grotto and take it to the holy tomb city of Necrom.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.o1.text: Slip into Necrom's tomb-house cellars and take the minute-book.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.o2.text: Intercept the shadow-secretary's ballot at midnight and read it.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The dead's votes lead from Necrom's tombs through the great houses to the lightless streets under Mournhold.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.pitch: A servant at Tel Branora whispers that the old masters are still signing documents.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_a.title: The Council of the Quiet
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.desc: The dead's votes lead from Necrom's tombs through the great houses to the lightless streets under Mournhold.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.o0.text: Sit in the Ald'ruhn warm seat's place and take its summons.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.o1.text: Open the plaza grating in Mournhold and descend to the lightless city.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.o2.text: Enter the mirror-hall and face the Speaker of the Quiet Vote.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.outro: The mirror-hall was silent when I left it, the long table still set for forty. I carried the minutes up to the daylight. The living will have to decide what to do with a dead majority.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.pitch: A servant at Tel Branora whispers that the old masters are still signing documents.
story.skycraft.q.lw_mor_4_b.title: The Council of the Quiet (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.desc: An empty seed-jar at a farm in the ash names two other pieces of a map. One is in Raven Rock, the other in a spiral grove.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.find: An old seed-jar in the yam shed holds nothing but a label in a careful Imperial hand: 'Third of three. The other two lie with Raven Rock's ledger and the grove that grows in spirals.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.o0.text: Recover the cornerstone's second map-piece in Raven Rock.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.o1.text: Follow the spiral bearing of Brodir Grove north through the Frostmoth ruins.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.o2.text: Open the sealed crates in Fort Frostmoth's cellar and take the greenhouse key.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The map's three parts point to a sealed cellar in the Nordic temple under the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.pitch: The yam farmer at Old Attius Farm keeps a jar that is labelled 'third of three'.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_a.title: The Last Seed-Bank
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.desc: The map's three parts point to a sealed cellar in the Nordic temple under the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.o0.text: Take the surveyor's key from the Ashfallow wizard.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.o1.text: Ask the Tel Mithryn master for his workbook and the route to the old temple.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.o2.text: Open the cellar of the lowest nave and face the warden of the green.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.outro: The cellar was cold and dry, its shelves lined with sealed jars, each labelled in a careful hand. I carried one out. In a year, the island may not need to eat ash.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.pitch: The yam farmer at Old Attius Farm keeps a jar that is labelled 'third of three'.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_1_b.title: The Last Seed-Bank (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.desc: A hunter's flute and a note at the lodge door say five of the island's stones answer and one does not.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.find: A hunter's cloak is spread across the lodge porch with a bone flute tucked in its folds. A scratch on the rail: 'Five answer. One does not. I have gone to ask it why.'
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.o0.text: Play the flute at the Hvitkald cairn and head for the stalhrim basin.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.o1.text: Harmonise the flute with the stalhrim and find the water stone in the west.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.o2.text: Play the flute at the water stone and bring its note back to the Skaal circle.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.outro: One thread of the trail ends here and the next begins. The five stones' songs lead to the Skaal's circle and a sealed barrow where the sixth waits.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.pitch: A Skaal hunter's door hangs open and the larder is untouched.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_a.title: Six Stones, Five Songs
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.desc: The five stones' songs lead to the Skaal's circle and a sealed barrow where the sixth waits.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.o0.text: Confront the Skaal elder and learn the sixth verse's first line.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.o1.text: Take the rubbing of the defaced post to the barrow by the east shore.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.o2.text: Sing the sixth verse before the barrow mural and free the hunter.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.outro: In the barrow, the mural sang its missing verse through my flute and the sixth stone woke, far away, with a sound like a kettle boiling over. The Skaal elder will have to be told, and will not thank me.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.pitch: A Skaal hunter's door hangs open and the larder is untouched.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_2_b.title: Six Stones, Five Songs (II)
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_3_a.desc: A trader's stove-lid carries a stamp and a drawer of bone charts, the last of four sets that belonged to a lost ship.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_3_a.find: A stove-lid in the trader's shed is stamped with a ship's-wheel and the words 'Chart Four of Four'. A lever behind it opens a drawer of oiled bone charts.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_3_a.o0.text: Take Chart Three from the reavers' table and find the wreck on the north shore.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_3_a.o1.text: Pry open the wreck's bow-chest for Chart Two.
story.skycraft.q.lw_sol_3_a.o2.text: Hear the skald's wrong verse and take Chart One from behind the trophy shield.
