story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.o3.topic: The honest ledger. Jelu's debt, repaid four times.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.offer: Do you believe a person can be owned? I do not. I have been told I am wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.outro: Jelu poled her own boat out of the counting-house canal that evening, and did not look back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.pitch: My cousin Jelu poled a debt-boat for a rice merchant three years. The debt was forty drakes. She has paid it four times over and the ledger shows it as forty and rising. The merchant says it is the interest. I say it is a trap with a very good accountant. Free her. I do not mind how.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_debt.title: A Boat Owed
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.desc: The botanist paid. Now someone wants to know how the Hist sapling died in the glass.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.reply: It sits in a glass box on my desk. It does not hum. It faces the window. I have, quite unreasonably, begun to talk to it. I need you to take it back before I lose my professional distance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.text: Meet the botanist at the Legion customs house
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o0.topic: The botanist has the sapling. Is it well?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.o1.text: Carry the sapling back to the Pool with Boatwife Mudtoe
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.outro: The sapling went back to the Pool, humming faintly. The money was not returned.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_glass.title: The Glass Box
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.desc: The reeds beyond the Dripping Reed whisper at night. Wet-Whiskers thinks a drowned man is asking the way home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o0.journa: The whisper said: "East. Left. East. The long way. Is the tide in? East." It repeated all night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o0.text: Listen to the reed-bank at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o1.journa: At the end of the route, a small pier and a tidy house. A widow on the pier looked at me as if she had been expecting me for a year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o1.text: Follow the whispered route to Alten Meerhleel
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.reply: Then we shall send word. A lantern in the window of the reed-bank, lit every night. He will see it. He will go home. Thank you. I think I shall sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.text: Tell Wet-Whiskers where he wanted to go
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.o2.topic: He was lost. He wanted to go home to Alten Meerhleel. His wife is still waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.offer: Do you sleep? I do not. The reeds are talking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.outro: The reeds no longer whisper. A lantern burns in the bank each night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.pitch: The reed-bank beyond the inn whispers at night. Not a wind-whisper. Words. The guests complain, and I cannot sleep for wondering what they say. A man drowned there last season. I think he is still asking his way home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_reed.title: Reeds That Whisper
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.desc: The sapling is planted. The Hist asks one more thing, in a voice only the Keeper can hear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.reply: It asks for a story. Not a prayer. A story, told by someone who has never heard the Hist before. Go to the Dripping Reed and ask Wet-Whiskers for the oldest tale the inn knows. Bring it back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.text: Ask the Keeper what the Hist wants
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o0.topic: The sapling is in the Pool. What does it ask?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.reply: That is the tale of the first boat. Nobody knows who built it. It floats on every canal on the same night once a year. Tell the Keeper the boat never sinks. Tell her it never lands. That is the whole tale.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.text: Ask Wet-Whiskers for the oldest tale
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.o1.topic: The Hist wants the oldest tale in your inn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.outro: The Pool took the tale and was quiet. In the morning, a new leaf had opened.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_sing.title: The Pool Remembers
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.desc: Trader Ocheeva is nine crates of wine short. She suspects the harbour pilot, a Tribune's cousin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.reply: A man with a Cyrodiilic accent and a Legion belt, in a boat with a hidden floor. He sells by the bottle at the Fourth Canal Steps at dusk. I did not tell you that. I did not tell you anything, and the price of not telling is six drakes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.text: Ask Sap-Fence Ruu who sold wine on the canals
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o0.topic: Nine crates of red. Who bought?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o1.text: Catch the pilot at the Fourth Canal Steps at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c0.lab: Let him pay it back quietly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c0.rep: Then it is quiet. It is also fair, which surprises me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c1.lab: Make an example. A public count.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.c1.rep: He will stand at the wharf with a sign. It is humiliating. It is also effective. I did not have the nerve myself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.reply: My cousin. Of course. A Legion belt on a rogue is the worst of all disguises. I shall see he pays Ocheeva back, in kind and in coin, and spends a week counting rice on the south wharf. Thank you for not making a scene.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.text: Tell Tribune Varro about his cousin
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.o2.topic: Your cousin's been selling the Trader's wine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.offer: You look like you can count bottles and not drink them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.outro: Ocheeva counted forty crates, and sold nine of them at a discount to the man who found them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.pitch: Forty crates of Cyrodiilic red landed at my pier three days ago. Forty crates were delivered to my cellar. In my cellar I count thirty-one. Nine crates have gone for a swim, or a walk, or a sale. I think the pilot, Tribune Varro's cousin, has been 'inspecting' them. Please be gentle. He is a Tribune's cousin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_lm_wine.title: The Thirsty Bottles
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.desc: Rice-Mother Mussa has a croak under the north paddy and sallow rice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o0.journ: At midnight, a bubble rose, and then a head: a bullfrog the size of a washtub, wearing the green-gold collar of a drowned noble. It croaked, regarded me with grave dignity, and sank.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o0.text: Watch the north paddy at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o1.text: Drive the toad-thing from the paddy
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.reply: A noble's collar. How very Cyrodiilic. I shall hang it on the scarecrow, as a warning. Thank you. Eat. You are still too thin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.text: Tell Mussa the paddy is clear
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.o2.topic: The croak was a bullfrog in a noble's collar. It is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.offer: Something croaks under the paddy at night. Not a frog. A frog has a cheerful croak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.outro: The north paddy greened by the next moon, and the scarecrow wore a collar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.pitch: The rice grows sallow in the north paddy. By night the water bubbles, and a low croak comes from the mud. A frog, say the children. A drowned man, say the old. I say a drainage problem, and I am a practical woman, but I cannot sleep for it. Look under the paddy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_croak.title: The Croak Beneath the Paddy
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.desc: Hunter Teek communicates, wordlessly, that the egg-nests of Murkmire have been raided three nights running.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o0.journa: At dusk, three shapes came out of the reeds: not thieves. Hatchlings, thin and fast, no larger than a hand, hungry enough to take eggs. They took one each and left the rest. They were not greedy. They were starving.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o1.text: Drive off the true raider, a marsh predator that has been driving the hatchlings from their feeding-grounds
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.reply: Then they will eat from the paddy, and no one shall begrudge them. I shall set out a bowl at dusk. The hatchlings will take it. You will not tell the elder. She will tell me she knew.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.text: Tell Rice-Mother Mussa the hatchlings are fed
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.o2.topic: The hatchlings were hungry. The bully is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.offer: ...(Teek holds up three fingers, then points at the reeds.)
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.outro: A bowl is set out at the village edge each dusk. It is always empty by dawn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.pitch: Teek says nothing. Teek holds up three fingers, then a clutch of eggs, then an empty basket. The nests at the edge of the village have been raided three nights running. Teek does not believe in thieves. Teek believes in hunger. Teek would like you to look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_eggs.title: Hungry Hatchlings
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.desc: Elder Nulaa invites you to walk the Spiral Path of Murkmire in silence.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o0.jour: The path wound three times about the middle. A frog watched me from a reed. Somewhere ahead, a fire crackled, and the mist smelled of cedar and rain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o0.text: Walk the spiral to its centre and hold your tongue
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.c0.r: Then you have answered. Take the coal. Walk it out, and do not drop it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.repl: Three questions. The first: what do you carry? The second: what do you leave? The third: where is your door? You need not answer aloud. You need only know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o1.text: Answer three questions from the elder at the centre
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o2.jour: The coal was warm as a held hand and did not once flicker. Halfway out I passed a child sitting at the path's edge, who looked at me, and at the coal, and smiled, and said nothing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o2.text: Carry the coal back out along the path
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o3.jour: I lit it. The coal went out with a sigh, and the fire it began burned a long time, and kept my hands warm. The mist closed around it like a hand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.o3.text: Light a fire at your own door
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.offer: You are not from the mire. Good. The path does not mind.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.outro: The mire kept your fire. You may find it again, if you stop looking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.pitch: Every child of the mire walks the spiral once. It is not a trial, it is a listening. You do not speak. You walk it, to the middle, where my fire burns. Then you carry a coal back along the path to your own door and light your own fire from it. Tell no one what the fire says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_mm_spiral.title: The Spiral Path
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.desc: Warden Scales-Her-Chains reports the north ziggurat's sleeping idol gone. Both hills blame each other.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o0.jour: The bridge swayed. Halfway across, a scrap of grey cloth snagged on the rail. A thief with a poor sense of balance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o0.text: Cross the bridge between the two ziggurats
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.repl: Four hundred and twelve ounces, a hair under. A thief would need a sling, not a pocket. Gorge-Eel uses a sling. He is a river man gone wrong. He sleeps in the gorge-caves under the south hill. Here: this is his cord. He tied it at the last job.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.text: Ask Stone-Carver Nook about the idol
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o1.topi: The idol is gone. Who knew its weight?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o2.jour: Footprints, a dragged sling, a dropped bandage. The ruins gaped, and in the middle of them sat a man with a stolen idol, rocking it like a child.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o2.text: Chase the thief down the gorge to the old ruins
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c0.l: Return it to the north hill's ziggurat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c0.r: Then the north hill sleeps well. The south hill will grumble. It is the order of things.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c1.l: Place it on the bridge, between the hills.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.c1.r: A bold thing. The bridge will have a god in the middle. Both hills will argue over whose it is. That is an improvement.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.repl: The idol is whole. One eye is open. The carver says it was always so; I say it is a new thing, and the south hill carved it. I do not know which of us is right. I could return it to the north hill's ziggurat, as the law says. Or I could place it on the bridge itself, between them, so that neither owns it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.text: Return the idol to Warden Scales
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.o5.topi: The idol, whole. The thief, down. What now?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.offer: You walk like someone who has never looked down. Good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.outro: The bridge held. The idol slept. One of its eyes was open, and nobody mentioned it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.pitch: The idol that sleeps in the north ziggurat was gone this morning. Not stolen, I think; borrowed, which in Stormhold is worse. Both hills blame the other. There is a bridge between them, and the thief used it. I want it back before the dusk bell, before the south hill hears and the north hill answers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_bridge.title: The Bridge Between
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.desc: Scout Fast-Eyes watched twelve people enter the White Rose prison dock and eleven leave.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o0.journa: A single lantern in a barred window. A prisoner, an old Argonian, writing on the wall with a splinter. The guards had been told to leave him a lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o0.text: Go to the old White Rose prison dock
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.reply: An elder who was convicted of a crime he did not commit, twelve years ago, and has been waiting for someone to ask. He does not wish to leave. He wishes to be asked. Go and ask him. Gently.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.text: Ask Warden Scales who the twelfth is
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o1.topic: Who is the twelfth in the White Rose?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.reply: Then I have seen it and never asked. A tenth of what I see, and the rest I carry. Thank you. I shall take him a pipe, and a witness.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.text: Tell Fast-Eyes what the twelfth wants
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.o2.topic: The twelfth wants to be asked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.offer: I saw something. I will tell you a tenth. That is a lot, for me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.outro: The old elder left the prison on the arm of a scout who had never before said more than a tenth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.pitch: From the south tower at dawn I saw a boat on the river carrying twelve people and putting in at the old White Rose prison dock. Twelve went in. Eleven came out. The twelfth did not. I am a scout, not a judge. Go and see. Tell me what the twelfth is doing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_eyes.title: A Tenth of What I See
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.desc: Stone-Carver Nook wants to know whether a block carved on the south hill was a gift or a theft.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.reply: A third party. A Hlaalu merchant with a rope-rig and a bill of lading nobody read. He sold it to both hills at the same price, on the same day, and left on the evening boat. I did not tell you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.text: Ask Pebble-Pocket who sold the block
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o0.topic: A block of north-hill stone ended up on the south hill. Who sold it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o1.journ: A rope-rig, a bill of lading, and a single ledger page with two names and one price. The merchant had sold the same stone twice, to two sides, and was long gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o1.text: Find the Hlaalu merchant's rope-rig below the south hill
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.reply: Both hills paid. Neither is owed. Then it is neither's stone. I shall carve it in half, and set each half on a hill, with a single seam that matches. Let them argue over the seam.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.text: Tell Nook the block has two buyers
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.o2.topic: Both hills paid for it. The merchant is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.offer: Have you ever felt a stone argue with you?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.outro: The seam is visible from both ziggurats, and neither hill will admit to looking at it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.pitch: A block was delivered to the south ziggurat from the north hill quarry, and the south hill has been carving it for a week. It is marked for the north. A mistake, or a theft, or a provocation. The mason on the south side says it is a gift. The north says it is a bribe. I say: I just carve what I am handed. Find out which.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sh_stone.title: Stone for the Wrong Hill
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.desc: Barge-Mother Seeth cannot row tonight. She needs you to carry a drowned man's urn to the Isle of Tombs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o0.reply: The lantern keeps the way. Do not let it go out. If it goes out, the passenger will wake, and ask where he is, and you must answer honestly. Take the urn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o0.text: Take the urn and the lantern
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o1.journ: The lilies were white, and then pale grey, and then blue in the lantern-light. A fish with eyes like lamps followed me for a while and then turned away.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o1.text: Row through the lily canals at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o2.text: Drive off the drowned dead that rise to board the barge
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o3.journ: The isle was a hill of white stone in black water. A single door, open, with a candle beside it. A priest waited there, patiently, and did not speak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o3.text: Bring the barge to the Isle of Tombs
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.c0.la: "You are at the Isle of Tombs. You are not alone."
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.c0.re: A good thing to say. He heard it. They always hear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.c1.la: Say nothing, and leave the lantern burning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.c1.re: Also a good thing. Some prefer quiet. The lantern will burn a year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.reply: Then we are his family, for as long as it takes. Tell him where he is. Out loud. It helps.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.text: Hand the passenger to Priest Eesh
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.o4.topic: I have brought him. He has no family.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.offer: You have a steady hand. My oar-hand is going. Will you steer?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.outro: The barge went home in the dark. The lilies on the far bed bloomed white that morning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.pitch: I carry one dead a night to the Isle of Tombs, and tonight I cannot. My arm will not hold the oar. The passenger is a young man, drowned, no family. He should not go alone. Board at dusk, row through the lily canals, and bury him on the isle. The canal is not empty at night. Bring a blade, and a good song.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_barge.title: The Last Barge
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.desc: Lily-Tender Pi has a bed that will not bloom. The kin say they are only waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o0.reply: The Teeb family. Their daughter went into the marsh to find a cure and never came back. They have kept her lantern lit for three years in the window. They will not bury what they have not lost. The lilies are waiting with them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o0.text: Ask Gaar the Lantern-Seller about the family
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o0.topic: A lily bed that will not bloom. Whose?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o1.journa: A tent, a pot of dried herbs, a journal. The daughter had found the cure and been bitten before she could carry it home. She had died a year ago, writing to the end, and her last line was: "Tell them I was not afraid."
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o1.text: Search the Green-Eye ruins for the Teeb daughter
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o2.reply: Then they will bury her, and the bed will bloom. White, I think. White for the quiet. I shall plant the first bulb myself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o2.text: Take the journal to the Teeb family
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.o2.topic: I found her. She was not afraid.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.offer: Do you know lilies? Do you know sorrow?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.outro: The Teeb bed bloomed white that spring, for the first time in three years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.pitch: One bed will not bloom. The same family, the same bed, three years. White for the quiet, red for the angry, and nothing for these. Not black either. Nothing. I have asked their living kin and they say they are not angry and they are not quiet. They are only waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_lily.title: The Lily That Would Not Bloom
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.desc: Mourner Kess-Ta wishes to see her brother's stone on the Isle of Tombs, but the living may not cross.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o0.rep: The rule forbids the crossing. It does not forbid the seeing. There is a lamp-post at the lagoon's edge, and from it the isle's third stone is visible on a clear night. It is his. Walk her there at dusk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o0.tex: Ask Priest Eesh whether there is a way
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o0.top: A living mourner wants to see her brother's stone. The rule forbids it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o1.tex: Walk Kess-Ta to the lamp-post at the lagoon's edge
"He is not. The priest tells them where they are."
Then he knows. That is enough. I will sleep tonight.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o2.rep: I see it. It is smaller than I thought. It is white, like a lily. Thank you. I can go home now. I shall tell Mother he is not alone. He is not, is he?
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.o2.tex: Stand with Kess-Ta while she sees the stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.offer: Are you a priest? A barge-hand? No? Then perhaps you can help.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.outro: Kess-Ta left Soulrest at dawn, lighter than she came.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.pitch: My brother lies on the isle and I have not seen his stone. The rule says the living may not cross; the barge-mother will not break it and I will not ask her to. But the rule says nothing of a lantern, or a letter, or a living person walked to the edge of the water. Speak to Priest Eesh. Find a way that is not a break.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_sr_mourner.title: The Living May Not Cross
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.desc: Hist-Keeper Eeka invites you to the sap rite: cut, carry and drink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o0.reply: Then take the blade. Do not hold it by the edge. Do not speak while the tree listens. Walk to the third root and make the cut where the bark is soft as a cheek. If the tree sighs, stop, and wait.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o1.journa: The bark gave under the blade like a held breath. A bead of gold rose and ran down the groove. Somewhere above me, something very large shifted in its sleep, and did not wake.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o1.text: Cut a sap-line at the third root without waking the tree
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o2.journa: The roots swayed. The sap was warm in my hand. Halfway across, a pair of eyes opened in the bark beside me. They did not blink. They did not need to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o2.text: Carry the sap across the rope-roots in the dark
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o3.journa: I drank. The pool rippled. In it I saw myself, and behind myself a green hall without walls, and in the hall a long table with one chair pulled out. I did not sit. I think that was the right answer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o3.text: Drink the sap at the pool at the base of the tree
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o4.c0.rep: Then it is yours. Go gently, hatchling of nowhere.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.o4.reply: Then the Hist has looked at you, and you at it. That is all the rite is. Take this. It is not a reward; it is a cup. Drink from it only when you are tired, and mind what you see.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.offer: You have never drunk sap. I can see it in your eyes. Good. It is better so.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.outro: The vision did not fade. It simply learned to wait.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.pitch: Every hatchling of Thorn drinks once from the Hist, at the year's turning, and sees what it will. It is not a test; it is a mirror. You are not of Thorn, but the Hist has asked for you. Take the blade. Cut a line without waking the tree. Carry the sap across the root-walks in the dark. Drink at the pool at the base. Tell me what you see. No. Do not tell me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_rite.title: The Sap Rite
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.desc: Three hatchlings are stranded on a mat of roots after a root-walk collapse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.o0.reply: Forty fathoms, soaked in pitch and good for a drop. Tie it round your waist, not your neck. Trust me. I have tried both.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.o0.text: Borrow a rope from Sap-Cutter Horu
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.o1.journ: Three small shapes sat in a circle on a bobbing raft of roots, passing a single reed-pipe between them. They looked up and did not seem frightened. One of them waved.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.o1.text: Reach the stranded mat by the broken root-walk
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.o2.text: Guide the hatchlings back across the roots
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.offer: You have two feet and a sense of humour. You will need both.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.outro: The three hatchlings were returned. The Hist, they said, had not wanted them. It had only been listening.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.pitch: A root-walk collapsed last week. Three hatchlings are cut off on a floating mat of roots in the dark pool, and the Keepers will not send a boat; they say the Hist wants them there. I say the Hist is not a mother. Bring a rope and a boat and a stubborn heart.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_roots.title: Where Roots Cross
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.desc: Sap-Cutter Horu hears something chewing in the third root of the great Hist tree.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.o0.journ: The bark was warm and trembling. Under my palm, something very small and very patient was gnawing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.o0.text: Listen at the third root with your hand on the bark
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.o1.text: Clear the grove-vermin that nest in the bark
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.o2.reply: Then the tree sleeps easy, and the sap runs clear. It has asked me to thank you. It does not say so in words. It hums a different note. You will hear it, if you stay.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.o2.text: Tell Hist-Keeper Eeka the tree is clear
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.offer: Do you hear it? Something in the third root is chewing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.outro: The sap ran clear that night. The root-walks stopped shivering.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.pitch: A cut is a conversation; but something else is talking to the tree through its teeth. The sap has run bitter since Sundas, and the root-walks shiver at night. I have listened with my hand on the bark. It is not the tree that is sick. It is what has nested in it. Kill it before the tree wakes in pain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_bm_th_tooth.title: The Tree Has a Toothache
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_after_confess: Harbourmaster Teodor Arenius walked to the Legion himself. Marga the Net-Mender has news.

He walked up the quay at noon with the tally book under his arm, and gave it to the Legion captain himself. They kept him in the cells for a month and let him out on a bond. He is the Keeper's assistant now, trimming wicks. I do not forgive him. I do not need to. He climbs the stair every dusk, and the lamp has not gone dim since. Take this. It is my best net-needle.
Hear from Marga what became of the Harbourmaster
Teodor confessed. What happened to him?
Teodor Arenius trims the wicks of the Anvil lighthouse under the Keeper's eye. Nobody in the harbour has forgiven him, and nobody sleeps badly.
Harbourmaster Teodor Arenius walked to the Legion himself. Marga the Net-Mender has news.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_after_shielde: You kept the wreckers' book from the Legion. Harbourmaster Teodor Arenius says he owes you.

I do. A man like me does not forget. Here is a harbour pass: it opens every gate on the quay, at any hour, and no tally will record it. I wish I could give you more. I wish I could give my brother what he is owed. Instead I give you a key. Use it well. And if you ever see a lamp go dim in Anvil, you will know whose fault it is.
You said you owed me a debt.
The Harbourmaster of Anvil has paid his debt in a pass and a promise. The beacon burns, and the tally book is ash, and nobody has asked.
You kept the wreckers' book from the Legion. Harbourmaster Teodor Arenius says he owes you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.desc: Marga the Net-Mender believes Anvil's lighthouse lamp is being dimmed on purpose, to wreck ships on moonless nights. She wants someone to climb the stair and look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o0.tex: Climb Anvil Lighthouse to the lamp room
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o1.jou: The shutter was not an accident of soot. Someone had hinged it, oiled it and fitted a pull-cord that ran down the outside wall. Whoever dimmed the lamp did not need to climb the stair at all.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o1.tex: Examine the lamp and recover the blackened lens shutter
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o2.rep: A cord. I have been blind in the left eye since last winter, and I did not look. Teodor Arenius brought a mason last spring to repair the gallery. The mason put in the hinge. I assumed it was a vent. I... I thought it was a vent. Gods forgive me. How many boats?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o2.tex: Ask Keeper Olwen Starrow who has the pull-cord
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o2.top: There is a cord on the lens shutter running down the outer wall. Who knows it is there?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o3.tex: Wait for a moonless night and watch the sea cave of Dunbarrow Cove
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o4.tex: Take the sea cave from the wreckers
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o5.tex: Defeat Gannet Skerry, the wreckers' master
The harbour will want to hear it from you, Teodor. Stand before them.
Then I will. Not this night. But this month. Take the book to the Legion tonight; I will walk up to them myself.
Keep the book. Your brother is dead to the sea. Let the harbour go on.
Then I am in your debt, and it is a debt I will carry for my brother. You may collect it whenever you like.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o6.rep: It is my brother's. Brannoc. He lost the family boat to the rocks three years ago and I am told the sea took him. He did not drown. He has been standing on that headland every moonless night for three years, and I have been paying him with harbour fees. I did not know about the lamp. I swear it. I did not ask, which is worse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o6.tex: Bring the tally book to the Harbourmaster
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o6.top: Three pages carry a name, scratched out. The same name. Do you know it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.o7.tex: Return to the lighthouse and relight the beacon with Olwen
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.offer: Marga, what boats are not coming back?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.outro: The beacon of Anvil burns steady gold every night now, and the pull-cord is gone from the wall. Marga mends nets in the harbour and does not say she told you so. Her needle says it for her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.pitch: Four boats in a month, all on moonless nights, all with a lamp that failed. It is not the oil and it is not the Keeper. Olwen has trimmed that wick every night for thirty years. Someone is putting the light out, and someone is waiting on the rocks to pick up what the sea drops. Go to the lighthouse. Climb the stair. Look at the lens. Tell me I am wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_beacon.title: The Dark Beacon
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.desc: The Drowned Compass's gull has stolen a customs man's brass ring and nested with it on the Benirus Manor roof. Bosun Eudora Pell wants it back before the customs man stops being polite.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o0.text: Climb to the gull's nest on the Benirus Manor roof and take the brass ring
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o1.reply: Room nine. Not a lodger. Cellar nine. There is a stair at the back of the Drowned Compass that goes down to the old storm drain, and the drain goes out to the cove. Every smuggler in Anvil used that room before the Legion came. The customs man was not polite by accident, child. He was looking for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o1.text: Ask Marga the Net-Mender what the stamped number means
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o1.topic: This ring is stamped with a room number at the Drowned Compass. Is it a lodger's token?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o2.reply: Cellar nine. Aye. It has been dry since my mother's day, and she told me never to count the steps. I will tell the polite gentleman that Gull ate the key. He will believe me, because he has met Gull. Take this. If you ever need a back door in Anvil, the door is here.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o2.text: Return the ring and ask Eudora about cellar nine
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.o2.topic: Your gull stole the key to cellar nine. The customs man was looking for the stair.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.outro: The customs man left Anvil unsatisfied and the Drowned Compass went on serving. Gull sits on the roof beam with a smug expression and a new bit of tin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.pitch: Gull is a thief. I have kept him because he is the only thing in Anvil that has never asked me for money. This week he took a brass ring off a guest's washstand and flew it up to the Benirus roof. The guest is a customs man and he is very polite about it. I want the ring back before he gets less polite.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_gull.title: The Gull That Counted
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.desc: Retired smuggler Cap'n Dufrane sells an honest map to a stash he cached thirty years ago at Tribune's Folly. He wants it fetched, for half.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o0.reply: It is. Mostly. There is one thing I should mention. The X is where the cache was. The stairs are where the cache is. These are not the same place. Do not look at me like that. A man must protect his retirement.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o0.text: Take the map from Cap'n Dufrane
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o0.topic: Give me the map, Cap'n. I will see if it is as honest as you say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o1.journa: The cache was a barrel of ship biscuit, three crates of Elsweyr moon-sugar and a letter. The letter was addressed to the finder and signed Dufrane. It said, in a spidery hand: If you are reading this, I am dead, and you have been very patient.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o1.text: Find the smuggler's cache at the Tribune's Folly
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o2.reply: Ah. I was afraid of that. I wrote it thirty years ago. I did not think the biscuit would last. I meant the gold to be there. A man gets used to his own lies. There was no gold, my friend. There never was. But I will give you half the sugar, and this, which is real.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o2.text: Bring the Cap'n what is in the barrel
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.o2.topic: It was a barrel of biscuit, some sugar and a letter. The letter says, "You have been very patient."
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.offer: Cap'n, you were selling a map?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.outro: Cap'n Dufrane has been sentenced to a lifetime of honesty and a pension of moon-sugar. He tells the story of the biscuit at the Drowned Compass to anyone who will buy him a drink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.pitch: A map. Honest. Sold for cheap, because the man who made it is dead and the man who sells it is old. There is a stash at the Tribune's Folly, a smuggler's cache I laid down thirty years ago, and I cannot get up the hill any more. Go and fetch it, and I will give you half. Mind the Legion. Mind the sea-wind. Mind the bit with the stairs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_map.title: Dufrane's Honest Map
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.desc: The net-menders of Anvil have stopped work over a rope tax. Chandler Hob Wetherly asks you to act as go-between for Marga and the Harbourmaster.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o0.rep: A fifth off, signed by the Harbourmaster's own pen. We mend the Count's nets for nothing in the autumn, in return. Nobody has ever asked what we would give. They only ask what we cost.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o0.tex: Hear the net-menders' terms from Marga
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o0.top: Hob says the strike is over the rope tax. What will you accept?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o1.rep: A fifth. In autumn. Well. The breakwater needs money, but a harbour with no nets earns nothing at all. I would have settled for a tenth if anyone had asked. Tell her I will sign tomorrow. And tell her that the Count's nets are not as bad as she remembers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o1.tex: Put the terms to Harbourmaster Teodor Arenius
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o1.top: The net-menders want a fifth off the rope tax, and will mend the Count's nets free in autumn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o2.rep: A fifth! Then I will have to lower my rope price or the harbour will think I am profiting. Take a coil. Have two. I shall be selling rope at a loss for a week, and every net-mender in Anvil will buy a coil from me out of spite.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o2.tex: Tell Hob Wetherly it is settled
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.o2.top: It is done, chandler. A fifth off, and free mending in autumn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.offer: The net-menders are on strike, chandler?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.outro: The net-menders of Anvil are back at work. The breakwater is half-built and the harbour is full. Hob Wetherly is selling rope at a loss and will tell you about it at length.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.pitch: The net-menders have put down their needles. Marga leads them. They want their rope tax lowered, and the Harbourmaster says the Count needs it for the new breakwater. Nobody is wrong and nobody is right and every boat in Anvil is ragged. I sell rope, I do not settle strikes. Can you go between them?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_an_strike.title: The Net-Menders' Strike
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_bell_rope.des: The Chapel's old bell-rope was cut by someone who wanted it silent. A chandler's mark that is not Hrodgar's has been found on the stone behind it.
Search the bell tower for the cut rope and the chandler's mark
Mine. Or rather, my father's. A two-flame mark. Old Bruma families used it before the Imperial wax tax. Only one house still has the die: the Brandt family smithy. Do not look at me. I sell candles, I do not cut ropes.
Show the rope to Old Hrodgar
The bell-rope was cut and a chandler's mark was left on the stone. Whose is it?
Keep the secret. A father protecting a daughter is not a crime.
Then I owe you a great deal of iron. Come by the forge.
Tell Sister Matina. The Chapel should know who cut the rope.
Then I will tell it myself, at the next service. Thank you for the courtesy.

Aye, my die. And aye, I cut it. My daughter was married under that bell, and the first night it rang after the old Count's death she woke up screaming and has not slept well since. I did not think anyone would climb that tower again. I am sorry. If it is to ring, let it ring. But put her in the Chapel garden first, please, before the old song starts.
Ask Brandt Ironsled about the rope
Your family die was left on the stone behind the bell. And the rope was cut.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_bell_rope.off: The bell, Sister. Something is still wrong with it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_bell_rope.out: The Chapel bell hangs with a new rope, spliced by Brandt Ironsled, and rings with the right note. Nobody has asked who tied the knot.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_bell_rope.pit: The rope was cut. Not frayed, not broken: cut, from one side only, by someone who knew which fibres would hold the weight and which would not. The bell has not rung properly since you woke it. I want to know who wanted it silent in the first place. Look at the stone behind the bell. There is a chandler's mark on it, and it is not Hrodgar's.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.desc: Old Hrodgar the Chandler is missing payment for three black candles, and someone is lighting them along the old Cloud Ruler road.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o0.tex: Follow the black candles along the old road to Cloud Ruler Temple
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o1.rep: Black candles are for the unmourned. Ysolde Frostbrow told me last winter that her husband, who took the pass in the Year of the Red Mountain's Smoke, was never found. Every winter she sets a candle on the road, and every winter she has said she would stop. I would not stop. I might light one with her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o1.tex: Ask Sister Matina why the candles are lit
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o1.top: Someone is lighting black candles along the road to the old temple. Do you know why?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o2.rep: He wanted to see the ridge-light from the other side. Went one night with a sled and a dog. I am told he waved. I am not told anything else. Hrodgar has written it all down, the dear fool, as a debt. I will pay it. But if you walk the pass again, and find a dog collar, I would like to know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.o2.top: Sister Matina told me. I am sorry for your husband.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.offer: You mentioned a candle of a certain kind.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.outro: The candles on the Cloud Ruler road have a name now. Ysolde Frostbrow lights one a year and pays Old Hrodgar for it, and neither of them speaks of the debt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.pitch: People ask for a black candle and then do not say what for. I do not mind. A man who keeps a black candle in a Talos town is a man with an honest sort of sin. But this season, three candles went out of the shop and not one came back to be paid for. Someone is lighting them in the old Cloud Ruler road. I would like to know who, and whether they are grieving or planning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_candle.title: A Candle of Little Weight
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.desc: Captain Ilsa Varro wants a rider to win Bruma's Stair-Race, then escort a sledge of Talos relics through the Jerall pass before the storm closes it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o0.text: Reach the top of the terraces for the Stair-Race
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o1.jour: The race was won by two breaths, mostly because a shopkeeper's dog got in front of the lead runner. Captain Varro said she had not seen such a clean victory since the Legion took the Gold Coast, which is to say never.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o1.text: Climb the three hundred and eleven steps to the Chapel gate with a sack of flour
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o2.repl: The pass. Aye. If the snow holds, it takes two nights. If it does not, I lose a fourth sled and you lose the relics. Walk beside me, keep your sword out, and do not talk when I tell you not to. Ice-sound travels.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o2.text: Find Wulf Three-Sleds to drive the relic sledge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o2.topi: Captain Varro says you know the pass. Will you take the sledge up to the relics and bring them down with me?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o3.text: Collect the relic case waiting at Cloud Ruler Temple
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o4.text: Bring Wulf and the sledge down to the Chapel through the blizzard
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o5.repl: Three bones, wrapped in blue wool, exactly as the letter said. You have done what I would have asked of the Captain and been too proud to. Now, do not move. Someone is climbing the tower stair, and it is not one of mine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o5.text: Hand the relic case to Sister Matina
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o5.topi: The relics of the Talos Chapel, Sister. All three bones.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o6.text: Defend the Chapel bell tower from the raiders of Heskel Snowmantle
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o7.text: Climb the bell tower and ring the old bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.o8.text: Face the thing that woke under the ridge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.offer: Captain, you said you wanted a rider.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.outro: Bruma remembers the Stair-Race for the dog, and the bell for what answered it. The relics sit in the Chapel under a blue cloth, and the sledge-driver has named his fourth sled Optimism.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.pitch: The terraces are Bruma. Every child here learns the steps before the alphabet. At first snow we hold the Stair-Race: top of the town to the chapel gate, three hundred and eleven steps with a sack of flour on your shoulder, and the Legion is expected to lose with dignity. This year the stakes are higher. The Chapel is to receive relics from the Imperial City, and the pass will close behind them. I need someone who can win the race and then carry the relics through the blizzard. In that order.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_br_wager.title: The Snow-Load Wager
The charter went back under the Lady. Mother Nettle suspects what you did, and has a word.

Suspect? Child, I have been at the foot of that stair for sixty winters. I know when the Lady has been disturbed. You put the thing back, and somebody smarter than I put a coin in her hand last night, and it was not a copper. Say nothing. I shall say nothing. It is the oldest way to keep a promise, and the quietest, and the surest. Take this. It is only an eel, but it is a very good eel.
Hear what Mother Nettle makes of the buried charter
The charter is buried. You suspect it?
The charter lies beneath the Lady, undisturbed. Someone leaves a gold coin in her hand each dawn, and Mother Nettle says it is only the tide.
The charter went back under the Lady. Mother Nettle suspects what you did, and has a word.
Captain Pellia Vorn read the Founders' Charter from the temple steps. She has news.

Loudly. Mother Nettle wept. Tomas Fenn tied a lucky knot in my sleeve and refused to take it off. The Count's clerk left on the morning boat. The tithe is paid to the poor now, from a box that the Lady holds in her hand, and every coin is counted twice. Ulrich was gone before the reading ended. I found a slate on my desk: THANK YOU. He will not be back.
Hear how Bravil took the reading of the charter
You read the charter. How did the city take it?
The tithe of Bravil is paid to the poor of the town from the hand of the Lucky Old Lady. Ulrich the Quiet is somewhere else, and has, one hopes, found a place to speak.
Captain Pellia Vorn read the Founders' Charter from the temple steps. She has news.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.desc: Mother Nettle and Tomas Fenn each claim the eel pool under Bay Bridge. She wants three eels from it as proof of who the pool answers to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o0.reply: Watch. Eels come when I whistle the old tune. A pool owner is one the eels know. Tomas, now, he has a piece of paper. Take me to the pool. Take the paper-man too.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o0.text: Bring Mother Nettle three Niben eels
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o0.topic: I have the eels, Mother Nettle. Show me what a pool owner can do.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o1.reply: Show them? They are eels. Fine. I will come, and I will bring the paper, and I will bring my lucky knots. The first one to make an eel obey wins, and I shall rule on the terms myself. No? Then you do it. Be fair. You have the face for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o1.text: Tell Tomas Fenn to come to the pool
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o1.topic: Mother Nettle says the eels know her. Come and show them your paper.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.c0.la: Tell Tomas gently. He was cheated too.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.c0.re: Then I will not write his name on the fraud list. The man is a fool, not a thief.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.c1.la: Let the Captain write him down. A fool with a paper still bought a stolen thing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.c1.re: Then it is written. He will have a day to return what the clerk gave him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.reply: A witness. And a clerk's paper, which, I may say, I have seen before, and which was sold twice, to two other men, and neither of them is Tomas. The pool is Nettle's. It has always been. I will put it in writing. Tell Tomas I will be sending a clerk of my own to talk about fraud.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.o2.topic: Two claims on the Bay Bridge pool, Captain. Mother Nettle and Tomas Fenn. I need a witness.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.offer: You mentioned a dispute over eels.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.outro: The eel pool under Bay Bridge is Mother Nettle's, in writing. She has not stopped whistling since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.pitch: My mother fished the eel-pools under Bay Bridge, and her mother before her. Now that jumped-up knot-seller Tomas Fenn says the pool is his, because the Count's clerk sold him a paper. I want an arbiter who does not care about either of us. I want you. Bring me three eels from the pool, living if you can, and I will show you what a pool owner can do that a paper-buyer cannot.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_eels.title: Eel Rights of the Bay Bridge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.desc: Captain Pellia Vorn suspects the Count's clerk of emptying the Lucky Old Lady statue's hand every dawn. Three townspeople tell three stories of the statue, and one is the key.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o0.reply: A girl, child. Fourteen, drowned in the first flood, dragged out by a priest of Zenithar who put her into a boat of stone and set her at the top of the stair, so that the next flood would see her first. The coins are her wages. The statue is what is left of the last girl who asked for nothing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o0.text: Hear Mother Nettle's version of the Lady
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o0.topic: Captain Vorn says you know the story of the statue.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o1.reply: A thief, saint-thief, which is a different thing. Stole a bishop's purse to feed four brothers and was drowned in the Larsius for it. The bishop felt such guilt he carved the statue at his own expense. Luck is what he hoped his guilt would buy. I do not charge for this one. I have only ever told it for coins.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o1.text: Hear Tomas Fenn's version of the Lady
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o1.topic: Mother Nettle says it is a drowned girl. What do you say?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o2.reply: The seal of the Count's own house is cut into the base. Under the moss, on the north side, there is a charter: the founders bound the city's tithe to the statue, to be held for the poor, with the statue as the seal. I have it from my grandmother, who is dead, and it is the only version I believe because she never once said it was a pretty story.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o2.topic: Everyone tells it differently. What do you say, Captain?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o3.text: Wait for dark, then watch the dock below the statue
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o4.journ: The barge hands carried small tarred jars, and each jar went into the hollow beneath the statue's hand. Whoever empties the hand at dawn is collecting more than coppers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o4.text: Stop the skooma barge crew unloading under the statue
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o5.reply: He scratches on the slate with a stub of chalk: THE CLERK. A WOMAN. A MAN. THE CLERK PAYS ME TO STAY SILENT. I AM ALREADY. He gives you a rueful look. The slate goes on: I WOULD LIKE TO BE SOMEWHERE ELSE.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o5.text: Question the barge pilot, Ulrich the Quiet
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o5.topic: You were the pilot. The skooma went into the statue. Who takes it out?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o6.reply: On my orders? On the Count's orders, as the Count's own steward, which is a very different thing. The statue is a municipal asset. Its contents are municipal. If a barge crew has been feeding it, then it is the barge crew who is trespassing. Brink! Show this person the yard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o6.text: Catch Clerk Vedius Hallow at the counting-house door
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o6.topic: Mother Nettle's barge crew say the hand of the statue is emptied each dawn on your orders, Clerk. Is that so?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o7.text: Break the clerk's man in the counting-house yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o8.text: Open the base of the statue and take the Founders' Charter
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.c0.la: Make it public. The poor of Bravil have a right to know what they are owed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.c0.re: Then I will read it from the steps of the temple on Morndas. Ulrich will have a day's start. I will see to it myself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.c1.la: Bury it. A city that knows what it is owed starts a war over it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.c1.re: Then I will keep it where only I can find it, and a hundred years from now someone braver will have it. I do not like it. But I will do it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.reply: It has been here the whole time. I could put this on the Count's desk, and the whole city would learn that its own founders gave its poor a right. The cost is Ulrich, because the barge crew will hang for it, and he was their pilot. Or I could bury it back and break the clerk quietly. Nobody else needs to know it was ever more than a statue.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.text: Take the charter to Captain Vorn and decide its fate
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.o9.topic: The charter is in the base, as you said. The clerk was stealing the tithe and using the hollow as a smuggler's drop.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.offer: Captain, what is the trouble with the statue?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.outro: The Lucky Old Lady stands at the top of the stair with her hand open. Some say she is a drowned girl, some a saint-thief. Captain Pellia Vorn knows she is a seal on a promise, and so, now, do you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.pitch: Every beggar and half the fishwives in Bravil leave a coin in the Lucky Old Lady's hand, and every dawn the hand is empty. I thought it was thieves. Then I thought it was a custom. Now I think it is the Count's clerk, and I cannot prove it, because the clerk is a very careful man. Ask three people for the story of the statue. Everyone in this town tells a different one, and one of them is true.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_lady.title: The Lady's Lucky Day
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.desc: Madame Ottilie Brand of the Lonely Suitor Lodge has a stack of anonymous love notes addressed to Captain Pellia Vorn. She wants to know who writes them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o0.te: Wait at the Lodge door for the next note to be pushed under it
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o1.te: Wait for dark and follow the footsteps from the Lodge door
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o2.re: He holds up the slate, then wipes it with his sleeve, then writes again, slowly: BECAUSE I AM A MAN WHO CARRIES SKOOMA. SHE IS A WOMAN WHO ARRESTS THEM. THIS IS WHY I WRITE. There is a long pause. Then, smaller: WOULD YOU DELIVER IT, IF I ASK?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o2.te: Follow the footsteps to the pilot of the skooma barge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o2.to: You write the notes. Why do you not simply say it to her?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o3.c0: Tell her it is Ulrich. He is a barge-pilot, and he is kind.
The pilot. The one who cannot speak. Of course it is. I should have noticed that every letter has the same tilt as his slate. I will find him. I will not arrest him. Not tonight.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o3.c1: Then I will wonder. I will go on wondering. It is better than knowing, and also worse. Thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o3.re: A letter. For me. I have been arresting this town for eleven years and nobody has ever once... Hm. This is beautifully written. Who wrote it? ... Ah. I see. Well. That makes it considerably more difficult. Do not say anything. I need to think.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o3.te: Give the note to Captain Vorn
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.o3.to: I was asked to deliver this. The writer is someone you know, though you may not like it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.offer: Letters under the door, you said?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.outro: The letters under the Lodge door have stopped. Madame Ottilie says they stopped the night Captain Vorn left a reply, and that the reply was only one word long.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.pitch: Every night, a note is slipped under the door of the Lodge, and every morning it is still there, addressed to the same woman and signed by no one. The woman is Captain Vorn, and she has never once received them, because I have been too embarrassed to give them to her. They are lovely. They are far better than anything I have ever received. Find the writer. If he is a fool, I will burn them. If he is a poet, I will weep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_bv_letters.title: Letters to the Lonely Suitor
The Great Oak was felled. Arden the Woodwright is carving the first bench from its trunk.

I made the first cut myself, and I told it first. It did not answer. That was the worst of it. I am carving a bench from the first ring, for the Chapel, with one name on it: the Oak. The town will be warm for twenty winters and cold for a hundred years of memory. Take this heartwood. Do not burn it. Make something that can be sat on.
Visit Arden the Woodwright at the felled Oak
The Oak is down. How is the work?
A bench of heartwood sits before the Chapel of Chorrol, with a single word carved on it. The town is warm, and does not speak of the Oak above a whisper.
The Great Oak was felled. Arden the Woodwright is carving the first bench from its trunk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_after_saved.d: The Great Oak was saved. Tarn Wexley is digging new wells and has opinions.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_after_saved.o: Eleven feet, and clean, and no root in it. I have dug six, and each is a better argument than the last. The Oak drinks from the east; the town drinks from the west; and the two of them have stopped speaking, as old neighbours do. It is the best compromise I ever made. Take this. It is the first fish from the new cistern. It is an honest fish.
Hear how Tarn Wexley is digging new wells around the Oak
The Oak is saved. How are the wells?
The wells of Chorrol are clean and the Oak is alive. Tarn Wexley calls it the best compromise of his career.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_after_saved.p: The Great Oak was saved. Tarn Wexley is digging new wells and has opinions.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.desc: Mabyn Hartwell of the Hungry Heron is afraid of the stuffed heron on her wall, and of the brass key that has begun to show beneath its leg. She wants it taken down, and opened.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o0.text: Take the brass key from the stuffed heron's leg
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o1.jour: The cellar door hid a stair, and the stair a small dry cellar with one chest. The chest held a hundred and twenty gold septims and a note in the dead husband's hand: For the day you stop being afraid of the heron.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o1.text: Open the cellar door behind the Hungry Heron's hearth
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o2.repl: Oh, you old fool. You stuffed a bird to hold a key and told me not to be afraid of it. A hundred and twenty septims. Is it the heron, or is it you? I do not know. I am going to take it down and put it by the fire, where it belongs. Take this, and drink on the house.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o2.text: Show Mabyn what her husband left
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.o2.topi: The cellar held a chest and a note. He left it for the day you stopped being afraid of the heron.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.offer: Mabyn, what is the story with your heron?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.outro: The heron now sits by the fire in the Hungry Heron, wearing the dead husband's hat. Mabyn Hartwell has been seen to talk to it, and sometimes to listen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.pitch: I have never told this to a living soul. The heron is my husband's. He stuffed it himself, the day he died, and he said, Mabyn, the heron knows. I thought it was the fever talking. Last week a bit of green ribbon slid out of the heron's leg. There is a key. I cannot reach it, because I am afraid of the heron. Will you take it down for me?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_heron.title: The Heron's Brass Key
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.desc: A letter has arrived at Weynon Priory that is sealed and written by a dead Count and dated next year. Brother Hesk will not deliver it himself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.o0.tex: Take the letter to the ruined house it is addressed to, near Weynon Priory
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.o1.tex: Drive the squatters out of the ruined house
Show it to Lady Cassia Vallarius. It is meant for her.
Then I will go with you. She has a right to it, and she deserves a kind face when she reads it.
Burn it. The dead should not write to the living.
Then it is burned. And I will say a prayer and not tell anyone. The ash shall go in the font.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.o2.rep: Then I will read it. "To my dearest Cassia: when you read this, I am gone, and the oak is in danger, and you are not yet the woman I hoped you would be. I will help you. Burn this when you are done. Do not tell Arden." It is the Count's hand. It is written on this year's paper. And yet here it is. I think someone has been writing in his name, and they do it very well.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.o2.tex: Take the letter back to Brother Hesk
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.o2.top: The house is empty. The letter was waiting there. I did not open it. Open it yourself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.offer: Brother Hesk, what letter is this?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.outro: Whatever wrote the Count's letter, it has stopped. Brother Hesk now keeps a second candle by his desk, lit, and does not say why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.pitch: A courier left it at Weynon Priory, wet to the wrist, and rode into the night. The seal is the Count of Chorrol's. The hand is the Count's. The date is next year. The Count has been dead twelve years. I would burn it. I cannot. It is the most remarkable thing I have ever held. Take it to the house it is addressed to. I will not go myself. I find I am afraid of what the house will say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_letter.title: The Letter That Should Not Exist
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.desc: The Great Oak of Chorrol is sick at the heart. Arden the Woodwright asks for bark samples, a cure, and a night's vigil against whatever is eating it from within.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o0.text: Cut bark samples at the third buttress of the Great Oak
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o1.reply: Dying? Not yet. A blight, a very particular one, spread by a beetle that lays its eggs in the bark crack. Cure the beetle, cure the Oak. For that I need two things: elves ear and juniper berries, from the roadside. Bring them, and I will make a tincture that the Oak will drink through its roots.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o1.text: Show the bark to Fenwick Thorne
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o1.topic: Arden says the Oak is dying from the middle. Is there a cure?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o2.reply: Good. Now the berries. I would go myself, but my hips and the highland road are old enemies.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o2.text: Gather three elves ear for Fenwick Thorne
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o2.topic: Here are the elves ear. Three, as you asked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o3.reply: Give me a night to steep it. Come back at dusk. Do not go near the Oak without a lantern. Something in it has begun to move.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o3.text: Gather three juniper berries for Fenwick Thorne
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o3.topic: Juniper berries, three. Is the tincture ready?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o4.text: Keep the Oak at dusk against the beetle swarm
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o5.text: Hold the Oak against the heartwood beetles
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o6.text: Cut down the Rot-Heart that has grown in the Oak's wound
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.c0.lab: Save the Oak. A town can dig new wells. It cannot grow a new Oak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.c0.rep: Then I will move the wells. Tarn Wexley will grumble and dig. I will give the Oak every night I have left, and thank you every one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.c1.lab: Fell it. The town drinks first. An Oak can be mourned.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.c1.rep: Then I will take the first cut myself. The Oak's wood is worth more than Chorrol, and the town will be warm for twenty winters. I will tell it before the axe falls.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.reply: Fell... Gods. The Count's steward has asked me three times. The wells have gone black and the roots reach the cisterns. If it goes, the water runs clear in a month. If it stays, I give it every night I have left. I cannot choose this one. You can. You have not been here two thousand years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.text: Tell Arden what the Oak needs
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.o7.topic: The beetles are dead and the Rot-Heart is cut out, but the roots are bleeding into the town wells. Will you fell it, or tend it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.outro: The Great Oak of Chorrol is a smaller thing than it was, or it is gone, or it is alive. In any case Arden the Woodwright tends what remains, and the wells run clear, and nobody in Chorrol will speak of it without lowering their voice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.pitch: It is not the Oak that is ill. It is the heartwood, and there is no stone in all Chorrol sharper than that distinction. The leaves are thin, the roots are black at the tips, and something is eating it from the middle. Take a sample of the bark at the third buttress, where the black began. Take it to Fenwick Thorne. He knows plants. I know only wood.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_oak.title: A Sickness in the Heartwood
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.desc: Tarn Wexley's apprentice went into the Crumbling Mine looking for clean water and has not returned in two days.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.o0.text: Clear the Crumbling Mine of whatever is biting
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.o1.text: Find Pip, Tarn Wexley's apprentice, in the lower gallery
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.o2.reply: Dirt. Of course. It is clean water or nothing, he said, and he must have thought dirt would tell him. I will keep him on, and he will carry buckets for a year. Thank you. Take this. It is the first clean sample from the new vein.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.o2.text: Bring Pip's news back to Tarn Wexley
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.o2.topic: Your apprentice is safe. He was stuck in the lower gallery with a cracked lantern and a bag of dirt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.offer: Tarn, the wells. Something is wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.outro: The new well in Chorrol runs clean, and a certain apprentice carries buckets and does not complain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.pitch: My apprentice Pip went down the old crumbling mine to find a vein of clean water for the new well, and he has not come back up in two days. The mine is full of things that bite. I am too old to be bitten. If you find him, tell him I am not angry. Tell him I will be angry later, at home, with soup.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ch_well.title: Deeper than the Well
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.desc: A Dunmer refugee grandmother haunts the Cheydinhal Great Chapel annex, begging for the ash of her hearth. Ilvesa Dren needs ash to lay her to rest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o0.reply: It is the nearest anyone could. It will do. Take it to the shrine yourself. She trusts you. She has seen you carry the deed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o0.text: Bring two portions of ash salts to Ilvesa Dren
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o0.topic: Ash salts, two portions. It is the nearest I could find to a Dunmer hearth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o1.text: Go to the Great Chapel annex shrine at night
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o2.journa: The old woman bent over the shrine and breathed in. Then she smiled, and for a moment the whole annex smelled of woodsmoke and spiced bread, and the air was warm.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.o2.text: Set the vial of ash on the ancestor shrine
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.outro: The ancestor shrine in Cheydinhal's Great Chapel annex is quiet. Ilvesa Dren has hung a small lantern over it, and the refugees leave a pinch of ash there on feast days.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.pitch: There is a spirit in the Great Chapel annex. An old woman, a Dunmer, who died the week we came. She was buried in Cyrodiil soil, and her family cannot bring her home. She stands at the shrine every night and asks for her hearth. I have no hearth to give. Bring me ash. Any ash that burned in a Dunmer fire. We will set her to rest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_ash.title: The Wrong Soil
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.desc: A free house by Cheydinhal's old wall stands empty because no Dunmer refugee will cross its threshold. Ilvesa Dren of the Refugee Hall asks you to find out why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o0.repl: Ungrateful, certainly. I let them have a stall at the edge of the market. I let them have the house for nothing. And they say it is haunted. Nobody has died in it. Nobody has so much as stubbed a toe. If there is a ghost it has very good manners.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o0.topi: The refugees say the house is haunted. You say they are ungrateful. What is your side?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o1.repl: They say it is not the dead. It is the living. Three families went in, and a fourth saw a man in the cellar window, in an old Ordinator's coat, with a hand on a hilt. Not a ghost. A man. The next morning the family was gone. Nobody has asked where.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o1.text: Hear the refugees' side from Ilvesa Dren
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o1.topi: Brenius says nobody has died in the house. What do the refugees say?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o2.text: Wait for dark, then watch the empty house by the wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o3.text: Break the landlord's men in the cellar
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o4.repl: I am no longer an Ordinator. I am a man who left. The landlord paid me to keep the families out, and I did, until I saw the children. I could not stop them. I could only hide the deed from the one who would take it. Here. It is yours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o4.text: Question the hooded man hiding in the cellar
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o4.topi: You are an Ordinator. You have been hiding here since the landlord's men drove the families out. Why?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.c0.l: Let Brenius make amends. The market and the Hall will both need him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.c0.r: Then I will tell him so tonight. He will cry. I hope it improves him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.c1.l: Arrest him. A forged deed is a forged deed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.c1.r: Then it is done. The Hall will have the house, and the market will have a new owner, and I will have a long night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.repl: A forged deed. So the landlord took the house in the name of a notary who does not exist, and has been renting it to refugees in a way that guarantees they will flee. I could arrest Brenius, who vouched for it. Or I could let him make amends, which is what a decent man would do. I leave the choice to the people who found the thing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.text: Take the deed to Captain Sarel
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.o5.topi: The landlord is a man with an invented notary and a hired Ordinator. The deed proves it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.offer: Warden Dren, what is wrong with the house?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.outro: The house by the old wall has a family in it now, and a candle in the window. Whether the market made peace with the Refugee Hall or the Hall made peace with the market, the street has a different sound after dark.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.pitch: There is a house by the old wall, free to any family that will have it, and not one Dunmer will enter. Brenius Marcus says they are ungrateful. They say the house is haunted. I have lived a long life and I have never seen a house that makes a refugee cross a street. Look at it. Talk to them. Talk to him. See what you find.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_house.title: The Empty House by the Wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.desc: Toll-Keeper Odell Corbolo has set three riddles on the stone of Corbolo Bridge. Their answers are somewhere in Cheydinhal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o0.rep: A roll. The roll of names. Always counted, never spent. Good riddle. Odell is better at them than he looks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o0.tex: Ask Ilvesa Dren: what is always counted but never spent?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o0.top: Odell asked me a riddle. What is always counted but never spent?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o1.rep: Debt. Do not look at me like that. It grows beautifully. Tell Odell I said so, and that I am not paying him a copper for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o1.tex: Ask Brenius Marcus: what grows in the market and never in the field?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o1.top: Odell asked me a riddle. What grows in the market and never in the field?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o2.rep: The bridge! Not a soul in twenty years has said the bridge. Well done. Through you go, toll-free, and here, the purse. It was only forty copper. The first traveller was a fool and the second a liar, and I am a toll-keeper who likes his riddles answered.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.o2.top: A roll. Debt. And one more, the one I worked out myself: the bridge itself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.offer: Odell, you said the toll is a riddle?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.outro: The riddles on the stone of Corbolo Bridge change every month. A few say they have been answered, most say they never will be, and Odell Corbolo smiles at all of them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.pitch: Today, at the bridge, three travellers will each pay in an answer. I have set three riddles on the stone. Their answers are a name, a place, and a thing. Bring me the answers, and I will let you through for nothing, and give you the bridge-keeper's purse that the first of them forgot.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_cy_riddle.title: The Toll of Three Answers
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_after_arboret: The Alessian seal went to the Arboretum. Archivist Pomponia Sedge wants you to see what has come of it.

It opened a bed. A single square of cold soil, under the glasshouse, which has never frozen or flooded in the six days since. I planted the warm blue bulb in it. It bloomed overnight. The Palace sent a clerk to demand it back. I told him it was still growing and could not be moved. He left a form. I am eating the form. Thank you, stranger. The city has a fourth ring now, and it is mine.
See what Pomponia Sedge has done with the Alessian seal
The seal went to the Arboretum. What did you do with it?
A cold bed of soil blooms beneath the Arboretum glasshouse. Pomponia Sedge keeps it watered, and has stopped answering the Palace's forms.
The Alessian seal went to the Arboretum. Archivist Pomponia Sedge wants you to see what has come of it.
The Alessian seal went to the Palace. Under-Chamberlain Verus Tiro has something to say about what came of it.

It sits under glass in a room that has no door, and is guarded by men who do not know what they guard. Each of the three cisterns has been sealed with a new grate and a very old lock. The Prefect is furious. The Archivist is furious. I am rather pleased. A city should know how many floors it has, and then pretend it does not. Take this, from the Palace stores.
Hear what the Palace did with the Alessian seal
The seal went to the Palace. What did you do with it?
The Palace keeps its seal under glass and its cisterns behind new locks. The Imperial City has three floors it will not admit, and one more lie it tells with a straight face.
The Alessian seal went to the Palace. Under-Chamberlain Verus Tiro has something to say about what came of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.de: Brother Calvus heard the last confession of a dying man who claimed to have murdered a child and buried her in the Memorial District graveyard. A small bell rings there at night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.o0: Walk the Memorial District graveyard after dark
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.o1: There was no child under the stone. Only a pewter locket, wrapped in a woman's kerchief, and a hole just wide enough to bury a very small coffin. Someone had dug the grave and not filled it.
Dig where the small bell rings and find the pewter locket
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.o2: Ennia Vanto. Eight years old, vanished in the Year of the Yellow Fever. Her mother, Maera Vanto, still lives in the Elven Gardens and still keeps a candle in the window. The dying man was her brother. He took the blame so that her mother would not know that Ennia ran away with a caravan and never came home. I have known that for a decade. I have never had the cruelty to say.
Ask Prefect Aurex who was missing from the Memorial District twenty years ago
I found a locket marked Ennia, in a grave with no body. Does the Watch have a record?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.o3: Tell Maera the truth. She has a right to hope.
Then you are braver than any priest. Take the locket and a blessing I am not permitted to give.
Let the lie rest. Some sorrows are load-bearing.
Then I will keep the secret and the candle, and answer to Arkay for both.

Then he lied for love, and told the lie to the only man who may not repeat it. Foolish brother. Foolish me. What will you do with the thing? A mother who thinks her child was murdered grieves one way. A mother who is told the child may have simply gone away grieves another, worse way, because there is hope in it.
Bring the locket to Brother Calvus
