There was no child in the grave. Only this. And her aunt wanted to be spared the truth.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.of: You mentioned a confession that will not stay buried.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.ou: The small bell has stopped in the Memorial District. Whether it rang for a lost girl or for the man who lied so that his sister would never wonder is a question Brother Calvus will carry to his own grave, with the rest of the city's heavy things.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_confession.pi: A dying man was carried into the temple three nights ago. He told me he had killed a child in the Memorial District, long ago, and buried her in the old graveyard with her locket. Then he died. The priest in me is bound, and the man in me is not. I cannot sleep for the sound of a small bell, which is somewhere in the Memorial District, and which is not there when I look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.desc: Archivist Pomponia Sedge suspects House Dolabella of cheating at the Imperial City Grafting Day contest. She wants someone to watch their greenhouse in the Nobles District.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o0.text: Watch the Dolabella greenhouse after dark
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o1.text: Stop the men carrying the real grafts out through the side door
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o2.repl: They were swapping nothing. Those were the Arboretum's grafts, delivered to us for safekeeping, and my men are guilty of an excess of zeal. Do not look at me like that. House Dolabella has won three ribbons because the Arboretum entered no tree of its own. The Archivist is afraid she has no talent left. Tell her that, from me. And tell her I lost my ribbon bet to her mother.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o2.text: Confront the Dolabella steward in the Nobles District
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o2.topi: Your masters were swapping the real grafts for their own, Under-Chamberlain. The Arboretum has the proof.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o3.repl: No. I did not. I thought mine would be second best, and I could not bear that. Then they were not cheating, only kind. Gods. And I sent you into the night for it. Take this, a cutting from the Silverbirch of the founders. Put it where it will grow.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o3.text: Tell Pomponia Sedge what the greenhouse hid
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.o3.topi: House Dolabella was holding your own entries, Archivist. You did not enter a tree for three years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.offer: You have a contest on your hands, Archivist?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.outro: On Grafting Day the Arboretum entered a tree of its own, a sorry little silverbirch, and lost to House Dolabella by a wide margin. Pomponia Sedge says it was the best day she has had in years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.pitch: Grafting Day, tomorrow. Every nursery in Cyrodiil enters one tree, and the Arboretum hands out the green ribbon. For three years the ribbon has gone to House Dolabella, and for three years their entry has been suspiciously perfect. I have heard they bribe the judges. I would rather catch them than accuse them. Go to the Nobles District tonight, and watch the Dolabella greenhouse. Whatever you see, do not touch the tree.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_graft.title: The Grafting Day Wager
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.desc: Odalis Fenn of the Third Ledger has found forty receipts for drinks she never poured. Someone is forging customs stamps and washing smuggled goods through her tavern books.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o0.r: Wax? Red wax is bought by everyone. Boxwood blanks, though, those are bought by one man. Gaius Tallyman, who says he is an assessor. He is certainly assessing something. I have not seen his work, you understand. If you were to bring me a blank, I could tell you whose chisel carved it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o0.t: Ask the stationer, Cato Merrit, who buys stamping wax in quantity
Odalis Fenn says the stamp on her receipts is false. Who in the Market District buys that much red wax?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o1.t: Wait for dark on the Waterfront
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o2.t: Catch Gaius Tallyman in the act at the Waterfront warehouses
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o3.c: Take the stamp to Prefect Aurex. The law keeps its receipts.
Then I will light a candle for the apprentice and not the master. Go on.
Keep the stamp. Every city has one man who prints the weather. Today, it is me.
Then we are friends, and these things cannot be said aloud. Go. Spend wisely, and always ask for a receipt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o3.r: That is my chisel work, or the work of one who learned from it. I taught the boy, you see. Three years my apprentice, and not a word of thanks. Take it to the Prefect, or take it to the bin, but please keep my name off the record. I will tell you where the rest of the ring meets, and in return, you will not have heard it from me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.o3.t: Bring the forged stamp to Cato Merrit
I caught Gaius Tallyman. This was in his coat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.offe: Your receipts. Something is off with them?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.outr: The Third Ledger now hands out receipts that match the cups poured. Whether Gaius Tallyman is in a cell or in a better coat is a matter between you, Cato Merrit and your conscience.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_receipts.pitc: Every cup in this house comes with a receipt, and every receipt has been stamped by the customs desk across the street, as the law requires. This week I counted forty receipts for cups I never poured. Someone is printing my stamps. They are using my tavern as a laundry for goods that never paid duty. I am not angry for me. I am angry because the numbers do not add up, and numbers are supposed to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.desc: Drainmaster Junius Pell has a sealed grate in the Waterfront that no Imperial map shows, and a key that fits nothing. Under the White-Gold Tower, older rings of the city may lie waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o0.reply: Seven keys, and the seventh is the one that frightens me. It was in the ring when I inherited it, and old Marcus before me never knew either. Go. If it is only a drain, I will buy you a drink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o0.text: Take the old key from Junius Pell
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o0.topic: Give me the key, Drainmaster. I will look at your grate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o1.reply: Seen? I have carried the river's own silt past it for nine years. The water goes in at the bottom of that grate and does not come out. Not a trickle. A thing that swallows a river and says nothing is not a drain. It is a mouth. Open it from the top. Do not go in from the bottom. The current is wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o1.text: Ask the bargewoman Dar-Meeska what the river says about the grate
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o1.topic: Drainmaster Pell says there is a grate behind the tannery wall that is not on any map. You carry what the river hands you. Have you seen it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o2.text: Find the sealed grate behind the tannery wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o3.text: Drive the vermin out of the culvert
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o4.journ: The first ring is a round cistern with a dry floor and a ceiling of green glass. The glasshouses above are sitting on it like a lid on a bowl. The walls are carved with branches that never end.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o4.text: Chart the first cistern, which lies beneath the Arboretum glasshouses
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o5.journ: The second ring is wet to the knee. The carvings here are of faces, hundreds of them, each different, each with its eyes closed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o5.text: Chart the second cistern, beneath the Memorial District
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o6.journ: The third ring is flooded to the roof. A pale lamp burns under the water and has done for a very long time.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o6.text: Chart the third cistern, beneath the Elven Gardens
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o7.text: Defeat the Cistern Warden and take the Alessian seal
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.c0.la: Carry it to the Under-Chamberlain. The Palace keeps what the Empire needs kept.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.c0.re: Then take it up the Tower stair and say nothing about how you found it. The Palace likes its miracles with the paperwork already filed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.c1.la: Give it to Pomponia. The Arboretum is the only place that still grows what the Ayleids planted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.c1.re: She will weep, and then she will make you a list of everything the seal opens. Take it. It is better in the hands of someone who knows what it is for.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.reply: Three. Of course there are three. Then I owe you a drink and the city owes you a great deal more, and the city will not pay it. Now. A thing like that does not belong in my ledger. Who do you give it to? The Palace will say it is theirs by right of tenure. Pomponia in the Arboretum says everything older than Alessia belongs to the living city, and she is the only one who has ever walked these rings with a lamp. I will not choose for you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.text: Tell Junius Pell what lies under his city
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.o8.topic: It is not a drain, Drainmaster. Under the city there are three rings of Ayleid cisterns, and the third was guarding this.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.offer: You wrote to the Prefect about a grate that is on no map.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.outro: Three rings beneath the three rings of the Imperial City are no longer a secret kept by one drainmaster and one dead Ayleid warden. Whoever holds the seal now holds a key to what lies under the White-Gold Tower. The city above carries on, as it always has, a little less sure of its own floor.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.pitch: The Prefect sent me a form, in triplicate, telling me to file a form. So I am asking someone who walks. Behind the tannery wall in the Waterfront there is a grate older than the wall, welded shut with Ayleid white-iron. I have the key ring of my predecessors, and one key on it fits nothing I have ever found. Open the grate for me. Come back and tell me it is a drain, and I will sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_ic_ring.title: The Ring Beneath the Rings
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.desc: Sister Ilvara keeps the chapel roll of Kvatch's lost, but it is incomplete. Dorrik the Bricklayer has found something in the rubble he will not show her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o0.reply: Twelve. That will do for the ward. Under the wall there was a cellar, and in the cellar a row of shelves, and on the shelves this brick. It is not Kvatchi work. I have been laying brick in this city for forty years and I have never seen that mark. I am afraid it means the city was not what it said it was.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o0.text: Haul twelve blocks of quarried stone to Dorrik at the east wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o0.topic: Sister Ilvara sent me. I have the stone. What did you find under the wall?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o1.journa: The roll lay under a collapsed pew, wrapped in an oilskin: three hundred and forty names in a dozen hands. At the end, in a smaller, slanted hand, a thirty-first page that was not in any copy: names of people who were never counted among the lost, because no one knew they had been there.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o1.text: Search the chapel crypt for the original roll of the lost
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o2.reply: My da carried me out. And a lady in a green cloak went the other way. Into the crater. She had a lantern. She did not come back. I asked Sister Ilvara and she said that is not a person, that is a bad dream. But I saw her. She had the same lantern as the brick.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o2.text: Ask Tilly Emmerich about the survivors she saw leave the crater
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o2.topic: Tilly, do you remember anyone leaving Kvatch the night of the burning, who is not on the roll?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o3.text: Follow the lantern woman's trail into Belletor's Folly
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o4.text: Go to the crater lip where the lantern woman was last seen
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o5.text: Seal the gate remnant before the new wall rises
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.c0.lab: Read them aloud. The dead should be heard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.c0.rep: Then I will ask Savlian for the chapel yard, and we will stand there. Thank you. It is a hard thing and a good one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.c1.lab: Write them in the roll and let it speak quietly. Some grief should not have an audience.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.c1.rep: Then I will write them tonight, in my own hand, and the chapel will be a quieter place for it. Take this, with my thanks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.reply: Thirty-first page. Oh. They are travellers. People who were here for the harvest, merchants, a dozen children of a family who had come for a wedding. Nobody counted them. Nobody was left to. Will you read them aloud at the ceremony? Or do I put them into the roll and let the book speak?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.text: Return the original roll and the thirty-first page to Sister Ilvara
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.o6.topic: The original roll, Sister. And a page of names nobody counted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.offer: Sister Ilvara, you said you need help with the roll.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.outro: The roll of the lost in Kvatch's chapel has thirty-one pages now, and Dorrik the Bricklayer has put the brick in the east wall where it can be seen. The new gate is shut and the old one is quiet. For now.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.pitch: The roll of the lost is on the chapel wall. It is not complete. The first copy burned with the old Chapel, and what I have is what survivors remember. I need someone to find the original, and to find what Dorrik found under the east wall. He will not say what it is. He looks at it at night. I think he is afraid it is a name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_ash.title: What the Ashes Keep
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.desc: A child, Tilly Emmerich, has lost her father's blue kite over the crater edge. She wants it fetched, and her escorted home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o0.text: Drive off the scamps at the crater edge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o1.text: Retrieve Tilly's blue kite from the crater edge
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o2.text: Take Tilly home to the Chapel field hospital
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o3.reply: Her father's kite. He made it from his own cloak the night before. She has not slept in four days. I will put it by her bed and say nothing. Thank you, stranger. Take this. It is only bread, but we have little else to give.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o3.text: Give the kite back to Tilly via Sister Ilvara
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.o3.topic: This is Tilly's kite. She is sleeping at the chapel. Keep it for her, Sister.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.offer: Tilly, what are you doing near the crater?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.outro: Tilly flies the kite from the chapel roof now, not the crater edge. Sister Ilvara says she can see it from the roll-wall, and that it is the most hopeful sight in Kvatch.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.pitch: My kite went over the edge. It is my da's kite, and it is blue, and the string broke on the wind. It is down there with the bad things. I am not allowed to go down. You are not my da. You can go down. You have a sword. Please?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_kite.title: A Kite near the Crater
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.desc: The rebuilding's pay-chest has been stolen, and a trail of bricks leads to the old fort at Dasek Moor. Quartermaster Fenn Pell wants it back before payday.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o0.r: Money? Nobody. Except a man who calls himself Wick, who bought the whole house a round on Morndas and paid in new Kvatch silver, still sticky with the mason's wax. He said he was a stone-merchant. I said I was a Cyrodiil queen. He laughed. He went east, toward Dasek Moor. I thought it was a funny thing for a stone-merchant to do.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o0.t: Ask Hetta Rooke who has been spending too freely at the Canvas Cup
The pay-chest walked. Who in Kvatch has suddenly got money to spend?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o1.t: Clear the thieves' camp at Dasek Moor
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o2.t: Catch Wick Hollis, who planned the theft
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o3.r: Whole! And warm. I assume that is the Count's luck. Keep the receipt, and the reward. The masons are paid, and the brick shall go up on time. Wick Hollis. I had my suspicions. A man who borrows my pen and never gives it back has something wrong with him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.o3.t: Return the pay-chest to Fenn Pell
The chest is whole. Wick Hollis will not trouble the masons again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.outr: The masons of Kvatch were paid on time and Quartermaster Fenn Pell has a new pen. The wall is a handspan higher than last week.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_kv_paychest.pitc: Three days to payday, and the chest walked. An iron-banded thing, locked, with the Count's arms, guarded by two men who say they never left their post. A trail of bricks leads to Dasek Moor. I do not care who has it. The masons have not been paid and a mason without pay is a mason on strike. Bring it back, and no one will ask how.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.desc: Orla Dunmoor has built a cask for Skingrad's Harvest Day downhill race and wants a runner who can keep it rolling through the market and out the east gate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o0.t: Take your cask to the top of the Rampart Stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o1.t: Roll through the market square without stopping
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o2.j: Three casks hit the wall, one bounced into a fishmonger's awning, and the Colovian wine merchant's cask sailed over the gatepost and into a hay-cart. Yours was the only cask that arrived upright.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o2.t: Reach the Count's gatepost beyond the east gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o3.r: Upright! Gods and spigots. Do you know how long I have been trying to make a cask that arrives upright? Twelve years. Drink the thing, it is two-thirds full of the Count's best vinegar. I put it there to keep the apprentices honest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.o3.t: Return to Orla Dunmoor with the winning cask
We hit the Count's gatepost. Upright. The hoops held.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.offe: Dunmoor, what is this about a cask race?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.outr: The Harvest Cask Run went to a strange and happy stranger on an upright cask. Orla Dunmoor tells the story every Harvest Day and has stopped mentioning the vinegar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_cask_run.pitc: Harvest Day. Every apprentice in Skingrad rolls a half-empty cask down the Rampart Stair, through the market and out the east gate, and the first to hit the Count's gatepost wins the cask, whatever is in it. I forged the hoops for eleven of them. Ten will be gone by the third turn. The eleventh is mine. I want a runner who will not stop. You.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.desc: Steward Lucan Rilus of Skingrad has lost a page of the Count's ledger bearing four names, one of them a relative. He wants it found and returned unread.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o0.reply: Cut that fine, and with a green seal? Only one hand in Skingrad cuts to the hair. Marro the Quill, who does contracts for people who prefer not to be named. He rents a room above the cooper's on the lower street, and he sleeps in the daytime. I did not tell you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o0.text: Ask the cork-seller Ferro Quinn who handles the Count's tithe paper
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o0.topic: The Steward's ledger is missing a page. Who sells vellum cut that fine in Skingrad?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o1.text: Wait for night, then watch the cooper's upper room
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o2.text: Corner Marro the Quill above the cooper's
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o3.reply: Put him up? Nobody. He ate here twice a week for a year, always in the corner, always paying in new coin from the Count's own mint. I thought he was an inspector. I have been giving him a discount ever since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o3.text: Ask Gaspara Vell who paid for the room
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o3.topic: Marro the Quill had a page. Who put him up at the Two Sisters Lodge?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.c0.la: Give it to the Count. A mint that cheats the Count is worse than a family that does not speak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.c0.re: Then I am glad you are not my sister's lawyer. Take this for the trouble.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.c1.la: Burn it. Let the brother-in-law owe you, and let the mint know someone saw.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.c1.re: That is a more Cyrodiilic answer than I expected. I will keep a copy. Always keep a copy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.reply: Green wax. Of course. The mint's own steward. Then the four names are those who profit from a tithe the Count does not know exists, and one of them is, yes, my brother-in-law. I will take it from here. Though I would like your counsel. If I give this to the Count, my sister loses her husband. If I burn it, I keep what is left of the mint's honesty, and none of it is honest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.text: Return the page to Steward Rilus
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.o4.topic: I have the page. I did not read it. Though I could not help noticing a seal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.offer: Steward Rilus, the page. Tell me what is on it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.outro: Skingrad's ledger has a missing page and a Steward who now sleeps a little better, or a little worse, depending on what he did with it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.pitch: Seventeen years of the Count's tithes, every cask, every fee, every favour, and in the middle of the Harvest Year a single page is gone. I know what was on it because I wrote it. Four lines. Four names. One of them is my own brother-in-law, and I would very much like to know whether I have been writing the lines I think I have been. Find the page. Find who cut it. Do not read it before you bring it to me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_page.title: The Page the Count Removed
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.desc: A column in the Count's Garden Chapel weeps wine at midnight. Brother Gallus wants a witness at the vigil, and an answer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o0.text: Keep vigil at the Garden Chapel after dark
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o1.jour: In the press-house cellar, behind a rack of dry casks, lay a winemaker's skeleton, face down, one hand outstretched toward a door that no longer opened. The ring was on his finger.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o1.text: Search the old press-house cellar the widow spoke of
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o2.repl: Then it is a wedding ring, and a grave, and a widow still waiting by a column. I will bury him at the chapel and say his name at the font. Tonight, the column should stop. Go in peace, and thank you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o2.text: Bring the ring back to Brother Gallus at the chapel
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.o2.topi: I found him in the press-house cellar, and the ring. He did not leave her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.offer: Brother Gallus, you wanted someone for a vigil?
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.outro: The Count's Garden Chapel column does not weep wine any more. Brother Gallus says he misses the taste, and that he has never said a prayer so grateful in his life.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.pitch: One of the columns of the Count's Garden Chapel weeps wine at midnight. It runs down the stone and fills the font, and I have tasted it, and it is very good. It is also terribly sad. I do not mind a miracle. I mind not knowing whose miracle it is. Keep the vigil with me. Tonight. Bring a lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_cyr_sk_widow.title: The Weeping Column
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_a_favour_for_rha: The Prince's cousin Rhal wants a rival's ship delayed in the harbour, without anyone knowing it was done on purpose.
Visit the Senchal Customs House and read the sailing roll
Delay the wool factor, as Rhal asks. A favour is a favour.
Ja'khar scratches a note. "Then the wool will sit three days for a stamp that has been lost. Ja'khar has done worse for less, and not enjoyed it."
Inspect the cousin's ship instead. Let the manifest speak.
Ja'khar's ears go forward with something like joy. "Ah! Ja'khar has wanted to open those barrels for a year. Tell the cousin nothing. Let him find out in public."

Ja'khar takes off his spectacles slowly. "There is always a customs reason, walker. Ja'khar will find one. And he will find, in the same breath, that the cargo of the cousin's own ship is carrying more than its manifest. Which of the two inspections would you like to see happen first?"
Ask Ja'khar when the wool factor's ship will sail
The wool factor's ship. Rhal wants her... slow. Is there a customs reason she might be?

Rhal beams like a man who has already forgotten he asked. "Marvellous! You are an ornament to Senchal. The Prince shall hear of you. Or perhaps he shall hear of me. Either way, you are paid, and I am delighted, and the wool is somebody's problem."
It is done. You will hear about it by evening.
You have the look of a person who might help the Prince's family.
Some favours leave a taste, and some leave a ledger entry. In Senchal it is generally both.

The Prince's cousin! Yes! You are so sharp. Rhal has a very small favour. A rival of his, a wool factor, is about to sail to Rimmen with a cargo that would, shall we say, embarrass Rhal at a banquet. If the ship were simply... slow. A day. Two. Nothing criminal. Just the kind of delay that happens to ships. Rhal would pay.
A Favour for the Prince's Cousin
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_lunar_ledger.des: Mane's Scribe Jaro of Torval cannot make the moon-sugar ledger balance: one blessed cask disappears every lunar cycle between the temple and the Exchange.
Read the tally-stones at the Shrine of the Twin Moons
Wait for night, when the stones record both moons' marks
Drive off the squatters at the Temple of the Purifying Moons
Tell the Mane's Court at once. A theft is a theft.
Ri'dar nods slowly. "Then Shahra will sing it at the hour of Secunda. Loudly. The thief will know before you do. Go with your claws out."
Find the cask first. A quiet thief makes a mistake.
Ri'dar almost smiles. "Good. Quiet. Walk the sugar roads at night, where the casks go. Ri'dar will keep the stone and an empty face."

Ri'dar turns the disc over twice and sets it down very gently, the way one handles a sleeping wasp. "Then it is not the scales. Then it is the road. Or someone who knows the road. Ri'dar will say nothing in the Exchange. Do you want the Mane told, or do you want the cask found first?"
Show Ri'dar the two columns of notches
The temple counts four hundred out. Your scales count three ninety-nine in. Look at the stone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_lunar_ledger.off: Why does a scribe look so unhappy at a column of numbers?
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_lunar_ledger.out: The stone was clear: the road itself had a mouth in it. The only question was who fed it, and where they kept what they swallowed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_lunar_ledger.pit: Because the column is wrong by one, walker. One cask in every moon-cycle, for a year. The temple blesses four hundred, the Exchange receives three hundred ninety-nine. Jaro has checked the scales, the ink, his own eyes. The cask is going somewhere between the shrine and the Exchange, and the road is not long enough to hide a cask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_moon_alignment.d: Ring-Keeper Dar says the moons will align over the third stone of Hakoshae tonight. A lens carried to the tomb below may open it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_moon_alignment.o: Su'ri weighs the lens in her palm and then lets it fall into yours, like trusting a bird. "A hard thing to give. Guardians do not leave the ring, and the lens has never left the ring either. It is your hour now. Mind the line. Mind your breath."
Ask Guardian Su'ri for the Alignment Lens
Dar says the hour is tonight. He says you keep the lens. May I take it?
Wait in the ring until both moons stand over the third stone
Carry the lens's line to the Hakoshae Tombs
Face the Tenant Beneath the Third Stone
Place it in the ring. The next Keeper will need it.
Dar settles the lens into a hollow in the third stone as if it were always meant to go there. "Then it waits. The ring thanks you. So do we all."
Keep it. Another door may open somewhere.
Dar bows his head. "Then you are the Keeper now, a little. Go gently. The moons are not always kind to those who carry their light."

Dar takes the lens, holds it up to the dawn, and sees nothing. "Good. Empty. The line is spent. The moons will not stand over that stone again for a century. Do you wish the lens placed in the ring, to point the way for the next Keeper? Or taken on your road, in case another door opens?"
The tomb is closed again. The tenant is at rest. Here is the lens.
Your ring of stones seems to be watching me.
The ring of moonstones is quiet. The tomb below it has closed its door for a hundred years, and its tenant, at last, rests on the other side of the stone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_moon_alignment.p: It is watching all of us, walker. Once in a long time the moons stand over the same stone, and a tomb below Hakoshae opens for a night. The Guardians keep the key; the Ring-Keeper keeps the hour. This is that hour. Su'ri cannot go alone, for the Guardians do not leave the ring. Take the lens. Hold the line. Carry the light to the tomb.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_nuri_tells_too_m: Nuri the fortune-teller has been paid in sand and is being watched by a rider who claims to know which of her cards is true.
Confront the rider who watches Nuri's tent

Nuri reads the letter and folds it in four with delicate paws. "Ah. A rival. Someone in Rimmen sells fortunes and has lost a customer. Nuri is flattered. Take this card, walker. The Tower. It will not mean what you think. It will mean exactly what you do next."
Tell Nuri what the rider carried
The rider carried a sealed letter. He was paid to see whether your cards ever lie.
The rider's letter is now a bookmark in Nuri's book of true cards, and a Rimmen fortune-teller has an enemy for life.

They are, walker. Nuri told a customer yesterday exactly how he would die, and he paid in a very large bag and left, and the bag was full of sand. Now there is a rider outside the tent who says he knows which of her cards is true. Nuri would prefer to hear it from a better liar than herself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_pattern_from_bel: Master Artisan Kahlil needs a lost seven-strand weaving pattern that is painted on a mural in the Rimmen necropolis. Gatewarden Sira holds the key.

Sira weighs you for a long, quiet moment. "He wants it for a commission. The dead have no commission. But the pattern was woven by one of them, and I think she would like to be seen again. Take the key. Bring it back before the second moon sets, and keep your lamp covered."
Ask Gatewarden Sira for the key to the necropolis
Kahlil wants a pattern from the mural. I would like to look at it, with your leave.
Open the necropolis gate and descend
Gallery Bone
Shroud-Walker
Fight your way through the lower galleries to the mural hall
Face the Weaver Who Would Not Stop at the mural
Give it to Kahlil. A master should wear the cloth of his craft.

Kahlil bows lower than a man of his rank ought. "Then the Prince will have his commission, and every apprentice in Rimmen will learn to weave seven strands as one. You have done Rimmen a great kindness."
Give it to Prince-Advisor Lek, for all seven guilds to share.

Kahlil's mouth tightens, and then he laughs. "Seven guilds will argue over it for a generation. That is how the Weaver died. But it is yours to give, and Kahlil will learn it from the copies like everyone else."
Return it. Hang it back in the dark where the Weaver can see it.
Kahlil closes his eyes. "Foolish. Noble. The sort of thing the dead understand. Very well. Rimmen will weave what it can without it. Kahlil owes you a debt, though he would rather not."

Kahlil reaches for the silk and stops himself, which costs him visibly. "For the Prince's commission. For the guild. For Rimmen, even. Kahlil would like to say for himself, and does not, which you may count as a small virtue. What will you do with what the dead made?"
Take the rubbing to Kahlil, or to whoever deserves it
I have your pattern. Seven strands, one cloth. Before I give it, who is it for?
You have the look of an artisan who has lost something.
The seven strands of the Weaver's pattern are known again, or buried again. Either way Rimmen has an artisan in its debt and a gatewarden who has stopped scowling at you.

Not lost, walker. Mislaid by my teacher's teacher, who took it into the necropolis with him in a funeral shroud. A pattern. A way of weaving seven strands into one cloth that does not tear, and Kahlil has a Prince's commission he cannot fill without it. The pattern is on the necropolis wall, painted by the dead. Only Sira can open the door, and Sira does not like Kahlil. She might like you.
Seven-Strand Aegis
A Pattern from Below
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_bitter_batch: Boiler Tema says someone is tainting finished sugar after the boil. She needs a stranger's tongue to judge three batches and trace the bad one.

Tema watches you chew with the intensity of a cat at a mousehole. "The second. Yes. You see? Sweet, then iron, then a long cold nothing. That batch left Sugar Boil House yesterday on cart-nine for the quay. Find cart-nine."
Taste the three batches Tema sets before you
Three plates, three sugars. I taste them in order. Which one is wrong?
Search Senchal Merchant Square for the nine-wheeled sugar cart

Ja'khar pulls a ledger and reads without hurry. "Nine. Stamped by... Rhal, the Prince's cousin, for a private lading to the black-hulled ship at the Black Kiergo. Ja'khar does not ask what a Prince's cousin carries. It is bad for the lungs."
Ask Ja'khar about cart-nine's customs stamp
Customs-Master, a sugar cart stamped nine passed your quay yesterday. Who paid its toll?
Climb down to the Black Kiergo and watch the black-hulled ship
Dock Enforcer
Confront Zahra the Bitter-Hand, the dealer who taints sugar
Give her the sluice again. She did it because she was afraid.
Tema is quiet. "Then Tema will be afraid for her. A boiler who remembers is a better boiler. You are not a gentle soul, walker, but you are kind."
Turn her in. She sold her vat, and cost a hundred their wits.
Tema nods once, hard. "Then it is done properly. The Customs-Master will be there at dawn. Tema will stir her vats and not look at the fourth floor."

Tema holds the brass token as if it were still hot. "Pali. Fourth floor. Tema trained her. Fed her. She will do it again if no one speaks to her. What should Tema do with a girl who poisoned a thousand sacks for a handful of silver?"
Return Tema's token and tell her what you found
The token was in a vat that was not yours. Zahra paid a boiler to tip a powder in after the boil.
Your arms are burned, but your face looks sicker.
The Bitter Batch was a poison with a name, a face and a price. Senchal's sugar is clean again, and its boilers are warier of strangers who offer silver.

The batch, walker. Third floor, vat Four-Fingers. Every sack she brews tastes right and sits wrong. Dockhands who eat it get slow and sweet-eyed, then they forget where their boats are. It is not my sugar. Tema would taste it blind. Someone is putting something in after the boil, and Tema cannot prove it. She can only make you taste three batches and tell her which one tastes honest.
Tema's Stirring-Paddle
The Bitter Batch
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_borrowed_ban: Rivals from a hill-village stole Orcrest's Claw Gate banner as a prank. Gate-Captain Raz wants a stranger to take it back in the night, quietly.
Scout the hill-village camp in Talon Gulch
Wait for night, when the prank-makers sleep
Take the Claw Gate banner from the rival camp
Slip away from Kasha Hill-Banner, who wakes
Walk up the hill. An old debt is lighter shared.
Raz straightens, almost smiling. "A cask and an apology. And a rematch, at knucklebones, honestly played. Thank you, walker. The gate will be braver for it."
Raise the banner and say nothing. Let the prank be the end of it.
Raz nods, and hoists the banner himself. "Then it flies. And the lads on the hill will know they won, quietly, and so will Raz. That is the nicest kind of war."

Raz looks at the banner a long moment, then at the gate, then, for the first time in your acquaintance, at his own feet. "Knucklebones. Thirty years. Raz cheated, you see. He knew. He has always known. Walker, shall Raz walk up that hill with a cask and an apology, or raise the banner and pretend he has not heard?"
Raise the banner over the Claw Gate
Your banner, whole. The rivals did not do it for malice. They were hoping you would climb the hill to fetch it, and say sorry about the knucklebones.
The Claw Gate banner flies again. A cask went up the hill at dawn with a very polite note, and an old game of knucklebones was, at long last, replayed.

Bare, walker, and Raz will not discuss it in the open air. The Claw Gate banner was lifted in the night by the lads of a hill-village that has never forgiven Orcrest for a lost game of knucklebones. They call it borrowing. Raz calls it a war. He cannot send guards: that makes it a war. A stranger may simply walk in, at night, and walk out again. If the stranger is seen, it was a misunderstanding. If not, it was a miracle.
Tathara's sugar fields were set alight from four corners at once. She does not want to name the neighbours she suspects.
Search the burned fields for the fire-setters' tracks
Catch the arsonists at Hanikhi Outpost

Tathara closes her eyes. "Guessed. Always guessed. The one with the new gate. The one who brought pies at the funeral of the crop. Walker, there will be a reckoning, and it will not be with fire. Tathara will plant again. She will plant it twice as wide, right up to his gate."
Tell Tathara who hired the fire
Four hired hands, paid by a buyer who wanted your land for his own cane. He is a neighbour. You may guess which.
The ash is cold. Whose fire was it?
Tathara's new cane stands close to a neighbour's fence, uncomfortably tall, and sweet as anything.

Not lightning. Not lamp. The fire began in four corners at once, in the dark of the new moon, and the wind that night was from the west, which would have pushed the fire back on itself. Four hands set it. Four people who know Tathara's fields. She does not wish to name them. She would be very happy for you to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_canal_regatt: Someone has been sabotaging Boatman Ajh's pole before the midsummer regatta. He needs a watcher in the boat and an eye on the bridges.
Hide in the boat shed and wait for the saboteur
Catch the pole-saboteur at the canal stairs
Ajh bursts out laughing so hard the boat rocks. "My singing! He sawed my pole because of my singing! Walker, I will win the regatta now just to sing the victory song louder at him."
Tell Ajh who wanted him to lose
The saboteur was paid by a rival boatman who cannot stand your singing. He is caught.
You hum off-key as a duty, Boatman?
Corinthe's regatta was the loudest in years. A boatman sang off-key through all of it, and the sawyer sat in the stands and was forced to listen.

Ajh is the best boatman in Corinthe and the worst singer. At midsummer there is a regatta, and Ajh has entered, and someone has sawn through his pole three nights in a row. Ajh would like to win, but more than winning, Ajh would like to know who is so afraid of a man who hums off-key. Sit in the boat. Watch the bridges. Bring a very sharp eye.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_cask_that_wa: The missing cask leaves a trail of sugar-dust along the caravan road to the Sugar-Slingers' Den. Ma'rish Half-Tail has been lending blessed sugar to strangers.
Follow the sugar-dust trail along Red Hand's Run
Watch the caravan road at night, where the casks change carts
Declare it. The Mane should know a warden was bought.
Jaro unrolls a clean sheet. "Then it is written. Shahra will have a new verse by moonrise, and Ri'dar a long night. Torval will remember you kindly, and him less so."
Burn the page. Ma'rish is dead, and the road is honest again.
Jaro feeds the page to the lamp. "Then the ledger balances at last, and nobody will know why. Ri'dar will weigh honest for the rest of his life, out of fright. That is not nothing."

Jaro reads three lines and goes grey to the ears. "The Purring Ledger's tab-book. Ma'tisha's own hand. But the pawprints here are not hers, walker; they are Ri'dar's. Or they are very cleverly Ri'dar's. What does one do with a thief who is also the man who counted for him?"
Here is where the cask went. All four hundred of them, one a moon.
One cask per moon had walked all the way from the temple to a den in the dunes. The ledger now balances, and what that cost is for the chooser to carry.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_cub_who_read: Cub-runner Tazhi accidentally read a sealed note ordering a cask moved past a bribed warden. She asks a stranger to return it unread.

Jaro takes the note and for a moment says nothing. Then, under his breath: "A cub. A cub, who read it. She is a very honest child, to return it. Walker, the note is not a thing the Court would like to have been read. Tazhi has done right. Jaro will see she is looked after, and a very good, very quiet apprenticeship found."
Return the note to Mane's Scribe Jaro, resealed
The cub dropped this. The seal has been mended. I did not read it.

Tazhi's ears flatten with relief, and then rise slowly, slowly. "A scribe! Tazhi has always wanted to be a scribe! But Tazhi will not read any more notes. Not even by accident. Tazhi will sneeze into a handkerchief, like a lady."
You did right. The scribe is looking after you. Say nothing, and you will be a scribe yourself one day.
You are a runner of messages.
A cub of Torval has an apprenticeship at the Lunar Ledger, and a handkerchief, and a great deal of respect for wax.

Runner, yes! Tazhi has read none of them. All of them. A very long one, today, from the Court to the Exchange, sealed with wax. Tazhi did not break it. The seal broke by itself, when Tazhi sneezed. The note inside says: move the cask at midnight, and the warden will not look. Tazhi did not understand it. Then Tazhi did. Tazhi does not wish to be a cub who knew. Please carry it back, sealed, and say nothing.
The Cub Who Read the Ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_dead_pay_no_: Tamhir's cellar has a silent visitor: a long-dead tenant of the old tomb-vestibule under the Sugar Bowl. The Masterworks may know what it wants.

Kahlil rolls his eyes and finds a ledger anyway. "A tomb-mason's wife, Mirra-jo. The mason ran off with a Baandari caravan and left her under the floor of a half-built vault. The roll says she wanted a roof over her. Not her grave. A roof. Her grave is fine. It is the roof that leaks."
Ask Kahlil in the Masterworks who the tomb-vestibule was built for
The cellar under the Sugar Bowl has a dead tenant. Do the masons keep a roll of who is buried there?
Fetch the lead-and-tile roofing the Masterworks keeps for the dead
Return to the Sugar Bowl cellar after dark

Tamhir covers his heart with both paws. "Water the wine! After this? She will be the first guest to leave a tip. Walker, the Sugar Bowl owes you a night, a bed, and a cup of the good stuff, which is the stuff that is not the house wine."
Tell Tamhir the cellar will be dry by morning
The tenant is satisfied. The roof is mended. She asks that you do not water the wine.
Is something wrong with the wine again, Tamhir?
A tomb-mason's wife has her roof at last, and the Sugar Bowl's cellar has never been so well kept. Tamhir swears the wine tastes better, and has never again been seen to water it.

No, walker, worse. The wine is fine. It is the cellar. Every night something sits at the end of the cellar and does not drink, just stares at the barrels. Tamhir has been to the Masterworks on the cliff, where the tomb-masons come up for air, and they say it is a prior tenant. The cellar was a tomb-vestibule once. The tenant has been complaining of damp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_dry_season.d: Cistern-Keeper Mala says a barrel is stolen from Orcrest's Third Cistern every fourth night, with no leak and no mark.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_dry_season.o: Inspect the rooftop cisterns of Orcrest
Hide in the Third Cistern's shaft until the water-thief comes
Follow the wet rope-marks to the Scar and recover the cracked seal
Corner Thirst-Lord Zadhir in Talon Gulch

Raz looks at the seal for a long time. "Sold back. To us. Water we owned." He does not smile, but his jaw does something close. "Mala was right. Raz will say it once. Mala was right. The Gate will open a morning early for you, any time, any day."
Show Raz the cracked seal and tell him of the thief
The water was being hauled out through a cut in the seal by a thief who sells it back to you. Zadhir is dead.
Your cisterns look full to me.
Orcrest's Third Cistern stays full. Mala keeps counting. Raz, grudgingly, keeps a chair for her at the Gate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_dry_season.p: They look full, walker. But Mala has counted every drop for thirty years, and the Third Cistern is lower by a barrel every fourth night. There is no leak. Mala has been down the shaft with a torch and a rope. Something is taking it, cleanly, the way a cat takes cream. Raz will not believe it. Raz believes only what he can hit.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_gardens_bees: Gardener-Priest Mura says the Garden Cathedral's oldest queen bee has been carried off to the hornet-haunted arch above the canals.
Climb to Khenarthi's Arch above the canals
Kill the Hornet-Queen that has taken the old queen's hive
Take the queen cell from the hornet nest
Put her in the Cathedral's hive, where she was born.
Mura nods. "The old way. The hive will remember her, and she will remember it. The eleven quiet ones will sing again by Fredas."
Split the cell. Let the eleven quiet hives each have a share.
Mura laughs, startled. "Eleven queens from one! The old priests would have fainted. It is a risk, and a good one. Walker, you think like a beekeeper."

Mura's veil trembles. "Wake? She will wake where she is welcomed. Put her in the hive nearest the bell, and bless her with the first honey of the morning. There are eleven hives that need her more than I need to say thank you."
Carry the queen cell to Mura without jostling it
The old queen's cell, whole. Where would you like it to wake?
The Garden Cathedral hums again. The first honey of the season has a faint taste of something that no flower in Corinthe has ever worn.

They are not unhappy, walker. They are quiet. Three hundred hives of the Garden Cathedral, and eleven of them have fallen silent in a week. A quiet hive is a hive without a queen. The Cathedral's oldest queen was carried out by a stranger in the night, and Mura thinks the stranger took her to the old arch above the canals, where the wild hornets nest. Bring her back, or at least bring back what she was carrying.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_gate_that_hu: Scout Sihe hears a deep note under Orcrest every dry-wind night. She wants someone to listen from the old shrine to Lorkhaj.
Listen for the hum at the shrine to Lorkhaj
Wait for the dry wind to rise after dusk
Silence what drums beneath the plateau in the Bone Pit

Sihe tilts her ears and stays very still for a long moment. "Nothing. The Gate is quiet. Sihe has not heard the plateau be quiet since she was a cub. It is... lonely. Thank you, walker. Sihe will miss it, which is not at all what she expected."
Tell Sihe the hum has stopped
A drum-priest was beating the dead beneath the plateau. The note is gone. Listen.
The Claw Gate no longer hums at night, and Sihe, who could hear it from the top of the world, has begun to sleep in the afternoons.

The Gate, walker. Hear it? On the first night of the dry wind, the Claw Gate hums. Raz says it is the stone cooling. Sihe was born in the watchtower. It is not the stone. It is a note, and the note is under the plateau, and every time it sounds the sand on the south road shivers, as if there is a drum beneath it. Go to the shrine to Lorkhaj on the edge of the mesa. It is the oldest hearing-place Sihe knows.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_hand_you_wer: Ma'tir of the Twin Moons keeps losing moon-phase wagers because a Rimmen rider feeds her false almanac phases.
Wait at the Twin Moons until the almanac-rider arrives
Stop the rider and take his bribed almanac
Ma'tir snatches the almanac and checks it against the sky out the window. "WRONG! By a whole phase! Ha! Ha! He has been fleecing me for a year, and I have been blaming the sky!"
Tell Ma'tir the almanac was bribed
The rider's almanac was pencilled wrong on purpose. Here is a true one.
You keep losing to the sky, Keeper.
Ma'tir now wins her moon-phase wagers about one night in three, and says it is a disgrace to the sky.

Every time, walker! Every wager. Tonight is the full of Masser and the new of Secunda, and Ma'tir has put her whole cellar on it being the other way round. She is a very bad gambler and a very honest one. A rider from Rimmen has been telling the house a different phase every night. Ma'tir thinks he has been bribing the almanac. Please follow him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_knot_that_is: One knot in Wheel-Master Khir's toll-tally is tied by a stranger's hand. He wants the cart behind it found.

Hajir looks left, right, and then at his barrel. "A cart. With a cloth over it. Every ninth night, gone by dawn. Hajir sold its driver three cups, and he paid with a coin so old it had a prince on it who is not a prince any more."
Ask Water-Seller Hajir who passes the hub at night
A blue-thread knot on Khir's tally. Who passes the hub after the Wheel-Master has gone to bed?
Stand watch at the hub of the Wheel until the cloth-covered cart appears
Stop the cloth-covered cart at the Sugar Stack Mart

Khir stares at the coin you give him and for once says nothing. "Old Prince's coin. Khir's own father took those. The knot was Khir's father's way of tying. He taught it to a nephew. The nephew... Walker, it seems the Wheel has been paying a debt that Khir did not know he owed."
Tell Khir who tied the blue knot
The knot was tied by a hauler who pays you in old coin to keep the hub quiet. He is stopped.
Something is wrong with your toll-tally.
The blue knot is still in Khir's tally. He says he will leave it there to remember by.

You see it too! One knot, walker. Blue thread, tied right-over-left. Khir ties left-over-right, always, since he was a cub. Someone has tied a toll that Khir did not take, for a cart Khir did not see. A hundred knots, and one of them is not his. Find the cart that paid a toll that was never collected.
The Knot That Is Not Khir's
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_lost_pilgrim: Pilgrim Ke has not returned from the Shrine of the Crescent, and Hamza fears the worst.
Search the Shrine of the Crescent for Pilgrim Ke
Drive off the bandits who have made camp at the shrine
Escort Pilgrim Ke back to Hakoshae
Your seventeenth bed is empty tonight.
Ke was found asleep in a bandit's bedroll, quite content, with a bandit's hat on. He says he has begun a third lap. Hamza says that is a lie.

It is, walker, and Hamza does not like it. Ke the pilgrim left four days ago for the Shrine of the Crescent. He always returns the same night, because he walks in loops. He has not. Ke is a gentle fool, and the road to the shrine is not gentle.
The Pilgrim Who Would Not Finish
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_lunar_champi: Prince-Advisor Lek wants an unbought stranger to win this year's challenge at the Hall of the Lunar Champion, so that none of the rival factions gains the pillar.
Enter the challenge at the Hall of the Lunar Champion
Defeat the Baandari duellist Ri'zhar Never-Lost
A road-pass. Rimmen's caravan roads, unquestioned, for a year.
Lek writes it in a clean hand and seals it with a ring. "A road is a good thing to want. It is nearly the same as a friend."
Nothing. Let the pillar be what it is.
Lek stares. Then, slowly, bows with all the grace his office allows. "That is the rarest answer in this city. The pillar is yours, and the Prince shall hear of you."

Lek tilts his head, calculating. "None. That is exactly the thing. The nephew will sulk, the Baandari will bow, and Torval will send a very large cat to be offended. Walker, name one thing Rimmen can do for you that a banner would have bought, and we shall pretend we are friends."
Tell Lek the pillar bears your name
It is done. The pillar says what I am. Whose banner do I carry in this?
The Prince's advisor wants a champion of his own, I hear.
The pillar bears a stranger's name for a year. Three factions grumbled, and one advisor slept very well.

Not for himself, walker. For the Hall of the Lunar Champion. Every Midyear the hall sets a challenge, and the winner's name is cut into the pillar. This year the other three challengers are the Prince's nephew, a Baandari duellist who has never lost, and a very large cat from Torval. Lek would very much like none of them to win, for reasons of diplomacy. You are a stranger, which is to say, unbought.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_missing_cara: Seven wagons of a Dune caravan never reached the Temar oasis. Camel-Driver Mizra wants to know what happened to them, and to her cousin, the eighth driver.
Check Nevoe Oasis, the first water on the Temar road
Follow the wheel-ruts to Teal Campsite
Find the eighth driver's bell among the wagons
Oasis Poacher
Clear the poachers off Temar Oasis
Zhirr's Digger
Face Zhirr the Oasis-Snatcher, who dammed the well
Tell the Wheel what Zhirr did. Let Khir hunt his gang.
Mizra nods. "Then every cart on the Wheel will remember. The Wheel-Master will send riders. There will be a day of drums for the eight."
Keep the story quiet. The families have grieved enough.
Mizra wipes her eyes with her wrist. "Then it stays with the bell. A kindness, and a hard one. Take the road-pass; no toll on any lane, for as long as Mizra drives."

Mizra holds the bell to her ear and nothing rings. "He tied it. The fool tied it so the wagons would not wake the thieves. It cost him his life and saved the camels. Mizra will carry it to the Wheel and hang it at the eighth lane. The Eighth Spoke is named for him, you know. Nobody remembers."
Bring the bell back to Mizra
Your cousin's bell. Zhirr dammed the well and let the caravan die of thirst. Your cousin tied the clapper so the bell wouldn't call him back.
You are a driver who has lost wagons.
Seven wagons and an eighth driver went to their rest at last, and a bell with a tied clapper hangs where only camel-drivers look.

Seven, walker. Left the Wheel ten days ago for the Temar oasis, and the oasis never saw them. Mizra drove that road for twenty years. Between here and there the only things that kill a caravan are thirst, bandits and a very bad mood, and none of those leave no bodies. Find them. Find the eighth driver, who is Mizra's cousin, and who always carried a bell.
Bell-Silent Bow
The Missing Caravan
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_missing_star: A star-chart showing a rumoured seventh moon has vanished from the star-haven lectern. The Starlight Adeptorium may know who wanted it.
Ask at the Starlight Adeptorium who copies star-charts in silver ink
Catch the copyist on the Saimisil Steppes

Zhazir unfolds the chart and stares at the faint pencil moon for a long time. "Seven. Not six. Not two plus a ghost. Seven. His tutor was not mad. Zhazir will not say this to the cubs. He will only look at the sky and count."
Your chart. The copyist sold copies to three rival adeptoria. The seventh moon is the same in each. It seems not to be a joke.
A seventh moon waits in pencil under the winter stars. Zhazir counts it every night, though no one else will say they see it.

They are. Three hundred and nine. Walker, a star-chart of the winter sky has left the lectern, and with it the only record Zhazir has of the seventh moon, which his old tutor swore appeared once in a century above the Starlight Adeptorium. The chart did not walk. It was taken. Someone with a very good hand for silver ink.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_naming_under: A Hakoshae cub must be named under both moons. Guardian Su'ri asks a stranger to carry the charm to the Temple of the Hidden Moon for its blessing.

Su'ri sets the charm in your palm with great care, and looks away, as one does from a thing that is not hers to see. "Two moons, two crescents, one thread. Say the name of the cub when both stand over the door. Do not say it before, and do not say it after. A name said at the wrong hour goes looking for someone else."
Take the unblessed charm from Su'ri
I will carry it. Tell me the words of the blessing.
Carry the charm to the Temple of the Hidden Moon
Wait in the temple for both moons to stand over the door
Name her for the road: Ja'hira, 'she who returns'.
Su'ri closes her eyes and says it over, very softly, three times. "Ja'hira. She who returns. It is a good name, and a brave one. Walker, Hakoshae will say it at every doorway."
Name her for the stone: Ri'sha, 'she who waits'.
Su'ri smiles into her collar. "Ri'sha. The ring keeps those who wait. It is a gentle name. The mother will weep, and the cub will sleep."

Su'ri takes the charm, and her voice is very low. "Warm. It is warm. The name took. Walker, the mother asks one thing: that the cub's second name be given by you. A cub with a stranger's second name is never lost on a road. What shall it be?"
Return the blessed charm to Su'ri
The moons stood over the door. I said the cub's name. The charm is warm. Tie it to her wrist.
Your spear is garlanded with ribbon.
A cub of Hakoshae bears two names, one from her mother and one from a stranger who held a charm and said nothing at the wrong hour.

It is a night for it, walker. A Hakoshae cub is to be named under both moons, and the rite wants a witness who is no kin and has no stake. The mother is ill. The charm has not been blessed. The blessing must be done at the Temple of the Hidden Moon, at the hour both moons stand over its door, and it must be done by a pair of hands that have not held a weapon since dusk. Su'ri cannot lay down her spear. Will you carry the charm?
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_netch_balloo: Balloonist Q'ri will trade a ride for a true story she has never heard. The Hill of Shattered Swords might provide one.
Walk the Hill of Shattered Swords and see what it says
Find the Shrine of the Cats Divine

Q'ri puts down her cup and stares. "Hums? She has been to the hill, and never once heard it hum. It hums for those who walk it. She will give you a ride, walker. And Q'ri will go walk the hill herself. That is the best thing you could have given her: a reason to go."
There is a hill planted with broken swords, and a shrine of giant cats watching it. The swords hum when the wind passes.
Is that a netch you fly?
Q'ri took the long way round to the hill, and did not come back for a week. She says it hums quite beautifully.

A balloon, walker. Grown from a netch's sac. Q'ri trades rides for stories, and she is out of stories she has not told. So: Q'ri will give you a ride to anywhere you like, if you bring her one story that she has never heard. Something that happened. Not something you made up. She can tell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_pear_that_wa: Matron Zhel's extinct white pear is being sold as cuttings in Valenwood, though she never kept one. Someone stole it from her grafting-book.
Ask after the pear at the Halls of Colossus, where the branch was found
Clear the machines that guard the colossus hall
Recover the pilgrim's cog, which hides the grafting notes
Catch Orlin Quick-Shears, the grafting-book thief
Put my name on it. Corinthe should know the pear's true grafter.
Zhel sniffs, moved. "A small tag, then. 'Gift of a stranger'. It will be printed on every crate."
Hide it in your book again. Some pears are meant to be rare.
Zhel closes the book with great gentleness. "Rare. Yes. That is the word the pilgrim used, too."

Zhel unfolds the notes with trembling fingers. "Every season at once. Zhel did not know the pilgrim wrote it down. Walker, you have brought back a recipe, not a pear. It is the better gift. Do you want your name on the first branch, or should Zhel hide it, as hiding has been her way?"
Bring Zhel the cog and the news
The pear was copied from your grafting-book by Orlin. I found the pilgrim's original notes, too.
Your grafting-book is locked. Is something missing from it?
A pear that tastes of every season is a secret of Corinthe again, or a gift for all of Pellitine. Zhel's book, at least, is safe.

A pear, walker. A white pear that does not exist in any orchard in Pellitine. Twenty years ago Zhel grafted it from a branch a Khajiit pilgrim brought down from the Halls of Colossus, and it fruited once, and tasted of every season at once. Then the tree died. Someone has been selling cuttings in Valenwood as "Corinthe white". Zhel did not sell them. Zhel did not keep a cutting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_purring_ledg: Ma'tisha of the Purring Ledger wants a cup of moon-sugar-wine carried unspilled from Torval to the Hall of the Lunar Champion in Rimmen, across a road that does not like cups.
Carry the cup across the sandy road to the Sugar Bowl at Rimmen
Do not rest. Arrive after dusk, when the cup is coldest
Set the cup at the feet of the Lunar Champion's statue

Ma'tisha laughs until she has to hold the bar. "A statue drank some! Then the caravan-master owes ME. Eleven tabs wiped, and one drink on the house for as long as you live, walker. Ma'tisha means it, which is the terrible part."
Tell Ma'tisha the cup arrived whole
The cup arrived. Not a drop spilled. A statue drank some, though.
Your tab-book looks heavier than it should be.
Eleven tabs were wiped clean in Torval that evening, and one stranger was entered in the Purring Ledger with no paw-print at all, which is the highest honour the house gives.

Ah, a clever one. Ma'tisha took a wager, you see. With a caravan-master from Rimmen. Whoever carries a full cup of moon-sugar-wine from the Purring Ledger to the Hall of the Lunar Champion in Rimmen, without spilling a drop and without a drop of help, wins eleven tabs wiped clean. Ma'tisha is too round to run. You are not.
The Wager of the Purring Ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_resealed_cas: A cask of blessed moon-sugar was opened and badly resealed in Senchal. Dar'jazad wants the culprit found before the Moon-Priests notice.

Ja'khar sets down his stamp. "A cask with a pried seal. Stamped by the Warden of the cask-store, one night, Tuesday. A cat with a scar and a very good alibi. Ja'khar has no evidence. He has a strong suspicion, and a tidy mind."
Ask Customs-Master Ja'khar which cart carried the cask
A blessed cask passed your quay with a broken seal. Whose cart?
Search the Forgotten Mane, where the cask-store keeps its overflow
Take down the Cask-Warden and recover the stolen share
Say a thief. The skooma lord can wait.
Dar'jazad nods. "A thief, then. A small lie. It will keep the temple calm, and the lord complacent. We shall see which of us is cleverer."
Tell the whole tale. The temple deserves to know.
Dar'jazad exhales. "The whole tale. Then there will be a reckoning, and it will be loud. But the moons love a plain truth, and Senchal has been quiet too long."

Dar'jazad turns the cask once and sets it in the lamplight. "The seal is mended. The share is returned. Walker, the Warden is dead, and the Moon-Priests will ask who. Shall Dar'jazad say a thief, or tell the whole tale of the skooma lord, and let the temple deal with it?"
Your cask, whole. The Warden took a share to sell to a skooma lord. It is returned.
Dar'jazad has a cask that should not be here.
A blessed cask was returned to its temple with the seal repaired, and a very quiet skooma lord in Senchal now sleeps rather badly.

Not here, no, and not like this, walker. The Moon-Priests' seal is on it, and the seal has been pried and mended with wax. A blessed cask is not to be opened except at the Temple. Someone opened it, took a share, and resealed it badly. Dar'jazad cannot return it to the temple unless the thief is found. A priest's wrath is a gentle thing, until it is not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_sand_sworn_w: The eighth driver's bell started something. A bone-pale warden has risen in the dunes north of Dune to demand the toll that his own prince promised him a thousand years ago.
Cross the Hill of Shattered Swords where the warden is said to walk
Wait for night. The warden walks only by moonlight
Put the Sand-Sworn Warden to rest

Khir presses the tally to his chest. "A toll. A thousand years. And you paid it. The Wheel has never been so quiet. Take this coin. It is the first copper ever struck for the Great Market. Khir has no right to keep it."
Tell Khir the warden is at rest
A warden walked the dunes demanding a toll the prince promised. I paid it in the only coin he understood.
The warden's toll is settled. The Great Market Wheel turns, and the eight lanes are quiet at night.
The Wheel That Would Not Turn
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_stolen_route: Route-Master Ha'bir's Baandari route book was stolen. A fence at Nekha Camp is the likeliest buyer.
Find the fence at Nekha Camp
Take the route book from the fence

Ha'bir counts the pages with his thumb and breathes out slowly. "Three copied. Three pages. Ha'bir will change those wells by morning. A route book is only a gift to the person who does not know the road has changed. Walker, the Baandari clans owe you a road-name."
Your book, whole. The fence had not yet sold it. He had copied three pages.
A route book is a heavy loss for a trader.
Three pages of the route book had to be made false, and a Baandari clan now has a name, in a code that only they can read, for the person who brought the book home.

It is worth a clan, walker. It lists every well, every ambush and every price. Ha'bir does not ask for the thief's head. He asks that you take back the book before someone sells a Baandari route to a rival clan. There is a camp west of here, Nekha, where bad men buy and good men look the other way.
Court Singer Shahra has lost her voice for the hour when neither moon is up. She must find the first singers of that hour, buried in the ossuary east of Torval.
Travel to the Tenarr Zalviit Ossuary
Quiet the restless dead of the ossuary
Silence the Hollow Choirmaster who sings the hour wrongly
Sing it the old verse yourself, Shahra. It remembers you.
Shahra stands. Her voice is rough, then clear, then terrible and lovely. The lamps in the Court gutter and steady. "There. It sang back. You are in the song now, walker, in the second line."
Let it rest. Choose a new hour, one nobody owns.
Shahra bows her head. "A sad answer. A good one. There is an hour at dawn that no one has ever sung. Shahra will have it, and give you the first verse."

Shahra's hand goes to her throat, and then she laughs once, low. "A conductor. Of course. Someone made the hour sing for them. Then the hour had nothing left for me. Will you teach it back its own song? Or shall Shahra take a new hour and let that one lie?"
Tell Shahra what you found in the ossuary
The first singers of the dark hour are not at rest. Someone has been conducting them.
You sing the hours. Is one of them giving you trouble?
The ossuary's dead were conducting themselves, in the end, by habit. Shahra has her voice, and the hour of the held breath has a verse for you.

One hour, walker. The hour when neither moon is up. Shahra has sung it every night for nine years, and last week she opened her mouth and nothing came. Not stage-fright. Nothing. The old song-keepers say the hour has to be paid for, with a verse, to the dead who first sang it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_els_the_wind_pays_fo: Zhaleh's inn, the Sweet Breezes, loses a window every night at the same hour. She suspects the culprit is no wind at all.
Keep watch in the third-floor room until the window breaks
Catch the intruder who climbs in through the bay window

Zhaleh blinks and then bursts into delighted laughter. "The wind is innocent! I have been scolding it for a month! I have been leaving it apologies on the sill! Walker, you have saved a poor old sea-breeze its good name."
Tell Zhaleh who was breaking the glass
It was a rope-climbing burglar in a bay-window-sized hurry. The wind is innocent.
The Sweet Breezes' bay window is whole, and a wind that had never done anything wrong now gets a saucer of milk on the sill each evening.

The ninth this winter, walker, and every one of them on the third floor, and every one of them at the same hour. The wind does not do that. Wind is a coward. It comes in whichever hole it finds. This one comes in at the same bay window, in the same shape, with a smell of old rope. I would wager my best pillow someone is coming through that window, and someone has been, for nine nights.
The Wind That Pays for Glass
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_ladys_unwearable: Lady Mei has a bolt of white cloth that will not hold a fold. She asks a stranger to carry it to an old weaver at the Black Lacquer Pagoda.
Carry the bolt to the old weaver at the Black Lacquer Pagoda
Drive off the Tsaesci who have taken the weaver's loft

Mei sits very still. "A person who has not yet come. Three hundred years. And I have been trying to sell it to people who already have. Stranger, I shall hang it in the window, and let it wait. If it was meant for you, you will know. Try it on. It will not hold a fold. But it will not fall off, either."
Return to Mei and tell her what the weaver said
The weaver said: the cloth is not wrong. It was woven for a person who has not yet come. It will not fold until it is worn by them.
You are looking at my cloth as if it were a riddle.
A bolt of white cloth hangs in a window in Tiger Plains, unfolded and unworn. The weaver at the pagoda has begun to expect a visitor.

It is, stranger. Mei weaves cloth that can be worn only one way, and in three hundred years, no foreigner has worn it correctly. She has begun to wonder if the cloth wishes to be worn differently. She has a bolt of white that she cannot sell, because it will not hold a fold. It refuses. She would like you to take it to the old weaver at the black lacquer pagoda, who may know why.
The Cloth That Cannot Be Worn
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_saarviks_barnacl: Factor Hjoldis of Dawnstar wants a captain's chart from under the hull of a wreck at Saarvik Landing on the Atmoran coast.
Sail to Saarvik Landing on the Atmoran coast
Clear the draugr crew that still guard the wreck
Take the barnacled chart from under the hull
Sail for it. A map is for following.
Hjoldis laughs aloud. "Then we sail. Hjoldis has not been out of Dawnstar in thirty years. She will need a coat. She will need two."
Hang it. Let the mystery be the reward.
Hjoldis smiles slowly. "Wise. A map you do not follow is a map you can keep. It will hang above my desk, and I will look at it every morning, and be very happy."

Hjoldis spreads the chart and for a moment says nothing at all. "A coast. A harbour. A mountain with a name. Stranger, there is a country on this map that no one has named since the world was young. And at the mark in red there is a word: HOME. Shall I sail for it, or shall I hang it on my wall, and let it keep being a mystery?"
Bring the chart back to Hjoldis
The chart was where you said. It shows a coast I do not know, with a mark in a red that is not ink.
Your map has a very large blank.
A chart from the oldest ship in the world hangs in a counting-house in Dawnstar, or leads a ship north. Either way it has finally been read.

It does, and Hjoldis would like it filled. A captain of the old ships, Saarvik, left a chart under the hull of his wreck at Saarvik Landing. A barnacled thing, in oilskin. It records a coast no Nord has seen since the First Era. Hjoldis does not ask for the treasure it may lead to. She only wants the map, intact, and your word that you will not use it before she does. The ice is cold, the wind is vile, and the ships are very old.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_ansei_hall_r: Scholar-Captain Anwar of Sentinel wants someone to reach the Hall of the Ansei in Yokuda and report whether the rumours of the Sword-Singers' record are true.
Reach the Hall of the Ansei across the Yokudan desert
Drive off the sand-wraiths that guard the hall

Anwar takes it with a shaking hand. He is old, so very old. Then he laughs, the laugh of a man who has been unexpectedly released. "Blank! A whole life for a blank scroll. Stranger, it is the best answer I could have had. The Singers still sing. Somewhere. Anwar will put down his pen. For the first time in forty years, he will sit in the sun."
Tell Anwar what the Hall holds
The Hall holds a library of one scroll. It is blank. Beneath it is a note: 'The Sword-Singers took the record with them. Ask the ones who still sing.'
You are looking for a very old thing.
A scholar who spent forty years chasing a rumour has put down his pen. The Sword-Singers sing on, somewhere past the edge of every chart.

Forty years, stranger. A rumour in an archive, and a shred of a chart. The Hall of the Ansei, on an island in a desert sea. It is said to hold the last true record of the Sword-Singers. Anwar is too old for the voyage. He is not too old for the questions. Go. See what is there. Tell him whether the stories are true. If they are, he will die happy. If they are not, he will die informed.
What the Hall of the Ansei Remembers
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_final_lesson: Master Sahar wishes to be beaten fairly by his best student, Jai, but cannot ask. He wants a stranger to spar with Jai and draw out the fourth stance.

Sahar sets down his cup. "The first stance is waiting. The second is cutting. The third is listening, which most never learn. The fourth is the one you invent. Take this chalk. When you spar with Jai, he will use all four. Do not be afraid of his rage. It is the only honest thing about him."
Receive the three stances from Sahar
Teach me. I will carry your Way to the student who needs it.
Spar with Jai until he draws the fourth stance
Stay. A teacher is never finished.

Sahar laughs, a very small, very old laugh. "Never finished. No. Very well. I shall teach until the sand tells me otherwise. And Jai will teach beside me. And the courtyard will have two masters, and neither will be sure which is the student."
Rest. The Way has a new keeper.

Sahar nods and closes his eyes. The pale figure on the bench rises, and for the first time, speaks one word: 'Good.' Sahar takes his hand. They sit together on the highest bench, and are, quite gently, no longer there.

Sahar is silent for a very long time. Then, slowly, he bows to you, and then to the empty bench where the ghost sits, and then, at last, to the sand. "Then the Way is passed. Not to Jai. Not to you. To the sand. Stranger, it will be there for the next student. Shall I stay, and teach, or go with the ghost, and rest?"
Tell Sahar what the fourth stance was
Jai drew the fourth. It was not the stance of any master I know. It was his own. He won. Then he sat down, and wept.
You have the stillness of someone who has had to wait.
The sword-courtyard of Yokuda has two masters now, or none. The sand bears no print of the fourth stance. It will be invented again.

A little. Stranger, the Way is passed from master to student, and from student to the next. Sahar has taught for sixty years. Jai is his best, and the angriest, and the Way will die with them unless one of them learns what the other knows. Sahar is old. He wishes to be beaten, and to know it was fair. He cannot ask Jai. Jai will take it as an insult. You are a stranger. Spar with Jai. Lose, if you must. Win, if you can. But make him use the fourth stance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_flagship.des: Coast-Watcher Caelir asks a stranger to infiltrate the Maormer flagship at night and free an Altmer scholar held in a brine tank.
Row to the raft-city by night
Wait until the fleet is dark and the watch changes
Slip past the Warden-of-the-Hold and take the coral key
Row the freed scholar back to Firsthold before dawn
Tell the Dominion. The island should be known.
Caelir nods slowly. "Then it is known. A thing that is known can be defended, or conquered. It is out of our hands. Thank you for the honesty."
Keep it between you. A secret kept is a life saved.
Caelir breathes out. "A secret. Yes. Between us two, and one scholar who forgets. It will be the loneliest knowledge in Tamriel. But it will be ours."

Caelir listens, and for a long moment does not move. "The Queen's hidden island. He knows where it is. Stranger, that is a dangerous thing. The Dominion would pay for it. The Maormer would kill for it. And Caelir would very much like to keep him alive until he forgets. What shall we do?"
Tell Caelir the captive is free
The scholar is free. He talked the whole way. He knows where the Queen's hidden island is.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_flagship.off: You have been looking at the sea for some time.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_flagship.out: A scholar was carried out of the Maormer fleet in a rowing boat, talking all the way. Whether the Queen's island is known to the Dominion or only to two, it is no longer safe.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_flagship.pit: Twelve years, and tonight is the first night the Admiral's fleet has been alone. Her flagship has a hold. In the hold, in a brine tank, there is a captive. An Altmer scholar, they say, who knew too much about the Queen's own island. Caelir wants him out. Not for the Dominion. For her own sake. She is tired of knowing what she knows, and doing nothing. A small boat. A dark night. A key, if you can find one. The Admiral sleeps lightly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_for_the_heart_of_the: The Plague of Thras spreads from the Coral Tower. Plague-Diver Ooma wants a stranger to dive to the heart of the reef and carry it out.
Reach the Coral Tower of Thras
Fight through the infected coral to the heart chamber
Defeat the Reef-Tyrant that guards the heart
Make the cure. The living should come first.
Ooma bows her head. "Then it will be done. It will be painful. It will be necessary. And I shall say a word for the heart, in the language of the pools. Thank you."
Return it. Let the reef take its own course.
Ooma nods slowly. "A hard answer. A kind one. The Plague will go on, and the heart will rest. Perhaps that is what the pools wanted all along."

Ooma presses it to her chest, and for a moment, she is quiet. "Afraid. Of course. A heart that has been in a tower for a thousand years does not wish to be carried out. Stranger, shall I make the cure, and kill it? Or shall I return it, and let the Plague take what it will?"
The heart. It pulses. It is afraid. It does not wish to be carried further.
You have the look of someone about to dive.
The heart of the reef was carried out of the Coral Tower, and whether it was used or returned, the polyps of Thras have turned, a little, toward the light.
