story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o1.journa: The inspector came, ate three bowls, and could not stop staring at the sign. He did not leave a tip. He left an apology.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o1.text: Bring the Council inspector to the pot for an honest tasting
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o2.reply: Then we have both survived an honest day. I will name a stew for you. Do not ask which one; it is the one nobody orders.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.o2.topic: The inspector has withdrawn the fine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.offer: You look like you have eaten somewhere worse than here.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.outro: The sign still has a rat on it. It now has a very small crown.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.pitch: There was a rat. It's on the sign. Last week a Council inspector found the sign, found the rat, and fined me for 'advertising a pest.' Prove the rat is a mascot, not a menace. The fine is nine drakes a day and my tolerance for this is limited.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_rat.title: The Rat in the Pot, Honestly
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.desc: Brarmin the egg-miner hears a tune rising from the tunnels beneath the Skar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o0.jou: The wrong third note comes from a row of clay pipes set into the wall, tuned to the wind. Somebody has built a flute that plays the whole shell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o0.tex: Follow the three-note tune down into the old egg tunnels
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o1.tex: Silence what has gathered to listen
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o2.rep: Then it was a prank by dead masons, and it will ring on the ninth day of every Sun's Dusk. I shall hang a bell in the cellar. If it chimes the third note, I will whistle the right one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.o2.top: Pipes in the wall. A tune only the wind could play.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.offer: You do not whistle, do you? Say you do not whistle.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.outro: The shell sings on certain nights, and everyone in Ald'ruhn now knows the proper third note.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.pitch: The shell has ribs, sera, and the ribs have hollows, and the hollows hum when the wind is right. Last night a new note came up through the floor of my cellar. Not a hum. A tune. Three notes, and the third was wrong. I do not like a song I have not been taught.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_ald_tunnel.title: Whistle Not Under the Shell
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.desc: The ledgers burned. The people they ruined want to say thank you, and some others want to ask why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.reply: Then somebody I know is out of debt, and somebody I used to know is out of work. I have a mind to throw a dinner. Go and make sure nobody throws a knife.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.text: Meet Nilena at the south-bank steps
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o0.topic: It is done. The ledgers are ash.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.o1.text: Defend the south-bank steps from the ruined bookkeeper's men
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.outro: Balmora ate well that night, and nobody asked for a receipt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ash.title: Ash on the Odai
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.desc: Factor Dron Hlaalu wants three ledgers from three places: a fence on the south bank, the Council Manor, and a toll-keeper on the bridge.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.re: A freight consultant never holds, sera; she merely receives. The ledger is in the second crate, left of the sacks. And, for free: whoever wrote it kept a second book in the Council Manor, and I am not the only one who knows.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.te: Buy the first ledger from Nilena Vandas
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o0.to: Factor Dron says you are holding something for him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o1.jo: The Manor smells of beeswax and old favours. A ledger sits unwatched in the steward's study, which means somebody wants it taken.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o1.te: Slip into the Council Manor and find the steward's ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o2.te: Take the second ledger from the steward's study
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o3.te: Meet the toll-keeper's ambush on the high bridge
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.c0: Sell all three to the Temple.
Splendid. Rivals are expensive. Temple justice is ruinous. I shall send flowers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.c1: Burn all three. The river has had enough.
A merciful fool, or a very clever one. I shall decide over breakfast.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.re: Now I own the river a little more than yesterday, and you are the only person who knows the number of ledgers I needed. I could pay you. I could sell all three to the Temple, who would pay far better and ruin my rival. Or burn them, and be clean. It is, I am told, a matter of taste.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.te: Hand the three ledgers to Dron
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.o4.to: All three. River dues, Manor tallies, and the bridge toll. What now?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.offer: A man in my position cannot be seen to ask what I am about to ask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.outro: The Odai ran as it always had, and nobody on either bank could say who owned it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.pitch: Three ledgers, three banks, one rival merchant who has hidden the truth of his river dues in each. I will not be seen to take them. You, on the other hand, are nobody, which is the most useful thing in Balmora. The first is with a fence on the south bank. Pay the fence. Do not ask for a receipt.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_ledgers.title: Three Ledgers, One River
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.desc: Sirela Marvos of Eight Plates wants a nameless girl's letter delivered to a ship, safely.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.rep: It is addressed to nobody and sealed in plain wax. Mind the Hlaalu men at the bridge; they have been asking after a grey cloak.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.tex: Take the letter from the ninth guest
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o0.top: I will carry it for her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o1.tex: Get through the bridge-watch asking after a grey cloak
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.rep: A letter for nobody. I have been waiting two years for this letter. The boat leaves tonight, and she will be on it. You never saw her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.tex: Give the letter to the silt-strider captain
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.o2.top: This is for the west-dock boat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.offer: You are hungry. Sit. No, not that seat. That one has a reservation.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.outro: The ninth plate was set out the next night too, and nobody sat at it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.pitch: Eight plates a night, no more. The ninth person goes hungry. Tonight she is a girl in a grey cloak who will not take charity, only work. She needs a letter carried to a boat at the west docks and she says it will end badly for whoever carries it. I would like it to end better.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_plates.title: The Ninth Plate
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.desc: Port-Master Orrel has a silt strider that will not budge, and he suspects something beneath her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o0.jo: A neat square hole under her middle leg, packed with silk. Somebody dug here and has been coming back at night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o0.te: Examine the strider in the caravan yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o1.te: Catch the smugglers coming back for their cache
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.re: Then she is a better citizen than half this town. Keep the silk, report the skooma, and for pity's sake, do not tell her she has been brave. It goes to her head.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.te: Tell Orrel what Dowager was guarding
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.o2.to: She was sitting on a smuggler's cache. Silk and skooma.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.offer: Do you have a calm voice? A very, very calm voice?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.outro: Dowager rose the next morning with a long, sceptical sigh.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.pitch: Old Dowager has not moved in six days. A strider will not stand still for six days unless it is sulking, ill, or sitting on something. I have checked sulking. Take a lantern and a bucket of sorrow and have a look under her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_strider.title: The Strider Who Wouldn't Walk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.desc: The ledgers are in the Temple. Witnesses are needed, and the factor's rival is not happy.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.repl: Then they will be crossing under my eye. I am not hiring a protector, sera; I am being thorough. Come at dawn and walk where I say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.text: Ask the bridge guard to escort the witnesses
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o0.topi: The Temple wants witnesses crossing the bridge by morning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.o1.text: Break the rival's attempt to drown the witnesses
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.outro: The witnesses reached the Temple dry and rather annoyed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_bal_trial.title: The Temple Reads the River
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.desc: Legate Corvus Pello wants the name of whoever is selling gate keys into the Dunmer quarter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o0.rep: Not 'who', sera, 'which'. There are three sellers and one customer. The customer is a Legion officer who buys one on the first of every month. I do not name officers for free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o0.tex: Ask Aryn the Informer who sells the keys
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o1.jou: At the third bell a guard unlocked the south gate, took a purse from a shadow and said nothing. He did not look back. He locked it again after the shadow had passed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o1.tex: Slip into the Dunmer quarter and watch the south gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.rep: My mother is sick. The Legion pays in coin that does not arrive. I sell the gate; I do not sell the walls. Please. Take this list, and this key. And tell no one my mother's name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.tex: Turn the guard who sells the keys
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o2.top: I saw you sell the south gate. I am not Legion. Tell me why.
Arrest the guard and publish the list.
Order restored. The Quarter will remember me as the man who punished a son for his mother. I will bear it.
Disarm the plot. Take the list to the Quarter Elders instead.
The Elders will decide, and decide wisely, which I could not. You have wasted the Legion's time and saved it from a mistake.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.rep: A guard, sixty drakes, a sick mother. I could have him flogged in the square. I could burn the list and let the gate go on as it has. Or I could keep the list, and have you walk it to the Quarter Elders instead. I will take the lesson you give me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.tex: Bring the list to Legate Corvus
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.o3.top: Here is your name. And your buyer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.offer: You are not Legion, not Dunmer, not Company. Good. You are nobody.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.outro: The south gate was locked properly that week, and a sick woman was found a physician.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.pitch: Someone is selling keys to the Dunmer quarter gate. A key buys a night's entry, a barrel's smuggling, a knife in the dark. I want the seller's name by sunrise and I would like it delivered quietly. A man who is arrested by rumour is a martyr by morning. Go in, ask, come out. Do not wear Legion colours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_bastion.title: The Bastion and the Quarter
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.des: Chaplain Loris needs an outsider to learn why three guards confessed the same sin.
At dusk the three guards left their posts together, crossed the bridge without speaking, and stood in a field of ash-flowers looking at a small stone. They did not pray. They saluted.
Watch the garrison walls at the lamp-lighting hour
Their fourth. Died last winter on a night watch when the lamp went out. They each left their post to tend a lamp for him. They would be flogged for it. They would do it again. Do not tell the Legate.
Ask Marga Ironhand about the stone
Three guards salute a stone in the ash-flowers. Whose?
Then I shall confess it for them, in the only way I can: I shall relight the lamp myself at the right hour, and let the walls think it is routine. Bless you. And bless a very quiet war.
It is a lamp for a dead comrade. Nothing worse.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.off: Do you confess? I do not ask, but I hear.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.out: The garrison lamp has not gone out since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_confession.pit: Three of the garrison have confessed the same sin this week, in three different words: a night off the walls, a gate left open, and a lamp left lit. Each was told to speak to no one. I must break the seal if I am to prevent it. I need an outsider to ask where they were, without ever asking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.desc: Felmin Rothal wants to know what the Company parrot's repeated sum means.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o0.jour: The parrot says: "Four hundred and twelve. Silk. Pay at dusk. Do not tell the Factor." Then it says a name I cannot print.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o0.text: Listen to the parrot in the customs yard
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.repl: A clerk named Vedran, fired last month for double-booking. He has been paying the dockhands to forward the silk his way. The parrot was his; he left it behind. Parrots, sera, are very poor at keeping secrets.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.text: Ask Aryn whose voice the parrot copies
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o1.topi: The parrot speaks like a Hlaalu clerk. Which?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o2.repl: A dishonest clerk undone by a bird. I shall give the bird a promotion. A small one. A cracker and a perch.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.o2.topi: The sum is a smuggled silk shipment. Vedran, the sacked clerk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.offer: Do you speak parrot? No? A shame. Neither does anyone here.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.outro: The parrot now says "Order. Order. Order." in a very flat voice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.pitch: A Company parrot has been repeating a sum in the customs yard for three days. Nobody knows what it means. It is either a ransom, a price, or a lottery. It is four hundred and twelve drakes, repeated every ten minutes, in a Hlaalu accent. Find out whose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_eb_parrot.title: The Customs Yard Parrot
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.desc: What you took from the vault is warm to the touch, and someone is following the heat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.re: I know three, and two will kill you. I will take the third. Keep walking the plaza; do not look behind you, sera, because everyone else will.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.te: Fence the brass through Ravos Dren
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o0.to: I have something warm. You know a buyer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.o1.te: Shake off the Temple's watchers in the plaza
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.outro: You ended the night richer and a little lighter in the head. The brass is somebody else's problem now.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_hotbrass.title: Hot Brass
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.desc: Lisara Tervyn, a palace archivist, has a map of a palace that exists only under Mournhold.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.repl: Right? It is the only one that is. Walk it backwards and you will find the throne room first. Do not sit in the chair. The chair is for someone, and he has been late for a long time.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.text: Ask Old Sedyn if the reversed palace map is true
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o0.topi: This map shows the Palace upside down. Is it right?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o1.jour: Stairs that rise when you go down. A window with an interior sky. A door where the map said, and a note in a clerk's hand: "Do not stay."
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o1.text: Walk the palace plan in reverse
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o2.text: Retrieve the seal from the reversed throne room
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o3.repl: Then the archive has a second basement after all, and I shall have to resign or go mad. Thank you. Please never come into my office again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.o3.topi: The reversed palace is real. I brought its seal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.offer: Can you hold your tongue about basements?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.outro: The archivist now files the second basement under "Weather".
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.pitch: Every palace map I catalogue is accurate except one, and it is accurate in reverse. It describes a palace that does not exist above ground. It describes the one below. Take this tracing to Old Sedyn and ask whether the maps are true; I am forbidden to ask, and cannot stop wondering.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_mirror.title: The Palace Has a Reflection
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.desc: The Temple is grateful and wants a favour done in the quiet hours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o0.r: The one who tried to lease the vault will try again, with muscle. Stand in the courtyard at dusk. You need not do anything but be seen to wait.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o0.t: Meet the Archcanon at the dawn bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.o1.t: Meet the lessor's hirelings at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_quietbell.outr: The courtyard bells rang at dusk and nobody ever mentioned why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.desc: Gaela Nelvan of the Silver Samovar found a ledger of names under her back table. It belongs to someone dangerous.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o0.reply: Camonna Tong collectors, sera, the bad-tempered kind. The ledger is what they lend against. Names and sums. Burn it and half of Mournhold sleeps; hand it to the Palace and the other half is arrested.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o0.text: Ask Ravos Dren who the three men were
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o0.topic: Three men, three pots of undrunk tea, a ledger.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o1.text: Meet a Legion officer behind the spice stalls
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.c0.labe: Burn the ledger. The debts die with it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.c0.repl: Half a city sleeps tonight. The other half will ask who did this. Not you, I hope.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.c1.labe: Give it to the Palace. Let the law have it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.c1.repl: The cells will be full by Fredas. I do not envy the clerks who must read it aloud.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.reply: The Palace will use it as a whip. The Temple would use it as a prayer-book. Neither is wholly honest. You are the only person with it who has nothing to gain. Choose a keeper. And choose quickly; the pot goes cold.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.text: Decide who should hold the ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.o2.topic: Gaela has a ledger of Tong debtors. Who should hold it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.offer: Do you take your tea hot or your secrets cold?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.outro: Gaela served the next pot hot, for the first time in a month.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.pitch: Three men sat at my back table and left one pot of tea each, undrunk and still warm, and a ledger of names behind. The ledger is not mine and the names are not kind. I would like the right people to have it. Everyone in this bazaar wants it to be the wrong people.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_tea.title: Cold Tea, Warm Hands
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.desc: Mistress Hlaren has a courier contract whose margin hides a map beneath the Great Bazaar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o0.reply: The crates are never meant to arrive, sera. The route ends at a drain under the Godsreach terrace. Find the sexton called Sedyn; he leads a lantern down there every Sundas and he is the only soul I trust with a drain.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o0.text: Take the contract and ask what the margin means
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o1.reply: Know it? I have a favourite spot in it. Go by the third lamp and say nothing to the ghosts; they take it personally. The twin plaza lies at the bottom. Whoever drew that map wants the vault under the twin Palace. Mind the Mirror-Warden. It does not like visitors who walk like they own the place.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o1.text: Find Old Sedyn and ask for a way down
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o1.topic: Hlaren says you know the drain beneath the Godsreach terrace.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o2.journa: The streets down here match the streets above, one for one, only dark and sunk and wrong-handed. A fountain runs backwards.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o2.text: Enter Old Mournhold by the Godsreach drain
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o3.text: Cross the twin plaza past the ruins' ghosts
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o4.text: Take the mirror key from the twin fountain
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o5.text: Open the vault and answer the Mirror-Warden
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.c0.lab: Re-seal the vault. Let the twin city sleep.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.c0.rep: Then it sleeps. The Temple will not forget this, and the Temple remembers everything, eventually.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.c1.lab: Rob it. The Temple does not need what it hides.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.c1.rep: How very Mournhold of you. The back stair is open. Do not use the front.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.reply: Quiet is the word. There is a lamp-lit reliquary below that the Temple has never admitted exists, and somebody in the Hlaalu Council has been trying to lease it. I can re-seal it, in which case it is as if you were never there. Or I can look away while it is emptied. I will not ask which I prefer. I would not like the answer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.text: Take the key to Archcanon Ulvani
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.o6.topic: The vault is open. It is yours to seal or rob, and I am told you asked for a quiet inquiry.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.offer: You look like someone who reads the fine print.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.outro: The twin city lies below, patient, with its lamps lit for no one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.pitch: A courier contract came through my stall for forty crates of lamp-oil. The route, drawn in the margin, runs not through the bazaar but under it. Somebody wants a way into Old Mournhold, and wants a bazaar guildmaster's stamp to look innocent. I would like to know who, before I am blamed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mh_twin.title: Beneath the Twin City
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.desc: Sister Mavia's ash-lantern has been stolen from the canton. She wants it back, unopened.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.o0.text: Search the harbour tunnels for the lantern-thief
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.o1.text: Take the ash-lantern from the thief's cache
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.o2.reply: Thank you. You know, nobody has ever asked me what I do with the ash. I plant it. Along the cliff road, one thimble at a time. The lilies there are the oddest shade. That is all of you, and all of us, and I thought it would be kind to say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.o2.topic: The shutter is closed. It was not opened.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.offer: Have you left anything behind lately? A footprint, a sigh?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.outro: A new row of pale lilies appears along the cliff road each spring.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.pitch: Someone has stolen my ash-lantern, the one with everyone's little bit in it. A thief of ashes is a thief of everyone's good name. It was last seen on the harbour tunnels' ledge. Bring it back, and do not open the shutter. It is not for you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_ashes.title: What the Living Leave Behind
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.desc: Orvyn Hlaalo of the Cinder Cup wants a Redoran inspector and a Hlaalu competitor brought to one table.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o0.reply: Soup. I have not had soup in this town in years. Tell him I will come, and tell him I will bring a notary, a bodyguard and my appetite, in that order of importance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o0.text: Carry an invitation to the Hlaalu competitor
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o0.topic: Orvyn invites you for soup. Bring your lawyers, he says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o1.reply: A Redoran at table with a Hlaalu is a curiosity. I shall attend, as a neutral. Neutral parties eat slowly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o1.text: Carry an invitation to the Redoran inspector
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o1.topic: Orvyn invites you for soup, Warden.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.o2.reply: Then I shall serve the soup with ladle and flourish and charge them four drakes each for the cooling. Do not tell them it is a joke. A joke is only funny if no one is warned.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.offer: You look hot. That will be four drakes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.outro: Both parties left friends, or at least bored with each other, which in Molag Mar counts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.pitch: A charge for cooling is a joke, sera, a joke my father made and I inherited, but now a Redoran inspector wants it banned and a Hlaalu competitor wants it franchised. I would like both to see sense, or at least each other. Bring them to the same table.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_cup.title: Paying for the Cooling
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.desc: Warden Ilu Dren of the canton lift wants a failed heat-vent examined and a magma creature put out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o0.journal: The baffle was cracked in one straight line. Someone cut it. Nothing hot makes a crack that clean.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o0.text: Examine the failed heat-vent beside the temple stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o1.reply: Not whom. What. A salt-cutter, bone-handled, the kind the glassworkers use. A man who wants a channel hotter wants one of three things: a cold room melted, a quiet grave, or a reason to sell insurance.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o1.text: Ask Dren the Lavacutter about the cut
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o1.topic: The baffle was cut, not cracked. By whom?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o2.text: Descend to the Underworks through the lift and clear the vents
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o3.text: Lure the Slag-Heart into the quenching pool
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.c0.labe: Close the lower station. Safety first.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.c0.repl: Then forty families climb a hundred extra stairs for the rest of their lives, and none will die in the heat. I will write it in the book.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.c1.labe: Keep it open, and put a guard on the vent every night.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.c1.repl: A guard is cheaper than a stair. It means I am the guard. I accept it; I wanted a reason to stop sleeping.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.reply: A quiet station. A longer stair. I knew it would cost something. Do I close it, and lose forty families their trade, or leave it open and risk the next flood? I would like someone else to say the word.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.text: Return to Warden Ilu with the core
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.o4.topic: The vent is sealed. But to seal it I must close the lift's lower station. That leaves forty families without a quick way down.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.offer: Do you mind heat? Good. Do you mind losses?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.outro: The Underworks glowed a little dimmer that night, and a little safer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.pitch: A heat-vent failed last night in the Underworks. The channel ran twenty degrees over and a lava-flow touched a cold room. Nobody died. Yet. Look at the vent, take the lift down, and put out whatever has woken in the pool. Do not touch the glass.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_mm_hot.title: The Channel Runs Hot
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.desc: Mirele Sathil of the Pilgrims' Rest finds one more candle each morning than she put out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o0.jou: Between the fourth and fifth bell, a candle lit itself in the alcove at the end. The shape beside it was a child, sitting with her knees up, looking at the flame.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o0.tex: Keep watch in the hostel alcoves overnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o1.rep: A pilgrim's daughter, nine years dead, who never reached the shrine. Her family walked on and never knew. Her candle is her request. Put a chair by it and say her name aloud. She wants to hear it said by someone who is not family.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o1.tex: Ask Keeper Salvu about the child
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o1.top: A girl in the far alcove. She lights a candle and watches it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o2.rep: Then I shall say it every night at the forty-second candle. Dahlia. There. That is not hard. I should have asked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o2.tex: Tell Mirele what the child wants
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.o2.top: Her name is Dahlia. She wants a chair and her name said aloud.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.offer: Count with me. Do you count in threes? Good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.outro: The forty-second candle now has a small chair beside it, and a card with a single name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.pitch: Every night I put out forty-one candles in the alcoves. Every morning I find forty-two. I do not mind the extra, but one more tomorrow might be a guest and not a candle, and I do not know how to charge a guest who is not in the book.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_candle.title: The Candle Count
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.desc: Keeper Salvu says the gravedigger Aldrin has refused to dig one grave and will not say whose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o0.repl: A Sathil. Dead forty years and no one buried her. Her bones lie in the family tomb with the door sealed from inside. I will not dig the grave she was meant to have, because I would be digging in her place. Her son is the heir and he has not been home since the fire.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o0.text: Ask Aldrin whose grave he will not dig
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o0.topi: Salvu says you put down your spade. For whom?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o1.jour: A farmstead gone to bracken. A man sleeps in the barn with a half-burned deed in his fist, and a ring on his thumb he does not remove even to wash.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o1.text: Track the Sathil heir to the plantation's farm
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o2.repl: Because he left, sera, in the fire year, when his mother was still breathing. A son who runs while his mother lies in the house is a ghost that has not yet died. We do not speak to him. We do not speak of him. Take this to the tomb, if you must go.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o2.text: Ask Elder Nerevi about the heir
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o2.topi: The heir is a Sathil. Why will no one let him home?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o3.text: Retrieve the Sathil ash from the sealed tomb
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.c0.l: Bury her. Let the son stand at the grave.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.c0.r: Then the Row has thirteen houses again. I shall tell Aldrin to find his spade.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.c1.l: Let the line lapse. Scatter the ash on the farm.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.c1.r: It is old law, and a gentle one. The farm will bear well. She will see to it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.repl: Now we may bury her, or we may let the line lapse; that is not mine to decide, and I would not decide it for the son. But you have walked among the dead on his behalf. You may speak for him. Choose, for him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.text: Bring the ash to Keeper Salvu
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.o5.topi: The ash is warm. The heir sleeps in a barn. What now?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.offer: The gravedigger will not speak to me. Perhaps he will speak to you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.outro: The next morning, Aldrin was seen walking toward the Row, carrying a spade and humming.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.pitch: Aldrin has dug four hundred graves in this town and tonight he laid down his spade and said he would not dig one more. Someone has asked him for a grave and he will not say whose. Ask him. He is a stubborn man, but he is also a sad one, and sad men tell strangers what they cannot tell the Keeper.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_grave.title: A Grave Not Dug
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.desc: Elder Nerevi wants to know who leaves plain candles at her husband's tomb.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o0.jour: A hooded figure arrived with a plain wax candle and lit it with shaking hands. She did not see me. She said one word: "Sorry."
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o0.text: Wait at the third house of the Row at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o1.repl: A young woman, a Legion cook's daughter, I believe. Her father was a Legion man who died on the same night as Nerevi's husband, in the same fire. She thinks she owes the old woman an apology for something she cannot name.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o1.text: Ask Tadrik who buys plain wax candles
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o1.topi: Someone buys a plain candle every night. Who?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o2.c0.r: Thank you. And you, sera. You may walk the Row. Mind the third step; my husband did.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o2.repl: Then I have been angry at a mourner. That is a thing a widow does not like to learn. Tell her to come in daylight. Tell her the Row is open.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.o2.topi: The candle is a prayer. A Legion cook's daughter, grieving.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.offer: You walked among the Sathil dead. Then perhaps you are not an outlander.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.outro: In daylight, a young woman and an old one stood at the third house and said nothing for a long time.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.pitch: My husband lies in the third house. Every night a stranger leaves a candle at his door, an outlander's candle, plain wax, without a name. I cannot tell whether it is an insult or a prayer. Learn who it is. If it is a prayer, I will let you walk the Row. If it is an insult, I will have a word with the Keeper.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_nec_widow.title: The Widow Who Guards the Row
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.desc: Magister Gaenor Dreth has bet his neighbour Ulveni that someone can steal her singing teapot. He chose you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o0.reply: Tel Naga. Four rope-bridges, one levitation gap that you cannot cross without a little something, and a guardian she will not name. The something is this potion. It will carry you six paces. Plan your landing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o0.topic: Where is the tower and what is the catch?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o1.journa: The ropes sang under my boots. On the fourth I looked down, which was a mistake; the lagoon is a long way off and the fungi are cheerfully luminous.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o1.text: Cross four rope bridges to Ulveni's tower
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o2.text: Cross the levitation gap and answer the lesser guardians
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o4.text: Take the singing teapot from the fourteenth floor
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.c0.lab: Return it to Ulveni. Let Gaenor lose his wager.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.c0.rep: Gaenor, you old tide-pool. Look who won. You owe me a tower's worth of embarrassment.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.c1.lab: Bring it to Gaenor. The bet is the bet.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.c1.rep: Honourable and tedious. He will be unbearable for a month. Go; I shall hold a grudge on your behalf.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.reply: I say: how delightful, and: do put it down, it is sulking. My rival wagered I could not be robbed. Now I have a choice, and I find I would like to make you make it. Return it to me and I owe you a favour. Take it to him, and he owes me one. Ha. Ha. Which favour would you prefer to be at the centre of?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.text: Face Magister Ulveni with her teapot
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.o5.topic: Magister. Your teapot. I would like to know what you say next.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.offer: You have a face that has never won anything. Wonderful.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.outro: The teapot hummed three notes at dusk. Both Magisters claimed it was in tune.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.pitch: I have wagered Magister Ulveni that a stranger can lift her singing teapot from her fourteenth floor in a single night. She says no. She says it with a number of guardians. Take the slip, cross the rope-bridges, and bring me the pot. If you lose, you will lose in an interesting way. I shall enjoy it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_bet.title: A Bet Between Towers
Magister Gaenor won the wager and feels the need to celebrate, loudly, in a place with an audience.
Now I take the pot to the Gateway Inn and play it for the room. Mind the crowd; some of them are Ulveni's, and her people are poor losers. Stand with me at the bar.
Break Ulveni's sulking partisans at the Gateway Inn
The teapot played, the crowd sang, and the inn needed new windows by morning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.desc: Skeema the Sporekeeper grew a new grey strain that eats the glowing gardens.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o0.tex: Clear the fumigation chambers of what the strain has woken
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o1.rep: I have the salts, I have the jars, and I have my doubts. I will sell you three measures at cost, which is a joke, because I have never once sold anything at cost. Do not tell anyone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o1.tex: Ask Fennik Sul for fumigation salts
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o1.top: Skeema needs strong salts. Anything that kills a spore.
The garden breathes again. I shall plant the blue ones where it grew and call it a lesson.
Keep one cutting, sealed, for study.
In the cellar. Under three locks. Under four. I shall call it the Quiet One and never speak of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o2.rep: I want to burn it. Every sensible part of me wants to burn it. But it is the first thing in my life that has surprised me in thirty years. Choose for me, because I shall regret it either way.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o2.tex: Decide the strain's fate with Skeema
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.o2.top: The grey cap is isolated. Burn it, or keep a cutting?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.offer: Do you have a strong stomach? Asking for a mushroom.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.outro: The back greenhouse is very quiet now, and Skeema checks it twice before every dawn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.pitch: I grew a grey cap in the back greenhouse that does not belong to anything. It does not glow, it does not sing, and the room around it is very quiet in a way I do not like. It is eating the other spores. Help me contain it. Do not touch it. Do not look at the gills.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_strain.title: The Grey Strain
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_ulveni_favour: Magister Ulveni owes you a favour and wants it spent quickly, on something small and impertinent.
I did. I would like to cash it in your name. Go to Gaenor's tower and swap his chair for a wash-basin. Quickly. He believes in sitting a certain way.
You said you owed me one.
Swap Gaenor's chair in the Council Spire terrace
Gaenor sat with great dignity in a wash-basin for nearly a minute before noticing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.desc: Apprentice Veya wants out of her ten-year indenture to Magister Ulveni.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o0.reply: Registered by a Telvanni notary and countersigned by a Legion clerk who is no longer in the Legion. I recall him. He had a wooden hand and a tendency to forget himself near rope-bridges. His practice was a few steps west of Sadrith, in the old customs shed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o0.text: Ask the garrison clerk for the registry copy
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o0.topic: Veya's apprenticeship contract is registered with the Legion. Can I see it?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o1.journ: A shed full of ink and dust. The notary kept a second copy of every contract and filed every clause under its loophole. I found Veya's. The loophole reads: "Void upon the Magister's first apology."
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o1.text: Find the notary's shed at the lagoon's edge
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.c0.la: Wait. She will find a way.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.c0.re: A fish, a fungus and a rope-bridge got the best of me. Veya. You are free. I am a monster.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.c1.la: Don't give her the satisfaction. Tell her to apologise to the lagoon.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.c1.re: The lagoon accepts. Hmph. Veya, you are, regrettably, free.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.reply: Ha. Hahaha. A clause. Good lord. I have not apologised since the Second Era. Leave me. I shall think it over. Come back when I have found a way to apologise to a fish.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o2.topic: Veya's indenture ends the day you apologise. To anyone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o3.reply: Then I am no one. Is that what it feels like? It feels like holding my breath and finding I do not need to. Thank you. I shall go to Mournhold. I shall learn to read other people's handwriting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.o3.topic: It is done. You are no one's apprentice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.offer: Can you read a contract? A really nasty one?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.outro: Veya left Sadrith before the fish heard.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.pitch: My indenture says I serve Magister Ulveni for ten years, and in the fine print, three more if she has a 'significant disappointment'. I have been a disappointment since the first spring. Find the clause that lets me go, or the person who wrote it, and I will carry your bags for the rest of my life. Which is, I hope, short.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_veya.title: The Apprentice Who Wanted Out
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.desc: Dalyne Hlaren of the Gateway Inn has a window that shows a woman who is not there.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o0.jou: At dusk the lagoon dissolved and a woman in a green shawl stood in a field of white flowers. She did not wave. She pointed, west and a little down.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o0.tex: Sit in room nine and watch the window at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o1.jou: A single stone, half-buried, with a shawl-pin at its foot. The engraving reads: "Waited here. Was never met."
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o1.tex: Follow where she pointed, to the base of the tower
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o2.rep: Then I shall set a second place at room nine each Sundas, and a fresh flower in the window. The Magisters can explain the resonance as they wish; I have a ghost with a reservation.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.o2.top: She was waiting for someone who never arrived. Here is her pin.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.offer: Do you believe in rooms that do not stay put?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.outro: Room nine now has a green shawl on the chair, and nobody is ever charged for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.pitch: Number nine's window showed the lagoon on Monday and the Ascadian Isles on Tuesday and, last night, a woman in a green shawl, waving. She waved at a guest who never checked in. The Magisters say it is a 'resonance.' I say it is a ghost with a view. Find who she is.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_sad_window.title: The Window That Lied
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.desc: The Temple is auditing the Hlaalu canton. Not everyone in it is thrilled.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.o0.repl: Counting is the one sin I have never been accused of. Lead on, and if anyone offers a bribe, please let me watch how it is done.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.o0.text: Fetch Brother Fendil to witness the audit
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.o0.topi: The Temple needs a witness who can count stairs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.o1.text: Turn back the canton factors who came to burn the books
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.outro: The books survived, and so did Warden Telyne's good name, in the oddest way: she was the one who brought them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_audit.title: The Temple Counts the Water
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.desc: Ilnoth the Pit-Caller suspects the Arena canton's champion throws fights on someone's cue.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o0.text: Win a bout against the reigning champion
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o1.reply: Wide, yes, I saw. He glanced at the bookmaker's boy. The boy glanced at the second balcony. Someone up there wears the Hlaalu green and has never once bet the same side as the crowd. Ask the boy. Gently. He bites.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o1.text: Tell Ilnoth the champion yielded to you
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o1.topic: He yielded the moment I swung wide. Not to me. To the window.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o2.journ: Slates stacked to the ceiling: each bout, each purse, and beside each in neat chalk the word 'Dron' with a number. A single patron has been quietly buying fights for two years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o2.text: Slip into the bookmaker's cellar under the pit
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.c0.re: Then the crowd gets the best bout of the year, and none of us fight in it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.c1.la: Sell him the slates. Split it with me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.c1.re: The odds were never honest. At least now I am paid for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.reply: I can name him from the stage, which ruins a man in Vivec. Or I can sell him the slates, and eat well, and the fights stay crooked but the crowd stays loud. I am a showman. Say the word.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.text: Decide what Ilnoth does with the slates
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.o3.topic: The patron is a Hlaalu factor. Two years of throws. Your move.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.offer: Do you gamble, stranger, or only fight?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.outro: The pit still roars. Whether it roars at the truth depends on which of you won the cellar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.pitch: Kemel-Ze has won thirty-one bouts and I would swear on the Tribunal that he lost four of them. A champion who falls down on cue pays whoever knows the cue. I want to know who. Win a bout of your own and let me watch what happens at the bookmaker's window.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_odds.title: The Reigning Champion Falls Down
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.desc: Ruvene Olvyn of the Sunken Lantern wants to know where Brother Fendil's 'Last Stair' coin ends up.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o0.jo: Fendil doesn't go home. He crosses three bridges and a ferry, and the purse he carries is heavier than a priest's has any right to be.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o0.te: Shadow Brother Fendil as he leaves the Temple stairs at dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o1.jo: A hospice, small, in a stair-end nobody uses. Sixteen cots. Orphans of pilgrims who died climbing, fed on blessings that cost a stranger four drakes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o1.te: Follow him to a canton alcove behind the canal market
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o2.c0: Report him. The Temple should fund the hospice honestly.
Honestly. Imagine it. I will be fined and the cots will be counted and perhaps, perhaps, someone will notice them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o2.c1: Say nothing. And leave a purse on the third cot.
Bless you, in a way that costs nothing. Pilgrims will still hit the wall. They will not know that the wall is a roof.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o2.re: Then you know the worst of me. The Temple's stipend would feed four. The pilgrims' pity feeds sixteen. Tell Warden Telyne and the hospice closes. Tell no one and I go on lying to the lonely. Choose, and forgive me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.o2.to: I followed you. The coin buys cots, not wine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.offer: You have a pilgrim's boots and a sceptic's eyes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.outro: Ruvene refunded three pilgrims out of her own till and refused to explain why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.pitch: Half my guests come back from the Palace gate looking cheated. Brother Fendil sells them a blessing for the last stair, and the stair is a wall. I do not mind a swindle. I mind the swindle sending them to my bar, crying. Find out where the coin goes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_pilgrim.title: The Last Stair Is Extra
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.desc: The Hlaalu canton owes you for its silence. A few debts want collecting before the water is forgotten.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.o0.repl: I want you to know the plantation still thirsts and will find another clerk. Hold the gate with me one night, sera, and I will pay you from the tithes nobody will ever count.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.o0.topi: The leak is closed. What do you want me to know?
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.o1.text: Hold the water-gate against the plantation's bravos
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.outro: The gate held. Tosa pours you a measure of canal water and a better measure of sujamma.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_quiet.title: A Dry Season of Silence
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_umbrellas.des: Bethal Aryon wants her umbrella crates recovered from the Lost Shipwreck. She is oddly incurious about what else is in them.
Find the wreck where her umbrellas went down
Drive off the scavengers and the drowned crew
Take the umbrella crate from the hold
Keep selling. I want a cut, and the handles sealed tighter.
A partner! Splendid. Mind the rain; it does not fall here, and neither do the Customs.
I'm turning the crate over to the Customs.
Then I wish you a damp and honest life. You will not be buying here again, sera.

Hollow handles. How curious. How dry my shop would be, without them. A lady in my position cannot be seen to sell sugar; a lady in my position can be seen to sell umbrellas. The Fane's Customs men are not curious. Are you?
Forty umbrellas, and one more thing: the handles are hollow and packed with moon sugar.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_umbrellas.off: You want an umbrella. Everyone wants an umbrella, eventually.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_umbrellas.out: Vivec has never been so well-covered against weather that does not exist.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_umbrellas.pit: My stock is a shipwreck's worth of oilskin umbrellas that never reached me. The wreck is out past the Ebonheart road: Lost Shipwreck, they call it, cheerfully. Bring back the crates. I'll not ask you what else is in them, and you will not ask me why I do not ask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.desc: Warden Telyne of the Hlaalu canton has wet stairs and a short water ledger. Tosa the Cantonkeeper knows more than she says.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o0.repl: Lighter by most of a cistern a week. Someone is draining the canton below the waterline, where no ledger can see. Row out past the Hlaalu pilings at slack tide and drop this line. Fourteen fathoms. You will feel the cut.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o0.text: Ask Tosa the Cantonkeeper about the ledger
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o0.topi: Warden Telyne says your gate-ledger is lighter than the canal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o1.jour: The line ran out at fourteen fathoms and came back with a fresh chisel-mark on the stone. The cut is square. Nothing in the sea cuts squares.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o1.text: Row out past the Hlaalu pilings and sound the old foundations
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o2.text: Follow the cut into the flooded maintenance shafts
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o3.text: Take the gate-wheel they cut from the sluice
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o4.text: Face the man selling the canton its own water
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.c0.l: Seal the shaft and burn the ledger. The canton never hears of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.c0.r: Then we have both done something we will remember at the bottom of a stair. Take this. It is not payment. It is silence with a price tag.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.c1.l: The Temple should count this water. Take it to them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.c1.r: Yes. Yes, that is the right answer, and I resent you for it. Go on. I will stand beside you, in front of everyone, which is the worst place to stand.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.repl: My nephew. My own sister's boy. ...Sit. Say what you will do with this, because I find I cannot decide, and I have decided everything for forty years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.text: Bring the wheel and the ledger to Warden Telyne
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.o5.topi: The leak is sealed. The ledger has your nephew's hand and your seal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.offer: You look like someone who can keep a secret and row a boat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.outro: The stairs were dry by the next tide. What it cost depends on whom you ask.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.pitch: Three of my stairs are wet that should be dry. Stairs do not leak; the walls under them do, and the Cantonkeeper will not tell me why her ledger is lighter than the canal. Speak to her, then go and look. By boat, naturally. Everything in Vivec is by boat if you are honest about it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_mw_viv_water.title: Water Under the Cantons
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_barrow_that_: Shroud Hearth Barrow snores at night. Wulfgar of the Vilemyr wants to know what is sleeping there so contentedly.
Enter Shroud Hearth Barrow at night
Silence the sleeper and its guards

Wulfgar sits down heavily. "A feast. Nine hundred years of dreaming about dinner. The poor soul. Stranger, I will make you a plate. The best the Vilemyr has. And I will leave a plate at the barrow gate, on the first night of every month, in his honour."
Tell Wulfgar the barrow is quiet
There was a draugr on a bed of stone, snoring. It had been dreaming of a great feast. It is quiet now.
You are not sleeping well, Wulfgar.
The snoring at Shroud Hearth is no more. A plate of roast goat is left at its gate each month, and it is always empty by morning.

The barrow, friend. Shroud Hearth. Right up the road. Every night, a sound. Not a moan. A snore. A great, slow, comfortable snore. The kind a man makes after a very long dinner. Wulfgar has lived beside it all his life and never heard it before. A draugr who snores is either very content or very new. Please look.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_blade_in_the: Foreman Hrolf's sawmill keeps ruining blades on swords buried in logs from Autumnshade Clearing. He wants the grove searched.
Search Autumnshade Clearing for the source of the swords
Drive off the spriggans that have been feeding trees iron

Hrolf rubs his jaw. "To keep it from the world. That is a generous thing, for a tree. Well, the saws will thank you. Take a plank, friend. It is Autumnshade oak, with a sword in it. It will make a handsome door."
Tell Hrolf why the trees hold swords
The spriggans were taking iron from a long-lost battle and pressing it into the trunks, to keep it from the world. They are done now.
The saws of Heartwood Mill run clean. A single door of Autumnshade oak, with a sword-shaped scar, hangs at the mill's gate.

Third time this season, friend. Something hard in a log. Last week it was a sword-blade, buried deep, grown into the heartwood, a very old kind of steel. The log came from the Autumnshade grove. A tree that swallowed a sword, and the sword has teeth. Hrolf would like to know what else is in that grove, before another saw is lost.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_brandy_that_: A barrel of brandy aged forty years in two days in Hjorth's cellar. He wants the cause removed before it ages him too.
Search the cellar of the Brandy-Mug farm
Destroy the thing that hastens time in the cellar

Hjorth uncorks the nearest barrel, sniffs and, with deep reluctance, sighs. "Just brandy. Ordinary brandy. Not even a year old. Stranger, I have never regretted a thing so quickly. The wisp's brandy was divine. But Hjorth will pour you a glass of the other, and it will be young, and honest."
Tell Hjorth the cellar is safe
A wisp had been feeding on the barrels, and aged them as it ate. It is gone. The brandy is only brandy again.
Your brandy is the colour of old money.
The cellar of the Brandy-Mug farm holds ordinary brandy, aged the ordinary way, and its owner has been heard to sigh at the barrels from time to time.

It is, friend, and it should not be. A barrel Hjorth laid down on Sunday is the colour of forty years by Tuesday. Smooth, deep, very fine. Quite wrong. It is not the cellar. It is not the barrel. It is something in the cellar, a thing that ages. He would like it out before it ages the cellar, the farm and himself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_bridge_that_: The bridge at Dragon Bridge hums at midnight. Aldis believes something under the river is singing, and the likeliest cave mouth is Pinemoon Cave.
Enter Pinemoon Cave and follow the sound downward
Clear the cave of what has been singing

Aldis stands very still with his ear to the stone. After a long moment, he straightens. "Quiet. Gods. I had grown used to it. A bridge ought to be quiet. It is the only thing it is good for. But, stranger, tonight I will miss it, a little. Hilde's will give you a bed, and I will pay for it."
Tell Aldis the bridge is quiet
The singers were wisps in the cave, resonating with the stone. They are gone. The bridge should be quiet.
You have been listening to your bridge.
The bridge at Dragon Bridge is quiet again. The tollkeeper says he does not miss the humming, and has taken to whistling at midnight, to fill the silence.

Humming, friend. A low note, under the stone, only at midnight. It was a bridge, a dumb thing of rock and mortar, and now it hums. Aldis put his ear to the ground. It is not the bridge. It is under the bridge. Under the river. A thing that does not belong, singing in its sleep. Pinemoon Cave is the nearest place a hole to the deep might come out.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_forge_that_w: The eternal forge of Narzulbur has gone cold for the first time in forty years. Grazbar suspects its deeper fire has been tampered with.
Follow the forge's fire-vein to Gloombound Mine
Clear the miners-turned-thieves who have blocked the fire-vein

Grazbar lights the forge with a taper and, with a roar, it takes. She laughs, huge and rough. "Light! Honest light! Stranger, the stronghold owes you a feast and a blade. Take an axe off the rack. It is my best work, and I have never been prouder to give it away."
Tell Grazbar the forge-fire can be relit
Bandits had blocked the vein with a boulder to steal the coal. I cleared it. The fire-spirit is free. The forge should take.
The forge of Narzulbur roars once more. A stranger carries an axe from the rack, and the smith-wife swears she will make a better one by spring.

It is, friend, and it has never been cold in forty years. A fire that does not go out, stone-lit, from the root of the stronghold itself. Then three nights ago, out. No ash, no smoke. The coals are good, the bellows are good. The fire simply will not take. Grazbar suspects a debt. The old Orsimer forges are fed from a deeper fire, and someone has tampered with the feed.
The Forge That Would Not Light
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_forsworn_in_: A Forsworn scout was found in an ore cart from the Karthwasten mine. Overseer Ulfhild wants the traitor in her mine found before Markarth closes the trade.
Question the miners at the ore-carts
Follow the scout's trail to Dragontooth Crater
Stop the Forsworn handler who passes messages

Ulfhild's shoulders drop. "No one inside. No one of mine. Thank the Divines. Stranger, the Markarth guards will hear it from my own mouth before the evening. And Ulfhild will keep a pick handy for the next hagraven."
It was a hagraven who hid messages in ore and used the scout to carry them. She has no hand in your mine. No one inside it did.
You have the look of someone who doesn't trust the quiet.
The Karthwasten mine was cleared of suspicion, and the ore carts roll to Markarth again, each one with a small bell tied to the axle, so everyone hears it pass.

I don't, friend. A cart left the mine on Fredas, full of ore, and arrived at the smelter at Markarth with a hidden passenger. A Forsworn scout, the Markarth guards say. Ulfhild did not put him there. Someone did. Someone in the mine is passing messages out in the ore. Find them, before the guards of Markarth shut Karthwasten out of the trade.
The Forsworn in the Ore Cart
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_goat_that_kn: A grey goat at Stonehills visits the same cave every day and comes back smelling of spice. Brunwulf wants someone to follow her.
Follow the grey goat to Dimhollow Crypt

Brunwulf smacks his forehead. "A herb! A patch of it! Seven days, and she has been eating my fortune. Stranger, I shall fence it in, and sell the leaves, and give you the first twenty. And the grey one shall have a ribbon. A goat of that wisdom deserves a ribbon."
Tell Brunwulf what the goat is chewing
There is a patch of rare mountain herb growing at the cave mouth. The goat has been eating it. It is a thing the apothecary in Dawnstar pays well for.
One of your goats is looking at me.
A grey goat at Stonehills wears a red ribbon and walks to the cave every day, with the air of a small, deliberate landowner.

The grey one, friend. She has been to the same cave every day for a week and comes back smelling of old spice. Not a goat's habit. Brunwulf followed her once and lost her at a rock the size of a house. She came out the other side an hour later, chewing something. Something not grass. Go and see what it is. A goat does not go to the same place seven days running for no reason.
The Goat That Knew Too Much
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_herbs_that_w: The herb-beds at the Sarethi farm wilt every dusk and recover at dawn. Rannveig believes something is sapping them each evening.
Watch the beds from dusk until the wilting starts
Destroy the thing that drinks the garden at dusk

Rannveig sinks to a stool. "A young one. Drinking my herbs to grow. Well. It is not the worst thing a child might do. Stranger, I shall plant a tree at that spot, for it, and say a word. And a bed of nightshade, in case it comes back."
Tell Rannveig why her herbs wilted
A young spriggan had taken root at the edge of the garden, and drank from the beds each dusk to grow. It is dead now.
The herb-beds of Sarethi bloom through the dusk. A single young tree grows at the edge of the garden, with a ring of nightshade at its foot.

They wilt at dusk, friend, every one. And by dawn they are green again, as if nothing happened. Rannveig has watched all night. Nothing. Not a shadow, not a rustle. It is as though the garden has begun to remember something sad and then forget it. She does not like it. A garden should not have bad dreams.
The Herbs That Wilted at Dusk
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_hole_that_gr: The Soljund sinkhole deepens a hand-span each month. Orm believes something in the depths is digging, and wants it stopped.
Descend into the deepest part of Soljund's Sinkhole
Slay the thing that digs in the dark

Orm stands at the edge and looks down for a long time. "As deep as it is going to be. Stranger, I had grown fond of the worry. A man needs a thing to worry about. I will find another. But thank you. The village will not fall in."
Tell Orm the hole will grow no more
A giant, blind scorpion had been digging for years. It is dead now. The sinkhole is as deep as it is going to be.
Your hole is larger than yesterday's.
The sinkhole at Soljund's stopped growing, and its delver, having lost his calendar, took to marking the month on a notched stick instead.

It is, friend, by a hand-span. Every month. At this rate, in a hundred years, Soljund's will be a lake. Orm does not mind a lake. He does mind what is making it. There is a thing in the bottom, moving in the dark, patient as a root. It grows the hole a little each night, like a snail grows its shell. He would like it gone before the village falls in.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_horse_that_c: Two horses were taken from the Snow-Shod farm and returned with sand in their hooves and ancient coins left behind.
Follow the hoof-tracks toward Nightingale Hall
Search the hall's stable-yard for the horse-thieves

Aldis turns one of the coins over, slowly. "A hoard. Old as dust. Well, stranger, I shall keep the coins. A horse is a horse, and a coin is a coin, and a thousand-year-old king is a very handsome thing to hang above the stable door."
Tell Aldis who rode his horses
A band of riders used them to move something across the Rift at night. They paid in coin from a hoard they found. They have gone.
You have a stable with an empty stall.
Two horses came back thin and wet, and a thousand-year-old king hangs above the stable at the Snow-Shod farm, as a mark of respect.

Two, friend. A mare and a gelding, taken in the night by a man who left a coin for each. Aldis took the coins to the smith. They are not Skyrim coin. They are old, very old, stamped with a face that has been dead a thousand years. The horses came back this morning, thin and wet, with sand in their hooves. There is no sand within a month's ride. Someone has been riding them far.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_horse_that_w: A grey mare at the Windhelm stables waits for a rider who was killed a month ago on the road. Brenuin wants the rider's last possession recovered.
Search the roadside near Riverside Shack where the rider fell

Brenuin takes the scarf and carries it to the stall. The grey lowers her head into the cloth, and breathes in, long and slow. Then, for the first time in a month, she lifts her head and eats. "Thank you, stranger," Brenuin whispers. "She has her rider back, in the only way she can."
Bring the saddle-bag to the grey
The bag was by the road, torn. A scarf was in it, and a letter. The horse should smell it.
You are looking at an old horse.
A grey mare in the Windhelm stables eats her oats with a scarf draped over the stall-door, and has begun, slowly, to look at the road again.

The grey, friend. Her rider was killed on the road a month ago. A wolf, they said. The grey has not left the stall since. She does not eat. She does not drink. Brenuin has sat with her at night. She looks at the door as if waiting. She wants her rider. Brenuin cannot give her that. But he thinks there is a thing the rider carried, that the grey would know.
The Horse That Would Not Leave
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_inn_that_wou: The ruined inn of Old Hroldan stands on rotten beams and sand foundations. Elder Guthlaf wants to know what is holding it up.
Search the cellar of the Old Hroldan inn
Clear the cellar of the draugr-bound pillar

Guthlaf nods, slowly, with great gravity. "A pillar. A guard. A thousand years. And it has held, quietly, without thanks. Stranger, I shall paint a name on that pillar, and burn a candle at its foot. Old Hroldan has stood because someone, once, did not let it fall."
Tell Guthlaf what holds the inn up
A stone pillar, set by an old Nord king, and a draugr guarding it. It has been holding the inn up for a thousand years. I left the pillar. I put the draugr to rest.
Your inn is held up by rope.
The inn of Old Hroldan leans on, held up by a pillar that has a name painted on it now, and a candle.

It is, friend. Rope, prayer and the occasional kick. The old Hroldan inn has been leaning for fifty years, and every winter Guthlaf expects it to go. It does not. He has examined the beams. They are rotten. He has examined the foundations. They are sand. It stands on something else. Something under the floor, quietly holding it. He would like to know what, before he thanks it.
The Inn That Would Not Fall
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_lamp_that_ne: The lantern of the Lamp-Wife's inn went out for the first time in nineteen years, and a guest has not returned from the dark.
Keep watch at the lantern until it is touched again
Stop the thing that snuffs the lamp

Hilde lowers her head, and for a time says nothing at all. "At rest. Well. It is something. He paid for three nights and stayed for one. Stranger, the lamp will burn again tonight. And I shall leave a second one lit, by the door, for him."
Tell Hilde what put out the lamp
It was a wisp, drawn by the flame, that smothered it and carried your guest into the dark. I put it down, and he is at rest.
You are the one with the lantern.
The lamp of the Lamp-Wife's burns every night, and a second, smaller one burns beside it, for the one who did not return.

Every night for nineteen years, friend. Hilde has not let it go out once. Last night it did. Not oil. Not wind. A hand, in the dark, closed over the flame. Hilde saw nothing. A guest, a good man, walked out into the dark and has not come back. She would very much like to know what put out her lamp, and where it put the man.
The Lamp That Never Goes Out
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_ledger_of_he: Mason Orvar wants the toll-ledger of Helgen, lost in the burning of the keep, recovered from scavengers in Bonechill Passage.
Search the scavengers' camp in Bonechill Passage
Drive off the bandits who have been burning Helgen's papers

Sigrun reads and her hand goes to her mouth. "Paid in full. He paid. He was not a smuggler, they said. They were wrong. They were all so very wrong. Thank you, stranger. Take what the Widow has: a cup of the good ale, and the window candle for the night."
Show Sigrun the last page of the ledger
Your husband's caravan is on the last page. It is not burnt. It lists a toll paid in full, and a name signed on the line below.
You are repairing a gate no one uses.
A scorched ledger told a widow that her husband had paid every toll he owed. The gate at Helgen has been reset a little straighter since.

Someone will. A ledger went missing from the tollhouse the night the keep burned, and with it the names of every caravan that paid to pass. There are heirs asking. There are debts to be settled. Orvar thinks a scavenger took it from the ashes. The ruins of the tollhouse are picked clean, but the bandits of Bonechill Passage have a habit of burning paper to keep warm.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_millstone_th: The great wheel at Anga's Mill is turning backwards against the current. Gudrun suspects something in the spring at Uttering Hills.
Follow the mill-race upstream to Uttering Hills Cave
Drive off whatever is turning the water

Gudrun watches the great wheel slow, turn once, and then, with a groan of wood, begin to move the right way. "True. Honest. As it should be. Stranger, the first flour out of this mill is yours. I will bake the bread myself. It will not be good bread, but it will be correct."
Tell Gudrun the wheel will turn true
A wisp had set up a whirlpool in the spring, and fish were swimming in circles. It is gone. The mill-race runs straight.
Your wheel is turning the wrong way.
The great wheel of Anga's Mill turns true. The first loaf was dense, round and entirely correct, and was delivered with a certain pride.

Backwards, friend. Against the current, against the wind, against all reason. The great wheel turns the wrong way, and the grain comes out as dust, or as seed, depending on the day. Gudrun is not a woman who minds a miracle. She minds a miracle that ruins her flour. The mill-race runs from the high spring at Uttering Hills. Something up there is turning the water.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_miners_wages: The Kynesgrove miners' wage-purse has been short by a tenth three weeks running. Foreman Dorlag wants the carter's route watched.
Watch the pay-cart's road near Gloombound Mine
Stop the ambusher who skims the pay-cart

Dorlag takes the purse and counts it, slowly, three times. "A tenth. A tenth of every wage. For months. My men have been feeding their families on nine-tenths of what they earned. Stranger, I will make it right, one tenth at a time. I will tell them it was you who found it. They will want to buy you a drink, and then another."
Tell Dorlag who was skimming the wages
Brynolf, a former carter. He kept a tenth of every purse and said it was a toll. The tenth is here.
The wages of Kynesgrove come whole again. Dorlag has made a ledger, in which a tenth is set aside, every week, for the carter's widow, and every man in the mine has signed.

They are, friend. Not by me. By the carter who brings the pay from Windhelm. Three weeks running, the purse has been light by a tenth. Dorlag does not wish to accuse a Windhelm man of theft without proof. The cart goes by Narzulbur and Gloombound Mine. A road of bad places and worse company. Ride the road. Watch what comes off the cart.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_missing_ash_: A row of ash-yams was carefully dug up at the Hlaalu farm in the night. Ysolda suspects a Dunmer who misses home.
Search Refugees' Rest, where the Dunmer homeless gather

Ysolda's face softens, and she wipes her hands on her apron. "A granddaughter who is sick. Stranger, tell her to come to the farm. Not for the yams. For the whole row. Ysolda will give her the rest of the field, and the recipe, and a corner by the fire. I should have grown more in the first place."
Bring Ysolda what you found at Refugees' Rest
An old Dunmer woman had dug them. She has no home, and no yams, and a granddaughter who is sick. She asked me to say sorry.
An old Dunmer woman has a field, a stew-pot and a corner by the fire at the Hlaalu farm. Her granddaughter is mending.

They are, friend. An entire row, taken in the night. Not stolen. Dug up, with a spoon, and the earth patted back down. Ysolda has no idea who would be so tidy. It would have to be a Dunmer, and a very particular one. Ash-yams are a thing a Dunmer misses when they are far from home. Find them, and find out what they need.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_oak_that_fel: Dagmar's husband was killed by an oak that fell against the wind. She asks a stranger to examine the stump and the clearing and tell her the truth.
Search the stump and the clearing near Meeko's Shack
Confront the hunter who set the felling-cut

Dagmar is silent for a long time. Then she picks up her axe, and carries it to the stump, and sets it there with the handle pointing up. "Thank you, stranger. Three years. It was never the tree. It was never the forest. I owe the oak an apology, and I shall give it, and plant a sapling in its place."
Tell Dagmar what happened to her husband
A poacher, hiding in the oak's shade, was spotted by your husband. He cut the tree to bury the witness. He is dead now, and he told me.
You look at that oak as if it had a name.
A widow planted a sapling beside an old stump, and, for the first time in three years, stopped cursing the forest.

It does, friend. Her husband's. The oak that killed him fell the wrong way, against the wind, against the grain, as if it chose. Dagmar has never been a fanciful woman. She has been trying for three years to believe it was only an oak. A woodsman from Haafingar swears it was cut with an axe too clean to be a man's. Go to the stump. Tell her what you see.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_pilgrim_who_: A pilgrim has stopped on the Seven Thousand Steps and will not move. Dagny asks a stranger to climb and ask him why.
Climb the Seven Thousand Steps to the stopped pilgrim

Dagny smiles, a thing she does rarely. "Waiting for the mountain. Yes. That is exactly the right thing. Stranger, I have been climbing and he has been waiting, and he is nearer the top than I. Let him be. I will climb past and nod, and he will nod back, and that will be a conversation."
Report the pilgrim's answer to Dagny
He said he is waiting for the wind to change. He is waiting for the mountain to say he may continue. He is an old man, and very content.
You are staring up a very long stair.
A pilgrim waits for the mountain on the thousandth step, and Dagny nods to him every time she passes. The mountain has not yet said.

I am, friend. A pilgrim stopped on the Steps three days ago. Sat down at the one thousand, three hundred and ninth, and has not moved. Not hungry, not cold. Dagny took him a blanket. He thanked her and said he was waiting. For what, he would not say. She has climbed past him eleven times and cannot stop thinking of it. Go up. Ask him. Please.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_rope_that_wa: Ferryman Bjarnhild's rope has been cut three times in a month. She wants the culprit caught on the far bank.
Watch the far bank of the Darkwater at night
Catch whoever is cutting the ferry-rope

Bjarnhild leans on the rope-post, and for a moment looks very tired. "A rival ferry. Upriver. At two coins cheaper. And a man who cut my rope to take my trade. Stranger, I would have given him a loaf and told him to ask. Thank you. The first ride across is on the house, as long as I am alive."
Tell Bjarnhild who cut the rope
It was a cart-driver from the road, paid by a rival ferry to cripple you. I convinced him of his mistake.
The Darkwater ferry runs on a new rope, and its owner sleeps lightly with a knife of her own under the pillow.

Cut, friend. Not frayed. Cut clean on the far side, in the night. Three times this month. A good rope is dear, and the guild-trader at the crossing says it is a rival. Bjarnhild thinks it is the wolves, as wolves chew things. But wolves do not carry a knife. Watch the far bank tonight.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_scarecrow_th: A scarecrow on the Battle-Born farm has been walking towards the house. Erlend wants it dealt with.
Wait at the farmhouse door for the scarecrow
Break the scarecrow and what inhabits it

Erlend takes the straw in both hands, shakes it out, and looks vaguely embarrassed. "A wisp. Bored. Well. I may have talked to it a good deal, the past month. It seemed lonely. Stranger, I shall make a new one, and put a hat on it, and a name. The wisp can have it, if it comes back."
Tell Erlend what was in the scarecrow
A wisp, bored, that had taken up residence in the straw. It is gone. The scarecrow is just straw again.
A new scarecrow stands on the Battle-Born farm, with a hat, a name and a lantern, and does not walk.

Four steps, friend, every night, towards the house. Erlend has put a stake through it. He has put a bell on it. He has asked it, very politely, to stop. It does not. Tonight it is at the door. He would prefer it were not there tomorrow. He would not like to say what he suspects is inside.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_silver_in_th: The Black-Briar Lodge's mead barrels are going out lighter. Steward Ravenna asks a stranger to find the skimmer, quietly.
Search the road to Lost Prospect Mine where the carts go
Catch the skimmer who has been tapping the barrels

Ravenna lets out a slow breath. "Not family. Good. Not family. The lodge may be a sinner, friend, but it does not eat its own. Orrin will be dealt with, quietly, in a way that leaves no ripples. Take this. It is silver. It is the only silver the lodge has ever paid for the truth, and it is the only truth it has ever wanted."
Tell Ravenna who was tapping the casks
A small ring, Orrin and two hands, selling the skimmed mead in the mine. No family. Just men with a long thirst.
You have been watching the casks.
