The Black-Briar Lodge's mead goes out whole again. Whether the skimmers were dealt with quietly or loudly, the stewards of the lodge sleep a little easier.

I have, friend. The Black-Briar mead goes out under a seal every week. Three barrels per cart. Last month, one was a quarter lighter. Lost, the carter said. Spilled. Nothing spills from a Black-Briar barrel. Someone is skimming. The lodge has no wish to find out it was family, so it would like you to find out for it, and tell no one.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_thief_who_re: Every saddle at the Riften stables vanished in a night and returned oiled and polished. Stablemaster Gunnar wants to know why.
Hide in the tack-room and wait for the thief to return
Catch the polishing thief in the act

Gunnar scratches his head, and then laughs for the first time in years. "A saddler who cannot sleep! Well. Stranger, I shall give him a post. Every stable could do with a man who polishes at night. And the leather has never looked so good."
Tell Gunnar why the thief took the saddles
The thief is a former saddler who lost his shop, and cannot sleep unless leather is clean. He took them to polish and brought them back. He meant no harm.
You look at the empty hooks.
The Riften stables now have a night-polisher on the payroll. The saddles have never been so well oiled, and the thief has never slept so well.

A thief, friend. Every saddle gone, every bridle, every blanket. Wiped clean in a night. And then, in the morning, back. Every one, polished and oiled, hung on its hook. It is the cleverest, strangest theft Gunnar has ever heard of. He does not want to catch the thief. He wants to know what a thief wants with a clean saddle for a night. He suspects a very odd sort of person is being very odd indeed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_tower_at_the: Ketil's plough keeps turning up Dwemer parts, and a ticking sound rises from the earth at night. He wants it silenced.
Descend into the Tower of Mzark from the field
Silence the ticking machine and its guardians

Ketil listens for a long time. "Silence. Honest silence. Stranger, I did not know how loud it was until it stopped. I may sleep for a week. Take this spur. It was the first thing the plough turned up. It is a very old, very good spur, and it should go with someone who rides."
Tell Ketil the ticking is stopped
A Dwemer clock, still running. The sphere guarded its key. It is stopped. Your field is safe.
Your plough keeps turning up things.
The clock beneath the Heljarchen field stopped, and with it a month of sleeplessness. The farmer keeps a Dwemer gear on the mantel, and says it is for luck.

It does, friend. Nails, a spur, a bit of chain. And last week, a dwarven gear the size of a plate. The Tower of Mzark is a good half-day off, but its old foundations run under my field, and something down there is waking. Ketil can hear it at night. A tick, tick, tick, like a very large clock. He would like it stopped.
The Tower at the End of the Field
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_the_wreck_that_s: The wreck of the Icerunner sings at night with a woman's voice. Torvald wants it quieted and the song explained.
Row out to the Wreck of the Icerunner at dusk
Quiet the drowned crew of the Icerunner

Torvald is quiet for a very long moment. "My mother. She sang it. She was a cook, on a ship, before I was born. Stranger, I never knew her ship. I never knew where she was lost. I have been trying to place that song for forty years. And you say she is quiet now?"
Tell Torvald whose voice was singing
It was the ship's cook, drowned with the crew. She was singing a lullaby, the one you used to hum, when you were a child.
You are looking out to sea.
The Icerunner sang once more, a single verse, as a man stood on the shore and hummed the second. Then it was quiet, and the tide went out.

At the Icerunner, friend. The wreck off the point. It has been a rotting hull for twenty years. Last month it began to sing. A woman's voice, high and thin, a song Torvald does not know. He is not a man who minds a ghost, but he minds a song he cannot place. There is a feeling, in the second verse, as if it were about him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sky_what_the_miner_f: Prospector Hakon found a strange black vein in Northwind Mine and wants it surveyed and a sample brought out.
Descend to the rock-fall at the bottom of Northwind Mine
Clear the creatures that nest where the vein lies
Chip a sample from the black vein

Hakon stares at the lump for a long time, and then he begins to laugh. "Coal! Four fingers. Coal! Friend, I have lost a finger, a week's wages and a good night's sleep for coal. It is the best coal Hakon has ever seen. Sell it to the smith at Riften. He will thank you, and Hakon will buy you an ale."
Show Hakon what the vein is
It is just coal, Hakon. Very old, very hard, very black coal. It nearly took your hand because the fall was unstable.
You are a man with a secret and one finger short.
The strange vein in Northwind mine was coal. Hakon sold it, drank to it and, in time, forgave the missing finger.

A vein, friend. In the deep of Northwind mine, past a fall of rock the others gave up on. A black vein, wet, that glints like a wet beetle and does not behave like ore. Hakon took out one chunk and it nearly took his hand. He would not go back. He would pay for the chunk's fellows. He would pay more to be told what it is.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.desc: Armourer Decimus Ravo of Fort Frostmoth is missing forty pairs of boots, and a trail of snow that is too clean.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o0.jour: The snow had been brushed smooth with a branch, from the fort gate to the farmhouse step. The thief had been careful, and kind; he had not wanted anyone to follow the tracks and be cold.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o0.text: Follow the too-clean trail to Hrodulf's House
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o1.repl: An old Nord, a cobbler once, who lost his sons on a patrol. He has nobody to cobble for. I think he took the boots to re-sole them. I think he is lonely.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o1.text: Ask Signaller Tisa who lives at Hrodulf's House
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o1.topi: Who is at the old farmhouse?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.c0.l: Let him keep a pair for himself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.c0.r: It is the least we can do. He has earned them, forty times over.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.c1.l: Hire him as the fort cobbler, with a stipend.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.c1.r: A cobbler at the fort. Well. It will be warm for him. Good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.repl: Re-soling. Forty pairs. For a garrison he has never met. I should be furious. I find I am only embarrassed. I shall pay him in barley, and I shall put him on the quartermaster's list, and I shall never mention the chimney.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.o2.topi: The boots are at the farmhouse. The cobbler is re-soling them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.offer: Do you know the sound a hundred boots make leaving? I do now.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.outro: The boots were returned with new soles and a note: "For the boys."
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.pitch: Forty pairs of winter boots, vanished from the armoury in one night, and not a lock forced. I do not believe in thieves who leave no tracks. I believe in thieves who leave tracks leading somewhere else. Look east, toward the old farmhouse where the snow is too clean.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_boots.title: Forty Pairs of Boots
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.desc: Signaller Tisa sees five flashes from a ridge tower nobody should be in.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.o0.jo: A tarnished lantern, a tin of oil, and a girl of fourteen with a bundle of letters. She was signalling her father, who died here, to say her mother was well.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.o0.te: Climb the ridge tower at midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.o1.re: Then I shall flash back, two, then three, then one: all well. The Legion has a code for that. It has never used it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.o1.te: Tell Tisa what the signals were
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.o1.to: A girl in the old tower. She was writing to her father.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.offer: You are not Legion. You are not afraid of the dark. Good.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.outro: The old tower lantern is now lit every night. Tisa answers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.pitch: At midnight, five flashes come from the old watch-tower on the ridge, from a lantern the Legion does not own. Five means the gate is open. It is not. It means someone out there is lying to us, in code, and has a very steady hand. I want to know who.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_lantern.title: Five Flashes at Midnight
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.desc: Commander Hale needs the garrison resupplied over thin ice and a gate-opener found.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o0.text: Collect the supply sledge at Raven Rock's gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o1.journ: The ice sang under my boots. Twice it cracked. The sledge went across at a run, and I went after it, and neither of us looked back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o1.text: Haul the sledge across the thin ice to the fort
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o2.text: Hold the gate against the thaw-raiders
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o3.reply: Five flashes, sera, from the south lantern, at the third bell. The pin was pulled by someone with a key. The key-holders are four: the commander, the chef, the armourer and me. I did not do it. Check the chef's pot.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o3.text: Ask Signaller Tisa who opened the gate
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o3.topic: Someone opened the gate. Who had the pin?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o4.text: Find the gate pin in the chef's stockpot
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.c0.la: Take the blame. The commander owns his gate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.c0.re: That is not what honour is. It is what loyalty is. Do not tell Orsk I said that.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.c1.la: Place it with Orsk. He opened the gate; he answers for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.c1.re: Then he answers. The garrison will go hungry for a week. Nobody died. That is the part I will hold on to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.reply: Orsk. Orsk, who has fed this garrison for eleven years. I have a choice. I can take the blame myself, say I left the pin in a careless hand, and keep him fed and loyal. Or I can place it with him, and be rid of a man who opened the gate for a girl in the snow, by his own account. Which would you do, stranger?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.text: Present the pin to Commander Hale
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.o5.topic: The pin was in the stockpot. The chef did it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.offer: You look like someone who can walk on ice and not on fools.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.outro: The ice held. The wall held. The stockpot was inspected thoroughly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.pitch: The supply sledge from Raven Rock was due four days ago. The ice is thin and the road is a lie. I need the sledge here by dusk. And I need whoever opened my gate last night to be found before the thaw-raiders try it again. The Legion does not ask nicely. I am asking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_ff_thaw.title: Thaw
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.desc: Sister Ilvani asks you to speak with two spectral sentries on the windward wall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o0.journa: Two shapes stood at the parapet, helmets turned toward the sea. One of them lifted a hand, and pointed to a hollow in the wall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o0.text: Keep watch on the windward wall at the second bell
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o1.text: Take the sealed orders from the hollow in the wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o2.reply: Orders to hold the line until relieved. They were never relieved. Their commander died before he could cancel them. Give me the paper; I shall read it aloud, at the second bell, with a lantern. Then they may go home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o2.text: Bring the orders to Sister Ilvani
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.o2.topic: Two sentries, a hollow in the wall, and these.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.offer: Can you stand watch in the cold? The dead do not stay still.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.outro: The windward wall is, at last, only a wall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.pitch: The windward wall has two sentries too many at the second bell. They wear Redoran colours older than the bulwark, and they stand where no one built a post. The living guards will not relieve them. The dead will not leave. Someone must ask them what they are waiting for.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_ash.title: The Sentries on the Windward Wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.desc: The shaft is sealed, but the five men are still unaccounted for, and families want the bodies.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.o0.rep: They want the names carved, and the bodies buried beside them. We can do the first. For the second, someone must go into the lower gallery before the seal is placed. I would not ask a stranger. I am asking.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.o0.tex: Speak to Sister Ilvani about the families
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.o0.top: The shaft is sealed. What do the families want?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.o1.tex: Recover the five miners before the seal is set
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.outro: The names are carved above the bulwark gate, five in a row.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_hollow.title: A Hollow Quiet
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.desc: Captain Veleth of Raven Rock's bulwark counts more dead miners than Foreman Gorm reports. She wants the difference explained.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o0.repl: Fourteen. Fine. Fourteen. Five of them did not die in the mine. They walked into the lower gallery after the second collapse, and did not come out, and I did not stop them. They said the digging was singing to them. Here is the tally. I scraped seven notches. I am sorry.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o0.text: Ask Foreman Gorm to count with you
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o0.topi: Nine, you said. The Captain counts fourteen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o1.jour: The headframe creaked in the wind. Below it, the shaft descended past a landing hung with lanterns, then a landing without. Somebody had nailed a board across the third level: "Do not listen."
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o1.text: Find the collapsed lower gallery at the foot of the shaft
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o2.text: Clear the gallery of what the digging has woken
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o3.text: Take the humming spike from the cracked wall
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o4.text: Face what the spike was holding in
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.c0.l: Seal the shaft. The ebony is not worth it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.c0.r: Then Raven Rock loses its income, and keeps its people. I will write that I sealed it myself, to spare you the hate.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.c1.l: Break the curse. Keep the mine open.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.c1.r: Then I shall keep the lanterns lit and the miners few. Pray it holds. I will not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.repl: Then the mine is cursed or merely haunted, and I do not have the staff to tell which. The Council will ask me whether to seal the shaft or to break the mine's curse. I would like to say: you tell me. You are the one who has stood in it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.o5.topi: The spoil heap, Captain. Five men, a humming spike, and something that I have put down.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.offer: You count well, I assume? Anything beyond your fingers?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.outro: Raven Rock sleeps, and some say it listens.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.pitch: The foreman reports the mine at nine dead since Frostfall. I count fourteen graves. The difference is five men, and the foreman's hand shakes when I ask. Walk the diggers' barracks, count who's missing, and tell me what is under that heap before the Redoran Council arrives and asks me the same thing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_spoil.title: The Spoil Heap Question
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.desc: The mine stays open, with a night-watch set to keep the humming quiet.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.o0.repl: You are a braver fool than I. Take the third landing at midnight. If it sings, hum back. I have no better advice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.o0.text: Set the night-watch with Foreman Gorm
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.o0.topi: The mine stays open. I will keep the watch with you.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.o1.text: Hold the third landing against what answers the hum
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.outro: The watch holds. The mine is quieter than it has been in a year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_vigil.title: The Ebony Vigil
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.desc: Rolan the dockhand wants a wharf dispute between ash-yam farmers and net-men settled.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o0.repl: The Redoran Council, with a cargo of timber from a Skaal trader. The Council wrote a lease and lost it. The Skaal trader kept the copy. Find the Skaal at Tel Mithryn's ferry, if you must, or ask Ashlander Tuvi, who remembers everything for a bowl of soup.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o0.text: Ask Tindra Hael who actually owns the planks
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o1.repl: North planks for the net-men, south for the yam-boats, and the middle plank, a single plank, for whoever arrives first at dawn. It was a joke the Skaal trader made. Both crews have been fighting over a joke.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o1.text: Ask Ashlander Tuvi what he remembers
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o1.topi: The wharf lease. What did it say?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o2.jour: Both crews arrived at the same moment, glared, and sat down, one on each side of the plank. The plank, I noted, is somewhat comfortable.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.o2.text: Walk the wharf at dawn and mark the middle plank
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.offer: You look dry, which is rare. Do you have a mind for arbitration?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.outro: The middle plank now has a bench on it, and both crews sit there at dawn arguing about something else.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.pitch: Two crews, one wharf. The ash-yam farmers claim the south planks; the net-men claim the north. There is a tide-mark on every plank and neither side agrees which it is. I have been punched by both. Settle it, or give me a good excuse to be on the next boat.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_rr_wharf.title: A Dispute Over Planks
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.desc: Elder Hjalmgerd needs the lost hundredth verse of the Skaal Telling before the dark moon.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o0.re: I was there when old Frodi died. His last words were a name: Haknir. Not a man. A shoal. He said, 'Tell it at Haknir's Shoal where the horkers sing.' Take my horn. It is the right pitch.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o0.te: Hear Aslfur's tale of the horn
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o0.to: Elder Hjalmgerd needs the story of where the Telling broke.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o1.re: The shoal is where my father lost a boat and found a song. A bone slip lies in the old cairn there, if the horkers have not eaten it. They are polite. They are not honest.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o1.te: Hear Torvald's tale of the shoal
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o1.to: Aslfur says Frodi named Haknir's Shoal.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o2.re: It knew it. It is holding it. The wind will not release a word until it is asked in the right place, with the right voice, by someone who has listened to all three tellers. You have. Go.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o2.te: Hear Wren's tale of the wind
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o2.to: The wind is quiet. Does it know the verse?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o3.jo: The horkers lined the shore like a congregation. One had a bone slip at its feet and watched me with shrewd, patient eyes.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o3.te: Go to Haknir's Shoal where the horkers sing
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o4.te: Take the missing verse from the cairn
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o5.c0: Sing it as it was written. The noble ending.
Then the Telling is whole, and kind to the dead. It is a good ending. It is not a true one. I will tell it in my sleep, and know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o5.c1: Sing it as it happened. The honest ending.
Then the Telling is whole and hard. Chief Frodi lost and was glad. The village will gasp. It will remember. It may even be better for it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o5.re: It reads: 'And the old chief was glad, for he had never meant to win.' Written, it is noble. Told as it happened, Frodi lost the fight and was glad because he lost. The Telling has always been written. Shall we tell it as written, or as it happened? You are the one who found it. You choose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o5.te: Return the verse to Elder Hjalmgerd
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.o5.to: The verse is whole. The last line is damp. Which shall we tell?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.offer: You listen like someone raised by storytellers. Are you?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.outro: The hundredth verse was spoken at the fire, and the wind began to blow again.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.pitch: The Telling is a hundred verses long, and ninety-nine are known. The hundredth went out of Chief Frodi's mouth with his last breath, and nobody caught it. At the next dark moon we must tell all hundred at the fire or the fire will forget us. Gather the tellers' stories, find what was lost, and bring it home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_telling.title: Telling at the Fire
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.desc: Aslfur Wide-Eye took a horn from a horker and found Dunmer runes carved on the inside.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o0.rep: A Dunmer fisherman's mark and a debt: 'I owe the bull one favour.' He tamed a horker pup, carved the horn, and set it free. The bull has been waiting, I think, to repay it. Look for a hut on the eastern headland.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o0.tex: Ask Ashlander Tuvi to read the runes
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o0.top: These runes. Can you read them?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o1.jou: A sunken hut, a lone chair, and a mouldering Dunmer coat on a peg. On the table, a bowl of fish with a rune drawn beside it. The bull had been leaving a fish each morning.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o1.tex: Find the fisherman's hut on the headland
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o2.rep: Then I shot the bull when it came to the fisherman's door. I am a poor hunter after all. Take the horn back, and set a fish at that door every morning, from me.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o2.tex: Tell Aslfur what the horn meant
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.o2.top: The horn was a favour owed. The bull has been repaying it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.offer: You have the eyes for it. Look at this horn and tell me what is wrong.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.outro: There is a fish at the headland door every morning, and no one admits to putting it there.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.pitch: I took this horn from a horker bull on the north shore, a good bull, a fat bull, and the horn has runes on the inside. Dunmer letters. Not Skaal. Somebody carved a horker, years ago, and let it live. Somebody wanted it to be found. I would like to know who, and why.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_trophy.title: A Trophy That Is Wrong
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.desc: Wren Wind-Listener asks you to visit three of the All-Maker stones with small gifts.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o0.reply: Say nothing. The stones prefer it. Leave the gift at the foot and step back three paces. The wind will tell you if it is pleased.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o0.text: Take the three gifts from Wren
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o0.topic: I will carry them. Tell me what to say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o1.text: Leave a feather at the Wind Stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o2.text: Leave a seed at the Tree Stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o3.journ: At the third stone, the wind lifted. Not a gust. A breath. It stirred the grass, once, and then went on its way over the hills, singing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o3.text: Leave a claw at the Beast Stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o4.reply: Then it was only waiting to be noticed. It always was. The quiet is back to being a quiet. Thank you. Ketil has a name for it, if you want to hear it. It is Frodi. He may be right.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o4.text: Tell Wren the wind has returned
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.o4.topic: The wind lifted at the third stone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.offer: Do you feel it? That is not silence. That is attention.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.outro: The wind blew again that night, with the first snow.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.pitch: The wind has gone quiet and I am the only one who thinks it matters. It will speak again if three stones are visited with the right gift: the Wind Stone, the Tree Stone and the Beast Stone. At each, a small thing: a feather, a seed, a claw. Place them and listen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_sk_wind.title: The Wind Has Gone Quiet
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.desc: Skald Hrolf wants a legendary snow-boar hunted for the hall of Thirsk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o0.repl: The ridge above the Beast Stone. Follow the wallows, count the toppled pines, and when the tracks stop, look up. It likes to watch you come. Do not let it have the high ground.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o0.text: Ask Brynja where the boar was last seen
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o0.topi: The Skald wants a snow-boar. Where?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o1.jour: The wallows ran in a ring around a snow-bank. In the middle of it, a toppled pine, and beyond it, a shape so large I took it for a boulder, until it breathed.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o1.text: Track the boar to the ridge above the Beast Stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.c0.l: Hang the tusk by the door. Let all see it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.c0.r: It is a great sight. It will be a great story. And a poor drinking-cup. Done.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.c1.l: Break it into cups for every hunter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.c1.r: Fifty cups of bone. Fifty hunters, every feast, remembering. Perhaps it will do us more good as dust.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.repl: A tusk! And such a tusk. Now, the hall must decide how to remember it. I could hang it by the door, and every guest will see it. Or I could break it into drinking-cups, one for every hunter in the hall, so each of us carries a piece. You killed it; you choose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.text: Bring the tusk to Skald Hrolf
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.o4.topi: The beast is down. Here is the tusk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.offer: You walk like a hunter. Do you hunt like one?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.outro: The Skald raised the first cup and spilled the first drop for the beast.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.pitch: I want a trophy for the rib arch. Not a boar. Not a wolf. Something with a story the bards can sing, a thing with a name. Brynja says there is a snow-boar the size of a hut on the high ridge. Track it. Bring it down. Bring it here, and I will see to it that the hall hangs your name beside the tusk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_beast.title: One More Beast
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.desc: A boar has fled the trophy yard of Thirsk with the hall's oldest rib-beam on its tusk.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.o0.journ: Trotters in the snow, deep prints, and a long scrape where a beam was dragged. The boar stood at the tomb mouth, the beam still on its tusk, pleased with itself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.o0.text: Follow the broken-fence trail toward Vahlok's Tomb
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.o1.text: Wear the boar down without hurting it
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.o3.reply: A scratch on the left. It has been there since the founding. Good. The boar was only taking it home. It was its grandfather's, the story goes. Whatever you say.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.offer: You have the hands for a rope. Do you have the nerve?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.outro: The boar was re-penned, and then given a better fence, at the Skald's own expense.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.pitch: A boar broke the fence at the trophy yard last night and took the oldest rib-beam with it, pinned on a tusk. It is not an escape. It is a theft. The beam is the first rib the hall ever hung. Find it, bring it back, and do not hurt the boar. It is the Skald's, and he is sentimental about pigs.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_boar.title: The Boar That Would Not Be Penned
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.desc: Ingrid Bone-Singer wants to catch Odd the Brewer cheating at dice once, in front of the hall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o0.reply: A drake a throw. And a free cup for the loser. Do not look at my left hand. It is the same hand. It has been the same hand for sixty years.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o0.text: Sit down to a game with Odd the Brewer
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o1.reply: Hollow on the six, lead on the one. They were mine; I carved them for his fortieth. I never asked what he did with them. Put them on the anvil and strike: the lead rings.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o1.text: Ask Sigrun to look at the dice afterward
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o1.topic: The dice have a weight. Can you tell which?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o2.reply: Then at the next feast, I shall sing the Ballad of the Honest Dice, and Odd will be astonished at his own talent. He will pay for the meads that night. Nobody will mind.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o2.text: Tell Ingrid the dice are loaded
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.o2.topic: Loaded. And Sigrun will say so in front of the hall.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.offer: Do you gamble? Do you hate being cheated?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.outro: Odd still cheats. He does it now with a flourish, and the hall applauds.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.pitch: Odd has been cheating at dice for sixty years and nobody has ever caught him. The hall places bets on it, privately. I want him caught, once, in front of everyone, and then forgiven, because he brews the best mead on the island. Be my witness at the next game.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_th_dice.title: Odd Dice
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.desc: Pelli Sporeheart and Magister Ildar want a judge for their annual contest of whose lights are brighter.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o0.journ: Dust like crushed teal glass, warm as breath, in the cracks of the stone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o0.text: Gather glow-dust at the Sun Stone for Pelli
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o1.reply: A lamp! A lamp, she says. It is a sophisticated luminous apparatus. It is, I admit, shaped like a lamp. Judge fairly. Judge, please, before dusk, when the effect is best.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o1.text: Ask Magister Ildar what he is hiding in the cap
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o1.topic: Pelli says you cheat with a lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.c0.la: The garden. It needs no lamp.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.c0.re: Ha! A garden wins. He will sulk for a week. A good week.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.c1.la: The tower. He has earned it with sheer nerve.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.c1.re: Nerve! It is true. He shall be unbearable. I shall bake him a cake and put salt in it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.reply: Choose, then. I shall be gracious in defeat. I shall be gracious in defeat for approximately an hour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.o2.topic: Both are very bright. I must choose.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.offer: You have eyes. Use them. Which of these is brighter?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.outro: Both lights burned until dawn, and nobody slept.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.pitch: The Magister swears his tower-cap glows brighter than my garden. I swear my garden outshines his tower. Once a year we hold a contest and he cheats with a lamp. Be the judge. And fetch me a proper glow-dust from the Sun Stone first; I will not lose on a technicality.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_glow.title: The Glow-Off
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.desc: Yarda Net-Girl sells rumours for cake. Fetch her some from Raven Rock.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.o0.re: A honey-cake, then, for a rumour. She does not know I have a rumour of my own. I will trade you both: take the cake, and I shall tell you where the wreck is.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.o0.te: Buy cake from Tindra Hael at Raven Rock
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.o0.to: A cake. For a girl who sells rumours.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.o1.re: The third rumour is that the Magister's nephew keeps a second mushroom in the cellar that eats compliments. Tell him he looks well. Watch what happens. That is all. That is the whole rumour. I am sorry.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.o1.to: Cake. And a rumour of my own in return.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.offer: Cake. Do you have cake? I deal in rumours, and rumours want cake.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.outro: The cellar mushroom grew a little, and Ildar looked unwell.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.pitch: I have three rumours and one cake-sized hole in my stomach. The first: a ship wrecked west of Raven Rock with a Telvanni crest. The second: a Nord on the road asking after the Magister by his old name. The third: I will not say it until the cake. Fetch cake from Raven Rock and I will tell you everything.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_rumours.title: Rumours for Cake
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.desc: Magister Ildar of Tel Mithryn needs three rare fungi to feed his tower.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o0.text: Gather a glow-gill from the Ashfallow ruin
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o1.text: Gather a whisper-moss from the Sun Stone
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o2.text: Gather an ember-stalk from the black altar
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o3.repl: Hold the lamp. When the chamber breathes, count to four, then drop the glow-gill into the bowl. If the chamber growls, drop the whisper-moss. If it screams, drop the ember-stalk and run.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o3.text: Help Duvren stabilise the test chamber
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o3.topi: I have the three. What do you need?
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o4.text: Quell the test chamber when it wakes
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.c0.l: The safe tutor. Take the year.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.c0.r: Dull. Wise. Take this tome and read it twice. You will thank me in eleven months.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.c1.l: The reckless tutor. A week, and a prayer.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.c1.r: Ha! I knew you had it. Hold on to something.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.repl: Good. Now, the choice. I may tutor you in the safe way, which takes a year and teaches little. Or in the reckless way, which takes a week and may kill you. My uncle would choose the second. I am not my uncle. But I would very much like to be.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.text: Present the spores to Magister Ildar
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.o5.topi: You asked for three. They are in the bowl.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.offer: Ah. A person with hands. Come in, mind the floor, mind the walls, mind everything.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.outro: The tower hummed, and a new room grew on the second floor, apparently by itself.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.pitch: My tower grows by a rule: for every spore it gives, it asks one back. I have run out of ones to give. I want three: a glow-gill from the Ashfallow ruin, a whisper-moss from the stone, and an ember-stalk from the black altar. Do not eat them. Do not smell them. If you smell them, I will know.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sol_tm_spore.title: A Spore for a Spore
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_a_bored_lords_wa: Lord Calantir has wagered a pearl that a visiting astronomer cannot sit an hour without looking down. He wants the chair tampered with.
Tamper with the chair, as Lord Calantir asked.
Ewen closes his eyes. "Then Ewen did not see it. A loose screw, a slight tilt. She will look down. The pearl will be won. And Calantir will be exactly as bored as before."
Tell Calantir to tell her a story instead.
Ewen almost smiles. "A story! Ha! The lord has never told one in his life. Walker, that is either the best idea Cloudrest has had in a century, or the worst."

Ewen looks at his hands. "Ewen could loosen a screw. Ewen could. But the sea-lift pilot does not tamper with seats on the Walk. If a lord wants a thing done, a lord should do it. Ewen suggests you tell Calantir that the best distraction is a very good story, told at exactly the right moment. And the best storyteller is the one who has never been bored."
Ask Ewen what might unsettle a chair above the sea
Lord Calantir wishes the astronomer to look down. What does a cautious man do, who is paid not to?

Calantir rubs his hands. "Splendid. The pearl will be won, or I will have learned a great deal about the character of astronomers. Either way, walker, I shall not be bored today. Take this. It is a very small pearl. It is not the pearl."
It is done. You will see how the wager falls.
You have not yet been shown the chair.
The wager was won, or lost, or never settled, and the chair stood empty for a week. Calantir was not bored for three days, which in Cloudrest is a record.

The chair, walker. Calantir has a chair in the middle of the Balcony Walk, directly above the sea. It is an excellent chair. But a visitor from Skywatch has boasted that she can sit in it for an hour without looking down. Calantir has bet a pearl that she cannot. He would very much like to win. He would like someone to tamper with the chair. Gently. Imperceptibly. He does not want to know how.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_a_match_gone_wro: A groom matched at Mara's Kiss has vanished on his wedding morning, and the bride's family is gathering with torches. Belenwe wants him found first.
Search the Shrine of Lamae Bal where the groom was last seen
Find the note he left behind
Stand between them. The groom was honest, not cruel.
Belenwe straightens her back. "Then she stands. A matchmaker is not a mother, but she may be a shield. Thank you. Four hundred and one, then, and she shall do it properly."
Tell the truth plainly. The family deserves to hear it.
Belenwe nods. "Plainly. A matchmaker's sin is to dress a thing up. Very well. The torches will come. The truth will be the only thing in the room that is not burning."

Belenwe reads the note and her lips tighten. "Loved someone else. And I matched him. Four hundred matches and not a single one has been wrong in this way. Walker, shall Belenwe stand between him and the bride's family, or tell the truth and let the torches fall where they will?"
Bring the groom's note to Belenwe
He ran off because he loved someone else. The note says: 'I cannot lie. I would rather be shamed than false.' He is waiting at the shrine.
You look like a person who has never been matched.
A wedding that did not happen was explained to a very angry family by a very small woman who had never once been afraid of fire.

Ha! Perhaps. Walker, Belenwe has a difficulty. One of her four hundred has gone badly. Not a divorce. A disappearance. A groom of a very fine family, Drathelin, left on the wedding morning, and has not been seen. The bride is of the better house, and her family is gathering outside with torches. Belenwe would like him found, and she would like him found before anyone else finds him.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_a_vow_broken_for: Novice Tevildo broke his vow of silence to comfort a dying traveller. He wants a stranger to hear why, and to carry the traveller's last message.

Tevildo speaks, hoarse from long silence. "She was a courier of the Dominion. She carried a letter. She was dying. She asked me to deliver it to a man in Dusk named Eilen. She said he would know what to do with it. I did not read it. She died before I could ask the man's house."
I will not tell the Abbot. Speak.
Tell Tevildo that the harbour will stand for him before the Abbot.
Eilen nods once. "It will. Harbourmasters speak, in the end, only when it matters. Tell him it matters."
Say nothing. Let the novice's act stand on its own.
Eilen is quiet. "Then it stands. Good. A kind thing needs no witness. But I shall remember it."

Eilen takes the letter and reads it. For a moment her face does not change at all, which is how you know. "My daughter. She went east three years ago. I had stopped hoping. Walker, a novice broke a vow to hold my daughter's hand as she died. I would like him to know that Eilen holds the harbour of Dusk, and that harbour keeps its debts."
Carry the courier's letter to Harbourmaster Eilen at Dusk
A courier died at Trebbite Monastery with a letter for you. A novice broke his vow to comfort her. I have it.
You write your name in the dust.
The Abbot, returning, found a novice in the garden who had broken his vow and had a harbourmaster's letter of thanks tucked inside his sleeve. The vow was amended.

To see whether it stays, walker. A vow of silence, and Tevildo has broken it. Not out of weakness. A traveller stopped at the gate, wounded and half-mad, and begged for a priest to hear her confession, and the Abbot was away, and Tevildo spoke. A few words. The wrong words. The Order will cast him out when the Abbot returns. He would rather be cast out for a reason than kept for a lie. He wishes only to tell it to someone who will not tell the Abbot.
A Vow Broken for a Reason
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_a_wish_with_a_se: Sail-Maker Yeli stitched a sail for a boy whose sister drowned, and it was never returned. She wants it found and brought home.
Search the old sail-store of the dockworks for the missing sail
Drive off the smugglers who store stolen goods in the Colossal Aldmeri Grotto
Find the sail with the hem-name

Yeli runs her thumb along the hem and finds the stitched name by touch. Her breath catches. "Kept. Folded. Oh, walker. Someone has looked after it all this while. I will take it to the boy. He will not know what to say. Neither will I."
Bring Yeli the sail and tell her where it was kept
The sail was hung in a smuggler's cave, folded with great care. Whoever kept it did not use it. They only kept it.
You look like someone who has been told a sail is a promise.
A sail with a name in its hem was carried back, folded very carefully, across the whole quay. The boy, now a man, did not speak for a long time.

It is a promise, walker. And Yeli has a promise to keep. A boy came to the loft three years ago, asking for a sail with his sister's name in the hem. He paid in shells. He was nine. The sister was already lost at sea. Yeli made the sail. She stitched the name, and the sail was taken out, and never returned. Yeli would like someone to find where it went. The boy has grown. He has not stopped coming.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_forty_rainbows.d: One of the forty rainbows of the Prism and Plover has gone missing. Ondolemar thinks it may have been taken, or wandered off.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_forty_rainbows.o: Follow the missing rainbow's colour to the Direnni Acropolis
Wait for noon, when the forty-first colour appears
Gather a shard of lens-quartz from the Acropolis columns

Ondolemar holds the shard to the roof and a fortieth rainbow blooms across the ceiling, bright and slightly smug. "Ha! Home. Walker, you have cost me no more than a small shard and a half-day's work. The house owes you, and the house always pays."
The rainbow was caught on a column of the Acropolis, which hung it like a banner. Here is the shard that kept it there.
Your ceiling has stopped sparkling, Ondolemar.
The Prism and Plover has forty rainbows again. Ondolemar insists the fortieth is a little brighter than the others, and a little prouder.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_forty_rainbows.p: It has, walker, and it was not a cloud. At noon the Prism and Plover makes forty rainbows. For three days, thirty-nine. One has simply left. Ondolemar has measured the ceiling. Every pane is whole. The rainbow went somewhere else. He is not sure if it is a theft or a vacation, and he would like it back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.de: One lamp on Dusk's south wall goes out every night. Lamp-Keeper Sen believes it is waiting for a lost boatman who never came home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.o0: Light the south lamp at dusk and watch it go out
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.o1: Follow the lamp's failing light to Dusk Keep, where the lost boat was moored
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.o2: Defeat the Skiff-Taker and recover the boatman's cap
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.o3: Keep it lit. Let it burn for the ones still out there.
Sen nods, and his eyes are very bright. "Then it burns. Not for him. For everyone. Thank you, walker. Dusk will never put it out."
Put it out. He is home now. Let him rest in the dark.
Sen takes the lamp down with great gentleness. "Then it is finished. A kindness. It will be hard to walk past that wall tomorrow, and easier the day after."

Sen holds the cap and for a moment the whole quay seems to hold its breath. "His cap. His ribbon. Walker, Sen has lit this lamp for nine winters and told himself the man was only late. He was not late. He was waiting for someone to bring him a lamp that was already lit. Shall we keep the lamp lit, or put it out?"
The boatman drowned beyond the headland, years ago. A thing took his skiff and kept it for company. It is at rest now. Here is his cap.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.of: There is one lamp on your wall that will not stay lit.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.ou: A cap with a lilac ribbon was brought home. The south wall of Dusk, whether lit or dark, is no longer waiting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lamps_at_dusk.pi: The southernmost, walker. A fisherman's lamp, hung when his boat went out and never taken down. It goes out each night at the same hour. Sen has changed the wick, the oil, the glass. It goes out because something is waiting for it to go out. A boat came in last week with no crew. The tide brought it. The harbourmaster has not been seen at her desk since.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.de: A twelfth lantern burns blue at the end of the Shimmerene quay, and ships docking beneath it have their cargo secretly swapped. Dock-Master Fen wants it explained.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.o0: Inspect the blue lantern on the dockworks
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.o1: Hide in the sail-loft and watch the quay at the tide
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.o2: Take down Sea-Captain Ssir-Vaal and his boarding crew
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.o3: Report him to the Dominion. The harbour cannot be sold.
Fen nods, grim. "Then it is done properly. The Thalmor will take him. It will break Yeli's heart. It is still correct."
Dismiss him quietly and warn the Maormer off.
Fen is silent for a moment. "A quiet answer. Perhaps a wise one. A harbour that cannot trust its cranes is a harbour that must be rebuilt. Fen will watch him for the rest of his life."

Fen reads the manifest line by line, and the colour drains from his face. "Yeli. The sail-maker's brother. He has run the east crane for ten years. Walker, I have a rota. I know every entry. I did not know this. What would you have Fen do with a man who sold a harbour for a handful of silver?"
Bring the second manifest to Fen
The twelfth lantern was a Maormer runner's signal. The cargo they swapped was weapons for the sea-raiders of Pyandonea. The manifest names the dock-hand who took the bribe.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.ou: The twelfth lantern was cut down, and its blue flame went out with a sound like a held breath. Shimmerene counts eleven poles again, and counts them twice.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_lantern_poles.pi: Eleven, walker. There should be eleven. There are twelve. The twelfth burns blue and no one hung it. Every ship that docks beneath it is boarded that night, and the cargo changes, and nobody on the dock can say who did it. Fen has a rota for everything on this wharf and cannot find a single entry for that lantern. He is very close to being very upset.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_marils_other_pla: Student Maril claims to have found an unrecorded planet and wants a secret witness to confirm it from the Star-Chart Terrace.
Climb to the Star-Chart Terrace after dusk and look where Maril points
Watch the southern sky for two hours

Maril claps both hands over her mouth, then lowers them very slowly. "You saw it. Walker, you saw it. A planet. Mine. Maril's. She will call it... no, she does not know. Something bright. Something stupid. She will think of it at midnight, and regret it at dawn. Thank you. You are the only other person in Tamriel who knows."
There is a small, faint light south of Masser. It moves. It is not on any chart I have seen.
You look like someone who has a secret.
A small, dim planet circles Masser in the margins of one student's notebook. When she names it, she will tell you first.

I do! Maril has a planet. A new one. It is very small and very dim and orbits Masser at an angle nobody expected. The charts say it does not exist. But Maril has seen it, four nights running, from the Star-Chart Terrace. She would like someone to confirm it. Someone who is not Maril, who is not Taleth, who will not tell Taleth. Taleth would take the credit. Taleth would be very gracious about it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_rilens_forbidden: Student Rilen believes a banned volume on the seventh colour of light sits in a private collection at the Direnni Acropolis. He wants someone to look, and only look.
Search the private collection at the Direnni Acropolis

Rilen sits down hard on a step. "Already seen it. Walker, did you... did you feel anything? No. Of course not. It was only a joke. It was only a very good joke, from a very old scholar who wished to be remembered for one clever sentence. Rilen is nineteen. He will remember it for a very long time."
Tell Rilen what the volume says
The volume was there. I read the first page. It describes a colour the eye cannot hold, and ends: 'if you have read this far, you have already seen it.'
You look like a student about to confess.
Rilen has stopped applying for the forbidden volume, and has started writing his own. The first page is a single sentence, and it is very good.

Confess! No. Rilen is not confessing. He is hypothesising. There is a volume in the Restricted Ring, "On the Seventh Colour of Light", and he has applied for access four times. The librarians say no. But Rilen has a theory: it is not in the Library. It was moved, long ago, to a private collection in the Direnni Acropolis. He would be very grateful if someone went and looked. Not removed. Looked.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_bell_at_midn: The dawn-bell of Dawnbreak rings by itself at midnight and ties its own rope in an unfamiliar knot. Sexton Aldaer wants the culprit found.
Keep vigil in the belfry until the bell rings
Strike down whatever is ringing the bell
Let him ring. Midnight is his hour.
Aldaer smiles, tired and very sincere. "Then he rings. Aldaer will sleep through the first stroke, and wake for the third, and say a prayer. A fair bargain."
Ask him to stop. The village needs its sleep.
Aldaer is quiet. "A kindness to the many. A cruelty to one. Still, Aldaer will ask him, politely, once. If he asks politely enough, I think the ringer will go."

Aldaer holds the rope and, for the first time in a fortnight, breathes out fully. "A drowned ringer. His boat was lost the night the third century ended. He is still ringing the hour he missed. Walker, shall we let him? Midnight is a quiet hour. Aldaer does not mind losing sleep, if the ringer has found his bell."
Tell Aldaer what rang his bell
A wisp, with a vex to help. They were ringing the hour a drowned bell-ringer once kept. Here is the rope.
You sleep with one eye on the rope.
The bell at Dawnbreak still rings at midnight, in its own time, or does not. Aldaer sleeps in a bed now, and the rope is tied in the knot the ringer taught him.

Two weeks, walker. Every midnight, three strokes. Nobody touches the rope. The bell is a plain bronze thing, cast in the third century, and it has never done this in its life. Aldaer has sat in the belfry with a lantern, a mallet and his courage. He fell asleep. When he woke, the rope was knotted in a shape he has never seen, and the bell was still swinging.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_bell_beneath: A second bell rings under the water at Firsthold at every tide-turn. Priest Cael wants it found, tuned or quieted.
Search the tide-pools of Greenwater Cove at the turn of the tide
Drive off the drowned that guard the sunken chapel
Hang it in the Rock Chapel. Let the two bells sing together.
Cael's voice is thick. "Two bells. One above, one below. And a priest between. Yes. It will be out of tune, and it will be the finest sound in Auridon."
Return it to the sea. Let the warden have his chapel.
Cael bows. "Then it goes home. Quietly, on the tide. A very good answer, and a very sad one. The chapel will have its bell. I shall ring mine alone, and listen."

Cael takes the clapper and holds it gently, as though it were a sleeping bird. "Four hundred years. Calling a congregation that was already under the water. Walker, shall I hang the clapper in the Rock Chapel, and let its voice join mine? Or return it to the sea, and let him ring his own congregation?"
The drowned bell's clapper, weed and all. The warden rang it every tide to call the congregation he lost. He is at rest.
Your bell rings, Priest. But it rings late.
The drowned bell of Firsthold rings no more at the turn of the tide, or rings in harmony with the chapel's own. A priest has stopped being annoyed.

Late, walker, because it is not the only one. At the turn of the tide, a second bell rings, under the water, a half-beat behind mine. It is slow and green with weed. A drowned bell, from a drowned chapel, that has not been rung in four hundred years. Cael would not mind a ghost. He minds that it is out of tune. He would like to hear it hushed, or tuned, or at least introduced.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_boat_that_re: Ferrywoman Olo carried a passenger she did not take aboard, and the extra crossing has thrown off the count she did not know she was keeping.
Climb Ceporah Tower, where the grey-cloaked passenger vanished
Drive off the shades that keep the tower's stair
Tell her. She has a right to know whose crossing she rows.
Quenel nods slowly. "She will be shaken. And then she will row, as she always has, with a little more care. A good answer."
Let her row. The man is at peace in his work.
Quenel closes his eyes. "A gentle answer. The strait is quiet. He is satisfied, and Olo is content, and neither will ever be the wiser."

Quenel is very still. "A man in a grey cloak. Tall. Walker, there was a Psijic, long ago, who rowed the strait before Olo. He drowned with his boat. He has not stopped his crossings. He is a very patient man. Olo has been doing his work, quite without knowing. The Order has a question: shall Olo be told, or shall the work go on?"
Ask Quenel who the grey-cloaked man was
Olo rowed a man who was not in her boat. He went to Ceporah Tower. Who was he?
Olo rows the strait of Artaeum. Whether she knows whose boat she rows, there is one more passenger on every crossing than there is room for, and she makes a place for him.

Eleven years, walker, and every crossing is the same number. Eleven thousand, give or take. I do not count. Something counts for me. Yesterday the number was one more than it should have been. I rowed over and rowed back, and there was a passenger in the boat who had never been in it. A tall man in a grey cloak. He thanked me, and he stepped off, and I have not been able to find the place he stepped to. I would like to know whose crossing I was rowing.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_eclipse_deba: Two Skywatch astronomers disagree on the date of the next eclipse. Ring-Keeper Ond wants a stranger to fetch a third reading from the old observer.

Taleth hands over a folded sheet with the briefest sniff. "Thursday. Obviously. My rival will claim Saturday, as he claims everything. He has not the patience to measure. Tell the observer to be exact, and to say so loudly."
Ask Taleth for her table of the eclipse
Two tables, two dates. Give me yours and I will carry it to the observatory.
Carry the contested table to the old observer in the Veiled Keep
Announce it jointly, so neither feels bested.
Maril claps. "Jointly! A diplomat! The pair of them will sulk for an hour, and then they will share a pot of tea and a table, and neither will say what they did to deserve it."
Let each find the error on their own.
Maril grins. "A cruelty with a bow on it. Very well. They will find it in a week. Each will say they found it first. Ond will keep sweeping."

Maril reads the third line, and her face does something complicated. "Friday. Friday! Neither, and both! Walker, please do not tell Taleth I laughed. Or the rival. They will each hate me. It is, I think, the first time they have ever agreed on being wrong."
Bring the observer's reading back to the Ring-Walk
The observer says: Friday. Neither of you is right. You each made the same error in the third line, from opposite directions.
You are sweeping a very clean ring.
The eclipse was on Friday. Two astronomers shared a ring-walk and a sulk, and the broom of Ring-Keeper Ond swept on, undisturbed.

I am, walker, and I am not looking up. Two astronomers in the ring-walk have been shouting for three days about the next eclipse. One says Thursday, one says Saturday. Both have tables. Both are certain. A stranger could fetch a third reading from the old observer at the Ring Observatory and settle it. Ond has a broom and a very strong feeling of not being his department.
A pane of the Cloudrest Balcony Walk has vanished without trace. Steward Aviel wants the gap found and what lies beneath it identified.
Walk the Balcony Walk and find the gap

Ewen grips the lever until his knuckles whiten. "Beneath. Walker, Ewen has taken the lift to the water ten thousand times and has never once looked down. He will look down now. Hold the rail. If the thing in the water speaks, please do not answer in Ewen's hearing."
Ask Pilot Ewen to lower the sea-lift beneath the gap
I need the lift lowered. Beneath the missing pane. Something is looking up from the water.
Defeat the Glass-Walker that haunts the water below the walk
Replace the pane. A floor must be whole.
Calantir sighs. "Duty. How dull. Very well. The Walk will be whole, and I shall tell visitors a ghost lives beneath it. They will love it."
Leave the gap. Let the thing see up, now and then.
Calantir's grin is slow and delighted. "A gap! A famous gap! Walker, you are very bad for the dignity of my house, and I adore you."

Calantir leans back in his chair and for the first time in years looks properly awake. "Wanted to be walked upon. A creature that wished to be a floor. Walker, this is the most interesting thing that has happened in my palace since the roof collapsed. May I ask: shall I replace the pane, or leave the gap, and have it be the most famous gap in Summerset?"
Tell Lord Calantir what was beneath his floor
There was a thing in the water that wanted to be walked upon. It took a pane to see if it was allowed. It is gone now.
You are counting something under your breath.
The Balcony Walk of Cloudrest has a gap in it, or does not, depending on who is asked. The thing in the water has stopped looking up.

Panes, walker. The Balcony Walk. Seventeen thousand four hundred and eleven, and then, this morning, ten. One has gone, and no one has seen it fall, and no fragments have been found on the rocks. Lord Calantir will not hear of it. He says a palace with no walls cannot have a missing floor. I would like someone to walk the length of the Walk and find the gap. And then descend by the sea-lift and tell me what is looking back up.
A tree at Shattered Grove has grown eleven feet in a week and has a heartbeat. Grove-Watcher Ilmen wants to know what is growing inside it.
Examine the growing tree at Shattered Grove
Destroy the Growing One before it breaks the trunk
Plant a seed. Let the grove begin again.
Ilmen takes a seed from his pocket, warm. "An acorn. Plain. A plain tree. After that, I think I could do with plain. Thank you."
Let it lie fallow. The grove has had enough.
Ilmen nods. "A fallow field. A fair season. We shall see what the earth wants, and not insist."

Ilmen lowers his gold ribbon, which has become a very long, very useless gold line. "Stopped. Quite stopped. Walker, a tree is a gift and a danger, and I have measured one and dissected another. Shall I plant a seed in the same hollow, and see what grows? Or let it lie fallow, in case the old thing was a symptom of something older?"
Tell Ilmen what grew within the tree
A spriggan, a very old one, was seeding itself inside the trunk to be born. It is dead now. The tree has stopped growing.
Your ribbon is not long enough.
The Growing One lies in the grove's soil, and the tree beside it has stopped counting its own height. Ilmen's ribbon is now a very handsome scarf.

It is not, walker. Eleven feet in a week, and it is accelerating. The tree is not a tree. It has a heartbeat, a slow one, in the second ring. Ilmen has put a stethoscope to it. Something is growing inside the trunk, and it is not a sapling. It would be wise to know what, before the tree reaches a size that makes the question academic.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_heir_in_the_: A young lord vanished from Cloudrest's sea-lift at dusk, leaving only his signet. Ewen wants him found.
Examine the sea-lift and take the lord's signet
Search the sea-caves and wreck below Cloudrest
Drive off the smugglers holding the young lord
Bring the young lord home through the sea-lift
Your lift is empty, Ewen. Why is your hand shaking?
A young lord of a very minor house rose by sea-lift at dawn, pale, damp and apologetic. Ewen looked at the water again that day, for the first time in a week.

Because it was not, walker. A young lord of a very minor house stepped in at dusk, said he wished to see the sea at its closest, and Ewen lowered him. When the lift came up he was gone. No splash. A signet on the floor. Ewen has not been able to look at the water since. If he fell, the sea has him. If he did not, someone took him. Ewen is a coward. He needs someone who is not.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_lantern_of_t: A pale lantern haunts the dunes behind Dusk, and three sailors who followed it did not return. Harbourmaster Eilen asks a stranger to put it out.
Walk the dunes at dusk to Dusk Keep
Wait for the pale lantern to appear
Face the Pale Dune-Wraith that carries the lantern
Hang it in the tower. Let it light the sea for the lost.
Eilen nods, and her eyes shine. "Under the first lamp, then. It will give no light, but it will give company. Thank you."
Bury it in the dunes where it was lit.
Eilen is quiet. "Where it waited. Yes. The sand will keep it. The dunes will be quiet. It is a kindness. It will be a hard walk to the place, and I will make it."

Eilen takes the small glass lantern, and for a long moment she says nothing at all. "For ships that did not return. And my daughter's name. It had been waiting for her. Walker, I shall hang it in the Lantern Tower, under the first lamp. A lantern that has waited that long is owed a place."
Tell Eilen what the lantern was for
The wraith was a keeper of the old keep, waiting for ships that never returned. It lit its lantern for them. It is at rest. The lantern is here.
You walk the quay like someone who has been told not to.
The pale lantern of the dunes no longer burns. Whether hung or buried, it is no longer waiting, and nobody has followed a light off the quay since.

I have, walker, and I am going to say it, once. The dunes behind Dusk are haunted by a lantern. A small, pale light, low on the sand, seen at the edge of the evening by those who work late. It does not move. It waits. Three sailors who followed it did not return. Eilen is not a woman who believes in lights. She has seen her own daughter's name written in the sand beneath it. Please put it out.
The Lantern of the Pale Dunes
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_missing_foli: The Great Library's Folio of Unbound Years has vanished with no record. Chief Librarian Maelia wants it found, quietly, by someone outside the staff.
Search the stacks by catalogue number

Rilen's ears go pink. "Nothing! I mean, a person. A tall one, in a grey hood. I did not see her face. She went east of the Orrery Court, carrying something flat. Walker, I would like to say I was reading a different book entirely."
Ask Student Rilen what he knows of the folio
The folio is missing, and the shelf-marks were changed by someone who knew the system. You study here every night. What did you see?
Follow the grey-hooded librarian to the Direnni Acropolis
Confront the Unlent Reader who has taken the folio
Return it to the shelf. Books are for readers.
Maelia nods slowly. "A librarian's answer. It will be on Shelf Nine, and I will move no shelf-marks. Thank you, walker. You have brought a book home."
Lock the original. Copies for the scholars.
Maelia pauses. "Prudent. A cold answer, but a safe one. The copy will be on Shelf Nine, and the original in my desk. Thank you."

Maelia holds the folio to her chest, and for a moment looks very much younger. "Finish reading it. Oh. Of course. She was the Chief Librarian before me, and she never had the chance. Walker, the folio is a book of years not yet lived. Shall I return it to its shelf and let the library lend it, or shall I make a copy for the scholars and place the original under lock?"
Your folio. It was taken by a former librarian, long dead, who wished to finish reading it. It is safe.
Your ledger is the only thing in this library that looks angry.
The Great Library lost a book and found a ghost, and the ghost, having finished, rests. The shelf-marks have been put back, and no one has changed them since.

The Folio of Unbound Years, walker. A single volume in the Restricted Ring, absent from its shelf for seven days. Not borrowed: the catalogue has no record of anyone touching it. The library has, in forty years, never lost a book. It has been mislaid, and the shelf-marks changed behind it, by someone who knew the cataloguing system in more detail than I do. I would like to ask you very quietly to find out who.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_net_that_sin: Fisher Lyn's net hums a tune it picked up from a sunken stone ring. She wants someone to find the ring and answer the song.
Follow the net's tune along the shore to Greenwater Cove
Wait until the tide drops and the stone ring is exposed
Quiet what sings beneath the ring

Lyn is quiet. Then, softly: "An eel. A lonely one. It is a sad thing to answer a song and silence it. But thank you. Lyn will keep the net, with its tune. A net should remember whom it has been called by."
Tell Lyn the song is finished
It was an eel, an old one, calling for a mate that died long ago. It is quiet now. Your net will hum no more.
Lyn hangs the net each night where the sea air can reach it. It hums, very softly, and she says it is more peaceful.

It does, walker. It hums. Not the wind. A low, patient melody, the same notes every low tide. Lyn pulled it from the water last month. It was snagged on a ring of old stone, deep, where there is no shipwreck in any chart. The tune is sweet. It is also getting louder. Lyn thinks something under the water would like to be answered.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_ring_that_si: The fourth ring of the Orrery Court sighs every night. Orrery-Keeper Thalor believes something is trapped inside.
Wait in the Orrery Court until the fourth ring sighs
Drive off the bronze things that crawl from the fourth ring

Thalor listens in profound silence. "Tired. Of turning. Walker, a ring may wish to rest, may it not? May it rest in a different place? It is a heavy thing, to ask the heavens to change a little, to please a machine. But we have asked greater things of heaven for worse reasons. Thalor will turn the ring. Slowly. And see."
Tell Thalor what the ring wanted
It was not a person. It was the ring itself. It is tired of turning the same orbit and wishes to turn one other way.
You are very still for someone beside a machine.
The fourth ring now turns in a gentle reverse for one hour a night. It no longer sighs, and the astronomers say the sky is a little more interesting for it.

The ring sighs, walker. The fourth. Every night at the hour of Secunda's zenith, a tiny, human sigh, as if the ring were bored. Thalor has oiled it, tightened it, pulled it apart. It sighs. Thalor believes there is a person inside. He does not wish to know how. He would like you to ask it what it wants.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_seneschals_g: Seneschal Valia's loyalty test went wrong: thirty crowns vanished from a room only she entered. She wants an outsider to find the thief, even if it is herself.
Search the third room of the Palace test-wing
Hide in the room and watch the coins at night
Catch the one who takes the gold

Valia looks at the coin you place in her palm and for the first time, a smile flickers. "She was after my list. Of course. The Chancellery has been trying to learn who is trusted and who is tested for years. Walker, you have found a thief, and you have also found that Valia is not the only tester in Alinor. That is a very useful piece of knowledge, and a very unwelcome one."
Tell Valia who took her gold
It was a courtier of the Chancellery, veiled, who was trying to learn who else was tested. She wanted to know your list.
You seem to have been waiting for someone honest.
Thirty crowns returned to their room. Valia now leaves a second set, in a second room, just in case.

Honest is a very expensive thing in Alinor, walker. Valia leaves gold in unlocked rooms, and notes who takes what. Last week, thirty crowns vanished from the third room, and the only person who entered was Valia herself. She is very sure she did not take it. She is slightly less sure she did not forget. Valia has never been a suspect in her own tests before. It is a most unsettling experience.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_sixteenth_av: Prism-Smith Ildren believes Alinor's plan hides a sixteenth avenue, struck from the map by a lost order. He has cut a prism to reveal it and wants it walked.
Walk the avenue that leads from the Royal Palace, prism in hand
Walk the avenue that leads past the Golden Gryphon Garret
Walk the avenue that ends at the Alinor Docks
Open the sealed seam beneath the Crystal Tower
Defeat the Warden of the Sixteenth Gate
Publish it. The city should know what it forgot.
Aelwen bows, very slightly. "Then the avenue will be walked again, and the exile's name read at the Hall of Law. Alinor will remember. It will be uncomfortable. Perhaps it should be."
Seal it. Some gardens are better left in mourning.

Aelwen takes the leaf and sets it, gently, back in the Ledger. "Then it returns to its place, and the city remains as it believes itself. A mercy. You have the Chancellor's gratitude, and her silence."

Aelwen reads the leaf in total stillness. When she is done she folds her hands. "It was struck because it led to the mourning garden of the first Queen's sister, who was exiled. The Court wished the avenue forgotten, and the sister with it. The Chancellery has kept this leaf for three thousand years, in the one place no one would think to look. Walker, shall it be published, or sealed?"
Bring the leaf from the sixteenth avenue to Chancellor Aelwen
The sixteenth avenue is real. Behind the gate lies a single page of the Ledger. It records why the avenue was struck.
You are looking at the city the way I look at a stone.
Alinor has sixteen avenues now, or has always had, depending on who is asked. The mourning garden is quiet, and the prism is back in its smith's window.

Walker, count the avenues with me. Fifteen from the Crystal Tower, I was taught, and the plan on the Chancellery wall says sixteen. The sixteenth was struck out in the third century, by an order that has been lost. I have cut a prism that shows what a mason's eye is trained not to see. Walk each avenue with it. Tell me where the city is lying.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_slipped_ring: The Great Orrery of Skywatch is slipping by seven minutes a day. Astronomer Taleth suspects a hidden gear and wants someone to climb the rings and find it.
Measure the slip on the ring-walks
Climb to the Veiled Keep above the outer ring, where the hidden gear is said to be
Stop Valdis the Unwinder, who has been slowing the rings
Return to Skywatch and wait for midnight, the moment of true alignment
Report the theft. The Dominion should know the southern sky is missing.
Taleth pauses. "The Dominion will want to know why we kept it. They will send a Justiciar. A grim answer. But the rings are aligned, so perhaps a grim answer will do."
Search for it ourselves. The southern sky is ours.
Taleth sets her three spectacles very straight. "Then we do. Quietly. Walker, you are the first outsider the Orrery has ever trusted. Do not make me regret it."

Taleth takes the gear with both hands. "Set it. Hold it. Count to seven. Now release. The rings align. Listen, walker. Hear that? Nine rings, one sky, at last. Valdis stole a star-chart of the southern sky. It is still missing. Will you search for it, or shall I report the theft to the Dominion?"
Set the seventh gear into its place at midnight
The gear is whole. Valdis was unwinding it, a degree each day, to hide a theft in the star-charts. Let us set it back.
The Great Orrery of Skywatch keeps true time again. Nine rings, one sky, and one very grateful astronomer in three pairs of spectacles.

Late, walker, by seven minutes a day. A week of it. The outer rings keep slipping behind the inner, and the Orrery now shows a sky that is a week out of date. A week! Navigators will steer by it. Farmers will sow by it. I have measured every gear. All are whole. One alone is unaccounted for: the seventh. It is missing from the log. It should not exist, and I cannot take the Orrery apart to find it. Climb up. Find what is hiding in the machine.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.de: The key to the Tide Gate of Firsthold was stolen by a hag and replaced with a copy. The gate is jammed, and the next high tide will flood the lower town.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.o0: Check the Tide Gate and confirm the jam
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.o1: Cross the causeway at low tide to the shoal-caves beyond the Veiled Keep
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.o2: Defeat Old Maud Saltrib and take back the key
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.o3: Race back across the causeway before the tide turns
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.o4: Report her. The gate cannot be trusted to anyone with a grudge.
Ro sighs. "Then she will be found, and brought, and judged. It is right. It will not feel right. Thank you."
Let it lie. She is old, and the sea has already taken everything else from her.
Ro looks at the water for a long time. "A mercy. Ro will say nothing. The sea will keep its own accounts."

Ro fits the key and the gate begins to move, shuddering and grinding like a very old man standing. Water thunders against it and holds. "In time. Barely. Walker, you have saved the lower town from a drowning. Shall Ro report Maud's theft to the Watch, or let it lie? She was a gate-keeper before me, and she did not mean harm."
The key is whole. Maud kept it as a keepsake. She said she wished to feel the sea lock behind her at least once.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.of: Your gate-key looks heavier than it should.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.ou: The Tide Gate of Firsthold holds against the flood. The lower town was spared, and an old woman in a cave goes unreported.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tide_gate.pi: It is, walker. The key is not the one the gate was made for. Ro found the real key was taken by a hag in the shoal-caves, who left a copy of rusted iron in its place. The gate is jammed half-closed. At next high tide it will flood the lower causeway with half the town on it. The tide waits for no one. You have until the water turns. Cross at low tide, get the key, bring it back before the flood.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_traitors_doo: A fragment of the Traitor's Vault is leaking into the ruined Psijic college on Artaeum. Adept Quenel wants a stranger to enter the vault and silence the door that wears a face.
Cross to Artaeum by Olo's ferry
Enter the Traitor's Vault and begin the corridor of doors
Defeat the Door That Wore a Face
Lock it in the Order's vault. Some temptations do not belong in the world.
Thel inclines his head. "Then it is bound, and I am bound to it, and neither of us will speak of it again. It is a heavy answer, and a safe one."
Break the shard. Let no one look into it again.
Thel does not hesitate. The shard shatters in his palm, and the hall seems to breathe out. "It is done. I will never know whether the old man was a vision or a vice. Thank you."

Thel does not speak for a very long moment. "I looked into it once, for three hours. I saw myself as a teacher, an old one, with a hundred students. I said yes. I would have stayed there forever. Walker, I do not know whether to break the shard or keep it. Shall I lock it in the Order's vault, or return it to the world?"
Show the mirror shard to Initiate Thel
The mirror is broken. A shard remains. It shows whatever the holder would say yes to.
You have a very careful way of holding a broom.
The Traitor's Vault has one fewer door. The initiate who sat before the mirror spoke again that evening, and said only: 'Good morning.'

Careful. Yes. The stones of this place do not like to be hurried. Walker, I have a difficulty. A fragment of the Traitor's Vault has begun to leak into the college. A mirror that shows what one would say yes to. An initiate sat before it for three hours last night, and has not spoken since. The Order has asked me to deal with it quietly. I would prefer you did, since I would very much like to be a person who has never seen the mirror. Take this token. It is how the island knows you are expected.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_tree_of_two_: Two old women of King's Haven have fought over an apple tree for a hundred years. Syllaen wants the original deed found in the Direnni registers.
Search the old registers at the Direnni Acropolis

Syllaen stares. Behind her, her neighbour sits down on the step. Neither speaks. Then, slowly, Syllaen takes the eleventh apple from your hand and offers it across the fence, and her neighbour takes it, and the two old women eat it between them, on the wall, in the sun. Neither says a word, and neither needs to.
Read the deed to Syllaen and her neighbour together
The deed is clear. The tree is held jointly. It was always meant to be shared.
You are carrying an apple like an unexploded charm.
A hundred-year quarrel ended with a single apple, divided. The tree has been well pruned since.
