It is a gift, walker, from the other woman. She leaves one every day. Syllaen has eleven in her cellar, rotting. She cannot throw them out. She cannot eat them. The tree is theirs, both. A hundred years of lawsuits. The neighbour is old. Syllaen is old. Someone should settle it before one of them dies and the tree goes to cousins. Find the original deed. The Direnni Acropolis keeps the older registers.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_winner_never: Every winner of the Golden Netch race sails off and never returns. Racer Quil wants a stranger to win, find out why, and come back alive.
Win the race by crossing the line before the sun is at its height
Ride the winning balloon to the end of its course at the Gryphon Aerie
Take the Winner's Banner from the nest where the previous winners landed

Quil laughs until she has to hold her sides. "A cliff! A very good view! Nine years! They were embarrassed. Of course they were. Walker, I have never been so pleased to be second. I shall go up there next year, and ask them how they managed to lose a balloon and keep their dignity."
Return to Quil and tell her where the winners went
The winners did not vanish. They landed on a cliff nest, and were not able to climb down. They have been waiting, with a very good view, for someone to come and ask them about it.
Nine winners were found waiting on a cliff, none of them keen to be rescued. Quil is still second. She has never been happier.

Second in everything, walker, and proud. The Golden Netch race is a whole afternoon of balloons and cheating and sweetmeats. The winner takes the Golden Netch up, and waves, and sails over the sea, and never comes back. Not once in nine years. Quil thinks it is a secret. Quil thinks there is a prize in the sky that nobody tells about. Quil would like to know, and would like it not to be Quil who finds out. Go up in her balloon, and win. Then, please, come back.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_wrong_knot.d: One knot in Navigator Tor's memory-string was re-tied by a stranger, steering him toward the rocks. He wants the tamperer found.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_wrong_knot.o: Yeli puts down her needle and her face goes thoughtful. "A man in a very good cloak, who said he was a ship's broker. Spoke Altmer like a Maormer, if you follow. He bought a bolt of teal and asked after Tor's cabin. Yeli thought nothing of it. She thinks something of it now."
Ask Yeli which sailor was seen in Tor's sail-locker
Someone re-tied a knot in Tor's string. You see everyone who goes into the loft. Who was there?
Follow the broker's trail to Galorne Obelisk
Take down Sethis Knot-Cutter, the Maormer agent
Tell the Dock-Master. Every cabin should be searched.
Tor nods. "Then it will be done, loudly, with a ledger. A good answer. A dull one. Tor is very fond of dull."
Leave the wrong knot. Let it lead the Maormer astray.
Tor smiles, slow and cold. "A false string for a false sailor. Tor will keep the wrong knot in the chart, and see who follows it. It will be a very interesting season."

Tor holds the string and does not speak for a long time. He runs his thumb along the wrong knot, and then, very deliberately, ties it right. "Thirty years. A Maormer in my cabin. Walker, shall Tor tell the Dock-Master, and have every cabin searched? Or keep it, and use the string to lead them somewhere the Maormer wish they had not gone?"
Return the string and tell Tor who tied it
The knot was tied by a Maormer agent who hoped to wreck your ship on the Galorne rocks. He is dead. The string is whole.
You are staring at a bit of string.
A navigator's string has one wrong knot, either put right or kept as bait. Somewhere off Galorne, a Maormer ship has begun to follow a very old, very trusted lie.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_the_wrong_knot.p: I am, walker, because it is wrong. A hundred and four knots, seventeen colours. Tor has steered by it for thirty years and never once been lost. Last week, near Galorne Obelisk, the string said port and the coast said starboard. One knot in the middle. Wrong. Not slipped. Re-tied, by a hand that knew the pattern. Somebody has been in his cabin. Somebody wants him on the rocks.
story.skycraft.q.mq_sum_what_orla_sells_: Every crew that bought a candle from the Pale Merchant Orla has vanished at sea. Wenlin cannot find a single complaint against her, which worries him more.
Visit Orla's stall after dusk and watch her sell
Buy a candle and light it at the quay at midnight.
Orla's eyes glint, once. "Brave. Take it. Light it where the water is deepest, and say a name. We shall see which of us was right."
Break the stall and burn the candles.
Orla does not move. "A pity. But a very natural reaction. The candles will burn, of course. They always do. And what they light, I cannot say. Go carefully, walker."

Orla smiles, pale and lovely and entirely without warmth. "The colour of the hour, dear. The light before the dark. A fisherman who burns one will find his way home, though he may not like where he finds it. I do not sell death. I sell a light that guides the lost. If they do not return, it is the sea that does not release them."
Ask Orla what is in the candles
Your candles are very fine. What gives them their colour?
Face Orla's true shape at the quay at midnight
Your quill is hovering rather than writing.
The Pale Merchant's stall stood empty from that night, and the book of ships has a single clean page at the back, in lilac ink, in Wenlin's hand: 'The sea is not hungry tonight.'

There is a new page, walker, and Wenlin does not like it. For three weeks, the same name has appeared in the book of ships that did not return: a Pale Merchant's. Every one of them bought a candle from Orla's stall on the night before they sailed. Every one of them was never seen again. Orla is a pleasant person. Everyone says so. Wenlin has not been able to find a single complaint. That, to him, is the most alarming thing about her.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_debt_of_firefl: Pip's tavern fireflies are sulking because someone has jarred the wild swarm near the audience hall. He wants the swarm released.
Search the grounds of the audience hall for the jarred swarm
Stop the collector who jarred the swarm

Pip claps his paws to his chest in relief. "Free! Oh, the poor things. And Pip, who thought he was the villain! I have been releasing them on the stroke of midnight and they hate it, and I have never asked. Walker, from tonight, they will go out whenever they like. The Firefly Lantern will be as dark as it pleases."
Tell Pip the swarm is free
The swarm is free. The collector was a lantern-seller who did not care for the midnight ceremony.
The jars have gone dim, Pip.
The fireflies of Silvenar were freed by a stranger and a very contrite tavern-keeper. The midnight ceremony has been quietly retired.

They have, walker, and it is not the glass. The fireflies are sulking, and no firefly sulks for a month unless its relatives have been shut away. Someone has jarred the wild swarm that lives by the audience hall, and the tavern's own flies are sulking in sympathy. Pip has no idea who. Pip is going to be sick.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.de: The seeds of Arenthia's oldest terrace were stolen and carried east across Waterdancer Falls. Gardener Eld wants them replanted at dawn.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.o0: Cross Waterdancer Falls by the old stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.o1: Stop the seed-thief and the Fall-Stalker that guards the stair
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.o3: Plant them on the old terrace, as the grandmother did.
Eld bows and digs. "The same hole. The same depth. It will be a wonder."
Plant half on the old terrace, and half on the poor-quarter's bare wall.
Eld looks at you, startled, then grins. "A garden for the ones who have none. Walker, the old gardeners would have hated it. Eld loves it."
Eld's hands tremble as she lifts the pouch. "The half-sun. Quick. Quick. Walker, you plant with me. The garden is half yours."
Plant the seeds on the bare terrace at dawn
The seeds, whole. Let us put them in the earth at the half-sun hour.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.of: You have the dirt of a hundred terraces under your claws.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.ou: The oldest terrace of Arenthia is green again. Within a season there will be roses where there was only wall, and the waterfall sings above them.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_garden_lost.pi: The seeds, walker. The old seeds of the Hanging Gardens, kept in a pouch by Eld's grandmother and stolen out of the temple on the last night of winter. A garden may be replanted, but not from nothing. Without the seeds, the oldest terrace stays bare. They went east, over the falls, with a thief who knew a path that Eld has never walked. Waterdancer Falls, the old stairs. Bring the pouch back before dawn, and Eld will tell you where the garden grows best.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_staff_from_a_l: An old, lame pilgrim cut a living ash for a walking staff, breaking the Green Pact. Root-Tender Maelin wants a stranger to find him and decide what is to be done.
Climb to the Winter site and find the lame pilgrim
Take the cut staff from the pilgrim
A year of tending the grove where the ash grew.
Maelin nods, and his shoulders ease. "A year of tending. The ash will heal. The pilgrim will heal. And the city will not lose a man to a law that did not wish to be cruel."
Report him to the Wardens. The Pact is the Pact.
Maelin lowers the staff very slowly. "The Pact is the Pact. Yes. It is also the only law that has never failed us. It is a hard answer, walker, and an honest one. The Wardens will come."

Maelin sets the staff upright against his shoulder. The sap runs slowly down it. "A young ash. Bleeding. A very old man. Walker, the Pact does not say how. It says only: do not cut. And a tree is a person, to us. A very quiet one. What shall be the penance? A year of tending? Or the Wardens, and his hands?"
Bring the staff to Maelin and speak for the pilgrim
The pilgrim is very old and very sorry. He cut one young ash to be able to reach the city. The tree is bleeding. What will you ask of him?
A walking staff of green ash stands in the Root-Tender's hall, either as a reminder or a warning. The tree it came from has stopped bleeding.

They are, walker. A pilgrim cut a young ash on the climb to the Winter site, to make a walking staff. A living tree. In sight of the city. The Pact is not a suggestion. He is old, and lame, and he did it so that he could walk the last mile to see the city before he dies. The Wardens will want his hands. Maelin wants to know what justice looks like, and cannot see it from here.
A Staff from a Living Tree
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_a_wagon_through_: Trader Sha'ka needs her wagon of silk and sugar escorted through Green Pact country to Marbruk without breaking a single root.

Sha'ka's ears twitch. "Silk. Sugar. Eleven rolls of Pact-green cloth the Wardens do not know I own. Walker, take the waiver, and if a patrol asks to look, show them the silk, and talk about the weather."
Take the Waiver of the Green Pact from Sha'ka
I will see the wagon through. What is in it, truly, besides silk and sugar?
Cross the Pact's tithe-walk at Reaper's Henge
Drive off the Hagraven that haunts the cairn road
Bring the wagon into Marbruk without breaking a root
Tell the Pact's Wardens about the eleven rolls of green cloth.
Mohr nods grimly. "It is the Pact's cloth by right. A Warden will visit Sha'ka. She will be furious, and she will, I think, forgive you."
Keep the secret. Sha'ka's cloth is her own.
Mohr almost smiles. "Good. A secret is a better cargo than silk. She will remember it."

Mohr stretches, which takes a surprisingly long time. "Through the Pact and out the other side. Sha'ka owes you a bolt of silk and she will not say it. Mohr says it for her. Take this. It is an honest shield, borrowed, and it has never been struck."
Return to Mohr at the Caravan Gate and report the wagon safe
The wagon went through. Nobody was stopped. The Pact was not offended, as far as I know.
A wagon full of canvas and a face full of worry.
A wagon passed through Green Pact country without bruising a root, and a cloth merchant of Rawlkha now owes a stranger more than she is willing to say aloud.

Wagon, walker. Silk and sugar for Marbruk, three days away, through Pact country. A wagon is made of wood. The Pact forbids a felled tree or a cart wheel that bruises a root. The Pact has patrols. Sha'ka has a waiver, signed by someone who may or may not exist. If the wagon is stopped, say you are with me. If it is not, say nothing, and stay off the rootways.
A Wagon Through the Green Pact
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_chasing_the_walk: Pilgrim Hael has chased Falinesti for eleven years. He wants to ride the city across a river crossing, and needs a companion for the water.
Reach the Spring site before the city leaves it
Travel to the Summer site with the walking city
Wait until night, when the roots move
Defend the crossing from the Drowned Ford-Warden
Settle. Let the city carry you now.
Hael closes his eyes. "Then a door. A small one, on the second branch. Hael will plant a tomato and tell it all about the road. Thank you for the crossing."
Keep walking. The city is not the whole forest.

Hael laughs with sudden joy. "Not the whole forest! Of course. There is Reaper's March, and the coast, and the Orcs of Drabul, who owe Hael a song. Walker, Hael will walk to the end of the world in your honour."

Hael sits down on the bank like a man who has put down a very heavy parcel. "Eleven years. Hael has been so busy following that he never thought what he would do on arrival. A house? A garden? He has never owned a door. What would you do, walker?"
Find Hael on the far bank
We crossed. The city is on the other side of the river now. Hael, the road ends here. Will you settle, or keep walking?
You look like someone who has been walking behind something.
A pilgrim of eleven years finally arrived. What he did next was his to choose, and the walking city, patient as ever, moved on.

Eleven years, walker. Hael has followed Falinesti from spring to summer to autumn to winter and back, and has never once been at the gate when it opened. Always a day late, always a day early. He has made a bet with himself. Today he will stand where the city will be, not where it is. He needs someone to take the crossing with him. He does not like water.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_fortunes_in_a_br: Pura's loom has produced the same fortune for three different customers. Someone is tampering with it, and she wants the tamperer found.
Hide among the silk bolts at Pura's loom and wait for the tamperer
Catch the tamperer at the loom

Pura laughs behind her paw until she has to wipe her eyes. "A commercial fortune! Three customers sent to Arenthia for the same pretty garden. Walker, that is the first honest fortune Pura's loom has ever told. She will weave it herself next time, and charge a commission."
Tell Pura what the tamperer was weaving
A rival weaver from Arenthia wanted the same fortune woven for three customers, to make them all travel to the Hanging Gardens. A commercial fortune.
Your bracelet is pulling at its thread.
The Hanging Gardens had a very busy summer, and Pura's loom, for once, was satisfied.

It is, walker, and it should not. Pura weaves the fortunes. Pura does not choose them. But three customers have returned with the same fortune, in different threads, the same shape, the same knot at the end. Someone has been tampering with her loom. A fortune is not a thing a tailor should be tampering with.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_moon_sugar_in_th: Guard Mohr found a hoard of moon-sugar hidden in a wagon-wheel hub. The owner, a stall-keeper, is nearby. He asks a stranger to decide what to do with it.
Take the hub to the Caravan Gate and confront the wheel-wright
Face Zar'ha the Wheel-Wright, who will not surrender his hoard quietly
Pour it into the river. Let the sugar be forgotten.
Mohr nods, and carries the hub to the bridge. The crystals dissolve in a long grey cloud that tastes, faintly, of honey. "Gone. A pity. But a clean one. Thank you."
Sell it quietly and give the coin to the Caravan Gate's widows.
Mohr hesitates, then, very slowly, smiles. "Widows. Yes. A fair use for a foul thing. Mohr will see it done."
Report it to the Wardens. The Pact is the Pact.
Mohr straightens. "Reported, then. It is correct. And it will be burned. Mohr will not enjoy it. Thank you for being brave enough to say it."

Mohr turns the hub over, slowly, and the grey crystals glint. "A fortune, walker. A fortune that would buy Mohr a year of sleep. It would also bring the Wardens down on a hundred Khajiit honest traders who did nothing. What do you say?"
Decide the fate of the moon-sugar with Mohr
Zar'ha is dealt with. The sugar is here. Report it, pour it out, or sell it?
You have the look of a guard who has found something.
A hub of moon-sugar was found in a wagon-wheel at Rawlkha, and was poured, spent or burned, depending on the voice that spoke last.

I have, walker, and I wish I had not. A wagon-wheel at the Caravan Gate was too heavy for its size. Mohr rolled it into the guardhouse and cracked the hub. Moon-sugar. A fortune of it. The wagon's owner is a Wheel-Wright called Zar'ha who runs a very honest stall by day. Mohr could report him. The Pact's Wardens would burn the lot and break his hands. Mohr could pour it in the river. Or sell it. He has thought about all three.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_sound_in_the_mid: Seven Root Gate lamps were stolen without damage to the wood and are being sold cheaply in the Middens. Wardress Lirael wants the clever thief.
Search the Middens for the stolen Root Gate lamps
Corner the fence, Peddler Sorwe Rat-Tail
Apprentice him to the Gate. He has the hand for it.
Lirael nods slowly. "A thief at the gate is a lock that knows the key. Very well. He will sweep the stair for a year, and then perhaps trim lamps for a decade."
Fine him and let his master pay. The master is the real thief.
Lirael's ears flick. "Then the master will pay. In coin, in lamps and in the opinion of the Gate. A good answer. A harder one."

Lirael sets her jaw. "A boy. A very good hand. Hm. The Pact says no harm to the living wood, and he never harmed it. He is a better thief than the Gate is a guard. Do you want him punished, or apprenticed?"
Tell Lirael who was cutting her lamps free
The fence was Sorwe Rat-Tail. The cutter is a boy, a gate-lantern apprentice, who has a very good hand and a very bad master.
Your gate has a bruise under its paint.
The seven lamps hang in their brackets again, and a boy with a very good hand has been told that it is a gift, not a licence.

It has, walker. Seven lamps have gone missing from the Gate in a month. Not the oil. The lamps. Cut right out of their brackets, no damage to the wood. A Bosmer may not damage the wood, so whoever did it was a Bosmer, and a good one. And every lamp that vanishes turns up for sale in the Middens, for a quarter its price. Find the buyer. Find the seller. Find whoever is clever enough to cut without cutting.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_tevas_tasting_me: Cook Teva must serve a fussy Pact-Warden three properly-named beasts. She needs a boar, a stag and a hare from the wilds near Marbruk.
Hunt a boar in the Shrouded Vale
Bring back three portions of game

Teva looks them over and tastes, very carefully, a single crumb. "Named. Properly. You have done this before. Walker, you will eat first tonight, and no one at the Warden's table shall be told. It is the best feast Marbruk has had in a decade, and you are not in the book."
Three portions. A boar, a stag, a hare. Named by the hunter, as the Pact demands.
You taste like someone who is very hungry.
The Warden ate in silence, then asked for the cook. Teva was never seen to blush before or since.

Hungry is a good start, walker. Teva has been asked to cook a feast for a visiting Warden, and the Warden is a very fussy eater who will only eat meat, which is the Pact, and who will only eat meat that was properly named, which is a thing Teva has never heard of. Find the three beasts she has asked for. A boar, a stag, a hare. Properly named.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_bough_that_b: The Green Bough inn has grown a door in its new ceiling, with no stair leading up to it. Host Tamlin would like it opened by someone else.
Climb to the top floor of the Green Bough
Wait until night, when the door is said to open on its own
Take what waits behind the ceiling door

Tamlin turns the acorn in the lamp-light. "An acorn. That is the whole reason. The bough has been building a floor a year to say: plant me. Plant me nearby, so the bough can have a child to look at. Walker, Tamlin will plant it at the edge of the yard. And the inn will stop growing, I think, when the child is tall."
There was an acorn behind the door. It twitched. The bough wants it planted.
Your inn seems to be growing without a builder.
An acorn was planted by the yard-gate at the Green Bough, and the inn has not grown a floor since. The bough, they say, hums in the evenings.

Every year, walker. A new floor. No hands. No axes. The bough simply puts out another storey, always on the first night of Rain's Hand. Tamlin has stopped counting rooms. Last night, for the first time, the new floor grew a door facing the sky. A door in the ceiling, with no stair. Tamlin does not wish to open it. He would like you to.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_child_on_the: A cub from the Woodhearth ground-camp is stuck on a high node of the Weave. Elder Hush asks a stranger to bring her down.
Climb the Great Weave to the high node
Drive off the nesting hawks that guard the high node
Escort the cub, and Hush, down to the ground-camp
Your camp is quieter than usual, Elder.
The cub came down the Weave on a stranger's back, and said only that the bridge-people were not nearly as tall as they let on.

Because the youngest cub of the camp has not come down, walker. Twelve stories up the Weave, on a node, since last night. She went up to see whether the bridge-people were really as tall as everyone says. She is stuck. The Warden has a rope and a dislike of heights. The camp has a ladder that is much too short. Hush does not wish to ask the Weave for help. She is asking you.
The Child on the High Node
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.desc: Bridge-Warden Tilu says three of Woodhearth's main bridge-knots have been rotted on purpose. Someone is climbing the Weave and feeding the nodes with a mushroom paste.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o0.t: Climb the Great Weave and inspect the soft node
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o1.t: Wait in the shadow of the hub until the saboteur climbs
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o2.t: Catch the saboteur on the Weave
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o3.c: Have the ground-camp rebuild the Weave. Let them earn the right to cross it.
Hush's eyes shine. "A bridge built by the hands that have been told they cannot cross. Yes. The camp will weave a rope that will outlast the Warden herself. And the Warden will have to look at us."
Pay the camp to repair the nodes, and bring Tilu in to oversee.
Hush nods. "A fair wage and a fair eye. Not quite a victory. A beginning. Thank you."
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o3.r: Hush is silent for the length of a long breath. "Because nobody listens to those who live below. Raik told the children it would make the bridges sing, and they believed him. They are cubs, walker. They have been told for years the bridges are not for them. Now someone has made the bridges ask for them."
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.o3.t: Ask Elder Hush why the ground-camp's children were seen on the Weave
The saboteur, Raik, said the camp's children have been hauling mushrooms up the Weave. Why would they do that?
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.outr: Raik Mushroom-Hand was cut down from the Weave, and the ground-camp's children, to their great astonishment, were handed ropes and told they were wanted.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_fraying.pitc: It is, walker. Three nodes on the Weave have gone soft in a month, and none of them near water, none of them near any rot. A bridge-knot rots when it is helped. Somebody has been feeding them, with a paste that smells of mushrooms, and whoever it is climbs better than any warden. Tilu would catch them herself, but she is afraid of heights. She does not tell anyone.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_hymn_that_wo: The monks of Dokrin cannot stop singing the same hymn. A harp in the monastery vault seems to be the cause.
Descend to the monastery vault where the harp plays
Drive off the shades that dance to the harp

Brother Hael tries to speak and nothing comes. He stands, mute, for a very long time. Then he bows low, and the other monks bow, and a silence falls on the monastery for the first time in three days that is not a silence of fear. It is a silence of rest.
Tell Brother Hael the harp is still
The harp is silent. I unstrung it. It will not be heard again.
The monks of Dokrin slept for a day and a night. When they woke, the first thing they sang was a different hymn: very short, and very grateful.

Three days, walker. The hymn of the third hour. It began at dawn and none of us has been able to stop. We do not know why. If one monk falls silent, the others weep. We sing in shifts and still cannot rest. We think it is the harp in the vault. It began to play on the first morning, and has not been silent since. Silence it. Please.
The Hymn That Would Not End
Hermit Orlen has a line of prophecy he does not wish to carve. He asks a stranger to see whether it has already come true.
Orlen reads it and sags with relief. "The hermit rests. Yes. After forty years. Thank you. I will go and see the sea."
Orlen stares, then laughs until he has to sit. "Just wood! Yes! Forty years I carved, and was afraid of wood. Walker, you are a very rude and very wise stranger."

Orlen's paws tremble. "'The stranger at the door will carry the burden of the last line.' Walker, you are the stranger. You are at the door. And Orlen does not know what the last line is, only that it is you who will carve it. Take the chisel. Please. Say what you will."
Read the unfinished line on the doorframe
Return to the supplication house at dawn to see what the prophecy has done
Your doorframe is a very long sentence.
A prophecy of forty years ended with a stranger at a door. Whatever the last line said, the hermit was free.

Forty years, walker. A line a year. It began as a joke, a hermit's scribble. Then the lines started coming true. A flood in the ninth year. A king's death in the twelfth. A lost brother returned in the twenty-sixth. Orlen has a line for this winter, and he does not want to carve it. He wants you to go and see if it is already true.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_mist_toll_di: A Baandari trader and a Pact-Warden quarrel over the mist-toll at Silvenar. Gate-Warden Wren wants a stranger to broker peace.

Ethelwe taps the ink-stain on her finger. "Both. The court calls it a gift in the first clause and a tax in the third. It has been this way for four hundred years. Whoever reads one clause is right. Whoever reads both is a politician. Tell them to read the whole page, and sign it together."
Ask the Silvenar's Scribe for the court's own wording of the toll
The Gate-Warden would like a clear ruling. Is the toll a gift or a tax?
Suggest the Baandari pay half in coin and half in song.
Wren snorts. "Song. For a toll. It will not work, and the Silvenar will adore it. Done."
Suggest the Warden waive the toll for traders who carry court post.
Wren nods slowly. "A trade, then. Fair. The trader gets his road. The court gets its letters. And the Warden is spared the quarrel."

Wren watches the two of them read, grumble and, at last, tie the ribbon between them with a grim kind of courtesy. "Together. Huh. Well. Walker, that is the first thing anyone has done at that stair in a year that did not end in blows. Take a seat at the Firefly Lantern. Pip owes me a favour, and I have decided to spend it on you."
Bring the ribbon to the quarrelling pair at the south stair
Here is the court's wording, both clauses. The toll is a gift and a tax. Sign the ribbon together.
You are the first person I have not turned back today.
The mist-toll of Silvenar is both a gift and a tax, and a silver ribbon with one wrong knot hangs at the south stair for everyone to see.

Because you did not argue, walker. A Baandari trader is arguing with the Pact's Warden at the south stair about the toll. The Baandari says the toll is a gift. The Warden says it is a tax. Wren does not care which. She wants them to stop. If you can carry an offer from one to the other, and persuade them both, she will pretend that she did not hear a word of it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_net_that_cau: Net-Trader Orwen received an unmarked net that catches nothing. The stone it came wrapped around may tell what it was meant to catch.
Cast the net into Echo Pond and see what it does
Wait at the pond until the net stirs
Kill what the net has caught in the still water

Orwen pulls at his ear. "Lights. Of course. A net for lights does not catch fish. It catches, hm, a different kind of prey. The weaver would be a Wispmother's apprentice, or a bored witch. Orwen will weave a second net, the same, and send it on, for the sender's sake. They will need two."
Tell Orwen what the net was meant to catch
It was made to catch lights. A will-o-wisp, a marsh-light. Someone wanted one alive, and sent the net to the best net-trader in Greenshade.
A net-trader who looks bothered is a rare thing.
A net that catches nothing has caught something after all, and Orwen has begun to wonder who is knitting at the other end of the string.

Orwen has woven nets for forty years, walker. This one he did not weave. It arrived in a crate with no sender, wound around a single stone. It catches nothing. Fish, birds, flies, nothing. A net that catches nothing is not a net. Orwen would like to know what it is a net for.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_plank_of_sre: Two neighbours of Sren Ja have each swept the same bridge-plank for six years. A deed with a smudged stamp might settle it, if someone neutral reads it.
Find the old deed in the flooded record-house at Old Sren Ja Docks
Recover the Deed to the Disputed Plank

Maral stares at the deed. Across the bridge, her neighbour stares back. A very long silence follows. Then, haltingly, he lifts his broom. She lifts hers. They sweep the plank from opposite ends, and when they meet in the middle, they stop, and look at each other, and neither says a word. But both of them are smiling.
Read the deed aloud to both neighbours
The deed says the plank belongs to whoever sweeps first. The smudge, held to the light, is the stamp of a former reeve: it says: both. At the same time. Together.
You look very tired of sweeping.
The plank of Sren Ja has been swept by two brooms at once for a month, and it has never been cleaner. They do not speak. They do not need to.

Six years, walker. Six years. He sweeps from the east, she from the west, and every dawn they meet in the middle and say nothing, and sweep the dust back where it came from. Each of them knows the other is wrong. The deed says whoever sweeps first. The deed is not clear who that is. A third party might read the smudge at the bottom, and see what is really written there.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_prayer_behin: Priestess Sel hears her prayers answered in someone else's voice from behind the waterfall. She wants a witness.
Stand behind the falls at Lorion Falls and listen
Wait until night for the voice to answer

Sel is still. Then, very quietly: "My own voice. A year older. Walker, it is not Y'ffre. It is Sel, the next year's Sel, calling back. She says do not stop. Then Sel will not. Thank you. You have given me a very great gift: a reason to continue."
It answered. In your own voice, Sel, but a year older. It said: do not stop.
You pray from behind a curtain of water.
Sel prays every morning behind the falls, and every morning the water answers in a voice a year older, with something very like a smile.

It is easier, walker. Sel has prayed behind the falls for eleven years. Last month, the water changed. It carries an echo now. Sel says a prayer and hears it answered, not in her voice. She does not know if it is Y'ffre or something older. She would like someone to stand where she stands and listen.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_root_festiva: Fenwe wants someone to enter the archery contest of the Root Festival and take the Arrow, if only to quiet the muttering about her champion cousin.
Enter the archery contest at Elden Hollow
Defeat the nine-time champion, Archer Lewen Nine-Arrows

Fenwe's ears go flat, then up. "She did not cheat! Ha! Then the muttering will go on, but about you, which is entirely fair. Walker, drink first tonight. The Hollow Acorn bows to the Arrow, whoever holds it."
Bring the Arrow back to Fenwe
I won the Arrow of the Root Festival. Your cousin shot cleanly; she did not cheat. I was simply better, once.
The Hollow Acorn is awfully full for a weekday.
The Arrow of the Root Festival was won by a stranger, and Lewen Nine-Arrows took the defeat with a very straight back and a very fast second round.

It is the Root Festival, walker! Three days of archery and three nights of arguments about archery. The prize is the Arrow, a gold-tipped heirloom, and the cup is all to the Hollow Acorn, where the winner drinks first. Fenwe has a cousin who has won it nine times and the other tables are muttering that she cheats. Fenwe is certain she does not. But she would be very glad to see someone else take the prize, just once, so the muttering stops.
The Arrow of the Root Festival
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_season_the_c: Lorekeeper Eri has found evidence of a fifth season, deliberately cut from the chronicles of the walking city. The autumn site may remember it.
Visit the Autumn site and search for what the chronicles cut
Find the buried Acorn of the Autumn Site
Write it into the chronicles. Let the grove be found.
Eri inks the margin with a steady hand. "Then it is written, for the first time. Some will go looking. Some should. The city will not mind."
Keep the secret. The city planted it for itself.
Eri closes her notebook gently. "Then it stays between you, the acorn and me. A walking city is entitled to one thing it has not told. Thank you for the hard choice."

Eri turns the acorn over twice, and her breath catches. "A planting. The city dropped it deliberately. In the fifth season, it did not walk. It stopped, and grew a thing, and that thing was a grove. Walker, there is a grove somewhere that the city planted for itself. And the Tenders cut the season from the record to stop anyone from finding it."
This acorn grew from a seed the city dropped on a season it did not record. It is a fifth planting.
Your memory looks heavier than your satchel.
A fifth season of Falinesti is known to two people, or to everyone, depending on whom you ask.

It is, walker. Falinesti has stood on four sites, in four seasons, for a thousand years. But Eri has a fifth in her notes. A season the city stood somewhere none of the sites are, and no chronicle records. A season that was cut out of the record, by someone with a knife and a very good reason. Eri wants to know what the city did during it. Whatever it was, the roots remember.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_silent_court: The Silvenar has been silent for nine days. Ethelwe suspects the cause is a scroll he borrowed from the Root Archive, which she wants retrieved.
Find the east path to the Firefly Gate

Wren looks at you for a very long, flat moment. "The Scribe's word is the Scribe's. Mine is mine. You will walk the south stair and not the north. You will not touch the fireflies, and you will not, under any circumstances, speak to the root-wrapped thing in the bottom archive."
Win an audience at the Firefly Gate
I carry word from the Silvenar's Scribe. I would like to enter, quietly, and speak with the Archivist.
Descend the south stair to the Root Archive
Defeat the Root-Wrapped Archivist that guards the lowest stacks
Burn it. A king should not be told what he will say.
Ethelwe lays the scroll on a lamp and watches it curl. "The page was blank, and now it is ash, and the Silvenar will speak tomorrow, and not know what. It is a mercy. Perhaps."
Put it back. Let him read it when he is ready.
Ethelwe ties the ribbon again with reverent care. "A kinder cruelty. Perhaps he will read it. Perhaps he will not. It will wait. Thank you."

Ethelwe takes the scroll with unsteady fingers and does not unroll it. "Blank. Then it is the Silent Scroll, the one that records what the Silvenar will say, not what he has. He asked for it so he would know. I think he has known, and it frightened him. Will you have me burn it, or put it back?"
I have your scroll. The page is blank. Whoever wrote it did so for a reader who has not yet been born.
You write as if in a hurry.
The Silvenar spoke the next morning, brief and clear, as if a weight had left his shoulders. Whether the scroll was ash or shelf-bound, Silvenar had decided to be unafraid.

The Silvenar has not spoken in public for nine days, walker. Ethelwe writes down everything he says, and for nine days the page has been blank. The Court says he is meditating. Ethelwe thinks he is afraid. There is a scroll in the Root Archive that he asked for on the tenth night, and has not returned. If you can enter the Court and reach the Archive, bring it to me. Before anyone else reads what is on it.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_thorn_wall.d: The Thorn Wall of Marbruk has been bent in three places by someone who respects the Pact's laws and robs the town regardless. Ranger Cael wants the gap closed and the intruder caught.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_thorn_wall.o: Inspect the bent places in the Thorn Wall
Hold the gap at night until the intruder returns
Stop Gurzun Wall-Breaker at the gap
Seal it with new thorn, as the Pact asks.
Huln nods once. The thorn will take a season to grow, but it will be the wall's own, and no one will ever bend it.
Weave an iron cage over it. The Pact can forgive iron in a crisis.
Huln looks pained. He weaves the cage anyway, and the thorn will grow around it. A compromise, and an ugly one, but strong.

Huln looks at the stone for a long while. Then, with the visible effort of a man who spends words like coins: "No iron. Thorn. Plant a thorn. Let it grow. Let the Pact do the work." He nods. That is all seven words. He folds his arms and says nothing more.
Take the gap-stone to Huln and ask what can seal it
The wall has been bent in three places and the thief is dead. Can you seal them?
Your wall looks sound. Your shoulders do not.
The Thorn Wall stands whole. A season from now the new thorn will have grown over the gap, and no one will remember where it was bent.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_thorn_wall.p: The wall is bent, walker. Three places this month. Not cut. Never cut. The Pact forbids it, and the wall would grow back in a week anyway. Someone bends it, and goes through, and goes out again, and takes something each time. A sheep. A sack of salt. Last week, a child's shoes. Cael does not know what they are practising for. He is afraid it is the real thing.
Sap-Tapper Beron says the Elden Tree is feverish. The sap darkens at each tier, and whatever began in the Crown is spreading down the trunk.
Test the sap at the root tier, in Elden Hollow
Climb to the second tier, where the Orrery hangs in the boughs, and test the sap again
Climb to the Crown of the Elden Tree
Cut the Blight-Heart from the Crown bough
I did it to save the tree. The Pact was written for a healthy forest.
Aeth lets out a breath. "A fair answer. Not the one the Court wants. But the one Aeth would have given. The Silvenar will hear it as you said it. He may even agree."
I did it because the tree was dying, and nobody else would.
Aeth's shoulders ease a hair. "Then you have done what the Pact's wardens could not. They will not forgive you for it. The tree might."

Aeth is quiet for the length of a long breath. "The Pact forbids us to harm the living wood. You have cut a living bough, in the Silvenar's own city. By the letter, you have broken the oldest of our laws. By the spirit..." He stops. "The Court asks what you did it for. Say it plainly, and the Court will decide whether to thank you or to judge you."
Tell the Silvenar's Voice what you found in the Crown
A blight was eating the Crown from within. Black sap, and a heart that was not the tree's own. It is cut out, and the bough is dying.
You sound as if you are listening to something.
The Crown bough was cut, and the sap runs amber again from root to leaf. A law was bent, for the sake of a tree, and Elden Root has not yet decided whether to be grateful.

The roots, walker. Listen. The lanterns pulse with the tree's own heart, and for a month now the beat has been wrong. Beron has tapped the first tier, the second tier, and the third. At each tier the sap runs a shade darker. Whatever is wrong began at the Crown and is running down. Climb with Beron's sap-gauge, tier by tier. Find the sick place. And then decide what is to be done with it, because Beron cannot.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_truce_of_dra: A Bosmer hunting-party has vanished between Drabul and a nearby village, and each side blames the other. Chieftain Borgakh wants the truth found before blood is spilled.
Search the Arorin Ruins where the hunters were last seen
Drive off the wolves that have scattered the hunters
Walk Borgakh to the village to meet the hunters and settle the matter
Your hall is quiet for an Orc outpost.
The hunting-party was found alive and half-eaten by embarrassment. Orc and Bosmer shared one very awkward feast, and the truce of Drabul has never been stronger.

It is, walker, because Borgakh has told his warriors not to touch a thing for three days. A Bosmer hunting-party has gone missing between Drabul and the village across the stream, and both sides think the other has taken them. Borgakh has the truce to think of, and no wish to start a war over a lost sheep-boy. Find the party. Quickly. Quietly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_wardens_miss: The Warden's hound was lost in the Shrouded Vale three days ago. Smith Huln, who rarely speaks, asks a stranger to find her.
Search the Shrouded Vale for the Warden's hound
Stop Gorrun Hound-Taker, who has her in a snare

Huln looks at the hound. The hound looks at Huln. He kneels, and something very large moves in his throat. "Thank you." That is two words, and he looks as though they have cost him a week of coin. Then he takes your hand, and does not say anything at all, for a long and perfectly fluent time.
The hound is safe. She was snared by a poacher. She wishes to be fed.
You are Huln, and you are not speaking.
The Warden's hound is home, and Smith Huln has a rare and treasured habit of nodding to a stranger in the street.

Seven words. Spent. The Warden's hound. Gone. Vale. Three days. Please. Find. That is eight words, and Huln is very sorry. He has the look of a man who has run out of gold and is now spending silver. Take the hound's collar from the hook. The vale is the Shrouded Vale, east of the wall. Bring her home.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_the_weavers_thre: Weaver Wynn needs three dyes gathered where water meets light, each of which turns if collected in anger.
Gather falls-silver from the mist at Waterdancer Falls
Gather dawn-pink at the pool of Lorion Falls

Wynn uncorks the silver and watches it settle. Then, slowly, she begins to laugh. "They hold! Gladly gathered, and they hold. Walker, you have a gift. Few can gather gladly, in a forest that taxes a smile. Wynn will weave your name into the border, in a thread that only shows at dawn."
Bring the three dyes to Wynn
Three dyes: moss, silver, dawn. Gathered gladly. Will they hold?
You have the green of a good weaver on your sleeve.
A banner of three colours hangs in the Silvenar's hall, with a border thread that shows only at dawn. It is said to spell a stranger's name.

It is a bad weaver's green, walker, and I am ashamed of it. Wynn has an order from the Silvenar himself, for a banner of three colours: moss-green, falls-silver and dawn-pink. She has only ever managed one. The other two come only where water meets light, and there is a place for each: the falls' mist, the dawn pool and the gardens' lowest terrace. The twist is: if you take them in anger, they run. They must be gathered gladly.
story.skycraft.q.mq_val_trial_by_a_stran: Champion Mauhulakh wants a stranger to witness a duel between his two sons and judge whether it was fought fairly.
Wait for dawn at the Jathsogur dueling-ground
Stop the duel when the younger son breaks the rules
Name the elder the rightful heir.
Mauhulakh bows his head. "It is as I hoped, and I am sorry for the younger. He will have the forge, and a lesson."
Name neither. Let the clan decide in a month.
Mauhulakh grunts, then slowly smiles. "A month. A cooler head. You are wiser than a hundred witnesses."

Mauhulakh listens without moving. "Struck from behind. A thing a son of mine should not do. And the elder gave a chance. That is all a father needs to hear. Walker, the clan owes you nothing, and has never been so grateful."
The younger son struck from behind. The elder gave him a chance to yield. I stopped it before blood.
You wish a witness, not a challenger.
The stronghold of Jathsogur has a new heir, or a new month. The stranger who witnessed it was thanked with a full cup and an empty promise.

A witness. You owe the clan nothing, and so you may see it without a bias. Jathsogur has two sons who each claim the right to lead after Mauhulakh. They will duel at dawn. The loser lives, the winner leads. Mauhulakh has agreed to abide by the stranger's word on whether the duel was fair. He will not say which son he hopes will win. He will say only that he hopes it is fair.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.de: Eno Hlaalu has deciphered the Brotherhood letter. Their cell hides in an abandoned Velothi tomb west of Vivec. He has signed a writ for every one of them.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o0: An abandoned tomb west of Vivec. Here is the writ. It names the whole cell, and it is the first of its kind in a hundred years. Go.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o2: Execute the writ on the Brotherhood assassins
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o3: I left the Grandmaster's writ on the altar of their tomb. When the Brotherhood comes looking, they will know it was lawful, and who signed it.
Kill the cell's leader, the Speaker Darvame Hleran
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.o4: Then stand there and hear me.
The writ is served. The cell is gone.
story.skycraft.q.mt_grandmasters_writ.ou: I served the Grandmaster's writ on the Dark Brotherhood's cell in Vvardenfell. Eno Hlaalu named me an Exalted Master of the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.desc: Ethasi Rilvayn of the Morag Tong hall in Balmora will accept me if I learn the code and execute a sanctioned writ against Ovys Hlerano, an extortionist.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o0.r: Listen closely. I will not say it twice.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o0.t: Hear the code of the Morag Tong
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o1.j: I left the writ folded on Hlerano's chest, as the code requires. The farmers he burned out will know who answered them, and that it was lawful.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o1.t: Execute the writ on Ovys Hlerano
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o2.r: And you left the writ. Good. You are an Associate of the Morag Tong. Mephala watches us all. Try to make her proud.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.o2.t: The writ is served. Hlerano is dead.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.offe: I want to join the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.outr: I executed a sanctioned writ against Ovys Hlerano and joined the Morag Tong.
story.skycraft.q.mt_sanctioned_writ.pitc: Then you will learn the code, and then you will carry a writ. Ovys Hlerano, an extortionist who burned a family's farm when they refused to pay him, has been sentenced. He drinks at a shack on the road south of town. Leave this writ on his body.
story.skycraft.q.mt_threads_of_the_websp: Mephala, the Webspinner, blessed the Morag Tong with sacred threads. Three have been lost: one at her shrine, one in the ruin of Yansirramus, and one in the hands of a renegade in Vivec. Eno Hlaalu wants them home.
Travel to the shrine of Mephala
Kill the spiders nesting in the shrine
Take the thread from the shrine
Travel to the ruin of Yansirramus
Banish the daedra guarding the ruin
Find the renegade Ralvas Indrano in Vivec and take back his thread
Return the first thread to Eno Hlaalu
Indrano's thread. He won't need it now.
I returned the three Threads of the Webspinner to Eno Hlaalu. Mephala herself has bid the Tong cut the Dark Brotherhood out of Morrowind.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.d: Ethasi Rilvayn gave me a writ for Captain Seleth Mavus, a smuggler running skooma and slaves through the docks of Ebonheart.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.o: Fight through Mavus's crew on the docks
When Mavus fell, the hold was opened. The captives inside walked out into the sun and did not look back.
Execute the writ on Captain Seleth Mavus
The writ said nothing about the cargo. The code says nothing against kindness, either. Well done.
Mavus is dead, and his cargo set free.
Do you have another writ for me?
I served the writ on Captain Seleth Mavus at Ebonheart, and his captives walked free.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_captain_mavus.p: Captain Seleth Mavus runs skooma through Ebonheart on a hull full of slaves. The Council sealed the writ yesterday. His crew will fight; the writ names only him, but the code permits you to defend yourself.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.des: A writ has been sealed against Ser Varo Andalas, a Vivec noble who poisoned his cousin and bought the magistrates' silence.
Andalas offered me his cousin's inheritance to walk away. I left the writ on his desk instead, beside the bribes he had been counting.
Execute the writ on Ser Varo Andalas
Of course he did, and of course you didn't. That is the whole difference between us and the hired knives. Grandmaster Hlaalu has heard your name.
Andalas offered me gold to leave. I didn't take it.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.out: I served the writ on Ser Varo Andalas in Vivec and refused his bribe.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_ser_andalas.pit: A delicate one. Ser Varo Andalas, a minor noble of Vivec, poisoned his own cousin for an inheritance and bribed the magistrates to look away. His cousin's widow came to us. The Council agreed. He keeps guards, and he keeps them close.
story.skycraft.q.mt_writ_the_infiltrator: Grandmaster Eno Hlaalu has issued a writ against Fevila Sarano, a Dark Brotherhood assassin hiding in Balmora who murdered members of the Morag Tong.
The quiet one who never takes coin from anyone? Odd for a clerk. She keeps a room above the old warehouse on the east bank.
Ask Nevos the factor about the clerk Fevila Sarano
There's a clerk named Fevila Sarano. Where can I find her?
Execute the writ on Fevila Sarano
A Brotherhood cipher. I can read it, given time. Meanwhile, there is a matter of faith to attend to. Mephala's threads have gone astray, and we will need her favour for what comes next.
Bring the coded letter to Eno Hlaalu
Sarano is dead. She carried this.
I executed the Dark Brotherhood infiltrator Fevila Sarano in Balmora. Her coded letter will lead us to the Brotherhood's cell in Vvardenfell.

Two of our members have been murdered in their beds, without writs. That is not our way, and it is not the way of anyone in Morrowind. The Dark Brotherhood has come to Vvardenfell. One of them hides in Balmora as a moneylender's clerk, Fevila Sarano. Here is the writ.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.desc: Chief Burguk gro-Dushnikh of Dushnikh Yal will consider me as Blood-Kin if I kill the giant that has been killing the stronghold's herds.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o0.journa: The giant had a goat under each arm when I found it, and it did not want to give either of them back.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o0.text: Kill the giant raiding Dushnikh Yal's herds
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o1.text: Take a knucklebone from the giant
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.reply: A good bone, from a big one. It will make a fine charm against sickness for the little ones. Go and tell Burguk the wise-woman is satisfied. He will pretend that does not matter to him.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.text: Bring the knucklebone to Murbul the wise-woman
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o2.topic: Chief Burguk said you'd want this.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o3.reply: Then you have fed the stronghold instead of eating from it. That is the beginning of being Orc. You are Blood-Kin to Dushnikh Yal. Eat with us tonight, and do not complain about the food.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.o3.topic: The giant is dead, and Murbul has her bone.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.offer: I want to earn a place among the Orcs.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.outro: I killed the giant that preyed on Dushnikh Yal's herds. Chief Burguk named me Blood-Kin of the stronghold, and so of the Orcs.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.pitch: Then earn it. A giant has come down out of the hills and is stamping my goats flat for sport. Kill it, and bring Murbul something of it for her charms. Then we will talk about places.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_kin.title: Blood-Kin
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.desc: The ancestral axe of Dushnikh Yal has been stolen, and Chief Burguk blames Chief Larak of Mor Khazgur. He wants the axe back, or blood-price paid.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o0.repl: The axe of my line. Twelve chiefs carried it. Larak of Mor Khazgur has wanted it since we were boys. Go to his stronghold and tell him to give it back or pay the blood-price. I would go myself, but then there would be a war, and Murbul says we cannot afford one this winter.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o2.repl: Burguk would blame me for the snow. Forsworn raided us both the same week. They took my brother's shield and three of my hunters. The raiders came out of Bruca's Leap Redoubt. Go there if you want Burguk's axe. Bring back my brother's shield and I will call it even.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o2.topi: Burguk says you took his axe.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o3.text: Clear the Forsworn out of Bruca's Leap Redoubt
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o4.jour: The Briarheart had hung the Orc trophies from the roof of the redoubt: a shield, a helm, and an old iron axe notched along the haft.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o4.text: Kill the Briarheart who led the raids
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o5.text: Take back the axe of Dushnikh Yal
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.repl: Hm. So Larak is not a thief. Only ugly. What would you have me do now, Blood-Kin? You have earned an opinion.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.text: Return the axe to Chief Burguk
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o6.topi: Your axe. The Forsworn took it, not Larak. They hit Mor Khazgur too.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c0.l: Send Larak the shield I took back, and a gift of your own. End the feud.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c0.r: A gift. To Larak. Murbul will laugh at me for a month. ...Fine. Peace is cheaper than war, and the Forsworn are the real enemy.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c1.l: You accused him in front of your clan. Pay him the blood-price for the insult.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.o7.c1.r: Blood-price, from me, to him. That is the Code, and you are right. I will pay. It will hurt more than any axe.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.outro: The Forsworn, not Mor Khazgur, stole the axe of Dushnikh Yal. I took it back from Bruca's Leap Redoubt, and on my advice Chief Burguk settled things with Chief Larak instead of starting a war.
story.skycraft.q.orc_blood_price.title: The Blood-Price
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.de: Murbul, wise-woman of Dushnikh Yal, sent me to the shrine of Malacath in Wrothgar to learn the meaning of the god's Code.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o0: Travel to the shrine of Malacath in Wrothgar
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o1: Two ogres were using the shrine's offering bowl as a cooking pot. Malacath, I suspect, found that funnier than I did.
Drive the ogres away from the shrine
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o2: I did not hear a voice. I heard the wind, and the fire, and my own breathing. And then, somehow, I understood that I had been told not to kneel.
Kneel before the shrine and listen
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o3: It always does, if you are not too proud to hear it, or too humble. Tell me, then. What did the Furious One teach you?
Return to Murbul at Dushnikh Yal
I went to Malacath's shrine. I think it told me something.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.o4: That strength is something you carry for others.
Yes. A strong Orc alone is only a bandit. A strong Orc with a stronghold is a wall.
That nobody gives you a place. You take it.
That is how most of us learn it. Just remember that what you take, someone may take from you.
That he doesn't want to be begged. He wants to be proven right.
Ha! You heard him clearly. The cast-out god, proven right by the cast-out. That is the whole of it.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.ou: I knelt at Malacath's shrine in Wrothgar and came back with an answer. Murbul taught me the Code of Malacath and marked my brow with ash from her fire.
story.skycraft.q.orc_code_of_malacath.pi: Blood-Kin who do not know the Code are guests with sharper teeth. Malacath is the god of the cast-out and the cursed, and his Code is how the cast-out live. Go to his shrine in Wrothgar, beyond the mountains, and listen. Then come back and tell me what you heard.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.desc: King Gurak means to honour me before the chiefs in the Hall of the Clans. Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun, who despises outsiders, has demanded the right to test me first, as the Code allows.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o0.re: Bazrag wants several words with you, and most of them are fists. He says no outsider should stand among the chiefs. The Code says he may test you. It does not say he must survive it, but I would rather he did. He has a good stronghold.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o0.to: I hear Bazrag wants a word with me.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o1.jo: Bazrag hit like a falling wall. When he finally went down to one knee, he spat out a tooth, laughed, and held out his hand.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o1.te: Beat Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun in the ring
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o2.re: He did, and now he says you are the best fight he has had in ten years. Stand there. The chiefs are watching, and I have something to say.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.o2.te: Stand before the chiefs in the Hall of the Clans
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.outro: I beat Chief Bazrag gro-Fharun in the ring, and King Gurak named me an Honored Chief of the Orsimer before every stronghold in Wrothgar.
story.skycraft.q.orc_honored_chief.title: Honored Chief
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.de: King Gurak is rebuilding Orsinium's walls. He wants the keystone of the old gate recovered from the ruins of Old Orsinium, and stone enough to set it.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o0: Travel to the ruins of Old Orsinium
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o1: Drive the ogre clan from the ruins
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o2: Thurga had made a throne of the old gate's stones and was sitting on the keystone itself. She did not take kindly to being asked to stand.
Kill the ogre matriarch, Thurga Stone-Chewer
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o3: Recover the keystone of the old gate
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o4: Older than my grandfather's grandfather, and still square. Good. Now the masons need stone to bed it in. Bring cut stone to the Forgemaster; she is keeping the tally.
Bring the keystone to King Gurak
The keystone of the old gate, my king.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.o5: Thirty-two, all square. The masons will set the keystone at dawn. Stay and watch, Blood-Kin. You will want to say you were there.
Bring thirty-two stone bricks to Forgemaster Ghamrash
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.of: Forgemaster Ghamrash says you're rebuilding the walls.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.ou: I recovered the keystone of Old Orsinium's gate from an ogre clan and brought stone to set it in. The new gate of Orsinium stands on the bones of the old.
story.skycraft.q.orc_stone_upon_stone.pi: Every time Orsinium has fallen, we have built it again from its own bones. The keystone of the old gate lies in the ruins of Old Orsinium, and an ogre clan squats on it. Bring me that stone, and enough cut stone to set it in, and the new gate will carry the old one's name.
story.skycraft.q.orc_the_forgemasters_or: Word of my deeds has reached Orsinium. Forgemaster Ghamrash gra-Shura of the Hall of the Clans has sent for me: the city's forges are starving for orichalc.

I did. The orichalc seam at Coldperch Cavern feeds half the forges in this city, and a pack of durzogs has moved into the workings and eaten two of my miners. The King wants walls. Walls want steel. Steel wants ore. You see the problem.
Speak with Forgemaster Ghamrash in the Hall of the Clans
The durzogs had denned in the deepest gallery, among the miners' abandoned picks. The pack-mother was the size of a pony and twice as bad-tempered.
Kill the durzogs infesting the mine
Bring up a load of orichalc ore
Green right through. Good ore, better miner. I'll have the crews back down there by morning. Here: I made this from the last of the old stock. Orsinium steel for an Orsinium friend.
Bring the ore to Forgemaster Ghamrash
The mine is clear. Here's the first of the ore.
I cleared the durzogs from Coldperch Cavern and brought orichalc ore back for Forgemaster Ghamrash. The forges of Orsinium are burning again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.desc: Brelas Indarys, assistant to Quaestor Aurelian Vesk, took a Dwemer regulating rod from the great coil in Alftand. Then something below started clicking.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.o1.journal: Brelas died in a pipe gallery with his satchel clutched to his chest. The rod still hums.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.o1.text: Recover the regulating rod from Brelas's satchel
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.o2.reply: ...He would. He was always more careful with the artefacts than with himself. I sent him there. I shall carry that, and I shall put his name on the paper, first, above mine. Leave me now. Please.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.o2.text: Bring the rod and the news to Quaestor Vesk
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.o2.topic: Brelas is dead. He kept this safe to the end.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.outro: Vesk's next memorandum to the Arch-Mage is titled 'On the Alftand Coil, by Brelas Indarys and A. Vesk'.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.pitch: Quaestor Vesk at the College sent his assistant into Alftand. The boy never came back. Vesk pretends he isn't worried. He's worried.
story.skycraft.q.pl_alftand.title: The Quaestor's Assistant
story.skycraft.q.pl_ancients_ascent.desc: The dragon Sahlokvir, raised from the mound below Greywater Grotto, nests on Ancient's Ascent and preys on the southern roads of Falkreath.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ancients_ascent.o1.j: Sahlokvir is dead. Grimvar will not get his song at Dead Man's Drink, but someone will.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ancients_ascent.outr: The shepherds south of Helgen bring their flocks back to the high pastures, and the Falkreath bards argue over who will write the song.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ancients_ascent.pitc: There's a dragon roosting on Ancient's Ascent. It came up out of the old mound below Greywater Grotto. Grimvar the hunter went up to kill it. His bow came down without him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.desc: Durz gro-Ushnar of Largashbur went into Angarvunde for a Nord dead-king's blade, hoping it would lift his stronghold's curse. His sister Gula wants him found.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o1.journa: Durz lay under the fallen wall in the deep hall. He had broken more draugr than I'd have believed of one Orc.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o1.text: Lay the Warden of Angarvunde to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o2.text: Find Durz's tusk-charm in the dark
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o3.reply: ...He was brave. He was a fool. Both go to Malacath's halls. I will tell the chief he was brave. I will not tell the chief he was a fool. That one is mine to keep.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o3.text: Bring the charm to Gula at Largashbur
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.o3.topic: Durz died in the deep hall. He fought to the end. He wanted the chief told he was brave.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.outro: Gula has her father's tusk back, and her brother's story to tell. Largashbur's curse is unbroken, but one Orc there is no longer waiting by the road.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.pitch: An Orc lad from Largashbur walked into Angarvunde after a Nord blade. His sister Gula sits by the road every night. Speak to her, if you're the barrow-diving sort.
story.skycraft.q.pl_angarvunde.title: The Brave Fool
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.desc: A cell of necromancers led by Master Feldir means to wake Hrodvald Iron-Breath, the chieftain buried in Ansilvund. His oath can only be broken by the blade that sealed it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.o1.journal: The oath-blade hung around the neck of the eldest guard, too short to fight with. It was warm, as though someone had just let go of it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.o1.text: Take the oath-blade from the oath-guard
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.o2.journal: When the oath-blade touched him, Hrodvald stopped fighting and simply lay down. I think he had been waiting a long time to be allowed to.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.o2.text: Break Hrodvald's oath and lay him to rest
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.outro: Ansilvund is silent now. The hunters say the sighing has stopped.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.pitch: Robed folk have been chanting in Ansilvund since Last Seed. The hunters say the barrow sighs at night. If they wake whatever's buried in there, it won't stop at the barrow door.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ansilvund.title: The Blade That Sealed It
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.desc: A green-scaled dragon has nested on the old shrine at Arcwind Point and hunts the herds south of Autumnwatch Tower. The Legion scout who watched it recommends that someone else kill it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.o1.jou: The dragon fell across the old shrine stair. Its scales, close up, were the colour of birch moss after rain.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.o1.tex: Slay the dragon of Arcwind Point
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.outro: Arcwind Point is empty again. Scout Valens can have her transfer, or keep her post, with one dragon fewer to observe.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.pitch: The dragon on Arcwind Point took a Legion scout last week. It hunts every third day and comes home at dusk. If you're the sort who fights dragons, now's your chance.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arcwind_point.title: Wings over Arcwind
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.desc: Magister Avidius Pell died in Arkngthamz. His Tonal Lens remains in the lower chamber, where the Dwemer machines wake when the stone sings.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.o1.text: Destroy the machines guarding the singing hall
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.o2.journa: Through the lens, the ruin's song is clear: a single long note, rising. It sounds almost like a question.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.outro: The Orcs of Dushnikh Yal say the stone sings softer since the lens left it. Their forge burns hotter for it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.pitch: A scholar from Winterhold went down into Arkngthamz with a crystal lens to measure the ruin's singing. The Orcs of Dushnikh Yal brought his bones back up. The lens is still in the singing hall, and the College would pay well for it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_arkngthamz.title: The Fourth Harmonic
story.skycraft.q.pl_ashfallow_citadel.de: The renegade Telvanni Seryne Dralas raises ash spawn at Ashfallow Citadel. When she has thirty, she means to march on Raven Rock for its ash; when she has a hundred, on Tel Mithryn.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ashfallow_citadel.o0: Break the ash spawn that guard the citadel
story.skycraft.q.pl_ashfallow_citadel.o1: Seryne Dralas is dead. Her ash creatures crumbled where they stood, all facing south, toward Raven Rock.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ashfallow_citadel.ou: The yard of Ashfallow Citadel is full of grey heaps that were soldiers once. The Telvanni at the Sun Stone has gone home, relieved.
story.skycraft.q.pl_ashfallow_citadel.pi: There's a cast-out Telvanni at Ashfallow Citadel raising ash spawn like a herd. Her creatures all stand facing Raven Rock. The Redoran Guard can't spare anyone. Can you?
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.desc: An Imperial expedition to Avanchnzel found a Dwemer key that quiets the machines, and woke the one guardian it does not. Lucan Varro's last wish was that the key never return to his Society.
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.o1.journa: Lucan Varro died in a maintenance crawlway with the key clutched to his chest. It hummed when I touched it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.o1.text: Find Lucan Varro and the resonance key
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.o2.journa: The Key-Warden fell, and every machine in Avanchnzel went quiet for a long moment, as if listening.
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.o2.text: Destroy the guardian of the lower hall
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.outro: I have the resonance key, and Lucan Varro's wish that it go into Lake Honrich. Whether it does is up to me.
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.pitch: Those Imperial scholars that went into Avanchnzel? The Orcs at Largashbur found one of their journals by the gate. Something in there is still guarding something.
story.skycraft.q.pl_avanchnzel.title: The Resonance Key
story.skycraft.q.pl_bannermist_tower.des: The bandits at Bannermist Tower signal passing carts to their gang on Knifepoint Ridge. Their signal lamp is the key to it all.
With the signal lamp gone, Knifepoint Ridge will be watching a dark tower and wondering why.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bannermist_tower.out: Carts reach Half-Moon Mill again without being counted on the way.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bannermist_tower.pit: Every time the lamps blink at Bannermist Tower, a cart goes missing on the mill road. Put those lamps out and the Knifepoint gang goes blind.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bards_leap_summit.de: A heartbroken bard carved a verse on the rock above Bard's Leap: he dropped his lost love's ring into the pool beneath the falls, and whoever finds it may keep it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bards_leap_summit.o0: Read the verse at the top of Bard's Leap
story.skycraft.q.pl_bards_leap_summit.o1: Wedged in the stones where the falls strike the pool: a gold ring, engraved inside with the name Ingrith.
Search the pool beneath the falls for the ring
story.skycraft.q.pl_bards_leap_summit.ou: The ring was never meant for you. It fits anyway.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bards_leap_summit.pi: There's a verse on the rock at Bard's Leap about a ring dropped in the pool below. Lots of folk have looked. Nobody's thought to look where the water actually lands.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.desc: A troll called Old Blackhide has taken over the lower shaft of Bilegulch Mine and stolen the clan's founding pick.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.o1.te: Kill Old Blackhide in the lower shaft
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.o2.jo: The pick was in the troll's nest, its haft gnawed but whole. It belongs on the hook by the shaft.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.outro: Shagrol hangs the pick back by the shaft and, after a long silence, offers you a place at the fire.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.pitch: The Orcs at Bilegulch lost their founder's pick to a troll in the deep shaft. Old Blackhide, they call it. Bring the pick back and they'll call you clan. That's worth more than gold, with Orcs.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bilegulch_mine.title: The Founder's Pick
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.desc: Grunnar Bear-Tooth went into Bleakcoast Cave to kill a great white sabre cat and never came out. The Jarl's bounty still stands.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.o0.j: The white cat is dead. Grunnar lay deep in her den, his grandfather's bow still across his knees.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.o0.t: Hunt down the white sabre cat
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.o1.t: Claim the Jarl's bounty in Winterhold
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.outr: The furrier in Winterhold makes a fine coat from the white pelt. You leave Frostsinger with Grunnar, as he asked.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakcoast_cave.pitc: There's a white sabre cat in Bleakcoast Cave that killed Grunnar, the best hunter in Winterhold. The Jarl's offering ten septims a tooth. Big cat, lots of teeth.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.desc: A giant from Bleakwind Basin took Brindle, a cow from Pelagia Farm. Farmhand Gunnvor wants to know the cow is alive and well, and wants her bell back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o0.j: Brindle stood by the giants' fire, fat and content, a young giant scratching her ears. Her bell lay on a rock nearby, very carefully untied.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o0.t: Look in on Brindle at Bleakwind Basin, quietly
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o1.t: Take Brindle's bell without waking the giants
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o2.c: She's happy there. The young giant loves her. Let her stay.
...A giant's pet. Well. There are worse lives for a cow. I'll hang the bell on the barn door so I remember her. Severio will grumble, but he grumbles at everything.
Take cheese. The old herders say giants will trade.
Cheese! I knew it. I'll take a wheel up there myself at dawn, and if they won't trade, at least they'll know we came politely.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o2.r: Alive! Gods. Is she well? Tell me true, should I go and fetch her?
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.o2.t: Brindle is alive. Here's her bell.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.outr: Whatever became of Brindle in the end, Gunnvor says she has stopped losing sleep over giants.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bleakwind_basin.pitc: A giant from Bleakwind Basin stepped over our fence and walked off with Brindle under his arm. I watched them for days. They're good to her. But she's ours. Could you go and see? Bring me her bell, at least, so I know she's well.
story.skycraft.q.pl_blind_cliff_cave.des: A Reachwoman named Aiwen was sold to the hagraven Ulvra Ash-Tongue at Blind Cliff Cave, to be made into a hagraven herself. Without Ulvra's rite-knife, the becoming cannot happen.
With the knife in hand there can be no becoming. Aiwen was gone, and a cut rope hung by the smoke hole. Someone had come for her first.
story.skycraft.q.pl_blind_cliff_cave.out: Two pairs of footprints led away from Blind Cliff Cave toward the Lover Stone: a woman's, and a miner's heavy boots.
story.skycraft.q.pl_blind_cliff_cave.pit: The crones at Blind Cliff Cave mean to turn a girl into one of their own come the dark of the moon. Poor thing threw a message out of the smoke hole. If someone took the old hag's knife, there'd be no rite at all.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.desc: Lady Arnvor's vampire court at Bloodlet Throne takes a tithe of travellers from the Pale Pass road and records each one on the Red Tithe Roll.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.o0.t: Go to Bloodlet Throne, by day if you are wise
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.o2.j: Lady Arnvor is ash. The Red Tithe Roll was on her table, beside a cup of something that was not wine.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.o3.r: Hallvard the pilgrim. The Legion courier we wrote off as a deserter. The miller's boy who came home pale and won't say why. Gods. Every family on this list deserves to know. I'll read it out in the square myself, and the Jarl can stop me if he dares.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.o3.t: Bring the Red Tithe Roll to Bailiff Eirik
Bloodlet Throne is cleared. This is their list of the taken.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.outr: The names on the Red Tithe Roll are read aloud in Falkreath's square, and the Pale Pass road is a little less quiet at night.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodlet_throne.pitc: Travellers vanish on the Pale Pass road below Bloodlet Throne. A pilgrim smuggled a letter out: vampires, a dozen of them, and their lady writes down every name. Bailiff Eirik needs that list, so the families at least know.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodskal_barrow.des: Grave robbers stole five ancestral urns from Raven Rock's tomb, including a silver-banded urn of House Morvayn, and hid them in Bloodskal Barrow. Sergeant Mileth Indaram wants them back, quietly.
Deal with the grave robbers in Bloodskal Barrow
Recover the Morvayn urn and the others
Ransomed. Of course it was. The ancestors will be back in their niches by nightfall, and the Councilor will never need to know how close it came. That is the Redoran way: the wall holds, and no one sees the cracks.
Return the urns to Sergeant Indaram
Your urns. All five. The Morvayn one was to be ransomed back to the Councilor.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodskal_barrow.out: The urns are home. Mileth has had the drainage cut in the tomb wall bricked up, and placed a guard on it who is, he admits, mostly for show.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bloodskal_barrow.pit: We are. Grave robbers broke into the town tomb and took five ancestral urns, one of them from the Councilor's own family. The tracks go north to Bloodskal Barrow. I can't spare four guards. I can spare you, if you'll go. Quietly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bonestrewn_crest.des: The dragon Sahqovul has made Bonestrewn Crest its roost and counts its kills in claw-marks on a boulder. Eydis the Bold and her company died trying to take it sleeping.
Sahqovul is dead. I scratched one last mark on its counting-stone, and it was not one of mine.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bonestrewn_crest.out: The giants of Steamcrag have started grazing their mammoths below the crest again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_bonestrewn_crest.pit: A dragon roosts on Bonestrewn Crest, sleeping on a bed of mammoth tusks. Eydis the Bold went up with three friends. Only her journal came down, and that was carried by a giant.
story.skycraft.q.pl_boulderfall_cave.des: A necromancer at Boulderfall Cave has been buying bodies from someone at Riften's Hall of the Dead. Her ledger would name the seller.
The ledger names the seller: a junior attendant at the Riften Hall of the Dead. It also names Sister Hrolfa, at Ruunvald, as a buyer.
story.skycraft.q.pl_boulderfall_cave.out: Magister Venn's workshop is closed for good. Her apprentice Teodor, if he lives, is free of her box of hair. The Hall of the Dead in Riften will be getting a visit.
story.skycraft.q.pl_boulderfall_cave.pit: Bodies are going missing from the Hall of the Dead. Somebody's carting them up to Boulderfall Cave. Ask me, the priests know more than they're saying.
story.skycraft.q.pl_brinewater_grotto.de: A signal roster from Brinewater Grotto shows a wrecker crew luring ships onto the rocks north of Solitude. Their leader, Saltjaw Hroar, sells the plunder to the smugglers of Broken Oar.
story.skycraft.q.pl_brinewater_grotto.o0: Clear the wreckers out of Brinewater Grotto
story.skycraft.q.pl_brinewater_grotto.o1: Hroar is dead. No more lanterns will swing at the grotto mouth.
