story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_hircine_high_: Huntmaster Gaspard Lorne of Evermor has lost hounds and men near the shrine of Hircine in Stormhaven. The steward of the Old Lodge believes his master, Lord Remy Belcourt, has become what he hunts.
Go to the shrine of Hircine south-west of Evermor
When the beast fell it was Lord Remy Belcourt again, with a smile on his face and his hunting ring cutting into a swollen finger.
The Master of the Old Lodge
Hunt the beast of the Old Lodge
Take Lord Belcourt's hunting ring as proof
Tell them the truth. Others who were bitten need to come forward.
You're right, curse you. If there are more bitten men in Evermor, they'll only come forward if they know what they're facing. I'll tell the family myself.
Tell them it was a bear. Let the man be mourned, not feared.
A bear, then. A very large bear. I'll swear to it myself. I'm a poor liar, but grief makes people want to believe.
Remy. Gods. We hunted together as boys. What do we tell his family? The truth will ruin them. A bear would let them grieve in peace.
Tell Huntmaster Lorne in Evermor what you found
Your beast was Lord Belcourt. He's dead.
The autumn hunt rides again from Evermor next season. Huntmaster Lorne will not go near the Old Lodge, and no one asks him to.
Huntmaster Lorne in Evermor keeps telling everyone it's a bear by the Hircine stone. He's a terrible liar. Ask him what it really is. Then bring a silver blade.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_hircine_morro: Hircine has marked his prey for the season on Azura's Coast: a bull kagouti called Ashtusk, with one tusk snapped into a crown. The Huntsman's rules: your own hand, and the tusk, not the head.
Go to the Huntsman's altar on Azura's Coast
Ashtusk goes down hard, and for a moment the scrub is silent. Then, far off, something howls. It sounds pleased.
Take the crowned tusk, as the Huntsman's rules demand
Ulath Morvel pays, as promised, and asks you to sign his hunting book. Ashlander trackers nod to you on the coast road now, as one hunter to another.

The Telvanni huntsman posted a challenge at the Hircine altar west of Sadrith Mora. Some monster of a kagouti, Ashtusk. Four hunters dead. Go and read the rules before you try it. The Huntsman cares about the rules.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_mehrunes_dago: A cult calling itself the Unbroken Ash holds the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon west of Necrom. Its speaker, Sul Indaram, killed Ordinator Dral and wears his mask at the rites. The Ordinators of Necrom ask for outside help.
Go to the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in Molag Amur
Break the cultists of the Unbroken Ash and their summoned dremora
Indaram dies looking at the statue, not at you. He looks almost relieved.
Sul Indaram
Kill Sul Indaram, speaker of the Unbroken Ash
Recover Ordinator Dral's mask
The Ordinators of Necrom take Dral's mask without a word, clean it, and lay it in the mortuary. One of them, later, buys you a drink, and still says nothing, which is high praise from an Ordinator.

Four Ordinators came back from the Dagon stones. The fifth's mask is on a heretic's face now. The Temple won't say it, but they're asking for help. Read their report at the shrine, if you dare go that close.
The Unbroken Ash

A cultist called Vorondil and his 'Returning Dawn' have bound two dremora at the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north of Alinor, beside the memorial to the Oblivion Crisis dead. With a third, they mean to reopen the old gate in the hillside.
Banish the bound dremora at the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon
Vorondil is dead. With his last breath he told me the Justiciars knew, and let him be, because a frightened city is an obedient one.
Vorondil
Kill Vorondil, Keeper of the Returning Dawn
Take the crystal gate-key from the altar

So small a thing, to open so large a door. I shall have it ground to dust in the Tower's lowest kiln, and I shall add Vorondil's name to the memorial roll. Under 'causes', not 'casualties'. And the Justiciars? Ah. I shall say nothing. I am old, not foolish.
Bring the gate-key to Lorekeeper Tirenwe in Alinor
Vorondil is dead. This is what he meant to open the gate with.
The offerings at the Dagon shrine stop. The memorial beside it gets fresh flowers instead, left by someone who climbs very slowly.

Old Tirenwe at the Tower says someone's trying to open a gate at the Dagon shrine north of the city, same place the Daedra came through in the Crisis. The Justiciars won't move. Tirenwe can't climb hills any more.
The Returning Dawn

A Bosmer firebrand called Caedwen the Ashen is burning circles in the forest around the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north-east of Woodhearth. She means to light the seventh herself at the dark of the moon. Warden Ilthaer wants her stopped.
Go to the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon north-east of Woodhearth
Caedwen died laughing, with the brand in her hand still burning. The trees around the shrine did not catch.
Caedwen the Ashen
Stop Caedwen the Ashen before she lights the seventh circle
Take the Seventh Brand from her hand

Caedwen. I taught her to track, when she was small. She asked why we could not build like the Altmer and I told her it was the Pact. I suppose that was not answer enough. I'll drown this brand in the harbour, and then I'll go and tell her mother.
Bring the brand to Warden Ilthaer in Woodhearth
Caedwen the Ashen is dead. This was her torch.
The burned circles of Greenshade are slow to heal. The wardens plant nothing, as the Pact requires. They only wait, and the forest comes back on its own.
Warden Ilthaer is hunting whoever's been burning the forest by the Dagon shrine. She'd take help from a stranger. That's how bad it is: a Bosmer warden asking an outsider for help.
The Seventh Circle
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_meridia_cyrod: Sister Aurelia Vanne kept Meridia's light on a hill north-east of the Imperial City. A necromancer named Corvus the Pale has raised the Ayleid dead beneath it and set them round the statue to smother its light.
Break the ring of Ayleid dead around the statue
Corvus dies cursing the light. The skeletons fold to the ground like puppets with their strings cut.
As you lift the lens, the grey film slides from it like ash in the rain, and a thin clean light comes up out of the glass, as if the statue had drawn breath.
Lift the Lens of the Dawn from the statue's hands

When you set the lens back, the statue blazes for a moment so brightly that the farmers below come out of their doors to look. Meridia keeps her bargains. A sliver of Ayleid glass is waiting at the statue's feet.

The Meridia statue past the farms has gone dark. Skeletons standing round it in a ring, and a man in black behind them. The sister who kept the light left a journal there. Someone should read it, and then do what it asks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_meridia_hamme: A bone-singer calling himself the Dune-King has raised a whole caravan in the hills north of Rihad and taken an old Ansei's sword from its grave. The Ash'abah who camp at the shrine of Meridia are too few to stop him.
Find the Ash'abah camp at the shrine of Meridia north of Rihad
Lay Jafar's walking caravan to rest in the hollows north-east of the shrine
The Dune-King is dead, and the drovers of Jafar's caravan lie still under the moon. The Ash'abah washed every one of them before dawn.
Daria of the Ash'abah looked at the old blade a long time. 'It sang for a monster,' she said. 'Let it learn to sing for you. Then perhaps it will forgive us all.'
The Ash'abah still may not sleep inside Rihad's walls. But the gate-guards nod to them now, and someone has started leaving bread at their camp.
The Ash'abah at the Meridia stone north of Rihad are asking for help. Not something they do. There's a necromancer in the hills with a dead man's sword. A sword-singer's sword.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_molag_bal_bla: Varis Hlervu, a Dunmer of a fallen House who calls himself the Chain-Lord, holds Saxhleel captives in chains at the shrine of Molag Bal near the Necrom border, as an offering to the Prince of Domination.
Go to the shrine of Molag Bal in the Shadowfen
You unlock nine sets of chains. The Saxhleel do not thank you in words. They walk south toward Helstrom together, and the last of them touches your arm as he passes.
Take the Chain-Lord's keys and free the captives
The warriors of Helstrom carry the Chain-Lord's chains home and drop them into the black pool. They drop a stone in, too, for you. It is a great honour, they assure you, though you are still alive.

Helstrom's asking for every spear. There's a Dunmer at the Molag Bal stones on the border with nine of ours in new chains. Calls himself the Chain-Lord. Says his Prince promised him our hides. Show him what the marsh promises.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_molag_bal_cyr: Jorunn Stone-Wife's daughter Hilde was taken on the north road from Bruma. Her basket was found near the shrine of Molag Bal in the Jeralls.
Climb to the shrine of Molag Bal north-west of Bruma
Kill the Chain-Keeper, Lady Ottilia Venn
Hilde is alive, blue with cold, still humming under her breath. She takes the key from your hand and unlocks her own chain, and then the carter's beside her, before she lets herself cry.
Take the Chain-Keeper's keys and free the captives
Alive. Alive! Oh, Kynareth, oh, Mara... Sit. Sit down. You'll never pay for a meal in this house again. Not one. Not ever.
Tell Jorunn in Bruma that her daughter is coming home
Hilde is alive. She's walking down the north road now.
You look like you haven't slept in days.
Bruma talks about little else for a week. Hilde sings in her mother's kitchen again, though she won't sing the song she was singing on the mountain.

My Hilde took bread up the north road four days ago. The watch says wolves. I found her basket by the Molag Bal stones with the bread still in it. Wolves eat bread. Whatever took her didn't. Please. I can't climb up there. I can't.
The Girl Who Sang in the Cold
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_molag_bal_ham: A slaver called Sallah Iron-Collar takes fisherfolk from the villages north of Taneth and sells them at the shrine of Molag Bal in the hills, tithing the old and weak to the Lord of Chains. Five captives are still in his pens.
Go to the shrine of Molag Bal north of Taneth
Cut down the slavers before they reach the pens
Iron-Collar died with his whip in his hand, calling on a Prince who did not answer.
Five captives behind the shrine, alive. The old woman who would not stop singing is among them. She sang all the way back to Taneth.
Take Iron-Collar's keys and open the pens
The Forebear Harbour Court pays the bounty with unusual promptness, and posts a notice thanking 'a friend of Hew's Bane' by no particular name.

Lord Ezhar's put a price on Iron-Collar's head. Fishers keep vanishing north of Taneth, and everyone knows they end up at the Molag Bal shrine. If you've the stomach for it, there's people in those pens.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_molag_bal_hig: Lord Tamrith of Shornhelm rode out to cleanse the shrine of Molag Bal west of the city and was killed by a vampire called the Lady of Chains. His groom still lives as her captive, and the family's ancestral sword is kept at the shrine as a trophy.
Go to the shrine of Molag Bal west of Shornhelm
Destroy the thralls guarding the shrine
The Lady of Chains is ash. Etienne Coste and three other captives were alive in the shackles behind the shrine. They walked home to Shornhelm on their own feet.
The old Shornhelm blade came out of the stone as if it had been waiting. The Dowager has sent word: a Tamrith sword belongs in a hand that will use it, and her son's will not. It is mine.
Draw the Tamrith blade from the stone
The Dowager Tamrith pays in full, bargains for nothing, and sends a lecture by courier on the proper care of ancestral steel.
The Dowager Tamrith wants her husband's sword back from the Molag Bal shrine. They say there's still somebody alive out there in chains. Only someone who isn't afraid of the cold, she says.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_namira_elswey: Za'mira's son J'kar stole a dark-moon pendant from the Dro-m'Athra at the shrine of Namiira and has walked with them ever since. His mother asks that the pendant be taken from him and brought into the light, whatever it costs.
Go to the shrine of Namiira north-west of Torval
J'kar falls, and for a moment, before the end, his eyes clear. He says 'tell Mother I'm sorry about the window'.
End J'kar the Moonless, and the dark-souled who walk with him
Take the dark-moon pendant out into the light
Za'mira buries her son with a candle burning, so he can see the way home. The Moon-Priests take the pendant and say they will drop it in the deepest well in Torval, where no moon has ever shone.
Old Za'mira left a letter at Namiira's stones for her son. J'kar walks with the dark-souled now. She wants the pendant off him, even if he has to die for it. Go by night. That's when they gather.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_namira_valenw: Bosmer Mandate-Breakers at the shrine of Namira north-east of Woodhearth have taken two net-boys from the docks, and mean to feast on them at the dark of the moon, claiming the Green Pact on their side.
Break the Mandate-Breakers at the shrine of Namira
Gorthil the Lean is dead. In the pit behind the shrine, the two net-boys were alive, thin and terrified, their wrists tied with net-cord.
Hunt them. They ate their own kin.
Then they'll be hunted, by every hunter in Greenshade. And what is done with them after is the Pact's business, not yours. Better that you don't see it.
Let them go. Show them the mercy they wouldn't show.
Mercy. The Spinners will make a tale of that, and argue about it for a hundred years. Very well. They are banished from Greenshade. If they come back, the mercy ends.

Good. Now the wardens can stop arguing. But the rest of the Mandate-Breakers fled into Greenshade. By the Pact, we may hunt them as enemies, and they know what that means. Or we can let them go. You found them. What would you have us do?
Tell Warden Ilthaer in Woodhearth what happened
The net-boys are free. Gorthil is dead.
The net-boys go back to their nets. They don't speak about the pit, and the dockhands of Woodhearth have learned not to ask.

Two net-boys went missing off the Woodhearth docks. Everyone knows the Mandate-Breakers at the Namira shrine have them. The wardens are still arguing over the Pact. The boys haven't got time for that argument.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_nocturnal_els: A gang called the Shadow-Claws robbed the shrine of Nocturnal near Senchal, taking the offerings and the bow that Rajhin the Footpad himself hung at the Lady's feet. Old Ja'khirr, the Last Footpad, asks for the offerings to be returned.
Go to the shrine of Nocturnal near Senchal
Deal with the Shadow-Claws mocking the Lady at her stones
Jo'vahn's last words are 'this one should have stayed a pickpocket'. Fair.
When you set the box at the statue's feet, its lid opens by itself. The coins and rings are inside. The bow is not. It is lying across your pack, as if it had always been there.
Return the Lady's offering box to the shrine
The thieves of Senchal will never say your name aloud. They will, however, never steal from you either, and in Senchal that is a kind of knighthood.
The Shadow-Claws robbed the Lady. Took Rajhin's own bow. Old Ja'khirr left a message at the stones for whoever's brave enough. Every thief in Senchal is cheering for you. Quietly. From very far away.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_nocturnal_hig: A smuggler called Black Tomas hid twelve Orcish blades near the shrine of Nocturnal west of Orsinium, as surety against a Breton buyer who cheated him. He never came back for them.
Go to the shrine of Nocturnal west of Orsinium
Under the black stone, wrapped in oilcloth with a crow feather: Orcish steel, rust-free and keen. Most of it is too heavy to carry far, but the finest axe is worth the walk.
Dig under the flat black stone south-east of the shrine
Black Tomas's crew never come asking. Either he is dead, or he has a new route. In Wrothgar, it is wise not to find out which.

Black Tomas the smuggler never came back from his last run over the passes. Story goes he hid a bundle of Orsinium steel by the Nocturnal shrine. Nobody's found it. Nobody's looked very hard, mind. Smugglers have friends.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_nocturnal_sum: The thief called the Moth has fled Auridon, leaving behind a letter at the shrine of Nocturnal west of Firsthold. In it she tells where she buried everything she stole from Magistrate Caladwe.
Go to the shrine of Nocturnal west of Firsthold
Under the cypress with the moth carved on its root: a strongbox of the Magistrate's jewels, a ledger of bribes, and a heavy gold ring. The circlet is gone. The Moth kept one thing after all.
Dig beneath the twisted cypress north of the shrine
Somewhere in the quarantine anchorage off Firsthold, a few sick sailors find coins in their bread. Nobody knows who left them. Nobody asks.
The Moth's gone. Fled the island. They say she left her stash buried by the Nocturnal stone. The Justiciars dug up half the hill. Either they dug the wrong half, or they're keeping quiet about it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_peryite_elswe: Ri'jasha's caravan of the clan Ra'zhan caught Peryite's orderly plague at the shrine north of Torval. She wants the clan's caravan bell brought back, so her people can one day be called home.
Go to the shrine of Peryite north of Torval
Drive off the plague-rats swarming the wagons
When you lift the bell it rings once, out of time, and every one of the counting Khajiit stops and looks up at the moons, just for a breath, before they begin again.
Take the caravan bell from the lead wagon

They looked up? Then they are still in there, somewhere under the counting. This one will take the bell to the Moon-Bishop. Perhaps the Lattice can call louder than the Taskmaster. Perhaps. This one will ring it every night until it does.
Bring the bell to Ri'jasha in Torval
Your clan's bell. And... they looked up, when it rang.
Every evening in Torval's market, a single caravan bell rings out of time. The Moon-Priests have begun to ring their own bells with it.

The Taskmaster happened. We stopped for water at the Peryite stones north of the city and this one's cousins caught his orderly plague. They walk in rows around the statue now, counting. This one cannot save them. But the clan's bell is on the lead wagon, and without it the Ra'zhan cannot call their dead home to the Lattice. Bring this one the bell.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_peryite_high_: Plague-cultists at the shrine of Peryite north-east of Wayrest have stolen Aldous Penhallow's case of remedies. Their leader, Velmont the Tender, means to brew an old plague from its last pages and send it into the city.
Velmont is dead. His plague-pots lie broken on the shrine, and none of them had yet been filled.
Stop Velmont the Tender at the shrine of Peryite
The green-bound case was under Velmont's cot. The red-sealed pages at the back are intact. Nobody has broken the wax.
Forty years of my life, all of it in one ugly box. Thank you. Is the red seal broken? No? Then the worst of me is still in there, asleep.
Return the case to Aldous Penhallow in Wayrest
I have your case of cures.
Burn them. No one should ever read them.
Yes. Yes, you're right. There. Forty years of cleverness, and the best thing I ever did with it was to watch it burn.
Keep them sealed. One day a healer may need to know how it works.
A healer, or a cultist. I'll give them to the Temple vault, under three locks, and pray that the right one finds them first.
I wrote them as a young man who wanted to understand the Knahaten sickness. I understood it far too well. You have earned a say in this.
Decide what becomes of the sealed pages
The Mortar by the Fish Bridge opens again, and old Penhallow leaves a free bottle of fen-cough tincture on his counter for anyone who asks.
Penhallow the apothecary lost his case of cures on the fen road, by the Peryite stone. Word is the cultists out there want one recipe in particular. The bad one.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_sanguine_cyro: Galen Vinicius, a vintner of Skingrad, lost his daughter Lucilla to a revel at the shrine of Sanguine in the hills west of the city.
Follow the music to the shrine of Sanguine west of Skingrad

Lucilla is not here. Only her green masque, and a note behind it: 'Tell Father I'm happy. Tell him the Shiraz here is better. Tell him not to look for me, because he'd find me, and then he'd have to choose.'
Search the revel for any sign of Lucilla
Tell him the truth: she chose to stay.
Chose. She chose. Well. She always did know her own mind, and never mine. I'll pour the first cup of this year's barrel on the soil for her. The Weald will know where to carry it.
Tell him she is dead, and spare him the choice.
Dead. Then... then at least I can stop listening for the music. Thank you. I'll bury the masque by the vines. She'd have liked that.
Her masque. She sewed the leaves on herself. What... what did the note say?
Tell Galen Vinicius what you found
I found her masque. And a note.
Music? No. Why do you ask?
On full-moon nights, a few Skingrad folk swear they hear a girl laughing in the vineyards. Galen Vinicius never mentions it.

My daughter Lucilla followed that music into the hills on her name-day. West of the city, where the Sanguine statue stands. That was a month ago. The Count's steward told me some young people are better not sought. I'm not the Count. Find her. Or find out.
The Last Dance of Lucilla Vinicius
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_sanguine_high: Young Lord Aubin Gaudrel went masked to the Revel of the Ninth Mask at the shrine of Sanguine west of Daggerfall and lost the family signet at dice to a red-eyed host. His mother, Lady Ysmene, wants the ring back before the court notices.
Find the Revel of the Ninth Mask at the shrine of Sanguine
The Host laughed even as it was banished. 'Well played,' it said. 'He'll be back, you know. They always come back.'
Win the signet back from the Red-Eyed Host, by the only wager it accepts
The signet lay among the Host's winnings. Aubin himself was asleep under the table, wearing a stag mask and one boot, and refused to be woken.
Take the Gaudrel signet from the Host's table

Under a table. His father proposed to me under a table, did you know? At a revel very like that one. I suppose it runs in the blood. Thank you. I shall have him fetched, and then I shall have him lectured until he wishes the Daedra had kept him.
Return the signet to Lady Ysmene Gaudrel
Your son's signet. He's alive, and asleep under a table.
Aubin Gaudrel comes home on a borrowed horse two days later and swears he will never drink again. He is at the next revel within the month.
Lady Gaudrel's boy is still at the Sanguine revel. Three days now. They say he lost the family ring to some red-eyed thing at dice. She won't say so, but she'd pay anyone who fetched it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_sheogorath_cy: Fulvius Pell of Bravil left a formal complaint at the shrine of Sheogorath: the Mad God's scamp has stolen his good hat. He would like it back. He will pay in buttons. Also money.
Go to the Mad God's shrine north-west of Bravil
The scamp bows deeply before it dies, and the hat stays on its head the whole time, which seems unfair.
You'll find Fulvius in Bravil eventually, or he'll find you. He'll wear the hat at exactly the same angle as the scamp did, and swear he always has.
You heard about Fulvius's hat? The Mad God's scamp has it. Wears it at an angle, Fulvius says. He's offering a reward. Mostly buttons, I think. But some money.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_vaermina_morr: Fevyn Andalor's brother Drals is one of the ash-sleepers who walk each night to the shrine of Vaermina, where a priestess called the Dream-Mother feeds on their nightmares.
Follow the sleepers to the shrine of Vaermina under Red Mountain
When the Dream-Mother falls, the ring of sleepers sways like grass in the wind, and then they all sit down at once, still sleeping.
Take the vial of stolen dreams from her body
Break the vial. Let him wake empty, but free.
Then he'll wake not knowing the last year. Not knowing he walked, not knowing I wept. Maybe that's a mercy. He'll think I just got old.
Give it to him. They are his dreams, even the bad ones.
They're his. Even the mountain, even the fire. He'll scream, the first night. And then he'll be Drals again, all of him. I'll sit up with him. I've had practice.
His dreams. All the nights he's lost. If I break it, will he wake? If I give them back to him... will he remember what she showed him?
Bring the vial to Fevyn in Balmora
The Dream-Mother is dead. I have this vial. Drals's dreams are in it.
The sleepers of Balmora stop walking, for now. The Temple calls it a blessing. Fevyn Andalor calls it you.

My brother Drals walks out of Balmora in his sleep every night, toward the Vaermina stones under the mountain. There's a ring of sleepers there, and a woman in the middle singing to them. She's drinking them. I can see it in his face. Please. Stop her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrine_vaermina_vale: Every night the sleepers of Arenthia walk north to the shrine of Vaermina, where a Bosmer dream-thief called the Lantern-Bearer harvests their dreams into a basket. Shazah, keeper of the Two Moons Inn, wants her stopped.
Go to the shrine of Vaermina north of Arenthia
The purple lantern shattered as Ellidir fell. For a moment every wisp around the shrine had the face of a sleeping child.
Take the basket of stolen dreams

Shazah can hear them. Listen: the golden cat walking across the sky. That is her cub's dream. Tonight Shazah will open the basket by the beds and let them fly home. And tomorrow, you drink at the Two Moons for nothing. For a month. Two months.
Bring the basket to Shazah at the Two Moons Inn
The Lantern-Bearer is dead. Here are the dreams she stole.
Arenthia sleeps through the night again. Shazah's cub dreams of the golden cat, and wakes up laughing.
Shazah at the Two Moons is offering good coin to whoever stops the dream-thief at the Vaermina stones. Her cub walks there every night now. Go at dusk. That's when the lantern's lit.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shroud_hearth_barrow: Asvar, a stonemason's son of Ivarstead, took a burial urn from Shroud Hearth Barrow and woke its Hearthkeeper. The knocking in the barrow has not stopped since.
Asvar was dead by the hearth door, the urn still in his arms. He had tried to put it back.
When the Hearthkeeper fell, I set the urn back in its alcove. The knocking stopped. The ash in the hearth-bowl was warm.
The knocking under Ivarstead has stopped. Hjorvald will bring his son home and bury him close to the hearth he was trying to mend.
Hjorvald's boy went into Shroud Hearth for a Ratway fence and an urn of silver. There's been knocking from the hill every night since. Put it right, if anything can.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.desc: A greedy woodcutter cut heartwood from the eldest tree of the Shrouded Grove, and its spriggan has turned savage. Liv Moss-Mother says the heartwood must go back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.o0.jo: The woodcutters were drying the heartwood by their fire to sell as alchemy stock. It still pulses faintly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.o0.te: Take the heartwood back from the woodcutters' camp
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.o1.jo: When the heartwood touched the trunk, the black rot drained from the elder spriggan's bark like ink washed from a page.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.o1.te: Return the heartwood to the eldest tree
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.outro: Liv leaves a jar of honey at the grove's edge. In the morning it is empty, and a sprig of snowberries lies beside it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.pitch: Old Liv the herb-woman says someone cut the heart out of the great tree in the Shrouded Grove, and the tree-women have gone mad over it. She wants it put right, not burned out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_shrouded_grove.title: The Stolen Heartwood
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.desc: The Falmer dragged miner Torbjorn Coal-Eye from Whistling Mine into the Sightless Pit. His wife wants his luck-charm back, whatever is left of him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.o0.jou: Torbjorn was beyond help. The Falmer had hung his silver hammer over their shrine, as if it were holy.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.o0.tex: Find Torbjorn's silver hammer in the Sightless Pit
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.o1.tex: Bring the charm to Torbjorn's crew at Whistling Mine
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.outro: The miners pass the little hammer from hand to hand, then send it to Torbjorn's widow with a month of their own wages.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.pitch: Falmer took a miner from Whistling Mine down into the Sightless Pit. His wife's asking for his luck-charm back. Brave folk only.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sightless_pit.title: Torbjorn's Hammer
story.skycraft.q.pl_silent_moons_camp.de: Hrodna, the bandit smith at Silent Moons Camp, forged a blade under both moons from the pale ore of Halted Stream. She calls it Moonsliver and keeps it locked by the lunar forge.
story.skycraft.q.pl_silent_moons_camp.o0: Fight past the bandits at Silent Moons Camp
story.skycraft.q.pl_silent_moons_camp.o1: Hrodna fought with a smith's hammer, not her fine blade. She never meant to use Moonsliver on anyone. She meant to sell it and be free.
story.skycraft.q.pl_silent_moons_camp.ou: Moonsliver is mine now. Under the moons, its edge gleams faintly blue.
story.skycraft.q.pl_silent_moons_camp.pi: The bandits at Silent Moons have a smith who's made something special, a blade that shines like the moons. I'd sooner it were in honest hands than hers.
story.skycraft.q.pl_silverdrift_lair.des: Halla Sweet-Voice, a skald of Dawnstar, went into Silverdrift Lair to copy the lost closing verse of the Saga of the White Strand.
Halla never finished her copy. Her charcoal was still on the tablet, half the verse traced out.
Find the tablet of the White Strand
Bring the tablet to the skalds of Dawnstar
story.skycraft.q.pl_silverdrift_lair.out: That winter Dawnstar hears the Saga of the White Strand sung to its end for the first time in four hundred years. The final verse is dedicated to Halla.
story.skycraft.q.pl_silverdrift_lair.pit: A skald went into Silverdrift Lair to copy some old verse. The bards in Dawnstar are fretting. Never seen so many people worried about a poem.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.desc: A College novice spent a night in the Skytemple Ruins on a dare and dropped his master's focus crystal down the inner stair. Something in the ruins speaks with the storm.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.o0.t: Find the focus crystal on the inner stair
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.o1.j: The thing that spoke in the stones was a storm spirit bound to the old altar. The lightning has stopped.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.o1.t: Silence the storm in the inner altar
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.o2.r: Faldrus? He crawled back to the College two days ago with frostbitten ears and a vow of silence. So that is where my crystal went. I shall make him write an essay on it. Thirty pages. With footnotes.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.o2.t: Return the crystal to Quaestor Vesk
Your novice dropped this in the Skytemple Ruins.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.outr: Faldrus survives his essay. The wager with Onmund remains, by mutual agreement, void.
story.skycraft.q.pl_skytemple_ruins.pitc: One of the College students went up to the Skytemple Ruins on a dare. Lost something precious down there, they say. And there's been lightning over the ruins on clear nights since.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sleeping_tree_camp.d: Arcadia of Whiterun wants a flask of sap from the great tree at Sleeping Tree Camp, guarded by giants. She advises approaching from the south, downwind, just after sundown.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sleeping_tree_camp.o: The giants snored by their fire while I filled the flask. One of them smiled in his sleep. I did not stay to find out what he was dreaming.
Tap a flask of sap from the Sleeping Tree
And not a giant's footprint on you! Here is your half, and a little more, for the quiet feet. Don't tell my Solitude buyer what I paid you.
Bring the sap to Arcadia in Whiterun
One flask of Sleeping Tree sap, as promised.
Arcadia's buyer in Solitude has his sap. Arcadia has a new respect for adventurers who know how to walk softly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sleeping_tree_camp.p: Arcadia will split a fat price for a flask of sap from the Sleeping Tree. You just have to tiptoe past a camp of giants. Quietly. Very quietly.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.desc: A hagraven in Snapleg Cave blows the stolen horn of the hunter Orgnar Bent-Bow to lure his friends and kin to her den. His widow, Haldis Copperhand, wants it back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.o2.jour: The horn lay on the hagraven's altar beside a bladder tied with a lock of grey hair. When I picked it up, the wind across its mouth sounded almost like a man saying thank you.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.o3.repl: It's quiet now. It was never quiet when he had it. ...I'll hang it over the door. If anything ever blows it again, I'll know to run toward it, not away.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.o3.text: Bring the horn to Haldis at Darkwater Crossing
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.o3.topi: Orgnar's horn. The witch is dead.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.outro: There is no more horn-calling in the hills below Darkwater Pass.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.pitch: Orgnar Bent-Bow's been dead a month, and his horn still blows at night from Snapleg Cave. His widow at Darkwater Crossing wants it back. I'd want it smashed, myself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snapleg_cave.title: The Calling-Horn
story.skycraft.q.pl_snowpoint_beacon.des: Snowpoint Beacon has stood dark for twenty years, since a wraith out of the ice froze its watchman at the top of the stair.
When the wraith broke apart, the ice fell from the watchman at the top of the stair. Hrongar can be buried at last.
Destroy the wraith that haunts the beacon
The beacon burns over the snowfields for the first time in twenty years.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snowpoint_beacon.out: At Fort Dunstad, the night watch sees the fire on Snowpoint and nearly sounds the alarm, out of old habit.
story.skycraft.q.pl_snowpoint_beacon.pit: Snowpoint Beacon's been dark for twenty years. Old Ulf says the watchman's still standing at the top, frozen. If you ever lit it again, they'd see it from Fort Dunstad.
The Solitude Lighthouse has gone dark three times this month, and a Company cutter has been lost on the rocks. The keeper's log says the great lens was stolen and taken to Brinewater Grotto.
The lamp-room is empty and the brass cradle broken. The keeper's log names Brinewater Grotto.
The lens was wrapped in sailcloth in the wreckers' chest. There was no sign of old Ulfgar but his hammer.
Recover the keeper's brass lens from Brinewater Grotto
By the Nine. I'll have it back in its cradle before dark. Ulfgar? ...No. I'll send a boat. I'll send two. Here, the Company's fifty, and a little more from me.
Bring the lens to Aulus Carvain at the Company office in Solitude
The light burns over the Karth again. Ships round the point safely, and somewhere in the dark the wreckers curse your name.
The lighthouse keeps going dark and ships keep dying. The Company's offering coin to anyone who can get that lamp burning again. Ask for Aulus at the warehouse.
story.skycraft.q.pl_south_shriekwind_bas: The widow Asta took her husband's ashes to the seventh alcove of South Shriekwind Bastion and has not returned. Sister Hilde of Falkreath fears the worst.
Clear the draugr from the long hall
Asta reached the seventh alcove. The urn sits in it, as she promised. She lies just beneath, her prayer beads in her hand.

She made it, then. She put him where he wanted to be, and lay down beside him. The seventh alcove was waiting for someone, they always said. I suppose it was waiting for two. Thank you. I'll pray for them both.
Bring Asta's prayer beads to Sister Hilde
Asta kept her promise. These were in her hand.
Sister Hilde hangs Asta's beads over the altar of the Hall of the Dead, and lights two candles each Sundas.

Asta took her husband's ashes up to South Shriekwind to lay them with his family. Five days ago. I told her it wasn't safe. She told me a promise is a promise. Please, go and see. If she's lost, bring back something of hers so I can pray over it.
Velmira Sarys, mistress of Southfringe Sanctum, has taken the dead of the Falkreath graveyard for some work in the sanctum's lower vault. Her ledger lists every name.
Put the stolen dead to rest
Velmira is dead. Her ledger lists every body she took from Falkreath, and a child called Sigrid among them.

Hrofar. Asgerd. The cooper's little one, Sigrid. I'll go down with a cart and Runil, and we'll bring them all home, every one. And I'll dig the holes myself, and I'll dig them deep. Thank you. The dead can't say it, so I will.
Bring the ledger of names to Ingrid in Falkreath
Velmira Sarys is dead. Here is her ledger of every grave she robbed.
Falkreath holds a second funeral for its stolen dead. The whole town comes, and even the Jarl.

The necromancer who robbed the Falkreath graves worked for a Dunmer woman at Southfringe Sanctum. She keeps a ledger of every body she's taken. Ingrid the gravedigger would give a great deal to read it, and to bring her dead home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.desc: A smuggler's map scrap from White Ridge Barrow says a stash of cut stalhrim was moved to the Stalhrim Source and buried under a slab marked with a Skaal hand, a dozen paces west of the black ice.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.o0.t: Find the slab marked with a Skaal hand, west of the black ice
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.o1.c: It belongs to the All-Maker. Take it back to the ice.
Then I will carry it to the source and say the words over it, and it will sleep again. The Skaal will remember this, outlander.
You know the words. Make something from it, for the village.
Hm. A spear for the young hunters, perhaps, worked with the proper prayers. The ice may accept that. It is better than a smuggler's purse.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.o1.r: I can feel it from here. It was cut without the words, and it is angry. What will you do with it?
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.o1.t: Decide what becomes of the stalhrim
I found a smuggler's slab of stalhrim.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.outr: Bjorn Cold-Hands' joke on Torvar ended in the snow. The stalhrim, at least, is out of smugglers' hands.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.pitc: Smugglers buried cut stalhrim near the Stalhrim Source and blamed the Skaal for watching it. A slab with a hand carved on it, they say. The Skaal would like that ice back where it belongs.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stalhrim_source.titl: The Slab with the Skaal Hand
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.de: A pilgrim from Dragon Bridge saw necromancers leave a bundle of bones at the steps of Meridia's statue. The Lady's light dims where it lies.
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.o0: Drive off the desecrators on the mountain
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.o1: Take up the black-corded bundle by the steps
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.o2: The bones burned white and were gone. The star in Meridia's hand blazed for a moment, as if in thanks, or in judgement.
Cast the bundle into the Lady's light
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.ou: Pilgrims climb Kilkreath again with their lanterns, and Helvi of Dragon Bridge leaves a new lantern by the plinth with your name scratched on it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_statue_to_meridia.pi: Some pilgrim's saying there are necromancers fouling Meridia's steps up on Kilkreath. Leaving bones about. The Lady doesn't take kindly to that, and neither do the pilgrims.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stendarrs_beacon.des: The Vigilants of Stendarr's Beacon were slaughtered by skeletons and a pale man from Redwater. The last of them asked that the fire be relit.
Drive the dead out of Stendarr's Beacon
I relit the beacon with the Vigilants' own flint. It burns again, and it can be seen from Riften.
Find the Beacon Log in the lower chest
story.skycraft.q.pl_stendarrs_beacon.out: Stendarr's Beacon burns again. The last Vigilant's log names Redwater, and the pale man who was proud of what he'd done.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stendarrs_beacon.pit: The Vigilants' beacon's gone dark for the first time in my life. Something came up the hill. The fire needs relighting, and whatever put it out needs putting out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.desc: Something in Stillborn Cave has been taking the midwives' charms from the cairn at its mouth, including Gudrun Warm-Hands' grandmother's antler cradle-charm.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.o0.jo: The spirit in the cave was rocking a nest of charms in her arms. When she faded, they spilled across the ice.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.o2.te: Tie the charm back on the cairn
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.outro: Gudrun ties a new red thread to the charm, and one more for Asta.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.pitch: The midwives' charms keep disappearing from the cairn at Stillborn Cave. Old Gudrun's grandmother's charm went this Frostfall. She's beside herself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stillborn_cave.title: The Cradle-Charm
story.skycraft.q.pl_stony_creek_cave.des: Nazira the Ford-Keeper's bandits rob Legion supply wagons at the Stony Creek ford and sell the loot to both sides of the war.
Clear the bandits from Stony Creek Cave
Nazira died wearing Legate Varo's cloak. Her accounts show she sold the Legion's arrows to Stormcloaks for two septims the dozen, and never once killed a legionary she did not have to.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stony_creek_cave.out: The Stony Creek ford is safe for wagons again. Both armies are quietly annoyed about it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_stony_creek_cave.pit: The Legion at the Eastmarch Imperial Camp is offering coin for the head of a Redguard bandit called Nazira, who robs their wagons at Stony Creek. Odd, a Stormcloak hold paying a Legion bounty. Coin's coin, though.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.desc: A hidden ledger at Sundered Towers shows that Vorald, a Silver-Blood factor, arms the Forsworn and then collects a reward for 'recovering' what they steal from Karthwasten.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.o2.j: Vorald, a factor of the Silver-Bloods, has been selling steel to the Forsworn and claiming rewards for returning the very silver they steal.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.o2.t: Find proof of who is arming the Forsworn
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.o3.r: Steel to the Forsworn, rewards from the Silver-Bloods, and us robbed in between. Vorald. Of course it's Vorald. Thonar won't hang him for it, but Thonar will hang him for not sharing. Either way, Karthwasten sleeps easier.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.o3.t: Show Vorald's ledger to Bergljot in Karthwasten
Look at what the Silver-Bloods' factor has been doing.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.outr: A week later, Vorald the factor was found at the bottom of the Karth. Nobody in Karthwasten asked how.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sundered_towers.pitc: The Forsworn at Sundered Towers have Markarth steel. Somebody's selling it to them. Find out who, and the miners of Karthwasten will owe you their lives, or at least their wages.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.de: The seal of Arkay over the inner door of Sunderstone Gorge has been pried loose and carried inside. Acolyte Sigvar went in after it. Sunder Grey-Hand walks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.o0: Enter the barrow at Sunderstone Gorge
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.o1: Put Sunder Grey-Hand back in his grave
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.o2: Sigvar's body lay beside the seal-stone, his hand still on it. He had nearly made it to the door.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.ou: Runil will have the seal-stone reset at the inner door, and Sigvar buried in the Falkreath yard with full rites.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.pi: Runil sent a young acolyte to bless the falls at Sunderstone Gorge. The boy found the barrow's seal broken and went in to set it right. He hasn't come back, and the water's still grey.
story.skycraft.q.pl_sunderstone_gorge.ti: Close the Door, and Close It Well
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.desc: Grelka, the fence at Swindler's Den, bought a sealed Legion dispatch case from deserters. She means to sell it to the Stormcloaks. The Legion camp near Rorikstead wants it back unopened.
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.o0.tex: Clear out the thieves of Swindler's Den
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.o2.tex: Take the Legion dispatch case from Grelka's strongbox
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.o3.jou: Captain Vell checked the seal twice before he believed it. He paid from his own purse, as he promised.
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.o3.tex: Return the case to the Whiterun Imperial Camp
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.outro: The Legion's dispatches reached Whiterun with their seal unbroken. Grelka's ledger has been closed for good.
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.pitch: The Legion lost a dispatch case and the fence at Swindler's Den has it, sitting on it till a Stormcloak comes along with coin. The captain at the Imperial camp will pay to see it home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_swindlers_den.title: The Sealed Case
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.desc: A great senche-tiger called Old Saffron escaped from Yusuf the beast-trader's cages on the Taneth quay and has taken to hunting near the shrine of Hircine north of the city. Yusuf will pay a hunter to end it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.o0.text: Go to the shrine of Hircine north of Taneth
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.o1.journal: Old Saffron died facing me, as a hunter's quarry should. Malik of the Hills, who watched from the rocks, said the Huntsman would be pleased. Yusuf will merely be relieved.
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.o1.text: Hunt Old Saffron at the dry well
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.outro: Malik of the Hills lays Old Saffron's skull on the Hircine stone, beside the lions. Yusuf the Tamer buys no more tigers.
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.pitch: Yusuf's tiger is out north of the walls, by the Hircine stones. Big as a horse, the colour of dates. The Hew's Bane hunters say she deserves a proper hunt, not poison. Yusuf just wants it over.
story.skycraft.q.pl_taneth.title: Old Saffron
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_atronach_stone.d: Thessaly Vane buried her soul gems and coin in a sealed pot a dozen paces south of the Atronach Stone, where the ground is warm and the snow never settles.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_atronach_stone.o: Search the warm, snowless ground south of the Atronach Stone
The pot held two soul gems, a purse, and a scrap of paper: 'If you are not me, you have earned it. If you are me, well done for escaping.'
Somewhere in Eastmarch, an adept is either very relieved or very cross.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_atronach_stone.p: A mage was robbed on the road by the Atronach Stone last month. Says she buried her soul gems before the Mistwatch lot caught her. Warm ground south of the Stone, she says. Snow never settles there.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.desc: Brynja's mother Ingrun dropped her wedding comb in the shallows beside the Lady Stone. Her father Ottar searched for it every spring for thirty years.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.o0.te: Row out to the Lady Stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.o1.jo: The comb was wedged between two stones under the water, right where a careless bride might drop it, and right where a searching husband might never think to look.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.o1.te: Search the shallows for Ingrun's comb
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.o2.re: Thirty years. Thirty springs he rowed out there. Oh, he'll be furious it was you and not him. And then he'll cry, and then he'll pretend he didn't. Thank you. I'll put it on Mother's stone, so she has it back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.o2.te: Bring the comb to Brynja at Half-Moon Mill
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.outro: Ottar the Wet rows out to the Lady Stone once more that year, this time with nothing to search for, and stays until the moons rise.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.pitch: My mother. She was wed at the Lady Stone and dropped her bone comb in the shallows there. Father swore he'd find it, every spring for thirty years. He never did. He's too old to row now, and I'm too busy to dive. If you're out on the lake... look, would you?
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lady_stone.title: A Comb in the Shallows
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.desc: A letter under the Lover Stone, from a Reachwoman named Aiwen to a Karthwasten miner's son named Leif, left her braided token behind for him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.o0.t: Take Aiwen's braided token from beneath the stone
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.o1.r: A Reach girl's token. So that's where he's been sneaking off to. He left two nights ago with his pick and a coil of rope, toward Blind Cliff Cave. If you're going that way... no. I won't ask. I'll keep this for him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.o1.t: Bring the token to Leif's mother, Bergljot, in Karthwasten
This was left for your son Leif.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.outr: Bergljot keeps the braided token on the shelf by her door, where Leif will see it when he comes home.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_lover_stone.pitc: There's a letter under the Lover Stone that's been there since the new moon. Meant for some lad in Karthwasten. Shame to let the rain have it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_ritual_stone.des: A necromancer called Moriva has been raising the dead buried around the Ritual Stone, sending grave dust to Fellglow Keep. She plans to raise them all at once.
Put down the risen dead around the Ritual Stone
Moriva is dead. Her grave-book names Fellglow Keep as the buyer of her grave dust.
Fellglow. Of course it leads back to Fellglow. I'll burn this book at the altar, and pray the stone's dead forgive us for being slow.
Bring Moriva's grave-book to Sister Hildrun
The dead at the Ritual Stone are quiet. This was the necromancer's.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_ritual_stone.out: The graves around the Ritual Stone are closed again. Sister Hildrun goes out once a month to sing over them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_ritual_stone.pit: Someone's raising the dead around the Ritual Stone. Sister Hildrun at the temple tried singing them back to sleep and nearly got killed for it. Put a stop to it, will you?
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_shadow_stone.des: A thief named Tova Quickstep buried an offering for the Shadow twelve paces from the stone toward Snow-Shod Farm, under a rock scratched with a crescent.
Under the crescent rock: a bundle of good picks and a small purse. The Shadow, it seems, is generous.
Dig under the crescent-scratched rock between the Shadow Stone and Snow-Shod Farm
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_shadow_stone.out: I found Tova Quickstep's offering to the Shadow. Shadows don't need gold, she said. She was right.
story.skycraft.q.pl_the_shadow_stone.pit: Thieves leave offerings at the Shadow Stone, everyone knows that. One of them buried a whole share. Whoever finds it keeps it, so the story goes.
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.desc: Tolvald went into the cave that now bears his name with his father's brass lantern. His mother in Riften still lights a lamp in her window every night. The Falmer have made his lantern into a god.
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.o1.tex: Defeat the Falmer who keep the lantern shrine
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.o2.jou: Tolvald's bones lay in a side passage by a pool of glowing mushrooms, facing the way he came in.
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.o2.tex: Take Tolvald's lantern from the shrine
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.outro: Tolvald's lantern is coming home to Riften. His mother can let her lamp go out at last.
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.pitch: Tolvald's mother still lights a lamp for him every night. If anyone could bring back something of his, even just that old lantern... it might let her blow the lamp out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_tolvalds_cave.title: A Light for Tolvald
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.desc: Three Stormcloak deserters have holed up at Traitor's Post with a stolen payroll. One of them is Bjorlam, son of Ingrid of Hollyfrost Farm.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.o0.tex: Confront the deserters at Traitor's Post
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.o1.jou: Bjorlam lay by the door with Kolgeir's axe in his back. He had been trying to leave. In his coat was a letter to his mother.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.o1.tex: Recover the payroll and search the cabin
Give her the letter and tell her the truth.
...Then he ran from something worse than war. That is my son. That is the boy I raised. Leave me the letter. I will read it until I can bear it.
Tell her he died fighting, cold and brave.
Cold and brave. Yes. His father died the same way. Thank you, stranger. I will tell the goat. She always liked him best.
Tell her the truth, and give her the strongbox too.
Four months' pay they never gave him, and you give it to me? The Palace will hang you for it. ...I'll hide it under the hearthstone. Nobody looks for coin under a widow's fire.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.o2.rep: I know that face. Every soldier who has passed this gate has worn it. Tell me. Tell me all of it, or tell me the part I can live with.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.o2.tex: Tell Ingrid at Hollyfrost Farm what became of her son
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.outro: There is a new stone on the ridge above Hollyfrost Farm, facing the cabin on the hill.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.pitch: The quartermaster in Windhelm lost a payroll and three soldiers. There's smoke at Traitor's Post. You do the sums. And mind, one of them's Ingrid of Hollyfrost's boy.
story.skycraft.q.pl_traitors_post.title: The Pact of the Three
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.desc: Bandits at Treva's Watch have claimed a 'tithe' on the river country, taking nirnroot from Sarethi Farm and breaking the arm of the farm's hand. Their leader calls herself Saltcheek.
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.o1.jour: Saltcheek wore a grey bear-cloak and fought like someone defending her inheritance. Maybe she was. It didn't help her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.o1.text: End Hjolfrid Saltcheek's claim on the river country
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.outro: The river tithe is cancelled. Avrusa Sarethi's nirnroot can sing in peace again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.pitch: Avrusa Sarethi's lost a dozen nirnroot to the bandits at Treva's Watch, and her hand Brelas got his arm broken for his trouble. Their chief's called Saltcheek. She'd pay well to see her gone.
story.skycraft.q.pl_trevas_watch.title: The River Tithe
Hadring Two-Coins, chief of the Uttering Hills Cave bandits, keeps a stolen survey of the Mzulft approaches in his chest. Its owner, Bertrand Vanne, waits at Kynesgrove.
The book was in Hadring's chest, wrapped in a pair of good Breton boots.
My survey! And, oh, my boots, they kept my boots in it. You cannot imagine. Here, take this for your trouble. I must go back over the route to Mzulft at once. Livia is somewhere at the end of it.
Return the survey to Bertrand Vanne in Kynesgrove
Bertrand Vanne is redrawing the road to Mzulft by the Braidwood Inn's fire.
Hadring Two-Coins at Uttering Hills Cave took a Breton scholar's book and boots and sent him off barefoot. The poor fellow's at the Braidwood Inn in Kynesgrove now, still shivering.
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.desc: Ulvo Nerano's assistant dropped a satchel of eleven tomb rubbings in the long hall of Vahlok's Tomb when the dead woke. The rubbings describe the Jailor's oath to guard an unnamed prisoner.
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.o1.text: Find the satchel by the dragon brazier in the long hall
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.o2.repl: Scorched is fine. Scorched is evidence of authenticity. Oh, look at this: they never name the prisoner, not once, in eleven panels. Do you know how hard it is to write that much about someone without naming them? Somebody was very frightened.
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.o2.text: Bring the rubbings to Ulvo Nerano at Tel Mithryn
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.outro: Ulvo Nerano has pinned the rubbings to his wall and is writing a paper. He says it will make Neloth jealous. Neloth has not noticed.
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.pitch: That scholar at Tel Mithryn, Ulvo Nerano, lost a satchel of rubbings in Vahlok's Tomb. His assistant ran out without his eyebrows. Nerano pays well, if you can stand him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_vahloks_tomb.title: Eleven Rubbings
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.desc: Ulfgar the Lamp-Keeper of Old Hroldan asked me to bring the soldier Ketil's shield back from the barrow of Valthume so his ghost can rest.
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.o2.journal: Among the warden's hoard of shields was a round one with a faded hawk. It felt lighter than it should have.
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.o3.reply: The hawk. Grandmother described it exactly. I'll hang it over the bed tonight, and tomorrow, for the first time in four hundred years, I'll let the lamp go out. Thank you. And thank you from him, I expect.
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.o3.text: Bring Ketil's shield to Ulfgar at Old Hroldan
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.outro: The lamp in the upstairs room at Old Hroldan has gone out. The shutters still rattle sometimes, but Ulfgar says that is only the wind now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.pitch: Not the Emperor, whatever the carters say. A soldier called Ketil, who died in that room when Hjalti took the village. His shield went into Valthume with the dead of both sides, and he's walked the floor looking for it ever since. My family's kept his lamp lit four hundred years. I'd like to be the one who lets it go out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_valthume.title: A Shield for the Upstairs Room
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.desc: Hulda of Dragon Bridge begs for news of her son Eirik, who climbed to the barrow of Volskygge after treasure nine days ago.
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.o0.text: Climb to Volskygge and search for Eirik
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.o1.text: Destroy Hrokk Iron-Jaw, warden of the barrow
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.o2.journal: Eirik died behind his barricade with his torch burned out. His mother's letter was still in his pack, unread.
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.o3.reply: ...His father's axe. It was always too heavy for him. Thank you for not leaving him up there in the dark. I'll cook supper tonight anyway. Habit. Someone should eat it.
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.o3.text: Bring Eirik's axe home to Hulda
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.outro: Hulda hangs the axe over her hearth. She still watches the road in the evenings, but now she watches the hills where Ragnvald is.
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.pitch: My Eirik. My youngest. He went up to Volskygge, the barrow on the mountain, after treasure, with his father's axe. That was nine days ago. His brother's gone to the war and his father's gone to the sea. Please. I can't lose them all.
story.skycraft.q.pl_volskygge.title: The Unburied Brother
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.desc: Miners at Whistling Mine broke into an ice pocket, and the ice wraiths inside have frozen two men at the ore face. The foreman offers a month's ore money.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.o0.te: Clear the ice wraiths from the lower gallery
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.o1.jo: The whistling has stopped. Now it is only the wind again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.o1.te: Destroy the great wraith in the ice pocket
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.outro: The miners go back to work, singing loudly, in case anything else down there was listening.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.pitch: Whistling Mine's shut. Ice wraiths in the lower gallery. Skuli the foreman's offering a month of ore money to anyone who clears them out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whistling_mine.title: What Whistles in the Dark
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.de: Bandits at White River Watch have been stealing Honningbrew's mead casks at the river ford. Eirik Mead-Hand wants their chief Kolskegg stopped and the store-room key brought back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.o0: Clear the bandits from White River Watch
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.o1: Kolskegg fought like a drunk, which is to say badly and with great enthusiasm. His store-room key is mine.
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.o2: Ha! I'll send a cart at dawn. What's left of the mead is yours to drink, but I'd sooner you took coin. Honningbrew doesn't forget its friends.
Bring the store-room key to Eirik at Honningbrew Meadery
Kolskegg's key. Your mead's in his store-room.
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.ou: Honningbrew's carts cross the ford safely again. Eirik has started drawing smiling faces on the casks.
story.skycraft.q.pl_white_river_watch.pi: Every cask that leaves this meadery gets stolen at the ford and carried off to White River Watch. Their chief, Kolskegg, keeps what he doesn't sell in a locked store-room. Get me his key and I'll make it worth your while.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whitewatch_tower.des: Bandits under Red Ingjald have turned Whitewatch Tower into a toll-gate on the north road, and keep a tally of every purse they empty.
Clear the bandits from Whitewatch Tower
Red Ingjald is dead. Whitewatch Tower watches the road again, for whoever comes next.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whitewatch_tower.out: The red shields of Whitewatch Tower are down. The north road is safe, for now.
story.skycraft.q.pl_whitewatch_tower.pit: Whitewatch Tower's bandits paint their shields red and rob anyone on the north road. Loreius lost farmhands to them. There's coin in it for whoever pulls down their red shields.
story.skycraft.q.pl_widows_watch_ruins.d: A verse carved into the stair at Widow's Watch asks that the widow's whalebone ring be carried down to the sea at the Orphan's Tear, so that she may stop keeping her lantern lit.
story.skycraft.q.pl_widows_watch_ruins.o: The ring lay on the top step, beside a lantern that burns without oil.
Find the widow's whalebone ring at the top of the tower
The ring sank without a sound. Behind me, on the headland, the green light went out.
Give the ring to the sea at the Orphan's Tear
The fishermen say Widow's Watch is dark now on foggy nights. Some of them miss the light.
story.skycraft.q.pl_widows_watch_ruins.p: There's a green light at the top of Widow's Watch. Old Brandr says she's waiting for her ring to go back to the sea. Strange errand, but it'd be a kindness.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.desc: Nirvel Twice-Sworn sells useless 'dream-ward' sachets to the sleepless folk of Dawnstar, and keeps his takings in Windward Ruins.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.o0.te: Confront Nirvel Twice-Sworn in Windward Ruins
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.o2.re: Seven hundred septims for a bag of salt and weeds. I'll see every family gets theirs back. Gods know we can't buy a good night's sleep with it, but we can buy bread.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.o2.te: Bring the money to Thyra Gull-Wife in Dawnstar
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.o2.to: Here's what Nirvel took from Dawnstar.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.outro: Dawnstar still dreams of the black door. But at least now it dreams with its coin back.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.pitch: That charm-seller who's been fleecing Dawnstar? He's holed up in Windward Ruins with a pack of thugs. Thyra Gull-Wife's been asking around about him.
story.skycraft.q.pl_windward_ruins.title: Charms Against the Dark
story.skycraft.q.pl_witchmist_grove.desc: Agnar Steam-Lodge's daughter Tova followed the lights of Witchmist Grove into the mist. Something tall and pale sings among the wisps with her voice.
story.skycraft.q.pl_witchmist_grove.o0.t: Disperse the wisps over the far pool
story.skycraft.q.pl_witchmist_grove.o2.j: Tova was asleep in a hollow under the far tree, cold but breathing, with her door-bell clutched in her fist. When she woke she asked where the pretty lady had gone. I told her the lady had gone home. I carried her to the road, and Agnar ran the rest of the way to meet us.
story.skycraft.q.pl_witchmist_grove.outr: Agnar has pulled down his lodge. Tova kept the bell. It has stopped ringing on its own.
story.skycraft.q.pl_witchmist_grove.pitc: Agnar the hunter built a lodge in Witchmist Grove, and now his little girl's gone into the mist. He sits by the Kynesgrove road asking every passer-by to go in. Nobody does.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wolfskull_cave.desc: Brother Ulvarr's ritual notes describe a choir of necromancers at Wolfskull Cave preparing to call on the Wolf Queen's name with the dead stolen from Solitude's Hall of the Dead.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wolfskull_cave.o1.jo: Ulvarr wore a circlet of wolf teeth for the ritual. It is cold as a grave. The green fire has gone out.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wolfskull_cave.outro: The priests of Arkay in Solitude rebury the stolen dead with their names, and no green light burns over Wolfskull for the rest of the year.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wolfskull_cave.pitch: Green fire over Wolfskull Cave again, and three graves dug up in the Hall of the Dead. Somebody's playing at the Wolf Queen's old games. Somebody ought to stop the game.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wolfskull_cave.title: The Wolf Queen's Choir
story.skycraft.q.pl_wreck_of_the_brineha: The wrecked Brinehammer carried three months of Legion pay in barrels marked with a red knot. Salvagers led by Ulfgar Wet-Boots mean to take it before the Legion knows.
Deal with Ulfgar Wet-Boots and his salvagers
Recover the red-knotted strongbox from the flooded hold
Quartermaster Ostorian counted every coin twice, then a third time, then cried a little.
Return the pay to the Pale Imperial Camp
The camp is paid, and for one night the coast echoes with Legion drinking songs.
The Legion lads at the coast camp haven't been paid in months, and there's a crew of divers working the Brinehammer wreck. You do the arithmetic.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wreck_of_the_pride_o: A Dunmer girl's diary from the wreck of the Pride of Tel Vos tells of her father's ancestor-urn, hidden in the captain's cabin. Her brother Dravyn still lives in Winterhold.
The urn is sealed and whole, wrapped in a child's shawl.
Find the urn in the captain's chest with the spiral lock
That shawl was Nivera's. She was nine. She wrapped it herself, on a sinking ship, so Father would not be cold. ...Forgive me. Give me a moment.
Bring the urn to Dravyn Dalvilu in Winterhold
I found your father's urn on the Pride of Tel Vos.
Sell them for the refugees of Winterhold
Then the Telvanni will feed the people they nearly drowned. That is a justice even Azura would smile at. Take a share for yourself, I insist.
Leave them in the sea where they belong
Yes. Let the sea keep the Master's treasure, as it kept so much of ours. I would not want to profit from that ship.
Master Dren's gems. He was paid in full to carry us, and he would have thrown us overboard to save the weight. What would you have me do with them?
Tell Dravyn what else was aboard
The purser hid Telvanni soul gems in the hold.
Dravyn sets the urn in the little shrine of his house. On Morndas he takes it to the Shrine of Azura, so that his father may see the dawn.
Looters are picking over the Pride of Tel Vos again. The Dunmer in town hate it. One of them, Dravyn, says his family's ancestor-urn is still aboard.
story.skycraft.q.pl_wreck_of_the_striden: Fennick, the cook of the Strident Squall, buried his life's savings in the shingle below the big black rock, thirty paces inland from the wreck's bow, before he swam for his life.
Fennick's sea-chest: thirty years of a cook's wages and a silver ring meant for his sister Ottilie in Anvil.
Dig below the big black rock, inland of the bow
Nobody in Raven Rock remembers a cook called Fennick coming ashore. Somewhere in Anvil, Ottilie is still waiting for her little house by the lighthouse.
Everyone went to the Strident Squall for the Company's strongbox. Nobody looked for the cook's chest. Old Fennick never trusted a box he didn't bury himself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.desc: Ragnhild Keel-Wright of Windhelm believes the prow carving from Yngol's ship can bless a new vessel against the Sea of Ghosts. She asks for it to be brought from Yngol Barrow.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o0.jour: The sea-wolf's head hung above Yngol's empty bier. Its oak was still warm, as if from sun on a deck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o0.text: Recover the sea-wolf carving from Yngol Barrow
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.c0.l: Touch it to the keel, then I'll return it
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.c0.r: Yes. A blessing borrowed, not stolen. Bring it back to him when the keel is laid. My sons will know whose luck they sail with.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.c1.l: Keep it. Your sons need it more than he does
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.c1.r: Perhaps. The dead have the sea already. Let the living have a little of its mercy. I'll set it in the prow myself.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.repl: You took it from his tomb? I asked for it, I know. But now that it's here, it feels like stealing from the dead. What should I do?
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.text: Bring the carving to Ragnhild in Windhelm
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.o1.topi: I have the sea-wolf from Yngol's ship.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.outro: Ragnhild's ship is launched in Sun's Height. She names it Yngol's Luck.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.pitch: There's a shipwright in Windhelm who's lost a husband to the sea. She wants something from Yngol Barrow to bless her sons' new boat. Strange request. Grieving folk make them.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngol_barrow.title: The Sea-Wolf's Blessing
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.desc: Ingrith, a Dawnstar fisherwoman, rowed out to Yngvild in a waking dream. Her sister Thyra fears she was called by whatever lives on the island.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.o1.journal: The Host of Yngvild is dead. Ingrith was among his 'bridesmaids'. She did not suffer long.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.o3.reply: ...She always said she'd be buried at sea. Now she'll be buried with Father, on the hill. Take the sword. My husband would have wanted it swung at something worse than herring.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.o3.text: Bring the ring to Thyra Gull-Wife in Dawnstar
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.o3.topic: I'm sorry. This is all that was left of Ingrith.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.outro: Thyra buries the ring beside her father. The lights on Yngvild do not burn again.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.pitch: Thyra Gull-Wife's sister rowed out to Yngvild in the middle of the night. Talking about a wedding. Thyra's offering everything she has to whoever goes after her.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yngvild.title: The Wedding on the Island
story.skycraft.q.pl_yorgrim_overlook.des: Saervi the Fox, a smuggler, hid her brandy money near Yorgrim Overlook under a stone marked with a fox.
Under the fox-scratched stone: a leather purse and a silver ring.
Find the fox-marked stone under the leaning pine
story.skycraft.q.pl_yorgrim_overlook.out: You do not spend it all on mead at Nightgate Inn. Most of it, perhaps.
story.skycraft.q.pl_yorgrim_overlook.pit: There was a smuggler, Saervi, used Yorgrim Overlook as a lookout. Legion caught her last spring. Her purse, they never found.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.desc: The Root Hist of Black Marsh is blighted and robbed by sap-thieves. Deeja-Sleeps of Stormhold wants pure sap saved before the tree sickens.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o0.text: Find the Root Hist in the deep marsh
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o1.text: Drive off the sap-thieves and the blighted beasts
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o2.text: Gather pure sap from the Root Hist
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o3.reply: The Hist will heal. And it will remember you. When an Argonian says that, walker, it is not a small thing.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.o3.topic: Pure sap from the Root Hist.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.pitch: A blight. It creeps up the roots of the Root Hist in the deep marsh, and sap-thieves bleed the trees while they are weak. Go to the Root Hist. Bring back sap that is still pure.
story.skycraft.q.prov_bm_hist.title: The Hist Remembers
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.desc: An Oblivion gate has opened above Kvatch, echoing the Crisis that once burned the city. Savlian Matius of the city watch needs someone to go through it and close it.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o0.text: Go to the Oblivion gate above Kvatch
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o1.text: Kill the dremora guarding the gate
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o3.text: Climb the Great Sigil Tower and defeat the Sigil Keeper
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o4.text: Take the Sigil Stone from its flame to close the gate
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.repl: Closed. Just like the Hero of Kvatch did it, two hundred years ago. Kvatch owes you, and Kvatch pays its debts.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.text: Bring the Sigil Stone to Savlian Matius
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.o5.topi: The gate is closed. Here's what held it open.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.pitch: A gate. In the hills. Two hundred years after the Crisis, an Oblivion gate is open again above Kvatch. Somebody has to close it before what's behind it comes through.
story.skycraft.q.prov_cyr_kvatch.title: Echoes of Kvatch
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.desc: Dark spirits haunt the Temple of the Two Moons. Moon-Priest Azadhi asked me to cleanse it by moonlight and carry word to the Mane.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o0.text: Travel to the Temple of the Two Moons
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o1.text: Wait for the moons to rise
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.reply: The Mane felt it, the moment the light returned. You are not of the moons, and yet you served them. Elsweyr remembers its friends.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.text: Present the Lattice offering to the Mane in Riverhold
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.o4.topic: The moons dance again over the temple.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.pitch: The Temple of the Two Moons has been desecrated by the Dro-m'Athra, the lost spirits. The Lunar Lattice cannot hold the moons' light while they haunt it. Cleanse the temple by night, when the moons can see you.
story.skycraft.q.prov_els_moons.title: Moons and Mane
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.d: Yasmin at-Sentinel offered to test me in the way of the Yokudan sword-singers: claim an ancestral blade from the Ra Gada tomb and win a duel at Hel Ra Citadel.
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.o: Travel to the Tomb of the Ra Gada
Lay the tomb's restless guardians to rest
Defeat the rival ansei in a duel
Then your blade sang, and you heard it. Keep it. A shehai is never given, only earned, and you have earned this one.
How does one become a sword-singer?
story.skycraft.q.prov_ham_sword_singer.p: You don't, not in one lifetime. But you can earn a shehai. Go to the tomb of the Ra Gada, the first warriors who sailed from Yokuda. Take an ancestor's blade, if its guardians let you. Then a rival waits at Hel Ra.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.desc: King Gurak gro-Morkul of Orsinium tests outsiders who would be friends of the Orcs: feed the forges, then kill the ogre of Wrothgar Peak.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o0.tex: Bring ten iron ingots for Orsinium's forges
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o3.tex: Kill the ogre of Wrothgar Peak
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o4.rep: Then the clans will sing of a pink-skin who climbed Wrothgar. Badly, but they'll sing. Orsinium's gates are open to you, blood-kin.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.o4.tex: Bring the ogre's tusk to King Gurak
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.pitch: Iron, for the forges. And a monster dead, for the clans to see. Bring ten bars of iron to the stronghold forge, then climb Wrothgar Peak and kill the ogre that eats our goats.
story.skycraft.q.prov_hr_orsinium.title: Orsinium Rising
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.de: Something is stirring in Red Mountain again. The Temple of the Tribunal wants the Great Houses' cooperation and someone to go into the heart of the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o0: Help costs. But a quiet mountain is good for trade. Hlaalu will open the roads. Tell the Temple we expect a discount on blessings.
Win House Hlaalu's support in Balmora
The Temple asks for Hlaalu's help on Red Mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o1: Redoran has been on Red Mountain for a thousand years. Go through the Ghostfence; our wardens will hold the gate behind you.
Win House Redoran's support in Ald'ruhn
The Temple needs Redoran on Red Mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o3: Fight through the ash creatures of Red Mountain
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.o5: Quiet for now. The Temple will keep this shard where no Sleeper can find it. You have the gratitude of the Tribunal, and of all three Houses, which is rarer.
Bring the shard to Tharen Veloth in Vivec
story.skycraft.q.prov_mw_red_mountain.pi: Red Mountain. Ash storms, and in the storms, voices. Sleepers walk out of the ash in Balmora and Ald'ruhn. The Great Houses argue; the Temple must act. Speak with Hlaalu and Redoran, and then go to the mountain.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.desc: A magister of Alinor says that recovering a stolen shard of the Crystal Tower might earn the attention of the Psijic Order, whose island of Artaeum appears only to those it chooses.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o3.text: Sail to Artaeum, which is suddenly on the horizon
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.repl: And so Artaeum let you land. Stay a while. The Order teaches nothing quickly.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.text: Give the shard to Celinar of the Psijic Order
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.o4.topi: I've brought the Crystal Tower's shard.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.offer: I've heard Artaeum can't be found.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.pitch: It can't. Unless the Psijic Order wants you. Maormer raiders stole a shard of the Crystal Tower; return it, and perhaps the Order will notice you. Perhaps.
story.skycraft.q.prov_sum_psijic.title: Isle of the Psijics
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.desc: Spinner Aerfin of Elden Root wants me to live by the Green Pact, the Bosmer covenant with their forest, and bring a graht-oak seed out of the thorn-choked Green Heart.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o0.t: Hunt three beasts, as the Pact allows
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o4.r: Then the Pact is in you, whatever your ears look like. We'll plant it in Falinesti's old ground. One day it'll walk.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.o4.t: Bring the seed to Spinner Aerfin
The Wilderking gave me the seed.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.offe: Tell me about the Green Pact.
story.skycraft.q.prov_vw_green_pact.pitc: Better: live it. Hunt as we hunt; take only flesh. Then go to the Green Heart, where thorns choke the old trees. The Wilderking guards a seed there. If the Pact is in you, he'll give it.
story.skycraft.q.ps_breaches_in_time.des: Ritemaster Iachesis sent me to close breaches in time that have opened on Summerset and Auridon. Daedra are crawling through them.
Find the time breach outside Firsthold
Inside the breach, a moment kept repeating: the same gull, diving into the same wave, over and over. When the last Dremora fell, the gull finally caught its fish.
Drive back the Daedra pouring through the breach
Find the second breach outside Alinor
Valzhar laughed as he died. He said the breach was not his doing, only his invitation.
Slay the Dremora holding the breach open
Collect a shard of the collapsed breach
