The widow's letter tells it plainly. Dravil poisoned his brother's wife for her dowry, and Ulvon killed him for it. Dravil wants Ulvon's bones gone because they are what keeps him shut in.
Othrelas Guardian
Open Ulvon's urn
Return to the Sandas tomb after dark
Dravil came at me with every lie he had left. When he broke, the tomb went quiet in a way it had not been for sixty years.
Sandas Bonewalker
Put Dravil's shade down for good
Read him the widow's letter.
So the murderer was the one asking for justice. Ulvon gets a lamp at our shrine from now on, and Dravil gets none.
Tell him Dravil found peace, and burn the letter.
Peace. Good. Then I can mourn him properly. Thank you, sera.
Tell me. I have been afraid of him for a month. I would rather know why.
Tell Ervyn what his grandsire was
Your grandsire won't visit again. But you should know what he wanted.
Your grandsire visits? Isn't he dead?
Two brothers, one tomb's worth of grudges. The Sandas house sleeps now, and Ervyn with it.

Very. Dravil Sandas, dead these sixty years. He comes in my sleep and tells me he was murdered, and that I must set it right before he can rest. I am a clerk, sera, not a hero. Would you go to our tomb and hear him out?
What the Dead Say
story.skycraft.q.side_pya_the_serpents_h: Gwaelin Saltbelly of Woodhearth says a sea serpent ridden by a Maormer herald has sunk seven fishing boats this season.
Sail south to the herald's coast on Pyandonea
Survive Vorrhaal the Old Coil
Woodhearth sawdust in the empty nests. Someone in my own harbor has been stealing serpent eggs, and the herald came to take them back.
Find the serpent rookery in the cove
Coil-Guard
Fight the herald's guard
Kill Iriel Wave-Rider
Take the egg Iriel recovered from Woodhearth
Hang the harbor master's name in the market and send the egg home.
Both. Today. Let the sea see we can be honest too.
Raise it. Woodhearth could use a guardian of its own.
A serpent of our own... The elders will howl. I like it.
The harbor master's crates. He swore they were Elsweyr melons. By the Pact, we'd have eaten a serpent egg if we'd known. Hungry or not, a stolen egg is a stolen child.
Bring the egg back to Gwaelin
This egg came from Woodhearth's harbor. Your people stole them first.
The sea is eating your boats?
The boats of Woodhearth fish again, and nobody in the harbor will touch a crate of 'melons'.

A serpent the length of the harbor wall, with a Maormer riding on its neck like a stable-boy on a pony. Seven boats this season. Our hunters say kill the rider and the beast goes home. Our hunters are very hungry. So are we. Sail south and kill the rider.
Old Coil's Scale
Wave-Rider's Harness
The Serpent's Herald
story.skycraft.q.side_pya_through_the_mi: Lieutenant Calaenor of Alinor wants the Maormer mist-lantern, which lets ships pass through the fog that hides Pyandonea.
Sail through the mist wall to Pyandonea
Fight the Maormer raiders on the beach
Take the mist-lantern from its coral post
Here. Do what you will with it.
Adequate work. The fleet sails within the season. You may go.
I broke it on the way back. The mist stays.
You... broke it. How regrettable. Take your fee and leave my sight before I find a law you've broken.
Ancient history, embellished by pirates. The lantern, please.
Return to Lieutenant Calaenor in Alinor
I have the lantern. The Tide-Singer told me why the mist exists.
I have seen the hidden coast of Pyandonea, and whether anyone else will depends on what I did with a blue glass lantern.

The Maormer hide their isles behind a wall of mist that no Altmer navigator has pierced in an age. Our agents report the Tide-Singers keep a lantern that parts it. Bring it to me, and the Sea Vipers will never again strike our coast from hiding. You will be paid as befits a minor instrument of Alinor's will.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_ashes_on_the_i: Ilvesi Dravyne of Winterhold asked me to recover her grandmother's ash-urn from the wreck of the Velothi Promise in Pilgrim's Trench.
Go to the wreck in Pilgrim's Trench
Drowned Pilgrim
Lay the drowned passengers to rest
Find the Dravyne urn in the hold
Captain Dren barred the hold from outside and took the only boat. The ice took him a few strokes from the wreck. He didn't stay at the wheel; he left everyone to die.
Take the ship's log from the captain's cabin
Silence Captain Dren's ghost
Ancestors be thanked. I will make her a shrine by the hearth. Did you learn how the ship was lost? The survivors never spoke of it.
Bring the urn to Ilvesi Dravyne
Your grandmother, Ilvesi.
He locked the hold and fled in the only boat.
Then the families of Winterhold will hear it, and his name will be cursed at every ash-shrine in Skyrim. That is justice of a kind.
The ice took them all. No one could have saved them.
Then it was the will of the sea. I can live with that. Perhaps it is better.
Tell me plainly.
Tell Ilvesi what the log says
The captain's log tells the story.
You seem troubled, serjo.
Ilmeni Dravyne's urn sits by her granddaughter's hearth in Winterhold. The Velothi Promise is sinking back under the ice.

Forty years ago the Velothi Promise ran aground in the trench below the ice, full of refugees from Morrowind. My grandmother's ashes were aboard, in the hold with the living. The ice shifted this winter, and the wreck shows again. I would have her back, and in a proper shrine.
Ashen Wake
Ashes on the Ice
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_coldveins_merc: In the snow outside Windhelm I found a frozen beggar, bled by a vampire and then carefully tended. The blanket came from the Grey Quarter's healer.

A man lies frozen under a thin drift, wrapped in a Grey Quarter blanket. Two small wounds on his throat have been neatly cleaned and bandaged. Whoever fed on him tended him afterward, and folded his hands.

He was dying already. Lung-rot. The Lady gave him a warm bed and a gentle end, which is more than this city ever gave him. You would rather he coughed his last in an alley? Go and see her, then. The old prison in the marshes south-west of here, past Mixwater Mill.
Ask the Grey Quarter healer about the blanket
This blanket is yours. The man wrapped in it was drained by a vampire.
Find the Lady's rest at the abandoned prison
Beside each name in Coldvein's book, the healer had written a diagnosis. Half of them were dockworkers, hale and strong. Nerasa had been sending her the healthy ones too.
Coldvein Thrall
Read the guest book by the door
Kill Lady Vigdis Coldvein
The Grey Quarter will judge you. I'll give them the book.
Then I'll stand there and let them. It's fair.
Burn the book. Spend the rest of your life healing for free.
Every day. Every patient. I swear it on my mother's ashes.
She said the strong ones lasted longer. That she could make them comfortable for weeks instead of days. She promised me... it doesn't matter what she promised. What will you do with me?
Confront Nerasa with the guest book
You sent her healthy men. It's in her book, in your hand.
The old prison is cold and empty again. In the Grey Quarter, nobody speaks of the Lady's rest.
Coldvein's Last Kiss
Coldvein's Mercy
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_ansilvund: Clear the necromancer crew at Ansilvund.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_cragslane: Clear the outlaws in Cragslane Cavern.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Shut down the wolf-pits in Cragslane Cavern.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_cragwallo: Clear the conjurers in Cragwallow Slope.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Recover the copper stills from Cragwallow Slope.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_cronvangr: Clear the spider nests in Cronvangr Cave.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Burn the web-nests in Cronvangr Cave.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_fort_amol: Clear the warlock garrison at Fort Amol.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Reclaim the pitch-casks at Fort Amol.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_gallows_c: Clear the outer hall of Gallows Rock.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Reclaim the timber tools from Gallows Rock.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_lost_knif: Clear the bandits in Lost Knife Hideout.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Recover the winter pelts from Lost Knife Hideout.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_east_morvunska: Defeat Haldor the Cinder-Tongue at Morvunskar.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.

story.skycraft.q.side_sky_salt_between_h: Ingrith Arnleif of Dragon Bridge says the Kolfinn family burned her timber, the latest blow in a twenty-year feud. She wants proof.
We didn't. But I'll not weep for it. Twenty winters ago their boys threw my Torvar off this bridge, and the river never gave him back. Ask them about that.
Ask Old Kolfinn about the fire
Did your family burn the Arnleif timber?
Search the riverbank below the burned woodpile
Follow the pitch-stained tracks to Pinemoon Cave
Saltcutter Smuggler
Fight off the smugglers in Pinemoon Cave
With Eldra dead, her lieutenant surrendered. He was Torvar Kolfinn, the boy who drowned twenty years ago. He burned the timber to keep the feud alive.
Kill Eldra Saltcutter
Both families should hear it. Today.
Aye. Let them all hear it. Maybe we can stop being fools together.
It's your family. You decide who hears it.
Then I'll go up to that cave myself. After that, we'll see.
Alive. And he let me spit at the Arnleifs every day for twenty years, so nobody would look at the water. My boy.
Tell Old Kolfinn his son is alive
Torvar is alive. He's been running smugglers past this bridge for twenty years.
Then who... No. Torvar? I was twelve. I cried for him. Gods, I cried for that boy.
Report to Ingrith Arnleif
The Kolfinns didn't burn your timber.
What happened to your woodpile?
Dragon Bridge has gone quiet, the way a house does after a long shouting match. The smugglers' boats no longer pass at night.
Somebody burned our seasoned timber, a whole winter's work. Everybody on this bridge knows it was the Kolfinns. Twenty years they've hated us. Find me proof, and the Jarl's reeve can deal with them.
Feudbreaker
Salt Between Houses
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_custodians: Corvin Vale, a Breton tinkerer at Nightgate Inn, woke a Dwemer centurion in Raldbthar. It walked out of the ruin and is crossing the Pale.
Find the centurion's trail near Loreius Farm
Destroy the machines trailing behind it
Ah. Well. There was a small brass key in a niche by its pedestal. I took it as a keepsake. You don't think it wants...? Oh. Oh dear. Please take it. Take it far away from me.
Ask Corvin why the machine is walking toward him
It isn't going to the farm, Corvin. It's coming for you.
Carry the key back to Raldbthar
The Custodian didn't want its key back. It wanted the thief, and to its mind anyone carrying the key was the thief.
Return the key to its niche beside the empty pedestal
I will never touch a Dwemer niche again. Probably. Here, take this. I made it from a centurion's spare knuckle. It seemed appropriate.
Your keepsake nearly flattened a farm. The key's back where it belongs.
The Custodian of Raldbthar lies in pieces at its post. Corvin swears he has given up Dwemer ruins for the study of moss.

I woke a Dwemer centurion in Raldbthar. Only for a moment! It was meant to recite its maintenance logs. Instead it walked out of the ruin, and now it is walking, very slowly, toward Loreius Farm, flattening whatever is in its path. I would very much like it to stop.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_false_beac: A watch-log near the Solitude lighthouse recorded a lantern burning where no lantern should be, on the headland above Broken Oar Grotto.

A lighthouse watch-log lies open on a rock, its pages flapping. The last three entries read the same: 'Lantern seen burning on the Broken Oar headland. No light should burn there. Reported to O.' The ink smells fresh.

That's my log! My boy Hakon keeps the night watch. Lights on Broken Oar, three nights? He never said a word to me. Two ships have gone on those rocks this season. Gods. Go and look, will you? I can't leave the oil.
Ask the lighthouse keeper about the log
Someone's been logging a false light on the Broken Oar headland.
Above Broken Oar Grotto a wrecker's lantern swung like a harbor light. The man holding it called himself Hakon.
Watch the Broken Oar headland after dark
Wrecker
Fight the wreckers in Broken Oar Grotto
Gunnhild's crew lured ships onto the rocks and sold the salvage to the smugglers of Haafingar. Hakon ran when she fell.
Kill Gunnhild Falsebeacon
Take the wrecker's lantern
He ran. If he comes back, it's for you to judge him.
Then I'll leave the door unbarred. And the lighthouse lit. He'll know which light is mine.
The Solitude guard should know his face.
...Aye. Two ships. Men drowned. I'll tell them myself.
Hakon's mark. I taught him to scratch it on his tools. He kept my lamp burning with one hand and that one with the other. Where is he?
Show Olfrid the lantern
This is the false beacon. There's an H scratched in the brass.
Only one light burns on the Haafingar coast at night now, and it is Olfrid's.
Lampwarden's Bow
The False Beacon
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_fellhammer: Sigrun of Winterhold says the dead garrison of Fort Fellhammer answers a roll call every night, and her father Asgeir's name is always called and never answered.
Be at Fort Fellhammer when night falls
Fellhammer Revenant
Put down the revenants of the garrison
The last real entry in the roll, in Hafgrim's hand: 'Six deserters sealed in the lower mine. Charges set. Let the mountain judge them.' Asgeir was the first name.
Take the garrison roll book from the commander's table
Behind the rubble I found six skeletons huddled together, and a Legion badge with Asgeir's name. They hadn't deserted. Their letters home were tucked in their boots, asking for leave that never came.
Search the collapsed mine behind the fort
Destroy Commander Hafgrim's shade
Strike his name from the roll. He's off duty now.
Struck. Let him rest. Let all six of them rest.
Write 'present' beside his name.
Present. He was always where he said he'd be. Thank you.
Sealed in. By his own commander. And for twenty years Hafgrim's ghost kept calling him absent, as if that made it his fault.
Bring Sigrun the garrison roll
Your father didn't answer because he wasn't on duty. He was in the mine.
Why avoid Fellhammer?
Nobody answers roll call at Fort Fellhammer any longer. The shepherds say the wind there sounds like ordinary wind now.

Every night the dead garrison of Fort Fellhammer answers roll call. Shepherds hear it on the wind. My father Asgeir served there before the mine fell in, and every night they call his name and he doesn't answer. I want to know why he can't rest when the others can't stop.
Roll-Caller
The Fellhammer Roll
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.d: Ulfgar Lean-Bow, a Falkreath hunter, thinks a werewolf is killing woodcutters and robbing the town's graves. He asked me to help him hunt it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.o: Search for tracks around Half-Moon Mill
At the Lady Stone I found Ulfgar's brother Eirik, a werewolf by his own admission. He swore another wolf, Runa the gravekeeper, was the killer.
Follow the footprints to the Lady Stone after nightfall
...I knew. I think I knew when he stopped coming to supper. If he's still himself, even a little, I won't put silver in him. Find the one who made him.
Tell Ulfgar what you saw at the Lady Stone
Your brother Eirik is one of them.
Find the pack's den at Moss Mother Cavern
Greymantle Wolf
Kill the wolves of Runa's pack
Runa Greymantle had kept Falkreath's graveyard for twenty years, and fed her pack from it for the last one.
Kill Runa Greymantle
Send him north, into the empty country, far from anyone he could hurt.
North. Aye. He always liked the snow better than I did.
That's your choice to make, not mine.
Then I'll make it at the stone, where he can see the lake. Thank you for leaving it to me.
He's waiting at the stone. He said whatever I decide, he'll accept. That's worse, somehow.
Tell Ulfgar that Runa is dead
Runa is dead. What about Eirik?
What are you hunting?
The graves of Falkreath lie quiet again. Ulfgar doesn't talk about his brother, and I don't ask.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_grey_maw.p: Two woodcutters dead by Half-Moon Mill this month, and the graveyard dug up besides. Jarl says sabre cat. No cat I ever tracked opens a coffin. Come hunt with me, and bring something silver if you've got it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_knock_belo: Hela Corundum-Hand of Darkwater Crossing says her night shift vanished in the new Veinhollow shaft after weeks of knocking from below.
Go down the Veinhollow shaft
Falmer Skulker
Kill the Falmer in the galleries
Someone had hammered a Dwemer resonance rod into the deepest gallery. The 'knocking' was the rod, ringing down into the dark. It called them up.
Pull the humming brass rod out of the gallery floor
That's the foreman's sounding rod. Bought it off a Markarth trader to find ore veins. He's been down there every night 'listening.' He went down with the night shift. Gods help him.
Show Hela the rod
Someone drove this into your floor. It's been ringing like a dinner bell.
Follow the Falmer tunnel to where it opens at Kagrenzel
The Gloomseer had been answering the rod's call for weeks, each night a little closer to the miners. Two of the night shift were alive in its larder.
Kill the Gloomseer who leads the raiders
Break it, and fill in the bottom gallery.
Rock and mortar, as deep as we can pour it. No more listening.
Keep it. If you hear it ring on its own, run.
Hmph. An alarm bell that answers back. I'll hang it over the shaft.
Two is more than I hoped. What do we do with that cursed rod?
Report to Hela at Darkwater Crossing
Two of your miners are coming home. The rest aren't.
Why is the new shaft closed?
The Veinhollow shaft is quiet now. Hela says the miners sing while they work, loudly, to drown out anything they might hear below.

We opened a new seam north of the crossing. Good corundum. Then the knocking started, from under the deepest gallery, steady as a heartbeat. Two nights ago it stopped, and the night shift didn't come up. Something else did.
Seam-Splitter
The Knock Below
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_lantern_sh: Three children have vanished from Rorikstead, the last of them Svana's daughter Hroa. The village blames the Khajiit caravan camped by the road.

Ri'shadi has heard what Rorikstead says. Rorikstead does not say that Ri'shadi saw a lantern of bone cross the fields at midnight, three nights running, going west. Small feet followed it. Ri'shadi did not follow. Ri'shadi is not brave.
Question the Khajiit trader Ri'shadi
Rorikstead says your caravan took their children.
Follow the lantern's path west to the Moldering Ruins
The toy's tail was tied with grey prayer thread. Only one man in Rorikstead braids Arkay's cord, and he had been very keen I search the Khajiit.
Pick up the wooden horse in the candle circle
Follow the trail of candle stubs to Serpent's Bluff
Lantern Thrall
Destroy the thralls guarding the sleeping children
Aslief died asking me to tell Ingrid he was sorry. The twins woke first, then Hroa.
Stop Aslief the Lantern Shepherd
Bring Hroa home to Rorikstead
Her horse. She calls it Mead. I... Aslief? Aslief, who sat at our table? Gods. And we nearly drove the Khajiit out with pitchforks.
Give Svana the wooden horse
Hroa's home. And this is hers.
Who are you looking for?
The children of Rorikstead came home. Svana took a basket of bread to Ri'shadi's caravan the next morning.

My Hroa's been gone three nights, and the Bjornsson twins before her. Folk say it's the Khajiit camped past the fields, that cats steal children to sell south. Brother Aslief prays with us every night. I don't want prayers. I want my daughter.
Shepherd's Mercy
The Lantern Shepherd
A grave outside Morthal named three women of one family, each drowned wearing the same torc. The last of that line still lives in Morthal.

A headstone has sunk to its shoulders in the marsh. Three women's names are cut into it, one below the other, and beneath each the same words: 'Taken by the water, wearing her mother's torc.' The newest name is barely weathered.

Then you know. Grandmother, mother, sister. The torc went to each in turn, and the marsh took each in turn. It's mine now. I keep it in a box and never go near the water, and still I dream of it. Take it. Find out what it wants.
Find the last woman of the family in Morthal
I found your family's grave in the marsh.
Go to the Kjenstag Ruins by night, where Jorunn's ancestor is buried
The carvings in Hulvard's barrow told the truth: Gunnolf Fen-Walker stole the torc from a sleeping woman. His ghost lied to me.
Find the Mire-Bride's barrow anyway
Fen-Draugr
Cut through the Mire-Bride's fen-draugr
When Hrafna fell, I closed the torc around her throat. The barrow sighed like a drained pool and went still.
Face Hrafna the Mire-Bride
Your ancestor stole it. The curse was the Mire-Bride's due.
So the hero of every story my grandmother told was a grave-robber. Good. I'm glad I know.
Gunnolf fought bravely. It's over now.
That's what Grandmother always said. Thank you for ending it.
I slept last night. All night. No water in my dreams at all. What did you find out there?
Return to Jorunn in Morthal
The torc is back where it belongs.
The Mire Torc lies on Hrafna's throat in her sinking barrow, and the women of Jorunn's line can walk by the water again.
Mirewalker Boots
The Mire Torc
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_ransomers_: A stone near Nilheim bore the marks of Stuhn the Ransomer, one of the old Nordic gods, and pointed to a forgotten hall in the hills.

A standing stone half buried in the slope, carved with a pair of open shackles above a hand full of coins. Below, in old runes worn nearly smooth: 'Stuhn takes the ransom. Stuhn opens the door.' A line of the same shackle-marks leads west into the hills.
Follow the shackle-marks to the hall in the hills
Pay your passage by defeating Gautr the Ransom-Warden
The tablet listed every warrior whose ransom Stuhn's priests promised and never paid. Gautr's own name was last.
Take the slate tablet from the ransom-altar

Stuhn. My grandmother still swore by him. Shor's brother, the god who paid for prisoners. If those names were promised a ransom, they've been waiting a long time. Read them aloud at the altar, every one. In the old days that was the payment.
Ask Brother Holgeir of Ivarstead about the tablet
This tablet came from a hall of Stuhn, in the hills.
Read every name on the tablet aloud at the ransom-altar
The cells of Stuhnhallr stand empty now. I left the tablet on the altar with every name read, and a coin on top for Stuhn.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_splintered: Bjarni Stonefist of Karthwasten says his wife Gerda went to a hagraven coven in the hills. He wants her brought home before she is changed.
Climb to Four Skull Lookout
Coven Briar-Guard
Defeat the coven's briar-guards
Gerda's letter was for Bjarni: 'Don't follow. You know why I went. Every bruise you gave me, I'm giving back to the stone.'
Take the letter pinned under the crow's skull
Follow the red wool markers to Bleakwind Bluff
Kill Sister Ashfeather

Then you know I'm not going back. The Mother says the change costs a heart. I thought she meant mine. Tonight she told me she means his, and I'm to fetch it. I don't want him dead. I just want to be gone.
Find Gerda at the Sundered Towers
I read your letter, Gerda.
Mother Crowsong died cursing me in a language older than Markarth. Gerda watched from the tower door and didn't look away.
Kill Mother Crowsong
Go to Markarth. A city is a good place to start over.
Markarth. Stone walls, and nobody knows my face. Yes.
Old Hroldan's inn always needs hands.
An inn. Warm, and full of strangers. That sounds like heaven.
Somewhere he isn't. That's all I ask of the world.
Decide with Gerda where she goes
The coven's finished. Where will you go?
She... Fine. Fine. Let her go, then. I paid you to bring her back, not to read me letters. Take your coin and get out.
Give Bjarni his wife's letter
She's alive. She left you this.
You look like a man who lost something.
Gerda never became a hagraven. She never went back to Karthwasten either, and I think that's how it should be.

My wife Gerda walked out of Karthwasten nine days ago with a bundle and her good shawl. Shepherds saw her on the road toward Four Skull Lookout, with an old woman in feathers. She went to the hagravens. I want her back before they make her one.
Talon of the Splintered Moon
The Splintered Moon
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_the_sweet_tith: Watch-Sergeant Vigge asked me to find the source of the skooma spreading through Riften's beggars.
Sugar? Nobody's got coin for skooma. But the widow Asta gives out sweet-cakes at the well every morning. Best thing in Riften. After a week you'd kill for one. That's not the same thing, is it?
Ask Brodd Half-Mitten where the beggars get skooma
Where do the poor folk get their sugar, Brodd?
The widow Asta's sweet-cakes were baked with moon sugar, and her supplier is a Khajiit named Dar'Vasha.
Search the widow's bakehouse near Merryfair Farm
Find Dar'Vasha's smugglers at Lost Prospect Mine
Sugar Runner
Clear out the sugar smugglers
Dar'Vasha's ledger listed a monthly payment to 'the sergeant with the red beard' for keeping the watch away from the well. Vigge has a red beard.
Kill Dar'Vasha Sugar-Tooth
Return to the bakehouse at night, when the widow bakes
Bakehouse Lookout
Stop Widow Asta Sweetmilk
The Jarl's steward gets this ledger. You'll answer for it.
Fair. I'll walk up to Mistveil Keep myself. Don't need an escort for that.
Keep the badge. Spend the rest of it cleaning up what you allowed.
Every shaking beggar in this city is mine to feed now. I'll do it. Thank you.
...Aye. I took her coin for a year. Then she started handing cakes to children, and I couldn't stomach it. I couldn't arrest her without her talking about me, so I sent you. Now you know.
Confront Watch-Sergeant Vigge with the ledger
Dar'Vasha paid a red-bearded sergeant to keep the watch away from the well.
You look like you haven't slept.
The sweet-cakes stopped. It took Riften's beggars a hard month to stop shaking, but most of them did.

Skooma's come back to Riften, and it's coming through the beggars. Half the poor in this city have the shakes. They won't talk to a man in a guard's helmet. You don't wear one. Find where it's coming from.
Sugar-Cutter
The Sweet Tithe
Hrodulf of Chillfurrow Farm says a giant keeps raiding his fields. He wants it dead and promised good coin for it.
The giant at Bleakwind Basin was sitting beside a mammoth whose tusks had been sawn off. Sledge tracks ran east.
Climb to the giant camp at Bleakwind Basin
Follow the sledge tracks to Halted Stream Camp
Tusk Poacher
Drive out the poachers at Halted Stream
Orvald carried a tally stick of buyers. The first name burned into it was Hrodulf of Chillfurrow.
Kill Orvald Tusk-Taker
Take back the mammoth's tusk from the poachers' sledge
Lay the tusk beside the dead mammoth
Leave a sack of grain at the basin every month, and it will leave you be.
Feed a giant? ...Fine. Cheaper than another ox, I suppose.
The Jarl's steward will see this tally.
Do what you like. But the Jarl's men won't plow my rows while I'm in the dungeon.
...So it was. Orvald said the beast was old and wouldn't be missed, and ivory fetches more than turnips. I didn't think the big one would know whose fields to walk through.
Confront Hrodulf about the tally
Your name was on Orvald's tally, Hrodulf.
Something flattened your fields.
The giant stopped coming down from Bleakwind Basin. Hrodulf still grumbles about the price of an ox.

Third time this month a giant's come down off the hill and stamped my rows flat. Killed my best ox last night. The Jarl's guards say giants aren't their concern unless they climb the walls. Go up to Bleakwind Basin and put it down, and I'll pay you what I'd have paid for a new ox, and then some.
Tuskbreaker
The Tusk Debt
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_broke: Purge the vampire thralls in Broken Fang Cave.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Thralls from Broken Fang Cave have been raiding the western moorland pastures after dusk.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_darks: You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Clear the predator den inside Darkshade.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_fellg: Recover the stolen excise rolls from Fellglow Keep.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Warlocks in Fellglow Keep carried off the hold's alchemy excise rolls.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_grayw: Clear the ridge den at Graywinter Watch.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Clear the ridge cave at Graywinter Watch so the cooperage wagons can pass.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_green: Clear the poacher camp at Greenspring Hollow.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Stop the poachers operating at Greenspring Hollow.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_guldu: Scatter the rustlers at Guldun Rock.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Ascend to Guldun Rock and scatter the cattle-rustlers.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_hamvi: Restore the burial seal at Hamvir's Rest.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Grave-robbers have broken the iron grate at Hamvir's Rest near Dustman's Cairn.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_rannv: Break the warlock traps at Rannveig's Fast.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
A rogue warlock has rigged the chute at Rannveig's Fast to trap passing drovers.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_redor: Reclaim the factor's signet from Redoran's Retreat.
Highwaymen in Redoran's Retreat stripped an old Dunmer factor's strongbox.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_shimm: Open the choked spring inside Shimmermist Cave.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Something inside Shimmermist Cave choked the farm's irrigation spring with webbing and brass scrap.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_silen: Drive the poachers out of Silent Moons Camp.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Poachers at Silent Moons Camp have taken over the old lunar smithy on the knoll.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_swind: Destroy the forged bond at Swindler's Den.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Mercenaries in Swindler's Den hold a forged grain bond against Rorikstead's harvest.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_whiterun_white: Clear the timber-taxers from White River Watch.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Bandits in White River Watch have been taxing timber rafts coming down from Lake Ilinalta.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_bleakcoas: You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Clear the frost trolls from Bleakcoast Cave.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_driftshad: Clear the mercenaries in Driftshade Refuge.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Reclaim the silver bars from Driftshade Refuge.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_fort_kast: Clear the necromancers holding Fort Kastav.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Free the captives at Fort Kastav.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_frostflow: Clear the cellar of Frostflow Lighthouse.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Relight the beacon at Frostflow Lighthouse.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_journeyma: Clear the bandits in Journeyman's Nook.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Recover the lockbox from Journeyman's Nook.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_mount_ant: Secure the ridge at Mount Anthor.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Cleanse the cairns at Mount Anthor.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_sightless: Clear the upper galleries of the Sightless Pit.
Reset the pressure valves inside the Sightless Pit.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_skytemple: Clear the draugr at Skytemple Ruins.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Copy the inscription at Skytemple Ruins.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_snow_veil: Secure the entrance of Snow Veil Sanctum.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Drive the grave-robbers from Snow Veil Sanctum.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_stillborn: You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Seal the ice-tunnel inside Stillborn Cave.
story.skycraft.q.side_sky_wint_yngvild_j: Defeat Voryn the Ice-Binder inside Yngvild.
You have my thanks, traveler. Here is the coin we agreed upon.
Slay Voryn the Ice-Binder in Yngvild.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_black_vein: Galdrem Hlaren says the deep gallery of Raven Rock's ebony mine collapsed with three miners and the foreman, Drovas Rethelo, still inside.
Go into the collapsed gallery of the Raven Rock mine
Ash Crawler
Kill the ash spawn pouring through the breach
Drovas pushed the dig past the Redoran safe-line for a bonus, and broke into a hollow full of old ash. That is what brought the gallery down.
Find the foreman's tally-board
The ash took Drovas and stood him up again. I gave him what rest I could. The trapped miners walked out behind me, blinking.
Put down what's left of Drovas Rethelo
The truth. Mark the line in stone so nobody else crosses it.
Hard on his widow. Better for everyone else's. I'll do it.
That the rock was bad. Let his widow keep the pension.
A soft lie for a hard town. All right. Take this, and keep it to yourself as well.
Past the red marks. For a bonus. His widow lives two doors from me. What do I tell the council?
Bring the tally-board to Galdrem
Your miners are out. Drovas didn't make it, and this is why.
Is something wrong at the mine?
The deep gallery is sealed with a red line painted across the rock. The miners walk past it every morning and don't look at it.

The new deep gallery came down this morning. Three of my miners are behind the fall, and our foreman Drovas went in after them and hasn't come out. The Redoran guard says wait for the council. I say the council can dig its own way in.
Gallery Helm
The Black Vein
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_deserter.d: Captain Ulvesa Dreth of the Raven Rock guard says Varon Telas deserted his post at Ashfallow Citadel. She wants him found.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_deserter.o: Search Varon's post at Ashfallow Citadel
Follow his tracks to the wreck of the Strident Squall
Fight through the reavers at the wreck

Ulfgar was my father. He found me in Raven Rock and told me to leave the citadel gate open one night, or he'd tell the council whose son I was. I couldn't open it and I couldn't stay. So I came to tell him no. He took it badly.
Your captain wants you back. What happened?
Take him back. He chose Raven Rock over blood.
A week of latrine duty for leaving his post, and then he's back on the wall.
Let him go to the Skaal. He can't serve under your eye now.
Hm. Perhaps that's kinder. I'll strike his name, not hang it.
And he went to face him alone instead of telling me. Brave, stupid and loyal, in that order. What would you have me do with him?
Varon ran so he wouldn't have to betray you. The reaver chief was his father.
Your guard looks a man short.
Varon Telas said no to his father, once, and meant it. On Solstheim that counts for more than a uniform.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_deserter.p: One of mine, Varon Telas, walked off his post at Ashfallow Citadel last night. Good soldier, which makes it worse. Desertion in time of reavers is a hanging matter. Find him and bring him back, and I'll decide whether to hang him after I've heard why.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_hunt_that_: By the headwaters of the Harstrad I found an old hunt-totem carved upside down. A horn keeps sounding from Frykte Peak, and nobody is there to blow it.

A log totem crowned with a wolf skull and a ring of antlers. The Skaal hunt-sign carved into it is upside down: the hunter beneath the prey. Every few heartbeats, far off toward Frykte Peak, a horn sounds.
An echo of an old hunt rides on Frykte Peak. It named me its prey.
Go to Frykte Peak when the moon is up
Hound of the Echo
Survive the hounds of the echo
Hold Frykte Peak until the hunt comes for you
Gharnvald was a Nord who tried to cheat in the Huntsman's own game by staking a Skaal guide as bait. He has been hunter and hunted on this peak ever since, and he was glad to stop.
Hound of the Echo
Kill the huntsman, Gharnvald the Twice-Hunted
Burn the totem. The hunt is over.
Good. Let the wolves forget that song.
Leave it. A warning for the next cheat.
The Skaal have never been short of warnings. One more won't hurt. Take this from the hunt's leavings.
Gharnvald. My grandmother's grandmother was the guide he staked out. She lived, and cursed him. The Huntsman of Daedra likes a curse with teeth. What became of the totem?
Tell Yrsa Wolf-Speaker in the Skaal village
There was an old hunt still riding on Frykte Peak. A Nord named Gharnvald.
Hircine's hunts are supposed to end at dawn. This one ran for three hundred years, until it caught someone willing to finish it.
Pelt of the Twice-Hunted
The Hunt That Did Not End
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_jailer_of_: Torvar Ashdrinker, a skald from Windhelm, wants to visit the tomb of his ancestor Thane Vorgrim in Gyldenhul Barrow so he can write his saga.
The bones at the door were Eyvind's, the barrow's jailer, and the carvings name him as Torvar's true forefather. Vorgrim was never honored here. He was locked in. And I just let him out.
Take the ring from the bones by the sealed door
Put Thane Vorgrim back in the dark
Sing Eyvind's saga. The true one.
'The Long Watch of Eyvind.' Sober, even. I'll sing it in Windhelm and watch them weep.
Sing the old one. Nobody wants a jailer's saga.
Coward's choice. Profitable, though. Here's an advance on the first performance.
A jailer. Not a thane. A man who sat by a door for the rest of his life so no one else would have to. Hm. That's a better saga, isn't it?
Bring Eyvind's ring to Torvar in Raven Rock
Vorgrim wasn't your ancestor. He was a prisoner. Your forefather was his jailer, Eyvind.
What saga brings a skald to Solstheim?
Eyvind kept his door shut for a lifetime and a long death. I opened it in an afternoon, and spent the evening closing it again.

My forefather, Thane Vorgrim, lies in Gyldenhul Barrow, honored above all the old Nords of this isle, or so my grandmother sang it. I'd like to stand at his tomb before I write his saga. The barrow is full of draugr, and I am full of mead. Come with me in spirit, and in person.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_last_muste: Near Fort Frostmoth I found the grave of a Legion tribune, Severa Callo. Someone wrote that she is still holding the fort.

A Legion headstone, half buried in ash: 'Tribune Severa Callo. She held.' Beneath, scratched in later by a less careful hand: 'Still holding.' The ground around the stone is churned, as if by boots that came and went at night.
Return to Fort Frostmoth after dark
Relieve Tribune Callo of her command
The roster's last entry asks for relief and names the courier sent to fetch it: Brenn. An old man in Raven Rock carries that name.
Go and stand one muster. Tell them relief has come.
Yes. Yes, I owe her that. I'll go tonight, in my old cloak, if it still fits.
She's at rest. Let it go.
At rest. Then I'll try to be, too. Take this. It was hers. I took it from her desk the day I left, as a promise to come back.
I never reached the ship. The ash came down, I hid in a cave for three days, and when I came out I just... kept walking. Fifty years. Is she still there?
Bring the roster to Cassius Brenn in Raven Rock
Frostmoth's garrison was still waiting for you. They called your name at muster.
A garrison held Frostmoth for fifty years after the war forgot it. Relief came late, but it came.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_snow_walke: Bjornolf Whitecairn of the Skaal says a great white bear killed two hunters near Hvitkald Peak. He wants it dead before it reaches the village.
A mother bear and her cubs were killed here and left to rot, with Skaal arrows in them. The fletching is Bjornolf's.
Search Brodir Grove where the hunters fell
Carrion Wolf
Drive off the wolves feeding on the waste
Climb to Hvitkald Peak
Wait on the peak for the Snow-Walker
The Snow-Walker fell without a sound and melted back into the drifts. Only its pelt was left, as white as fresh snow.
Face Hjornskar the Snow-Walker
Tell the shaman. The Skaal deserve to know.
Yes. I'll go to the shaman and do whatever penance is set. Take this. I haven't earned it.
It's done. Hunt better from now on.
I will. Every kill, every scrap. I swear it on the All-Maker.
We were showing off. Three hides in one morning. Then we heard it coming and ran. The bear wasn't sent to punish the village. It was sent for us.
Confront Bjornolf about Brodir Grove
Your arrows were in a she-bear and two cubs at Brodir Grove, and you left the meat to rot.
You look like a hunter with a problem.
The Skaal say the All-Maker gives the hunt. On Hvitkald Peak I learned that it also takes it back.

Two of our hunters are dead, torn by a white bear bigger than any beast has a right to be. The shaman calls it a spirit-beast, sent by the All-Maker. I call it a bear. It hunts near Hvitkald Peak. Help me end it before it comes to the village.
Snow-Walker's Pelt
The Bear Who Walks in Snow
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_spear_of_t: Ragnvi Spear-Widow of Thirsk Mead Hall says a riekling chief, Kruug Three-Tusks, has united the tribes and is raiding Thirsk. The rieklings also hold the hall's old spear.
Three-Tusk Raider
Drive the riekling raiders out of Thirsk
Strike back at the rieklings in Bristleback Cave
The war-totem bears the old seal of Thirsk and a long row of tally-marks: mead promised, mead delivered, then mead promised and never sent.
Bristleback Warrior
Take the tribe's war-totem
March on Kruug's camp at Benkongerike
Three-Tusk Warrior
Kruug's War-Troll
Fight through Kruug's war-band
Kruug is dead, and the old spear of Thirsk was in his hand. It was never stolen. Ragnvi's grandfather traded it for peace, then stopped paying the price.
Defeat Kruug Three-Tusks
Send them the mead you owe. Make the peace again.
A cask a season, carried by me personally. Grandfather would hate it. Good.
They've lost their chief. Let them be.
Then Thirsk will sleep with an axe under the bench for a while. Here, the hall's thanks.
That old miser. He told the hall it was taken in battle, and we drank to his courage every winter. The spear's yours, by right of the fight. What of the tribes?
Bring the war-totem and the truth to Ragnvi
Your grandfather gave the spear to the rieklings for peace, and Thirsk stopped sending the mead.
What grudge does Thirsk have?
The Spear of Thirsk was a peace-price, not a trophy. I carry it now, and I know exactly what it cost.

Rieklings. Two generations ago they took the chieftain's spear from this hall, and now a chief called Kruug Three-Tusks has gathered every tribe from Bristleback to Benkongerike and comes raiding for our casks. Break him, and bring the spear home to Thirsk.
The Spear of Thirsk
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_spire_of_n: Ilvesa Tavrin, a scholar at Tel Mithryn, wants the resonance prism from the heart of the Dwemer Spire of Nchurdrel.
Go to the Spire of Nchurdrel
The spire stopped singing when I took the prism. Whatever sum the Dwemer set it to work out, it will never finish now.
Take the resonance prism from the spire's heart
Keep it. Find out what it was counting.
I will. And I'll never tell my master it was here. Take your fee, and a little more.
Put it back. Some sums should finish.
Put it... You're right. I'll take it back myself, before I change my mind.
Silent? Four thousand years of calculation, and we pulled out the last digit. I'm not sure whether to weep or take notes. Both, probably.
Bring the prism to Ilvesa at Tel Mithryn
The prism. The spire went silent when I took it.
Somewhere in the Spire of Nchurdrel, a Dwemer calculation is either running again or never will. I've decided I'd rather not know the answer.

A Dwemer spire south of here that has been humming one note since before the Telvanni came to Solstheim. At its heart is a resonance prism, I'm sure of it. My master would give an arm for it, and would probably mean mine. Fetch it, and I'll pay well.
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_the_stalhrim_d: Eirvald Rimehand, the Skaal smith, says the village's stalhrim cache at the Stalhrim Source was robbed and that something now walks the wind there.
Go to the Stalhrim Source
Destroy the wraiths circling the broken wards
Banish the Hollow Wind
A child-sized Skaal mitten, stitched with a snow-hare. Eirvald's apprentice Olvir wears the other one. He has been in Raven Rock all week.
Pick up the mitten caught in the wards
My mother's cough is the bad kind. The healer here wants coin, and stalhrim is coin. I only took what I could carry. I didn't know the wards held anything in.
Find Olvir in Raven Rock
You left a mitten at the Stalhrim Source.
Forgive him, and help his mother.
The village will pay the healer, and Olvir will work the debt off at my forge. Twice over.
He broke the wards. Let him answer for it.
Then he stays in Raven Rock. I'll still send for his mother's healer. I'm not a monster.
Olvir. He could have asked. The village would have paid. Pride is a Skaal sickness worse than any cough.
Return to Eirvald with the truth
The wraith is gone. The thief was Olvir. He sold the ice to pay for his mother's healer.
Is your forge cold, smith?
The wind at the Stalhrim Source blows in a straight line again. Eirvald says that is how you know the ice is content.

Cold as my temper. Our stalhrim cache at the Source was broken open and half of it is gone. Worse, the wind there has gone wrong, and the hunters say something walks in it. Find out who took our ice, and quiet that wind.
Rimehand's Debt
The Stalhrim Debt
story.skycraft.q.side_sol_what_the_ice_k: In the frozen north of Solstheim I found a prospector frozen beside his pick, with a letter for someone named Astrid at Thirsk. Troll tracks lead into the Glacial Cave.

A man frozen sitting up against a rock, coat buttoned to the chin, a stalhrim pick across his knees. A sealed letter in his glove is addressed to 'Astrid, at Thirsk'. Huge, knuckled tracks lead from him toward the Glacial Cave.
Follow the tracks to the Glacial Cave
Kill the frost trolls in the cave
The trolls had dragged Hrolf's pack into their den. His claim marks a stalhrim seam deep in the cave, and his letter leaves it to Astrid, whatever his partner Kjeld says.
Recover the prospector's claim from the trolls' den
Give it to the Skaal. It's their ice, really.
Hrolf would grumble, then agree. He always did. The Skaal will remember Thirsk kindly for it.
Work it. And throw Kjeld out of your hall.
Oh, Kjeld's leaving tonight. Through the door or the window, his choice. Here, the first of the claim's luck.
Kjeld told me Hrolf sold the claim and ran off to Skyrim. Kjeld's been drinking on Hrolf's money all winter. Well. What do I do with a stalhrim seam?
Bring Hrolf's letter to Astrid at Thirsk
I found Hrolf near the Glacial Cave. I'm sorry. He left you this.
Hrolf found what he was looking for and froze sitting on it. The ice kept him and his letter until someone came along to read it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_marginalia.des: Irilwe Lanthenor, a scholar of the Crystal Tower, told me her research on the Tower's wards was stolen and her apprentice Calwen has vanished. She wants Calwen found before the Justiciars are called.
Search the sea-grotto where Calwen copied manuscripts
Calwen stole the notes to keep her own teacher from selling them. Irilwe had left that part out.

I didn't take them to sell. I took them because she was going to. A courier from House Valtaryon offered her a fortune, and she was thinking about it. Those notes show how to open the Tower like a coin purse. I hid them at Gullrock Steps, and now the courier's men are camped right on top of them.
Vaenor carried the seal of House Valtaryon, and a letter that was not addressed to Irilwe at all, but to someone he called the Patron.
Recover Irilwe's ward-notes from Calwen's hiding place
Lodge them with the Sapiarchs, where neither of you can be tempted.
Sensible, and humiliating. Very well. Tell Calwen she may come home. I'll be insufferable about it for a year.
I burned them. Calwen was right.
Eleven years, in a fire. Calwen always did take my side against me. Get out, before I thank you.
She thought I would sell? ... I might have. The offer was obscene. What do you intend to do with them?
Here are your notes. Calwen took them so you couldn't sell them.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_marginalia.off: You look like someone who lost an argument with a library.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_marginalia.out: Irilwe's ward-notes are out of reach of House Valtaryon. The courier's letter was addressed to a 'Patron', and Lady Haliwen Valtaryon of Alinor will want to hear about it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_marginalia.pit: I lost a library. Eleven years of notes on how the Crystal Tower's wards breathe, gone from my study in one night, and only my apprentice Calwen had the key. The proctors want me to call the Justiciars. I would rather you found her first. She is shy, and very bad at running away.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.desc: With Captain Ysla dead, the sea serpent she kept on a tide-song leash is loose off Saltreach. Nyssa still remembers the song that can call it to shore.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o0.re: I sang to the serpents in the Pyandonean pens when I was a girl. Take this conch. Blow it at Coilwater Cove after dark and Old Coil will come to it. Don't miss when it does. It won't.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o0.to: How do we draw the serpent out?
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o3.jo: Old Coil came up out of the cove like a tower falling sideways. The drowned fishers it had taken came up with it.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o4.c0: Then I'll tell them at the market, loudly. Anyone who has a problem with it can buy their fish in Alinor.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o4.c1: Some things can stay between a husband and wife.
Twenty years we've kept it. We'll keep it twenty more.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o4.re: She sang it to shore? My Nyssa? The village will want to know how a net-mender knows Maormer serpent-songs.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.o4.to: Old Coil is dead. Nyssa called it in for me.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.outro: With Nyssa's tide-song I drew Old Coil into Coilwater Cove and killed it. Saltreach can fish again, and Nyssa no longer flinches at blue sails.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_old_coil.title: Old Coil
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_salt_in_the_ne: Aranon Gullwhistle, a fisher of Saltreach on Summerset's south coast, has seen Maormer ships watching his village. A serpent-carved comb on his doorstep has frightened his wife Nyssa into silence.
Nyssa is Maormer. Aranon, I realised, had always known and never cared.

It's a betrothal comb. Pyandonean. Twenty years ago I ran from a captain who carved one for me, and I married a fisher who has never once asked about my accent. Ysla Brine-Veil does not forget a promise, even one I never made.
Aranon says the comb frightened you.
Scout the Maormer camp at Blackfin Landing
Ysla said she hadn't come for Saltreach. She had come to bring a runaway home. With her last breath she said Old Coil would come for Nyssa either way.
Old Coil was hers, bound to her by a tide-song. With Ysla gone the song is broken, and the serpent is loose and hungry. And it knows the way to Saltreach, because it followed her here.
Tell Nyssa that Ysla is dead
Ysla is dead. She said something called Old Coil would come anyway.
Captain Ysla Brine-Veil came to Summerset to drag Nyssa Gullwhistle back to Pyandonea. She is dead now, but her sea serpent is not.

Blue-sailed ships off the point three nights running. Maormer. They haven't touched a single boat, only watched. Then last night someone left a comb on my doorstep, carved from fishbone with a serpent on it. My wife went white as a gull's belly and won't say why.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_coral_lant: Shipwright Eldaran Halvenor of Firsthold told me four of his ships have wrecked on Summerset's western strand while steering by the Coral Lantern, and its keeper has gone silent.
Walk the Wrecker's Strand below the lighthouse
Drowned Sailor
Wreck-Picking Dreugh
Fight off what's picking over the wrecks
A shard of the lighthouse's lens had come down with the last wreck. It pulsed in my hand. Coral doesn't do that, and neither do Altmer lighthouses.
Search the newest wreck
Climb to the Coral Lantern
Coral-Bound Thrall
Salt-Bleached Sailor
Fight through the keeper's thralls
Orvandil was proud of the arithmetic: so many crews, so many oars, so many years until the fleet under the sea was ready. He had never once looked at the faces.
Destroy Keeper Orvandil Saltglass
Smash it, and every piece of that lens.
I'll send my strongest apprentices with hammers, and a new glass lens behind them.
Send it to the Sapiarchs. Someone should learn what the Sload are planning.
Then let the scholars lose sleep over it. I've lost enough.
A Sload. On Summerset. Every captain I ever trained trusted that light. What do we do with this shard?
Report to Shipwright Eldaran in Firsthold
A Sload grew a coral lens for the keeper. It drowned your crews on purpose.
You build ships? Where do they go?

The Coral Lantern was luring ships onto the rocks with a Sload-grown lens, and its keeper Orvandil was gathering drowned crews for a fleet under the sea. The light on the western headland is dark for now.

Down, lately. Four of my hulls wrecked on Summerset's western strand this year, every one of them steering by the Coral Lantern. That light has guided ships for six hundred years, and now it guides them onto the rocks. The keeper won't answer letters, and the Admiralty says it is a matter for the Admiralty. It isn't, apparently, a matter for anyone.
Lantern-Breaker
The Coral Lantern
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_grave_with: Outside Firsthold I found a headstone for one Neliril Sunhallow, dated next month, with no grave dug beneath it.
A new headstone in a field where nobody is buried. Neliril Sunhallow, beloved daughter, taken by the sea. The date carved beneath it is next month. Fresh cart-tracks lead away inland.
Follow the cart-tracks to a shuttered cottage

Then the mason's early. I owe the Debt-Wardens of Firsthold eight hundred gold, and they don't take no. A dead woman can't be collected from. Unless someone nosy leads them straight to her door. Which, I note, you may have just done.
Speak with the cottage's occupant
There's a headstone with your name on it, dated next month.
Debt-Warden
Fight off the Debt-Wardens who followed you
Marshal Aicantar told me debts are sacred. His own ledger disagreed.
Debt-Warden
Confront the Debt-Wardens' marshal at their camp
Neliril's debt had been paid twice over. The Debt-Wardens simply never stopped collecting.
Take the Debt-Wardens' ledger
Take back your name. Take the ledger to the magistrate.
Neliril Sunhallow, alive and owed. I'll have the mason carve that instead.
Stay dead if you like. The ledger can burn.
Dead and debt-free. The best of both. Thank you, stranger. Forget my face.
Twice? I sold my mother's loom for the second payment. ... So I can stop being dead? I'd grown rather attached to my headstone.
Bring the ledger to Neliril
Your debt was paid twice. Here's the proof.

Neliril Sunhallow had a headstone carved for herself to escape the Debt-Wardens of Firsthold, who had been collecting a debt she had already paid twice over. The marshal is dead, and Neliril chose which name to keep.
Neliril's Last Favor
The Grave With No Body
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_grey_indri: Faelwe, a groundskeeper on Artaeum, asked me to find out why the old indrik Dusk is losing his feathers, and what he has been eating on the cliffs.
Search the cliff grove where Dusk grazes
Pale Wisp
Pick the grey berries from the grafted bushes

Grafted. On Artaeum. The Order keeps a bound dremora in the sealed undercroft for 'study'. Last month he asked for books on gardening. Nobody thought anything of it, because nobody ever thinks anything of gardening.
Bring the berries to Faelwe
Someone grafted these bushes. They taste of brimstone.
Go to the Sealed Undercroft on the Mistward cliffs
Vashkyn wanted a mount worthy of a Daedra, so he set about growing one on Artaeum's own berries, one graft at a time.
Vashkyn the Gardener
Potting Scamp
Deal with the undercroft's escaped prisoner and his scamps
Cinderhoof had been one of Dusk's herd. Its feathers had burned down to embers, and it did not know me from its gardener.
Put down Cinderhoof, the Grafted Indrik
Burn them, root and graft.
I'll burn them myself and salt the ash. The Order can study the smell.
Keep one, under lock, so the Order learns what he did.
One bush, in a cage, with a sign. I'll make the sign very large.
Dusk ate a plain berry this morning and kept it down. A few blue feathers already. What should I do with the grafts?
Tell Faelwe the undercroft is quiet
Vashkyn is gone, and so is what he grew. What about the grafted bushes?
That indrik looks like it's been rained on for a century.
A bound dremora in Artaeum's undercroft had been grafting brimstone into the indriks' berries to grow himself a burning mount. Dusk is going blue again, slowly.

That's Dusk. He's two hundred years old, and he's never looked like that. His feathers are coming out grey. Indriks wear their health on their backs. Something on the cliffs is feeding him wrong, and I'm a groundskeeper, not a hero. Bring me what he's been eating.
Indrik-Feather Crown
The Grey Indrik
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_hawkspire_: Oriel Featherwright, a gryphon-keeper of Firsthold, told me smugglers stole an egg from the Hawkspire aerie, and the furious matriarch is raiding the pastures. She asked me to bring the egg home.
Find the smugglers' cove at Gull Hollow
Merric said the egg was already paid for, by a menagerie-keeper in Alinor whose family name I had heard very recently: Featherwright.
Take the egg from its heated crate
Climb to the Hawkspire Aerie with the egg
With the matriarch away hunting sheep, the harpies had been working up the courage to rob the second egg.
Drive the harpies off the nest
Keep the egg warm in the nest until the matriarch returns

My brother. He kept asking which nest was best, and I told him just to make him stop asking. I'll be on the next boat to Alinor, and he'll be seeing the matriarch in his dreams for a year. Take the sword from the cairn. She showed it to you; that means she wants you to have it.
Return to Oriel Featherwright in Firsthold
The egg's back in the nest. Merric's buyer was a Featherwright, in Alinor.
Is that a gryphon feather in your hat?

I returned the stolen egg to the Hawkspire aerie and drove off the harpies circling it. The matriarch showed me an old gryphon-knight's cairn under her nest, and Oriel's brother has some explaining to do.

Hawkspire's matriarch laid two eggs this spring. Now she has one and a temper, and she's taking sheep from Firsthold's pastures to make the point. Smugglers took the other egg; menageries in Alinor pay a fortune for gryphon chicks. Get it back before she decides sheep aren't enough.
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_last_branc: Quarendil Venwe, a genealogist of Alinor obsessed with proving his unbroken descent from the Crystal Tower's founders, sent me to question his ancestor Tirnaril's ghost in the family ossuary.
Go to the Venwe Ancestral Ossuary
Venwe Ossuary-Guard
Get past the ossuary's guardians
Tirnaril hadn't simply gone to sea. He had gone to a Maormer wife, and the son who came back to Alinor was hers. The letter asked that he be buried beside her on Auridon, at a cairn facing south.
Search Tirnaril's niche
Find the exile's cairn on Auridon
Tirnaril's ghost had followed his secret across the strait, and he fought me to keep it. Beside his cairn was a second, smaller one with a serpent carved on it.
Face Tirnaril's ghost at the cairn
It's true. The branch is closed. It just doesn't go where you wanted.
Then I'll draw her in. In blue ink. Thirty-one generations, and the one that matters is the one I nearly let go.
Tirnaril drowned at sea. That's all.
Drowned! Splendid. That is to say, how sad. Thank you. The branch is closed.
Sea elves. In the Venwe line. Do you know what the College would... no. Is it true? It's true, isn't it.
Bring Quarendil the answer in Alinor
Tirnaril married a Maormer. Your line runs through her.
Is that a family tree? It's taller than you are.
Quarendil Venwe's missing ancestor had married a Maormer woman and been buried in exile beside her on Auridon. Quarendil's family tree now ends one way or the other, because of what I told him.

Thirty-one generations, unbroken, back to the masons who laid the Crystal Tower's first course. Thirty-one, minus one. In the Second Era my ancestor Tirnaril is recorded only as 'gone to sea'. His bones are in our ossuary west of the city, and his ghost, I'm told, still talks. Ask him where he went. I need that branch closed.
Tirnaril's Sea-Knife
The Last Branch
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_patron_of_: Lady Haliwen Valtaryon of Alinor swore she never sent the courier who tried to buy the Crystal Tower's secrets. She asked me to read her house's oldest ledgers, which her steward Kynval guards jealously.
Go to the Valtaryon Terraces outside Alinor
There should not be scamps in a noble's wine cellar. There should certainly not be scamps wearing the house livery.
Liveried Scamp
Get past the vault's keepers
Find the oldest ledger in the vault
Follow the ledger's last entry to the Shrine of Clavicus Vile
Kynval shed his Altmer face like a coat. Beneath it was a dremora with nine centuries of patience and none left.
Defeat Kynval the Steward
Pay nothing more. Let the luck run out.
Then House Valtaryon will learn to be ordinary. I suspect we'll be dreadful at it.
Burn the ledger, and never sign anything you didn't write yourself.
A Valtaryon reading her own contracts. My ancestors would faint. Good.
Nine hundred years. Every vintage, every marriage, every lucky wind. Rented. And the rent was to be the Crystal Tower.
Tell Lady Haliwen who her steward was
Your steward was a dremora. Your family's luck was rented from Clavicus Vile.
Your house's courier tried to buy the Crystal Tower's secrets. He carried your seal.

House Valtaryon's nine centuries of luck were bought from Clavicus Vile through a dremora steward, and the final payment was to be the Crystal Tower's wards. The debt is unpaid, and the steward is gone.

Then someone in my house used it without me. House Valtaryon has had nine centuries of good harvests, good marriages and good luck, and I never once asked why. Perhaps I should. My steward Kynval keeps the oldest ledgers in the vault under the terraces and will not let me read them. Read them for me.
The Patron of House Valtaryon
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_sapiarchs_: Sapiarch Halcarion of Alinor asked me to find his pupil Ilyrae, who went to chart the stars at the ancient Starwell of Tirnalor on Summerset's western cliffs and has not written in five weeks.
Go to the Starwell of Tirnalor
Starwell Watcher
Get past the Starwell's watchers
The Sentinel had not woken by accident. Someone had taken its ward-runes off with a chisel, very neatly.
Destroy the Sentinel of Tirnalor
Come back and accuse him before the College.
With what proof? ... With you as a witness, and my original charts. Very well. I'll pack the brass.
Stay lost. I'll tell him the Starwell was empty.
Thank you. Tell him the stars are still drifting, and so am I.
He's worried about his treatise. Every figure I sent him, he published under his own name. I woke the Sentinel to keep his couriers out. I didn't plan for someone competent.
Speak with Ilyrae
Your Sapiarch is worried about you.
She's alive, and she knows whose name is on her work.
Ah. Well. Scholarship is a collaborative enterprise. I'm sure the College will... see it that way. Excuse me. I must re-read some things.
The Starwell was empty. She's gone.
Gone. A pity. A great pity. She had such a gift for figures. Mine, now, I suppose, for the last time.
Well? Is she alive? Did she finish the figures for the autumn quarter?
Return to Sapiarch Halcarion in Alinor
About Ilyrae.
Sapiarch, you seem distracted.
Ilyrae was not lost at the Starwell of Tirnalor. She was hiding there from the Sapiarch who had been publishing her work under his own name, and I decided what he would learn.

My pupil Ilyrae went to the old Starwell of Tirnalor on the western cliffs to chart the drift of the stars. She was to send her figures every week. It has been five weeks. The Starwell has guardians older than the College. If she has woken one, I would like her back before it finishes waking.
Ilyrae's Star-Rod
The Sapiarch's Pupil
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_tidewater_: On Auridon's southern shore I found a sealed urn stamped with a spire rising from the waves, holding a wreath of living flowers. Someone in Firsthold must know where it came from.

A sealed Aldmeri urn has washed up among the rocks, green with weed. Its stopper is stamped with a spire rising out of waves. Inside, perfectly dry, is a funeral wreath of flowers that are still alive.
The Tidewater Spire. Sank in the First Era with its whole choir still inside, singing. On calm nights you can hear them off the southern rocks. Pearl-divers don't go there. The pearls sing too.
Ask in Firsthold about the spire on the urn's seal
Have you seen a seal like this? A spire rising out of waves.
Find the Tidewater Spire on Auridon's southern shore
Drowned Chorister
Fight through the drowned choristers
Take the silver choir-bell from the spire's altar

Calanwe had kept her choir singing for four thousand years so the sea would never notice the spire had sunk. When she fell, the singing stopped, and the choristers lay down as if they had been waiting for permission.
Drowned Chorister
Silence Lady Calanwe
Ring it once over the water, so they know they can rest.
Hear that? Nothing sang back. Good. That's good.
You keep it. Your family listened to them longest.
I'll hang it over the door. If it ever rings by itself, I'm moving inland.
My grandmother swore that choir sang the tide in and out. We'll find out if the sea remembers how on its own. What will you do with the bell?
Bring the choir-bell to Old Merewen
The choir is quiet now. This was their bell.
Lady Calanwe kept the drowned choir of the Tidewater Spire singing for four thousand years. The choir is silent now, and the tide off Auridon comes in on its own.
Tidewalker's Boots
The Tidewater Spire
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_unasked_qu: I found a lectern standing alone on Summerset's western hills, with a note inviting me to a table and warning me not to eat the bread. Someone is testing me, and they are not being subtle about being subtle.

A lectern of pale wood stands alone in the grass, where nobody would put a lectern. On it, one page in fine Aldmeris: If you are reading this, you noticed something most people walk past. Come to the table. Sit. Do not eat the bread.
Find the table the note spoke of
The bread smelled wonderful for two hours. Then it turned to sand, and a grey feather lay where it had been.
Sit at the table and touch nothing
Follow the grey feather to the Glass Tarn
It fought with all my habits. Every feint I like, it liked first. I won by doing something I would never do.
Defeat the reflection that climbs out of the tarn
Three doorways, and mist pouring through all of them. I walked through none. The mist parted anyway, and beyond it, across the water, was Artaeum.
Stand beneath the Threefold Arch at night
Cross to Artaeum and find the Mistward Ledge
Give Seyvel another chance. He chose well.
Kindness. We'll call it a fourth trial and see whether he survives it.
He cheated. Let him own it.
Honesty. He will resent you for a decade and thank you for a century. That's a good trade, on Artaeum.

You passed his. He failed his own. His trial was to sit at that table himself; instead he spent a season finding a stranger who would do it for him. A novice who can find the right stranger is worth something, I suppose. So is the stranger.
Speak with Master Ansarwe
Seyvel says I passed his test.
A Psijic novice named Seyvel tested me with bread, a reflection and a doorway, because he was afraid to face his own trial. Master Ansarwe let me keep what I earned anyway.
The Unasked Question
story.skycraft.q.side_sum_the_white_hero: Envoy Thaurwen Copperleaf, a Bosmer diplomat in Firsthold, asked me to investigate three murders marked with the white heron of the Unbroken Circle, Altmer radicals who despise the Dominion's alliance with Bosmer and Khajiit.
Examine the orchard where the last body was found
The brush came from the Watch's own stores. Either the Circle had a friend in the Watch, or someone wanted it to look that way.
Search the orchard for anything the killer dropped
Find the Unbroken Circle's meeting place at Heron Cloister
Unbroken Circle Zealot
Circle Lector
Break up the Unbroken Circle's meeting

The Circle had argued for three meetings about who kept painting herons on corpses, and whether they ought to be grateful. One member had seen the painter: an Altmer in a Watch cloak, at the south road post.
Take the Circle's minute-book
Talonmir said Firsthold needed a reason to close its gates to beastfolk, and the Circle needed a crime worthy of them. He only gave each what it wanted.
Watch Loyalist
Confront the Watch-Captain at the south road watchpost
Tell the city the whole truth.
Truth is a diplomat's only real currency. I'll spend it, even on them.
Let the Circle carry the blame. They'd have done it eventually.
Convenient. Probably even true. I'll sleep badly, but I'll sleep.
Then Firsthold owes the Circle an apology, and I would sooner eat a candle. What do you advise?
Report to Envoy Thaurwen in Firsthold
The Watch-Captain painted the herons. The Circle is guilty of a great deal, but not these murders.
You look like you're counting exits.

The heron murders outside Firsthold were the Watch-Captain's work, dressed in the Unbroken Circle's colours to frighten the city into closing its gates. Envoy Thaurwen now decides what Firsthold hears.

Two Bosmer and a Khajiit dead in the orchards outside Firsthold this month, each with a white heron painted on the chest. The heron is the sign of the Unbroken Circle, Altmer who think the Dominion is a dilution of their blood. The Watch-Captain says he is looking into it. I'd like someone to look faster.
Heronfeather Bow
The White Heron
story.skycraft.q.side_thr_the_coral_ledg: Keeps-the-Tally of Lilmoth believes a Sload keeps a coral ledger of debts owed by Argonian clans since the old plague wars, and that it means to collect.
Land on the reefs of Thras
Reef Dreugh
Fight off the reef dreugh
Kill Old Shell-Mother
Find the coral vault beneath the reef
Drowned Clerk
Coral-Bound Debtor
Destroy the vault's drowned clerks
Kill Ghaavorth the Patient
Ghaavorth's ledger held four thousand years of debts, page after page of Argonian clan names, with Keeps-the-Tally's own near the end.
Take the Coral Ledger
Grind it to sand and give it back to the sea.
Sand forgets. The sea forgets. Then Lilmoth may forget too. Good.
Read the names to the Hist, so the roots remember them freely.
Remembered by roots, not by slugs. Yes. The Hist will hold them gently.
So heavy. So many names. Even mine. What should become of it?
Bring the ledger to Keeps-the-Tally
Here is every debt the Sload ever wrote down.
What debt are you tracing?
Ghaavorth the Patient waited four thousand years and collected nothing. Lilmoth's hatchlings sleep without dreams of slugs.

Our egg-mothers say the Sload never forget a debt. They write them in coral and wait for them to ripen. Now Lilmoth's hatchlings dream of a slug reading their names aloud. The water has a long memory. Go to Thras, find the book, and make it forget.
Debt-Breaker
The Coral Ledger
story.skycraft.q.side_thr_the_drowned_co: Brother Cassian Velle of Anvil was the only survivor of the Blessed Gull, whose crew walked into the sea off Thras. He asked me to lay them to rest.
Land on the coral shore of Thras
Drowned Congregant
Release the drowned crew of the Blessed Gull
Find where the hymn is coming from
Chapel Dreugh
Break through the dreugh guarding the coral chapel
Kill the Sload Thallomuth
The covenant traded the crew of the Blessed Gull for safe passage, one soul kept back as witness. It was signed by Brother Cassian Velle.
Take the kelp covenant from the Sload's lectern
Candles aren't enough. Tell Anvil the truth.
Yes. From the pulpit, this Sundas. Stendarr is the god of mercy, not of hiding.
They're at rest now. Carry it yourself.
I will carry it. Every day. Thank you for setting them free.
The ship was sinking. The Sload offered to calm the sea. I thought it meant only the sea. I have lit a candle for every one of them, every night, for two years.
Confront Brother Cassian with the covenant
Your signature is on this, Brother.
What happened to the Blessed Gull?
The hymn no longer rises from the water off Thras. In Anvil, Brother Cassian still lights his candles.

Her whole crew walked over the rail one calm night off the coral isles and into the sea, singing. I alone was left alive on a lifeboat. Now sailors say they hear the hymn from the water near Thras. I must know they're at rest. Will you go where I can't bear to?
Stendarr's Tide
The Drowned Congregation
story.skycraft.q.side_vw_a_knot_tied_wro: Spinner Hathel of Woodhearth helped his clan, the Ninth Root, call a small Wild Hunt for revenge. He tied the rite-cord wrong, and the Hunt turned on the clan that called it.
Go to the Ninth Root lodge in Greenshade
They still had clan tattoos under the fur. I tried not to look at them too long.
Drive off what's left of the clan
Find the rite-circle where the Hunt was called
Take the rite-cord from the circle
Empty. No... look here. The ninth knot. I tied it until hunger ends, when it should have been until the debt is paid. Debts end. Hunger never does. Not in Valenwood.
Bring the rite-cord to Spinner Hathel
Here's your cord. The lodge is empty.
The Wild Hunt Hathel called is still running because of one wrong knot. He says it will not stop until its heart stops.

Slavers from the sea took three of my clan this spring. The Ninth Root begged me to call the Wild Hunt, only a small one, only for the raiders. I tied the rite-cord myself. I tied it wrong. The Hunt took the raiders, and then it kept going, and it took the clan that called it.
story.skycraft.q.side_vw_cubs_of_two_cla: Headwoman Enwe Fernsong of Arenthia's son is missing, and so is a Khajiit kitten from Rashazi's caravan. Each side blames the other, and the border is close to blood.

Missing? Or hidden, so the Bosmer can say Rashazi's people took him? ... Jirr has been gone two nights. Jirr has also been talking for a month about Old Ash-Stripes, the senche that took our dray-beast in the eastern hills. Perhaps this one should have listened better.
Speak with Rashazi the Caravan-Mother
Enwe's son is missing too.
Two sets of small footprints, one with claws, walking side by side. Someone had drawn a very bad map in the mud with a stick.
Follow the children's trail into the eastern hills
Find Old Ash-Stripes' den
Two small heads popped up from behind a boulder as soon as the senche fell, both of them cheering.
Kill Old Ash-Stripes before it finds the children
Stolen? Jirr and Dellin are hunting! We were going to bring back the skin, and then nobody would fight, because nobody fights heroes. Jirr will run ahead and tell Rashazi. Was it a good plan?
Talk to the cubs
Your families think you were stolen.
Bring Dellin home to Arenthia
Split it between both clans.
Half a pelt each. Rashazi will want the bigger half. This once, let her have it.
Give it to the children. They earned it.
A Bosmer and a Khajiit sharing one blanket. There's a Spinner's tale in that, someday.
Together. With a stick-map. Rashazi is laughing so hard at her wagon that her guards have put their bows away. What do we do with the pelt?
Return Dellin to Headwoman Enwe
Your son and Rashazi's kitten went hunting Old Ash-Stripes. Together.
Are you expecting trouble with the Khajiit?
Arenthia's border feud ended with two children, one stick-map and a dead senche-tiger. Headwoman Enwe and Rashazi are not friends, but they now agree on something.

My boy Dellin is gone, two nights now, and the Khajiit wagons rolled in the day before. Their caravan-mother swears her people took nothing, then turns around and accuses us of stealing her own kitten. If nobody blinks by tomorrow, there'll be arrows in those wagons. Find my son. Quickly.
Ash-Stripe Claw
Cubs of Two Clans
story.skycraft.q.side_vw_lamps_under_the: Outside Falinesti I found a hunter's note in a broken Ayleid urn, warning of singing blue lamps under a strangler fig and the hunters who went down to them.

A cracked Ayleid urn half-swallowed by fig roots. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth, a hunter's note: The blue lamps under the strangler fig sing at night. Brannoc went down after them. Brannoc came back up singing, and he has not stopped.
Find the sinkhole under the great strangler fig
They kept humming even as they fought. The tune was not a Bosmer one.
Follow the roots down to the Ruins of Elnalorne
Pry the root-choked welkynd stone from its socket
Heliandil had been singing to the Bosmer for a hundred years, teaching them to dig him out one root at a time. He was three roots from free.
Ayleid lamps. My grandmother called them the stars that eat songs. I'll sink it in the deepest pool in the river, where nothing with ears can hear it. Thank you for not keeping it. Most do.
Bring the stone to a Spinner in Falinesti
This stone has been singing hunters into the ground.
Under a strangler fig outside Falinesti, an Ayleid lord named Heliandil had been singing Bosmer hunters into digging him free. The fig can keep its roots now.
story.skycraft.q.side_vw_mother_of_thorn: Old Ilwe Mossfoot of Falinesti told me an ancient spriggan matriarch called Mother Lirr has started killing foragers. The hunters want her dead; Ilwe says she wants to know why.
Mother Lirr let me walk out of her glade. She told me to bring her the name of whoever buys her children's bark.
Find Mother Lirr's glade west of Falinesti
Find the bark-strippers' camp
Bark-Stripper
Half-Peeled Spriggan
Drive off the bark-strippers
Rootwrath had been tied to a stake with its own vines and peeled a strip at a time, as the orders came in. It fought me because it could no longer tell one soft-skinned thing from another.
Put the half-peeled spriggan child out of its pain
Take the bundle of bark waiting for delivery
You stop buying, and I make peace with Lirr.
And the marsh-cough? ... I'll find another cure, or I'll be the one coughing. Go on, then. Tell her it was me.
Lirr killed three foragers. I'm going to finish her.
Then my basket stays full, and I'll sleep badly. We all pay for the cure somehow.
Spriggan-bark cures the marsh-cough. Half of Falinesti breathes because of my basket. I never asked where they peeled it, because I knew. Now what, hunter?
Confront Ilwe about the mark on the bundle
This bark is tagged with your mark, Ilwe.
