Enchanted spider-webs glow faint violet in the cages.
Gold veins gleam along the timbered adit walls.
Totems of bone and heather stand beside the smelter.
Mead casks and overturned tables litter the underground tavern.
Chitin arrows bristle from the oak bar.
Tiered stone ruins step down the twin waterfalls.
Two hagravens guard the summit word wall.
Clear underground streams rush through limestone basins.
An overturned rowboat rests on the gravel bar.
Stone canals channel dark water around the locked sarcophagus.
Saerek the Canal-Warden bursts the iron chains.
Hidden behind a rockslide, a Nordic stair drops into the cliff.
Sacrificial tables stand in the lower crypt.
Water cascades over the hidden cavern mouth.
Two concentric stone rings guard the ancient inner vault.
A single brass-domed Dwemer tower crowns the crag.
From the balcony, the Karth river winds far below.
A low stone barrow opens beneath a wind-scoured hill.
Three carved shields face a central weapon slot.
Stone steps climb past deer-hide tents to a high cave mouth.
An iron-worked sword pedestal stands inside.
A deep open-pit sinkhole drops into cut Nordic stonework.
Moonstone ore glitters in the torchlight.
Three opaque stone flasks rest on the vestibule pedestal.
Carved reliefs of a dragon priest line the iron doors.
Four animal-carved pull-handles stand before the inner sanctum door.
The summit word wall looks out across the northern crags.
story.skycraft.scene.scene_side_sky_rift: Torchlight glints off a high central balcony overlooking three iron gates.
Carved reliefs line the descending stairs.
Crumbling Nordic towers cling to the snowy crags of the southern pass.
A word wall faces the icy wind.
Two ancient stone towers straddle the high mountain saddle.
Charred bones ring the summit altar.
A natural stone bridge spans the shadowed cavern.
Soul gems hum beside a makeshift altar.
A notched iron helmet hangs on a stake outside the cave.
Stolen strongboxes sit behind a wooden barricade.
Dwarven stone arches ring a sunken star-map pedestal.
Birch leaves drift across the brass astrolabe.
Glowing mineral seams arch over a quiet stone shrine.
Crates of cut geodes rest beside a mossy pool.
Briar-vines twist around the spiral staircase of the tower.
Feather fetishes hang above the rooftop altar.
Bioluminescent fungi cast pale blue light over the underground falls.
Crudely lashed hides block the side tunnels.
Iron cages line the sunken courtyard of the ruined keep.
Cook-pots steam above the dog-runs.
The fortress-monastery rises stark against the snowy Jerall peaks.
Alchemical wells stand dry in the outer garden.
Timber palisades reinforce the crumbling stone walls.
Targets and weapon racks fill the inner bailey.
A deep shaft drops into the flooded cavern beneath Lake Geir.
Carved stone bridges arch over dark water.
Wooden beehives stand in neat rows beneath the golden birches.
Watch-dogs prowl the stone causeway.
Wild honeycombs drip from the mossy rock ceiling.
Sunlight slants across the cave entrance.
A wooden watchtower overlooks the narrow stone bridge.
Stolen merchant packs lie heaped behind the palisade.
Rusty ore carts sit where the mine gallery breaks into cut Nordic stone.
Blue burial flames flicker in the draft.
Stone stairs climb to an open plaza overlooking the volcanic tundra.
A curved word wall catches the northern gale.
Split honey-barrels lie scattered among the limestone boulders.
Claw marks score the pine props at the entrance.
Lanterns hang low in the subterranean taproom beneath the ruin.
A crimson spring bubbles up through cracked flagstones.
Dwarven stonework juts from the southern mountain slope.
Wind chimes of tarnished brass swing from the arch.
Wooden scaffolding rises across the cavern's buried temple face.
Charmed vigilants patrol the lantern-lit catwalks.
Splintered shields litter the base of the stone watchtower.
The signal brazier smokes on the roof.
Puzzle-pillars of weathered stone flank the iron portcullis.
Cold drafts whistle through the burial alcoves.
A tall stone beacon-tower guards the southeastern mountain pass.
Silvered torches burn bright against the mountain dusk.
A narrow escape tunnel opens behind the fort's outer wall.
The courtyard lever controls the heavy iron portcullis.
story.skycraft.scene.scene_side_sky_whit: Silver-mounted phials clink on a stone table inside the barrow.
A cold draft rises from the inner burial vault.
Sunlight streams through a hole in the cavern roof onto a rushing creek.
Bones and torn packs litter the mossy ledges.
Charred parchment pages flutter around the ritual table.
Archon Vayne turns from the brazier with a raised staff.
Gnawed oak barrel-staves litter the mouth of the cavern.
A battered hunter's horn hangs from a stalagmite.
Salted carcasses hang from a pine scaffold above the hollow.
Pelt-Stretchers line the sheltered rock overhang.
Painted ox-skulls mark the winding trail up the crag.
From the ledge, Whiterun's gilded roof gleams across the tundra.
Pried stone slabs lie beside an open sarcophagus.
Fresh boot-prints end abruptly at the inner altar.
An iron grate yawns beneath the snow-covered word wall.
Soul-gem shards glitter along the stone cages below.
An overturned Dunmer strongbox sits beside the bandit hearth.
Ash-salt jars lie smashed across the cave floor.
Cold mist pours from an ancient brass pipe wedged in the limestone.
Chaurus husks litter the ledges above the pool.
The circular stone forge still glows beneath the open dome.
Notched blades with pale-gold edges rest on the quenching rack.
Chests of stamped parchment sit behind the cavern waterfall.
The camp ledger lists half the steadings on the western plain.
Iron grapple-hooks hang beside the cave mouth overlooking the rapids.
A stack of stamped Riverwood pine lies inside the watch-chamber.
story.skycraft.scene.scene_side_sky_wint: Frozen bones and ship timbers litter the icy cave floor.
Sea-wind whistles through the ceiling fissures.
Weapon racks of silvered steel line the fortress hall.
A forge burns hot in the lower cellar.
Skeleton archers pace the snow-covered battlements.
Iron cell doors line the sunken courtyard.
Scratching sounds echo up from the glacial caverns beneath the cellar.
The great iron brazier on the roof waits for fuel.
A half-buried stone shelter opens beneath the snowbank.
Pages of arcane notes flutter near the campfire.
Icy winds scour the basalt steps below the shrine peak.
A weathered word wall overlooks the frozen valley.
Sunken Dwemer arches frame a vertical drop into the glacier.
Steam hisses from cracked bronze conduits.
Broken marble-grey columns crown the sea-swept island.
Waves crash against the ice floes below.
Stone steps descend beneath a snow-choked Nordic arch.
Frost runes glimmer on the inner doors.
Blue glacial ice arches over Chaurus chitin fences.
Frozen subterranean pools reflect the torchlight.
Sea-ice groans against the cavern walls.
Voryn the Ice-Binder stands beside a glowing soul-stone.
story.skycraft.scene.serana_wakes.0: The stone sarcophagus in the heart of the crypt slides open. A pale woman steps out, blinking, an Elder Scroll strapped to her back.
story.skycraft.scene.serana_wakes.1: Who are you? How long was I in there? Never mind. I need to get home. Castle Volkihar, in the north sea. Will you take me?
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.0: In the deepest chamber of Driftshade Refuge, silver-tipped arrows lie in bundles beside tanning racks no one wants to look at too closely.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.1: It's done. Without Krev and without Varek, the rest will scatter like crows. Stendarr keep me from feeling glad of it. I feel glad of it anyway.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_end.2: Jorrvaskr will drink to you tonight, Vigilant or no. Don't tell Vilkas I said so.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_list.0: Look at these names. A tanner. A woodcutter. A farmer whose only crime was selling mutton to Jorrvaskr's kitchen.
story.skycraft.scene.sh_the_list.1: The Silver Hand say they hunt beasts. I have hunted beasts for twenty years. Beasts do not keep lists.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath.0: Ah, a visitor! In the mind of Pelagius, of all places. He was so very interesting, before the strangling. Fix his little troubles and I'll go home. And you'll get a present!
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath.1: Leave me alone! Not you too! The Night Terrors, the Confidence, the Anger! They're all in here with me!
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_isles.0: Splendid! You've earned a holiday. Come along, come along, mind the door. It bites. Only on Tuesdays.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_isles.1: A door that was not there a moment ago swings open on a sky of impossible colours.
story.skycraft.scene.sheogorath_palace.0: My Isles! My city! My cheese! Take the staff, little mortal, and spread a little madness. Now off you pop, I have a lunch to forget.
story.skycraft.scene.side_aka_bone_beach: The beach is made of bones. Ribs as tall as ships' masts lean against each other, polished by the tide.
Dragon skulls line the path inland, each one carved with coiling serpent script, as if to say: these were ours to eat.
story.skycraft.scene.side_aka_drum.0: In a hall of blue ice an old Kamal sits alone, beating a great drum with a bone, slow and steady.
story.skycraft.scene.side_aka_drum.1: Sleep, sleep. The host sleeps while the drum speaks. Haskarr wants silence. Silence wakes the host. Let the drum speak, small warm one.
story.skycraft.scene.side_aka_shrine.0: You come for the Dragonguard's oath. They left it here as a promise: hunt every dragon in the west, and send the last of them home to us.
story.skycraft.scene.side_aka_shrine.1: They never sent it. The oath is broken. Their blood is ours to collect.
story.skycraft.scene.side_atm_landfall.0: Nothing moves on the Atmoran shore. The pines are cased in ice to their tips, and the wind makes them ring like glass.
story.skycraft.scene.side_atm_landfall.1: A longship stands upright a short way inland, frozen into a wave of ice that never broke.
Draugr sit at the long tables of the drowned longhouse, cups raised to a hearth that burns blue and gives no warmth.
One of them wears a Skyrim sailor's cloak, faded red, with a keel-and-hammer brooch at the throat.
Don't take the stone. We lit it, and it lit us. Eighty years at this table. Take it home and your whole hall will sit down with us.
story.skycraft.scene.side_atm_moot.0: The giants come out of the snow one by one and lay a block of ice on the cairn. Each block steams with cold.
story.skycraft.scene.side_atm_moot.1: When the cairn is high enough, the sea freezes to the south. Then we walk to the warm land, and the little men's halls become our larders.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_coral_speak: A voice bubbles out of the hold, thick and patient, as if spoken through a mouthful of water.
Little cough-city. Little cough-children. All so tender. My Voice has been very good to me. Come down and meet him.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_coral_unmas: Behind a curtain of rotting sailcloth sits a speaking-tube of brass, and beneath it a cask with a bladder sewn to its lid.
There was never a Sload aboard. Only a Dunmer with a good imagination, and a great many frightened acolytes who never thought to look.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_dream_hollo: The hollow is full of sleepers lying in the mud in a circle, breathing together. Their eyelids flicker.
Every hatchling in Stormhold dreams of me now. Such small dreams, such easy doors. Lie down with them, walker. It is warm.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_ebonroot_fo: Barrels of rock salt are stacked to the rafters, each stamped with the same ash-yam crest. Enough to kill every root for a mile.
Some of the Dunmer here have not yet heard that the war is over. Some of them have, and do not care.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_mourner_spe: A pale light hangs over the pool, shaped like a crouching mother with her arms around nothing.
They took my clutch-stone. Tsleeksh hands, Tsleeksh grandfathers. I take one egg every spring. I will take them until the stone comes home.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_ninth_muste: Ninth Legion, Second Cohort, present. Nobody relieved us. Nobody relieved us. We kept the gate.
The lizards came up out of the water and drowned my men. Honour us, citizen. Carry the eagle home and tell Gideon how we died.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_ninth_truth: Under the flooded cells the walls are scratched with tally marks. Hundreds of them, all made by clawed hands.
He opened the sluices when the rebellion came. The prisoners were in the lower cells. We heard them. We heard them until the water reached the ceiling.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_okeeh_heals: The holes in the bark close slowly, like eyes. Somewhere in the grove a frog begins to sing, then another.
The roots remember who bled them. The roots remember who stopped it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_okeeh_speak: Amber weeps from a dozen small holes in the bark. The leaves above are the colour of old bruises.
Thin. Thin. A mouth on every root and none of them ours. Find the hands, warm-blood. The hands know the names.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_ukalith_fal: Fool. The stone was not my treasure. It was my chain. Keep it turning, or the marsh forgets what year it is.
The embalmed priest folds into his robes like a dry leaf. The calendar stone ticks once in your hands, then again.
story.skycraft.scene.side_bm_ukalith_wak: The stair goes down further than the mound is tall. The air smells of resin and wet stone, and of something that has been asleep for a long time.
Count with me. Wet season. Dry season. Wet season. You are the first season in four thousand that walked in on two legs.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_anyandil_d: The sealed door of Anyandil slides apart at the touch of the brightened stone. Beyond it, a lump of black meteoric glass sits on a dais, and it is breathing.
You lit the wells. You opened the door. You were very kind. I have not stretched my wings in nine hundred years.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_boethiah_s: Snow hisses where it touches the shrine. The cultists part, and a Dunmer woman in grey steps forward, smiling.
The stranger who kills for us. Drevis promised you would come. He sent you to cut down Thalyn so he could climb, and now he hopes you will cut me down too.
A knife that knows whose hand it is in. How rare. Show me whether it can also choose.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_drowned_re: The stilt-houses of Drowned Rest are freshly painted and the people are very friendly. They sing to the water every evening, softly, like a lullaby.
No one here will say where the children are.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_grove_spea: Moonlight on the ruin of Talwinque. Among the stumps of an old grove, a woman made of bark and grapevine rises from the ground.
Two young men with one axe between them. Castellus and Merovane. They cut my grove to plant their first rows, and shook hands over the stumps.
Thirty summers I waited. Now their vines drink my sorrow, and they blame each other. Let them. I am not finished.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_hrota_meet: The smugglers' leader lowers her crossbow. She has the inspector's jaw and the inspector's habit of squinting at strangers.
So my father sent you. Of course he did. Ask him where the Saltworks crew get their papers stamped, and watch his face.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_istirus_ro: At midnight, pale shapes in Legion red form two ranks in the yard of Fort Istirus. Their necks are bent at the same wrong angle.
Roll of the watch! Twenty men present. Deserters, every one, and hanged for it. Again, from the top.
No ghost answers to the twenty-first name. The prefect never calls it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_lamp_lifte: The moment the lamp leaves its niche, every welkynd in the hall goes dark at once.
Thief. I kept that flame for four thousand years. You will not keep it for four minutes.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_lantern_fo: Past midnight, a single green lantern drifts along the far bank of the Larsius, too slow for a boat and too steady for a drunk.
It stops, as if waiting for you, and then sets off north.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_narindel_w: The air in Narindel tastes of old lamp-oil. Somewhere below, a blue light pulses slowly, like a sleeper's breath.
Another little Imperial with a lantern of her own. Come down, then. Every lamp in this place was lit with someone like you.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_naso_shrin: Inside Fort Naso, a statue of a hooded figure has been carved from a single block of grey stone. Every one of its hands holds a knife pointed at the one beside it.
Votive daggers lie at its feet, each bent and straightened three times.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_oath_break: A crack like a falling tree echoes across the mountains. Snow slides from every ledge above the barrow.
Far up the slope, on the Giant's Stair, something very large stands up and stretches for the first time in an age.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_oxhorn_mee: A minotaur kneels beside a moss-covered cairn, scraping old Cyrodilic letters back into the stone with one horn.
Not a beast. A watchman. The Saint sleeps here, and I keep her sleep. The baron's dogs have found us. Will you stand, or run like the last one?
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_rayles_roo: Feathers and bones hang from the broken gate of Fort Rayles, tied with ribbons of green and gold.
Gold and green. Do you know those colours, little errand-runner? I wore them once, before my brother cut me out of the book.
Every heir of Vallarius sickens at thirty because every heir of Vallarius forgets me. Tell Cassia that, if you live.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_skeldhaugr: Thieves in my hall. Do you not hear the ice groaning? I hold it shut. I have always held it shut. Put. It. Back.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_urn_speaks: The wax seal on the urn cracks the moment the necromancer falls. A thin grey shape coils up out of it, wearing a very disappointed expression.
Finally, someone competent. Do you know who carried me out of the shrine and sold me to that woman for forty drakes? My grandson. Forty! I was worth at least a hundred.
Ervyn said I talked too much. I am dead, outlander. Talking is all I have left.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_valcis_led: Most of the names in the undertaker's book end with a burial fee. Too many end with a second price, larger, beside the word 'sold'.
Pia? Is that you, girl? Go home. The dead don't mind being useful, and neither should you.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_well_wakes: The starved stone hums. Far down the dry well, something answers in a voice like glass being drawn across glass.
Two wells, and the door. Light them for me, walker, and I will show you a star that fell and did not break.
story.skycraft.scene.side_cyr_wendir_bea: A knight sits on a broken Ayleid step at Wendir with a black sword across his knees. He has not eaten in a long time. The sword has.
Another one. Good. This one is very tired. You look rested.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_choir_sing: Khajiit in scaled mantles kneel around a ribcage half buried in the sand, chanting one word over and over. The bones are smoking.
Alkosh sleeps in these bones! Sing, brothers, sisters! Sing until the Dragon-Cat remembers he has wings!
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_collector_: The air in the ruined counting-house smells of hot coins. A shadow stands up from behind the desk that has no one to cast it.
Twenty years of luck, paid. The debt is due. The merchant died owing; the debt passes to his blood. Unless you would like to pay it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_cove_night: Lanterns bob on the black water. The smoke over the cove is sweet enough to taste, and the crews singing on the beach do not sound happy.
Some of them wear farmer's sashes under their pirate coats.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_dark_rises: One by one, every lamp in the cistern gutters out. The dark that fills it is not empty. It breathes.
Light is a lie the moons tell. Namiira tells the truth: before everything, there was nothing, and it was hungry. Come and be honest with us.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_dragon_wak: The ribcage cracks. Flesh crawls up the bones like fire up a curtain.
ALKOSH? You sang a stranger's name to me for a hundred years, little cats. I am Morvunrah, and I am hungry.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_fields_gre: The cane stands tall and grey as ash. Where a stalk has split, the sugar inside is the colour of wet slate.
Ri'zhassa's grandmother planted this row. It glittered like the moons once. Now look at it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_hunger_hai: Green lamps burn along the rail of a ship that has been on the rocks for twenty years. Somewhere in the hold, someone is calling a name.
Keeper! Keeper, you put out your light and let us strike. Twenty years I have asked for you. Who are you, to come in his place?
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_lattice_ti: Nine standing stones ring the hill, each one carved with a phase of the moons. Three have been turned to face the wrong sky.
You see? A cub born under this hill tonight would be born under the wrong moons. Azirr cannot say what furstock it would be. No one could.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_palms_brid: The estate's great hall is laid for a wedding feast that rotted long ago. A bride in grey silk sits alone at the head of the table.
He promised forever, and then he aged. So inconsiderate. I kept him in the cellar as long as I could. Will you stay for the feast?
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_pazhi_gran: Oh, the big one is slow. Pazhi was nearly bored. Here is a riddle: why would a lord care so much for a little ring?
The Alfiq flicks its tail and is gone between two sacks of grain. On the floor it has left a tithe-receipt, sealed with a lion's head.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_pazhi_vill: Here is where the ring does its work. Tithe papers, sugar papers, papers that make farmers owe what they never borrowed. Pazhi only took the stamp. Pazhi is a very honest thief.
The lord's knife is coming. Pazhi is small, and leaves now. You are big. Good luck.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_tomb_opens: The tomb's door is carved with a lion-headed warrior holding a pass alone against a host. Sand pours from the cracks like water.
No one passes. No one reads. The First Claw sleeps with his glory. That is the bargain, and I keep it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_els_tomb_truth: It was Nahrisha who held the pass. Ja'khizzar ran. They needed a hero with a good name, and his was better than mine.
Nahrisha agreed to guard his lie forever, so the clans would not lose heart. A thousand years is long enough. Tell them, if you like. Or do not.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_bahzir_fall: My father was in the ninth wagon. Nobody hanged for it. Nobody even asked. So I asked him myself.
The risen dead fold to the ground as one, like puppets with the strings cut.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_brine_hollo: Rope pens stand under a fold of the cliff. Small faces look up from inside them. One of them is missing a front tooth.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_cistern_fin: The display case holds a gilded scimitar. Behind it, wrapped in oilcloth in a hollow of the wall, lies a second, plainer blade that rings like a bell when you touch it.
Tucked into the oilcloth is a note in Huzayra's hand: 'Leave the gilt one in the case. The fool will take it and the watch will take the fool.'
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_devilrock_c: Red thread is knotted to every thorn bush on the rock. Three women in grey sit around a spring that smells of rot.
The Mountain Witches set their Mother-Stone above our spring and turned it sour. Cut the stone with this thorn, and Devilrock will remember you kindly.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_drowned_cou: Steps lead down into a palace the sea took long ago. Lamps of whale oil burn on the flooded stair, and dancers move in the half-dark.
A guest who was not invited. The Selenu have held court beneath Sentinel since before its walls. We do not care for intrusions.
The boy came to us willingly, as his mother did once. Ask her about the price she never finished paying.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_faugta_serm: Bodies in caravan shrouds stand in rows like an audience. At the far end a gaunt man reads to them from a ledger.
Tell me who held the knife. Tell me, and I'll let you lie down again. That's all I ever ask of them.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_gullwhistle: Two longboats are drawn up on the shingle. The flag on the nearer one is a Forebear trading house's. The flag on the other is a Crown lord's. Neither is honest.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_khalid_conf: Enough. I yield. Forty years I waited for this and I find I'm too tired to die properly.
Ask Turaz why he lost to me the first time. A bookmaker paid him to. I won a duel I never fought, and I have carried the shame of it since.
He presses a folded slip of paper into your hand. The ink is old, but the name on it is clear.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_mother_ston: A standing stone wrapped in goat-hair rope leans over a dry gully. An old woman sits at its foot, carding wool.
Below her, in the gully, the Devilrock spring has cut a new channel straight through the Mountain Witches' graves.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_mzindhal_co: Behind the Warden's chamber a cage of brass rods hums in a single, unbroken note. A man is curled up inside it, very thin and very much alive.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_sahrazad_ju: The shade lowers her blade. Sand trickles from the joints of her armour like an hourglass running out.
You fight like someone who has buried friends. Good. My granddaughter's granddaughter sold my funeral gold to a Forebear dealer and sent you for the rest.
The sword goes with you, not with her. What you tell her is your own affair. Walk well.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_sahrazad_wa: The lamps in the burial hall have been cold for four hundred years. One of them lights itself.
A living hand, reaching for a dead woman's sword. My blood sends a stranger to do what it lacks the spine for.
Very well. In Yokuda the blade chose its bearer. Show me your hands are worth the choosing.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_salt_terrac: Twelve old blades are driven into the salt crust in a ring. A man in faded Ra Gada leathers waits inside it, eyes closed.
Turaz sends a champion. Of course he does. Draw, stranger, and let us see whether his school still teaches anything.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_starfall.0: The hollow is glassed over, black and smooth, as if a giant had poured out a cauldron of night. At its centre something glitters.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_starfall.1: Little warm thing. Carry me somewhere high and I will show you how the sky is made.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hf_thornwatch_: As the sun goes down, the empty walls of Thornwatch fill with figures in rusted half-helms. They take their posts without a word.
Relief? Is that relief? No. Another one come to tell us the passes are quiet. Get off my wall.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_aubert_cryp: Sixty years in a box, and my granddaughter was the only one who missed me. She opened the door. Did she tell you that?
The Vraseth do not die, child. We simply wait for someone who loves us to forget what we are.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_cellars.0: The cellars under the old ferry house are full of people: Orc families, a Reachman grandmother, two Khajiit children asleep on sacks. Nobody here looks like a smuggler.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_dunmoor_nig: Every curtain in Dunmoor Hall is drawn, and every candle is lit. In the dining hall the table is set for six. The food has been there for days.
From below, through the floor, comes the slow sound of someone very old climbing stairs.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_gaersmith.0: Among the dead apple trees stands a cart loaded with lamp-oil and bundled straw, and a stack of painted fire-wards: 'Blessed by the Bell-Ringer, two drakes'.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_glenmoril_g: Rings of pale mushrooms circle a hollow oak. Three women sit in its roots, sorting bones by size.
Wenna's errand-runner. She told us you'd come. The witchfinder Aldous Mire has one of ours staked out in his camp east of here, waiting on a dry day for the burning.
Bring her back to us, and the coven will owe you. On the day of a certain Prince, we can call him for you. That is a debt worth holding.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_hargrave_tu: Boots on the stairs. A big man in an oilskin coat comes down with a crossbow levelled at Mother Odile.
"Warden pays better than you, Odile," he says. "And the slavers in Daggerfall pay better than the Warden."
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_hawkston_we: The old tower is sheathed in web from the foot to the lamp-room. The lamp is dark. Something heavy shifts at the top of the stairs.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_heron_vigil: The chapterhouse roof has fallen in, but the stone heron above the altar still stands, one leg raised, waiting for something.
Who keeps vigil in my hall? Go to Copperston, if you would know where the Heron's honour went. I will be waiting.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_lornhallow_: At midnight the dust on the stairs lifts and settles into the shape of a woman in grey. She stands at the cellar door with her arms spread.
Not up. Not ever up. He stays below with what he did. Help me keep him there, or help me end him. I'm so tired of standing here.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_malcor_conf: They meant to sell her. Chrysamere. To pay the order's debts to a Wayrest banker. So I took her and I lay down here and I swore no one would.
You fight like a Heron. Take her. Better a stranger with honour than an order without it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_marrowgate_: Something that was a man sits under the gallows, flesh hanging off it like wet linen. It looks up at you with relief.
Did he send you? Oh, thank the Eight. Never to die, I said. He never said anything about not rotting. Please. Be quick, and don't make any wishes.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_mastercroft: Castle Mastercroft's hall is hung with red wool, the colours of the Daughters of Wroth, but stained dark. A woman in a white gown sits on the high seat.
Morwen sent you. My little sister never could do her own work. I left the Daughters because they would grow old and die on that mountain. I chose not to.
There is room in the Lyrezi for one more. Or there is room in the crypt. Choose quickly, I'm hungry.
I saw the orchard. I saw a woman with my mother's eyes and a tinderbox. I didn't want to see it. I never want to see any of it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_saerendil_f: Fool. Fool. Three thousand years I held it.
The floor-stone cracks from end to end. Heat pours up through the crack, and a horned shape climbs out after it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_saerendil_w: At the top of the spire a figure in rotten violet robes stands over a sealed floor-stone, both hands pressed flat to it.
Breton. Of course a Breton. Your grandfathers' grandfathers broke my house, and now you come to finish the job. Go home. I am holding something shut.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_thunderheel: Half the cairn is gone, carted off in neat orcish blocks. What remains is a ring of standing stones taller than a house, and a giant sitting among them, rocking, with a stone in its lap.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_vile_paymen: Paid in full. You see, I always keep my word. It's the listening that trips mortals up.
Your reward is in your pack already. Be careful what you wish for with it. Or don't. I do so enjoy my repeat customers.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_vile_summon: Mother Brannagh pours wine, salt and a hair from your head into the bowl at the shrine's foot. The air goes thick and sweet, like an overripe pear.
My day, my shrine, and a mortal with a coven's favour to spend. How delightful. Here is my price: a man named Marrowgate cheated me. Not of anything important. But I keep my accounts.
He is at the Gallowmoor crossroads, north of Camlorn. He wished never to die. Show him how generous I was.
story.skycraft.scene.side_hr_ysmay_rests: There. It's quiet. Give my ring to whoever owns this house now, and tell them to open the windows.
The grey shape drifts apart like breath on a cold morning. The ring stays in your palm.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_bloom_plead: I did not escape. He carried me out in a sack and left me for the crabs. He was too proud to burn a failure.
I can feel the grove thinking. It is slow and kind. Please. Tell the steward I died.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_bloom_turns: A binding-rune flares on the Bloom's bark-skin, carved there long before it walked out of the tower. The voice in the grove stops being Velsa's.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_bolvyn_fall: Tell Hjolfrid... no. Tell her I drowned. She's had twenty years to like that version.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_brass_track: Deep drag-marks run from the road into Arkngthand. Crates with Brucius Allene's salvage stamp lie at the door, empty, as if something carried their contents back inside.
Somewhere below, a valve sighs, and a heavy foot comes down in perfect time.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_cairn_opene: The Pact Cairn has been opened from the inside. The stones lie outward, and frost-rimed bootprints lead west across the Stonefalls scrub.
Three peoples swore. Three names were cut. Two remain. Bring me the one who took mine.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_coffin_knoc: One of the coffins stacked on the landing is knocking. Inside, under a crust of embalming salts, a man blinks up at you.
I came to bury my aunt. The embalmer gave me tea. Is this... is this Necrom? Why is it so dark?
The harvesters' camp is flattened. Among the wreckage stands a crate packed in wet kelp, and from inside it comes a soft clicking, like many small claws on wood.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_dravil_spea: A living foot in my house, at last. Listen. My brother Ulvon poured poison in my cup and smiled while I drank it.
His bones rest in Othrelas, among the family he married into. Carry them out and scatter them in the ash. Then I will sleep, and so will my grandson.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_lantern_lit: The old Velothi tower has been fitted with a lantern of gray glass. Its light falls not on the true channel but on the reef beside it, where hulls lie stacked like firewood.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_quiet_cup_l: You were sent to find me, not to ask me questions. Pity. Ask the scribe who writes my orders in such a lovely hand.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_ravani_empt: Tel Ravani's growth-vats stand cracked and dry. One was powered by a Dwemer regulator coil, wired in with a Telvanni's contempt for neatness. A trail of pale spores leads out of the tower and down to the shore.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_razor_wakes: The stone underfoot is warm. Rust-red veins in the walls pulse slowly, and the old altar is slick though no one has bled on it for an age.
Mortal. The Razor's shard waits on my altar. Take it, and carry Ald Kharvenu with you wherever you go. Or try to take it from me, and carry nothing ever again.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_runner_foun: Do not draw, walker. J'darr is not a smuggler. J'darr is a debt with legs. Llaro owns the debt, and the legs.
The Imperial lady sent you? Then she sent you to close a mouth. Here, read who she drinks with. J'darr would rather be poor than quiet and dead.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_sleepers.0: In the dark of Sharapli the sleepers sit in rows, rocking. They hum one long note through ash-grey lips, and none of them stops to breathe.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_spring_sour: The shared spring smells of bile. Pale shreds of gall-root float on the surface, and the netch drifting over it twitch and drop, then rise again too fast.
Ash comes sideways, thick as felt. Through it looms the strider, folded on its long legs like a tent with the poles kicked out. It moans softly. A man answers it in the same note.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_thelvas_fal: The ash-mask cracks and falls away. Beneath it is a tired Dunmer face, and the mouth shapes a single word before it goes still: Aldam.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_thelvas_spe: The Mountain's heart is gone, and still it dreams. It dreamed me. You knew me, once, under another name. Do you remember it? I am beginning not to.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_ulvon_speak: He sent you for my bones. Of course he did. While I lie whole, the Sandas door stays shut on him.
Dravil poisoned my wife for her dowry. I struck him down for it, and our mother hid the truth to save the family name. Her letter is in my urn. Read it, then decide which of us is lying.
story.skycraft.scene.side_mw_warden_fall: The Steam-Warden kneels, and its chest-plate swings open on an empty socket shaped for a single coil. Everything else it carried home is laid out in neat rows behind it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_pya_mist_parts: The mist hangs like a wall over the water, then parts in a tunnel exactly where your boat sails, closing again behind you.
On the shore, a lantern of blue glass burns on a coral post. Someone wanted you to find the way.
story.skycraft.scene.side_pya_rookery.0: Nests of woven kelp line the cove, each the width of a cart. Most are empty and torn apart. Woodhearth sawdust is scattered on the sand.
story.skycraft.scene.side_pya_rookery.1: So the tree-folk send a champion. Your harbor stole our eggs, warm-blood. The Old Coil only wants her children back.
story.skycraft.scene.side_pya_thessaril_: Your Lieutenant's grandfather burned our coast with the fleet of Alinor. My grandmother sang the first mist that night, so they could never find us again.
Carry the lantern back to him, and his ships will come through the wall. Or break it. Either way, I will not let you leave with it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_aslief_cou: Kynareth keep the little ones, wherever they've wandered.
If you mean to help, friend, start with the caravan by the road. Search the cats' wagons. I'd wager you'll find small shoes.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_aslief_rev: You shouldn't have come. They're only sleeping. I'd never hurt them.
Arkay closed his door on my Ingrid. But children breathe so easily. A little of their breath each night, and she opens her eyes. Just for a moment.
On a bier behind him lies a girl ten years dead, her cheeks painted pink, her hair freshly braided.
The old bakehouse smells of honey and something sharper. Crates marked FLOUR are packed with grey-white moon sugar.
A note on the oven, in a woman's round hand: 'Dar'Vasha. Twice the sugar next week. The children like them sweeter.'
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_beacon_nig: On the headland above the grotto a lantern swings slowly, side to side, the way a harbor light does.
Steady, steady. Another hour and she'll come right onto the rocks.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_coldvein_r: Clean beds, warm blankets, candles in every niche. Someone has made the old cells comfortable.
I take only the ones Windhelm has already thrown away. A warm bed, a full belly, and a quiet last night.
Tell me which of your Jarl's guards has done as much for them.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_coven_look: A woman's shawl hangs from the antlers of a Forsworn totem, neatly folded, as if left for someone to find.
Crow feathers are bound into the antlers with red wool. A folded letter is pinned beneath a crow's skull.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_crowsong_s: She came to us with a split lip and a finger set crooked. We offered her a beak and talons, so no man would ever lay a hand on her again.
The change wants a heart, little sword. Hers was too soft. So we'll take his. She was going to fetch it for us tonight.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_custodian_: Fences lie flattened in a straight line, as if something walked through them without noticing they were there.
The tracks don't lead to the farmhouse. They bend away north-east, toward Nightgate Inn, where Corvin Vale is waiting.
The great brass head turns toward the key in your pack, and the furnace in its chest roars.
Ahoy, the shore! I'm Ulvis Dren, master of the Velothi Promise. I stayed at her wheel until the ice took her. Every soul aboard, I tried.
Tell them that, when you go back. Tell them Dren stayed.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_dren_log.0: The last entry is barely legible: 'Hold locked to keep the panic down. Taking the boat for help. Will return.'
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_dren_log.1: The boat lies upturned twenty paces from the wreck, its hull stove in. The hold door is still barred from the outside.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_feud_pitch: The tracks from the burned woodpile smell of pitch. They run along the riverbank, away from both houses, toward the cave in the hills.
A naked man kneels before the Lady Stone, shivering, dried blood in his beard. He sees you and does not run.
Tell Ulfgar I didn't kill those woodcutters. I can't stop what I turn into, but I don't hunt men.
Runa does. She keeps the graveyard. She gathers us in Moss Mother Cavern and feeds us from the graves so we'll learn the taste.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_maw_tracks: The prints by the woodpile belong to a wolf, but each is as long as your forearm.
Walking in the same line, step for step, are the prints of a man's bare feet.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_moldering_: In the lee of the broken wall, someone has swept the snow into a neat circle and set five candle stubs around it.
A child's wooden horse lies in the middle. Its tail is tied with grey thread, the kind priests of Arkay braid into their prayer cords.
Garrison! Roll call! Bjornolf. Present. Sild. Present. Hrolf the Younger. Present.
Silence. The wind moves over the broken wall.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_stuhn_free: As you read the last name aloud, the chains in every cell go slack, one after another, like a held breath let go.
Ransom paid. Doors opened. Stuhn keeps his word, even late.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_stuhn_hall: Rows of stone cells line the hall. Every door stands open, yet in each a draugr sits chained to the wall, as if it chose to stay.
Stranger. In the old days Stuhn's priests bought back warriors taken in war, and kept the ransom here. Then the Dragon Priests came wanting our captives for their armies.
We would not sell. So they made us keep them forever. Pay the price of your passage, or become my newest prisoner.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_torc_barro: The barrow's walls are carved with a story. A woman sleeps on a bier, the torc at her throat.
A man pries it loose while she sleeps. He has Gunnolf's broad shoulders, and Gunnolf's axe through his belt.
Thief's blood. I smell it on the bronze. Bring it here.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_torc_ghost: A pale shape rises from the broken stones: a broad man with an axe through his belt and marsh-weed in his beard.
That torc was a gift. The Mire-Bride gave it to me with her own hands, for my courage.
Don't carry it back to her barrow. She'll drown you as she drowned my blood. Smash it here, on my stones, and be done.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_torvar_sur: A grey-bearded smuggler throws down his sword and raises both hands.
Don't. I'm Torvar Kolfinn. Yes, that Torvar. I swam out of the river that night and kept swimming, and Eldra's boat picked me up.
Every year the feud ran hot, nobody on that bridge watched the water at night. Burning the logs was my job. I'm sorry for it. Mostly.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_tusk_basin: The camp is quiet. A giant sits beside the carcass of a mammoth whose tusks have been sawn off at the root.
It does not rise when you approach. Around the carcass, the snow is trampled by boots, and a sledge track runs east.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_tusk_retur: The giant watches you lay the tusk in the snow. It keeps its club across its knees.
After a long while it lifts the mammoth's great head and settles it on the tusk, the way you would set a pillow under a sleeping friend.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sky_veinhollow: Picks and lamps lie where they were dropped. Falmer arrows stand in the timber props like quills.
At the bottom gallery a new tunnel climbs out of the floor. It was dug upward, from below.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_brodir_was: A she-bear and two cubs lie in the snow at Brodir Grove, skinned and left. The meat has not been taken. The arrows have Skaal fletching, white goose with a single black band.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_deserter_p: Varon's guard post at Ashfallow Citadel is empty. His bonemold cuirass hangs neatly on its peg, and scratched into the wall above it is a short line: 'Father, I won't.'
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_frostmoth_: A horn sounds from the empty walls of Fort Frostmoth. Pale shapes in Legion red form ranks in the courtyard, and a sharp voice calls the roll.
Relief column is late. Courier Brenn is late. Hold the walls, legionaries. The Empire does not forget its garrisons.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_gallery_co: The new deep gallery is half rubble. Grey ash trickles through the cracks like sand in an hourglass, and behind the fall someone is tapping on the rock: three short, three long.
Drovas went past the red marks! We told him! There's a hollow back here, and something in it's breathing!
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_hunt_begin: A horn blows on Frykte Peak, though no one is there to blow it. Hounds bay in the dark below, and the moon looks down like an eye.
Prey is named. Prey runs. Prey is the stranger at the peak. The hunt ends at dawn, or at the throat.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_kruug_spea: Tall-folk break promise! Grandfather-chief take spear for mead-peace. Tall-folk stop mead. So Kruug take hall. Fair. Fair!
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_snow_walke: The wind on Hvitkald Peak drops to nothing. Then the snow itself stands up, broad as a hut, with eyes like old ice and no footprints behind it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_spire_sile: The prism comes free, and the Spire's note stops halfway through. Every gear in the tower halts. Whatever it was counting for four thousand years, it will never finish.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_spire_song: The Spire of Nchurdrel is singing: one long, deep tone that rises from its foundations and makes your teeth ache. Brass gears turn behind every wall, counting something.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_vorgrim_wa: The ring slides off the jailer's finger. Somewhere deeper in Gyldenhul, a door that has been shut for an age swings open by itself.
Eyvind's line, come at last to let me out. How kind. I will start my thanks with you.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sol_wind_wrong: The Skaal cache at the Stalhrim Source has been broken open. The ward-stones around it are scattered, and the wind moves in a slow circle here, as if looking for something it lost.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_aerie.0: The aerie is a crown of sticks and bones on the highest crag of Hawkspire. One speckled egg sits in it, alone. Harpies are circling, and they have seen you.
Three doorways stand in a row on the hilltop, framing nothing but sky. Mist pours through all three at once, though the night is clear.
Most choose a door. A few choose to wait. Hardly anyone notices that the mist parts for those who stand still.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_choir.0: The spire's upper rooms are dry, held in a bubble of still air. From below, through the stone, many voices are singing the same four notes over and over.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_choir.1: Hush. Listen. My choir has sung the tide in and out for four thousand years. They are happy. They would tell you so themselves, if they could stop.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_coil_rises: The conch's note runs out across the water and does not come back. Then the sea in the cove rises in a long, slow hump, and keeps rising.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_grey_grove: Among the indrik-berry bushes on the cliff, a few have been cut and bound with fresh grafts. Their berries are grey, and the grass around them is scorched.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_keeper_spe: The lighthouse lamp is not glass. It is a great lens of pink coral, pulsing slowly, and the light it throws smells of the deep sea.

A Sload of Thras grew it for me. It shines twice as far as any glass. The crews it brings in... they are not dead, exactly. They row now, under the sea, for a fleet that will come back for Summerset one day. A fair price for such a light.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_matriarch_: A shadow crosses the sun. The gryphon matriarch lands on the rim of the nest with a sound like a sail filling, and looks at you for a long, long time.
Then she lowers her head over the two eggs and stops looking at you at all. Beneath the nest, the old sticks have fallen away from a stone cairn, and a sword-hilt glitters in it.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_seyvel_rev: On the ledge, a hooded Altmer is pacing. He stops when he sees you and throws back his hood. He is very young.
You passed. You passed all three. Do you know how long I've been looking for someone who would sit at that table without eating?
About as long as you've been avoiding sitting at it yourself, Seyvel.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_starwell_w: The Starwell is a stone bowl cut into the cliff, open to the sky, ringed with brass instruments green with age. Several of them have been moved very recently.
At the rim, a stone watcher turns its head with a sound like a millstone. Its ward-runes have been chiselled away, neatly, by someone who knew which ones mattered.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_strand.0: Ribs of wrecked hulls stick out of the sand like a beached whale's. Every wreck faces the same way: toward the light on the headland.
A small table stands in the grass, laid for two: a white cloth, a warm loaf, two cups of tea still steaming. There is no one for a mile in any direction.
Sit. The first question is whether you will eat the bread. Take as long as you like. I have, as they say here, all the time.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_tarn_refle: The tarn is perfectly still. Your reflection in it is a heartbeat slow, and then a heartbeat fast, and then it is climbing out.
I know every trick you like. I know which foot you favour. I know what you would never do. Let's see if you do.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_tirnaril_l: A pale figure in Sapiarch's robes drifts between the niches, straightening urns that do not need straightening.
A visitor from the family? Tell my descendant I went to sea for the glory of the Tower, and came home, and fathered a son as pure as Alinor glass. Now go. There is nothing else in here.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_vault_patr: The shrine is heaped with fresh flowers in Valtaryon blue. A tall figure in steward's grey is arranging them with great care.
You've read the ledger. Nine centuries of good fortune, and not one Valtaryon ever asked who was paying for it. Every bargain needs a steward. I have been theirs.
The last payment is due. I will collect it from you instead, if you insist.
story.skycraft.scene.side_sum_ysla_hails: Blue-sailed boats are drawn up on the shingle, their hulls painted with coiled serpents. A tall sea-elf in a veil of netting stands at the waterline.
Tell my betrothed she can come to me, or I can come to her village. I have been patient for twenty years. Old Coil has not.
story.skycraft.scene.side_thr_chapel.0: A full crew, delivered as promised. One soul kept back, as agreed, to tell the tale on the shore. Your priest signs a careful hand.
story.skycraft.scene.side_thr_congregati: Drowned sailors stand knee-deep in the surf, facing out to sea, singing a hymn of Stendarr in voices full of water.
Each one wears the patch of the Blessed Gull on his shoulder.
story.skycraft.scene.side_thr_vault.0: Every debt is written. Every debt is due. I have waited four thousand years for these names to ripen. I can wait while you die.
Small lights drift between the reeds, just at the height of a lantern held by someone walking slowly.
Come in, come in, the water's warm. He came. They all came. He was always so easy to call home.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_bog_wakes.0: With the wispmother gone, the fog thins. Four hunters lie curled in the reeds, breathing, eyes open, hearing nothing.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_bog_wakes.1: One of them, an older Bosmer with a grey braid, keeps whispering the same name: Aelwen. Aelwen. Aelwen.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_cellar_foun: Under a burial mound outside Woodhearth, a door of new oak has been set into old earth. The smell of rotmeth gives way to something sweeter and much worse.
Rows of feast-chairs line the dark. Each has a name carved on its back. The newest is still sticky.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_den_hunt_vo: Prey that walks into the den. The knot said until hunger ends. I am hungry still. I will always be hungry.
My son tied this knot. Tell him the Hunt is grateful. Then lie down. It is easier.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_echo_flatte: The carved antlers on the stone run with green light, though no sun reaches them.
There you are. I have waited a long time for someone strong enough to carry my face. I was the Wilderking. Greenshade remembers me.
My mask lies at the Thornless Throne. Wear it, or give it to the one who carved this stone. Either way, I will be king again.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_empty_lodge: The Ninth Root lodge is grown from three living trees, its doorways shaped by centuries of coaxing. Every door is torn open from the inside.
Bowls of cold meat sit half-eaten on the floor mats. Claw-marks run up the walls, too high for any wolf.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_flayed_grov: A dozen jaqspur trees stand stripped to the pale heartwood, bark peeled away in long careful sheets. They are still alive. Sap runs down them like sweat.
The cuts are not a woodsman's. They are a craftsman's, taken along the grain, choosing only the straightest wood.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_hollow_oak_: Inside the hollow oak, old carvings cover the heartwood: a man in a crown of leaves, binding an antlered shape with vines, sealing its face in a mask.
Beneath, in Bosmeris worn almost smooth: Here the King put the Wild's hunger into a face, and the face into the dark, so it would never be worn.
Clever little carrier. Too clever. Then I will wear you instead.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_horn_speaks: The shrine's stone is wet with fresh blood, though nothing lies dead on it. Far off, a horn answers a horn.
Run, little quarry. Run well, and you may yet become the hunter. Run badly, and you will feed the Huntsmen, and the Huntsmen are always hungry.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_ink_trail.0: The ink stains lead from Falinesti to the shrine like drops from a leaking quill. At the altar, they pool into a single word, written and rewritten until the stone is black.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_ink_trail.1: More? You've brought more? No... you are not a Spinner. You are only a reader. Readers are such poor meals.
Blue light leaks up through the fig roots. Somewhere below, a voice is singing in a language older than any tree in Malabal Tor.
One more root. One more, little digger, and the stars will shine on Heliandil again. Sing with me while you dig.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_legate_gree: The dead graht-oak has been hollowed into a fort, its roots shaped into palisades and its trunk cut with arrow-slits. Moss has grown over the Legion eagle.
Citizen! At last, the relief column. The tree-folk broke the truce and murdered my cohort in their sleep. Avenge us, and the Ninth will rest.
story.skycraft.scene.side_vw_lirr_speaks: The glade goes quiet. A spriggan taller than a house-tree unfolds from the largest trunk, moss sliding from her shoulders like a cloak.
Another little hunter. Do you carry a knife for bark too? Your kind peels my children like fruit and sells their skins in the city.
Find the peelers and the one who buys from them. Bring me a name, and I will stop taking foragers. Bring me nothing, and I will take more.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_dig_camp.0: The dig camp is abandoned. Tents flap over empty bedrolls, and a long, smooth trench winds away into the dunes.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_dig_camp.1: Every tent has been rolled flat in the same direction, as if something huge passed through looking for one thing.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_hazadir_tr: This sword never tasted blood. When the Doom came, I put my family on the first ship and I did not look back.
Tell her. Tell my descendant what her ancestor was: a coward who lived, so that she could.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_nhalar_rev: Jaffir sent you? Dear Jaffir. He thinks I came for scrolls. I came for the Ra Gada sleeping under this sand, and the Mother wanted payment for the way.
I paid her. One digger a night. Now they dig for me.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_tomb.0: The tomb lies half under the sea. Salt water laps at the feet of stone Ra Gada warriors lining the hall, swords raised.
story.skycraft.scene.side_yok_tomb.1: A child of my line sends a champion. Good. Come, then, and see what I was.
story.skycraft.scene.skjor_dead.0: Skjor went after the Silver Hand alone while we slept. They left him in the road like a hide on a rack.
story.skycraft.scene.skjor_dead.1: Gallows Rock. That's where they keep their trophies. We take it apart, all of it.
story.skycraft.scene.solitude_falls.0: Castle Dour's gate falls in. General Tullius stands alone in his war room, sword drawn, his officers dead around him.
story.skycraft.scene.solitude_falls.1: It's done. Skyrim is ours. Sovngarde will sing of this day.
story.skycraft.scene.soul_cairn.0: A portal of red light opens in the courtyard. Beyond it, purple skies and drifting souls: the Soul Cairn, a realm of Oblivion.
story.skycraft.scene.soul_cairn.1: Serana? You came. Then Harkon is still chasing that prophecy. I hid the other Scroll here so he could never have it. Take it, and stop him.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.0: I am Tsun, shield-thane of Shor. None enter the Hall of Valor without facing me, but you, you have come for other business.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.1: We have waited a long age to finish what we began on the mountain. Lead us, Dragonborn.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_heroes.2: The mist thins. Alduin circles the Hall, devouring the lost. Clear the sky with your Voice and bring him down.
story.skycraft.scene.sovngarde_portal.0: The staff slots into the pedestal. A column of light swallows the sky, and the stones of Skuldafn fall away beneath you.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_hist_dream.0: The sap is bitter, then sweet, then gone. The marsh tilts. The trees lean down and look at you with no eyes at all.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_hist_dream.1: Shadow-born. You were laid in the dark and hatched in the dark. The dark is not your enemy. It is your egg. Hunt now.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.0: The Tong came for us, and the Tong is buried in our mud. Hear me, all of you. The one who did this was born under the Shadow, like you, and is now more than you.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.1: I am old. I will need someone to speak for the Shadow when the King calls. Not yet. But soon.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_speaker.2: Around the enclave, the Shadowscales lower their heads and touch the ground. One by one, they hiss your name.
story.skycraft.scene.ss_the_traitor_name: Weighs-the-Coin. He was hatched two nests from mine. I taught him to hold a blade.
The Morag Tong pays well for the names of rivals. He gave them every one of us. Go after him, and do not let him reach the river.
story.skycraft.scene.stone_cleansed.0: Another stone of the All-Maker is clean. The wind on Solstheim smells a little more like the sea and a little less like ink.
story.skycraft.scene.summit.0: Hermaeus Mora gave me knowledge, and then chains. I will have neither. You came to my summit: then die here, little rival.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.0: The room in the Waterfront hideout is dark except for one lamp. A figure in a grey hood sits behind it, and his face slides out of memory as soon as you see it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.1: Armand speaks well of you. I need someone who can go where I can't, and do it without leaving bodies for the Watch to count.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_gray_fox.2: This cowl was stolen from Nocturnal herself, long ago. It hides who I am from the whole world. Including the people I love. I mean to be rid of it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_homecoming.0: This ring. I would know it anywhere. Where did you... no. He's home. He's in the courtyard, isn't he? I can feel it.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_homecoming.1: Millona Umbranox crosses the hall without another word. Through the window, two figures meet beside the fountain and do not let go.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.0: The Gray Fox unrolls the Elder Scroll. Light that is not quite light pours over his hands, and for a moment the hideout seems to remember a different past.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.1: There. It's done. The world will remember a man named Corvus Umbranox, Count of Anvil. He didn't vanish. He only went away for a while.
story.skycraft.scene.tgc_scroll_read.2: And the cowl stays with the Guild. Someone has to wear it. I think it should be you.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.0: Orvanwe's family has served the Dominion for nine generations. He sold all nine of them for Windhelm gold.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.1: You found him, you judged him, and you did not hesitate. The Emissary has written to Alinor about you. I have been asked to read her letter aloud.
story.skycraft.scene.th_high_justiciar.2: The letter is short. It names you High Justiciar, and asks that you be given whatever you need.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.0: Music drifts through the embassy hall. Jarls' cousins and merchant princes hold their cups very carefully and smile at the Thalmor guards.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.1: Look at them. Every one of them hates us, and every one of them came. That is what power is: an invitation no one can afford to refuse.
story.skycraft.scene.th_reception.2: Mingle. Someone in this room has been selling my letters. Find out who before the wine runs out.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.0: The Scroll unrolls itself. The world goes grey; the snow freezes in the air. You stand among three warriors of an age long past, watching Alduin fall from the sky.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.1: Dragonrend has struck him! Now, while he is grounded!
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.3: It isn't enough. He won't die. Felldir, the Scroll! Use it now!
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.4: The vision tears apart. The three words of Dragonrend ring in your skull: JOOR, ZAH, FRUL. And above the summit, a black dragon descends.
story.skycraft.scene.time_wound.5: Dovahkiin. You are too late. Your Shout is a toy in my claws.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_ilunibi.0: Deep in Ilunibi, the walls are crusted with ash and something like wet bark. Low chanting echoes from a chamber below.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_ilunibi.1: A pilgrim of the false gods. How sweet. Come closer. Dream with us. The Sleeper is waking, and he remembers you.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.0: Beneath the High Fane, the Archcanon lays a hand on your brow. The light through the great windows is the color of Vivec's own city at dusk.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.1: You walked the Graces, purged the Sixth House, healed the blighted, weighed justice and mercy, and stood fast at Ghostgate.
story.skycraft.scene.tt_patriarch.2: The Temple has many servants. It has few shepherds. Rise, Patriarch.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_archmagister.0: Gothren falls among his own enchanted pillars. The tower of Tel Aruhn shudders once, and is still.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_archmagister.1: By Telvanni law, the strong rule. Gothren refused to step aside. Now he has, permanently. Archmagister, the Council awaits you, mostly with resentment.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.0: The Telvanni Council House is a forest of grown stone and silence. The masters sit far apart, each pretending the others are not there.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.1: My new Mouth will speak for me today. Listen, or don't. You usually don't.
story.skycraft.scene.tv_council.2: At least this one has some manners. More than the last.
story.skycraft.scene.und_drinking_contes: Glirion slams two tankards on the table. The ale inside is dark, thick, and smells faintly of pine tar.
The rules are simple. We drink. Whoever's still upright at the end gets to talk. Whoever isn't gets carried.
Five tankards later, the hall is spinning and Glirion is singing a song about a troll and a bishop that has at least nine verses too many.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.0: The three of them stand around the old horn as if it were a sleeping animal. Then Glirion hangs it on the trophy wall, in the empty space that has waited there for years.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.1: Every Undaunted who ever lived has looked at that empty peg and lied about filling it. You didn't lie.
story.skycraft.scene.und_legend.2: Don't let it go to your head. Your name goes on the wall. The next idiot has to beat it.
story.skycraft.scene.und_pledges_counted: Barrow, ruin, tomb, pyramid, Dwemer pit. Five pledges, five cultures, and you came back with all your fingers.
Most of them come back with fewer. Glirion lost a toe in Volenfell and still won't tell anyone how.
It was a gear. A very rude gear. Now, there's one delve left that none of us have finished, and I'd like to drink to it before we try.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.0: Beneath the Skyforge, in a hollow of rock, Skjor waits by a stone basin. Behind him stands a great wolf with Aela's eyes.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.1: The Circle carries a gift. Some call it a curse. Drink, and you become one of us in blood as well as name.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.2: The blood burns. For a moment the world smells of rain and fear, and you hear every heartbeat in Whiterun.
story.skycraft.scene.underforge.3: You will hunt now, and you will never be cold again.
story.skycraft.scene.vaermina.0: You walk in my dream, little thing. Erandur betrayed me once. Will you betray him, and take my Skull?
story.skycraft.scene.vale.0: Through Darkfall Cave the snow gives way to a hidden valley of waterfalls and pale trees, lit by a sun that never seems to set.
story.skycraft.scene.vale.1: You've come for the bow. Many came. The Snow Elves made sure none returned.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hall_burning.0: Smoke rises over the Hall of the Vigilant. The doors hang open, and on the snow outside lie Vigilants in their grey robes, very still.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hall_burning.1: They came at dusk, more than I have ever seen together. A lord of the Volkihar leads them. He is still inside. Stendarr guide your hand.
story.skycraft.scene.vg_hand_of_stendarr: The Hall can be rebuilt. The Vigilants who died here cannot. But they died holding the line, and you finished what they started.
Stendarr's Hand is not a title we give lightly. It goes to the one who stands when everyone else has fallen. Kneel. Rise, Hand of Stendarr.
Outside, the surviving Vigilants have begun clearing the snow from the Hall's steps.
story.skycraft.scene.voyage.0: The Northern Maiden noses out of Windhelm's harbor and turns north and east, into the Sea of Ghosts. Two days later, ash falls on the deck.
story.skycraft.scene.voyage.1: Raven Rock: a Dunmer town under a sky the color of an old bruise. Red Mountain smokes on the horizon.
story.skycraft.scene.whiterun_falls_legi: The rebels are breaking! Hold the gate! Whiterun stands with the Empire!
So be it. Whiterun has chosen. Gods help us all.
story.skycraft.scene.whiterun_falls_stor: The gate's down! For Skyrim! Whiterun is free!
Enough. Whiterun yields. Tell Ulfric he has his city.
story.skycraft.scene.windhelm_falls.0: The Palace of the Kings is quiet. Ulfric Stormcloak kneels in his own throne room and does not ask for mercy.
story.skycraft.scene.windhelm_falls.1: It's over. Skyrim stays in the Empire. Make sure the soldiers know who won this for them.
story.skycraft.scene.wrothgar.0: The mountain does not care who your parents were. Climb it, and kill what lives at the top. Then you are Orsimer enough for me.
story.skycraft.speaker.side_sum_grey_voi: A Voice in a Grey Hood
story.skycraft.speaker.side_vw_horn_voic: A Voice Like a Hunting Horn
